nodes.title: The quantitative Ekedahl geometric sieve (Bhargava, Theorem 3.3; Bhargava-Shankar, Theorem 2.17)
nodes.statement: Let B ⊂ ℝ^n be a compact set and let Y ⊆ 𝔸^n_ℤ be a closed subscheme of codimension k ≥ 1 (Krull dimension of its coordinate ring ≤ n + 1 − k). Then there is a constant C = C(B, Y) such that for all reals r ≥ 1 and M ≥ 2, #{a ∈ rB ∩ ℤ^n : a mod p ∈ Y(𝔽_p) for some prime p > M} ≤ C·(r^n/(M^{k−1} log M) + r^{n−k+1}).
hypotheses: r ≥ 1 and M ≥ 2 (the source allows all positive r and M; see sourceIssue ArithmeticStatistics/E309)
The content is for k ≥ 2; for k = 1 the right side is of order r^n and the statement is trivial
The region is a fixed compact set dilated by r; Bhargava's Theorem 3.5 (diagonal SL_n-transforms of rB) is a variant not needed by the consumers here
proofSteps: Reduce to Y irreducible; pick the irreducible Y′ ⊇ Y of the same codimension cut out by the eliminated f_1, …, f_k; assume M > M_0 by enlarging the constant.
Points of Y′(ℤ) in rB: O(r^{n−k}) by ArithmeticStatistics:ST.2/lattice-points-on-a-subvariety-in-a-dilated-region.
Points a ∉ Y′(ℤ) reducing into Y′(𝔽_p) for some p with M < p ≤ r: O(r^n/(M^{k−1} log M)) by ArithmeticStatistics:ST.2/geometric-sieve-small-primes.

Points a ∉ Y′(ℤ) reducing into Y′(𝔽_p) for some p > max(M, r): O(r^{n−k+1}) by ArithmeticStatistics:ST.2/geometric-sieve-large-primes (a point is counted at most once per prime, and the count of pairs bounds the count of points).
Sum the three bounds.
acceptance: Bhargava-Shankar apply it with n = 5, k = 2, r = X^{1/6} to Y = V(Δ, ∂Δ/∂e) on binary quartic forms and obtain O(X^{5/6}/(M log M) + X^{2/3}) (their Theorem 2.18); the cubic analogue has n = 4, k = 2, r = X^{1/4}, giving O(X/(M log M) + X^{3/4}).
Ekedahl's qualitative statement is the limit form: lim_{M→∞} lim sup_{r→∞} r^{−n}·#{…} = 0 for k ≥ 2.
For k = 2 and Y = V(x_1, x_2), the left side counts points with a prime p > M dividing gcd(a_1, a_2); its density is 1 − ∏_{p > M}(1 − p^{−2}) ≍ 1/(M log M), so the first term is sharp.

sources.excerpt: Theorem 3.3 Let B be a compact region in R^n having ﬁnite measure, and let Y be any closed subscheme of A^n_Z of codimension k ≥ 1. Let r and M be positive real numbers. Then we have #{a ∈ rB ∩ Z^n | a (mod p) ∈ Y(F_p) for some prime p > M} = O(r^n/(M^{k−1} log M) + r^{n−k+1})

nodes.title: Strong and weak multiples of p^2: the sets W_p, W_p^(1), W_p^(2) of binary quartic and binary cubic forms
nodes.statement: Let f ∈ ℤ[x_1, …, x_n], a ∈ ℤ^n, p a prime and j ≥ 1. The value of f is strongly a multiple of p^j at a if f(a′) ≡ 0 (mod p^j) for every a′ ∈ ℤ^n with a′ ≡ a (mod p); it is weakly a multiple of p^j at a if p^j | f(a) but f is not strongly a multiple of p^j at a. For binary quartic forms V_ℤ ≅ ℤ^5 (coefficients (a, b, c, d, e) of ax^4 + bx^3y + cx^2y^2 + dxy^3 + ey^4) with the discriminant Δ = (4I^3 − J^2)/27 of ArithmeticStatistics:ST.0/invariants-height-and-eligible-pairs, put W_p(V) := {f ∈ V_ℤ : p^2 | Δ(f)}, W_p^(1)(V) := {f : Δ is strongly a multiple of p^2 at f} (equivalently p^2 | Δ(f + pg) for every g ∈ V_ℤ) and W_p^(2)(V) := W_p(V) \ W_p^(1)(V). For binary cubic forms U_ℤ ≅ ℤ^4 (coefficients (a, b, c, d) of ax^3 + bx^2y + cxy^2 + dy^3) with Disc = b^2c^2 − 4ac^3 − 4b^3d − 27a^2d^2 + 18abcd, put W_p(U), W_p^(1)(U), W_p^(2)(U) in the same way.
hypotheses: p is a rational prime; the definitions make sense for every p, but the splitting-type descriptions below hold only for p ≥ 3 (sourceIssue ArithmeticStatistics/E308)
Strong divisibility depends only on a mod p; weak divisibility of p^2 depends on a mod p^2
For j = 1 there are no weak multiples: f(a′) ≡ f(a) (mod p) for a′ ≡ a (mod p)
proofSteps: The predicates are decidable conditions on residue classes: strong divisibility quantifies over the finitely many a′ mod p^j with a′ ≡ a (mod p).
For j = 2, Taylor expansion f(a + pb) ≡ f(a) + p Σ_i b_i ∂f/∂x_i(a) (mod p^2) (MvPolynomial.pderiv) shows: f is strongly a multiple of p^2 at a iff p^2 | f(a) and p | ∂f/∂x_i(a) for every i.

GL_2(ℤ)-invariance of W_p, W_p^(1), W_p^(2) on V_ℤ and U_ℤ: Δ(γ·f) = Δ(f) (resp. Disc(γ·f) = Disc(f)) for γ ∈ GL_2(ℤ) because det γ = ±1 and the weights are even, and γ·(f + pg) = γ·f + p(γ·g) with γ·g integral.
acceptance: The source's example: the characteristic function of the forms with squarefree discriminant is the complement of the union of the W_p.
The splitting-type description of W_p^(1)(V) (for p ≥ 3) and of W_p^(1)(U) (for p ≥ 3) was checked by enumerating all residue classes for p = 3, 5, 7; for p = 2 it fails (six classes each).

nodes.title: Strong multiples of p^2 reduce into the codimension-two locus f = ∂f/∂x_n = 0
nodes.statement: Let f ∈ ℤ[x_1, …, x_n] and let Y_f ⊆ 𝔸^n_ℤ be the closed subscheme V(f, ∂f/∂x_n). (a) For every prime p and every a ∈ ℤ^n at which f is strongly a multiple of p^2, a mod p ∈ Y_f(𝔽_p). (b) If f is primitive (the gcd of its coefficients is 1) and f and ∂f/∂x_n have no common factor of positive degree in ℚ[x_1, …, x_n], then Y_f has codimension 2 in 𝔸^n_ℤ.
hypotheses: In (b) the hypothesis is coprimality of f and ∂f/∂x_n over ℚ; the source assumes f irreducible and nonconstant in x_n, which implies it
Primitivity excludes vertical components: if every coefficient of f were divisible by p_0, the whole fibre over p_0 would lie in Y_f
proofSteps: (a) Taylor: f(a + p t e_n) ≡ f(a) + p t ∂f/∂x_n(a) (mod p^2) for t ∈ ℤ. Strong divisibility gives p^2 | f(a + p t e_n) for all t, hence p | f(a) and p | ∂f/∂x_n(a).

(b) Horizontal part: coprimality in ℚ[x] makes V(f, ∂f/∂x_n) ⊆ 𝔸^n_ℚ of dimension ≤ n − 2, so the closure in 𝔸^n_ℤ has dimension ≤ n − 1. Vertical part: over a prime p_0, f mod p_0 is a nonzero polynomial by primitivity, so the fibre of Y_f over p_0 lies in the hypersurface V(f mod p_0) of dimension n − 1. Hence dim Y_f ≤ n − 1 = (n + 1) − 2.
acceptance: Bhargava-Shankar's Y: for f = Δ on binary quartic forms and x_n = e, Y_Δ = V(Δ, ∂Δ/∂e) ⊆ 𝔸^5_ℤ has codimension 2 (ArithmeticStatistics:ST.2/discriminant-loci-of-codimension-two).

nodes.title: The discriminants of binary quartic and binary cubic forms are primitive and coprime to their derivatives in the last coefficient
nodes.statement: (a) The binary quartic discriminant Δ(a, b, c, d, e) = (4I^3 − J^2)/27 ∈ ℤ[a, b, c, d, e] is primitive, has degree 3 in e with leading coefficient 256a^3, and Δ and ∂Δ/∂e have no common factor of positive degree in ℚ[a, b, c, d, e]. (b) The binary cubic discriminant Disc(a, b, c, d) = b^2c^2 − 4ac^3 − 4b^3d − 27a^2d^2 + 18abcd ∈ ℤ[a, b, c, d] is primitive, has degree 2 in d with leading coefficient −27a^2, and Disc and ∂Disc/∂d have no common factor of positive degree in ℚ[a, b, c, d]. (c) Consequently Y_4 := V(Δ, ∂Δ/∂e) ⊆ 𝔸^5_ℤ and Y_3 := V(Disc, ∂Disc/∂d) ⊆ 𝔸^4_ℤ have codimension 2.
hypotheses: The polynomials are those of ArithmeticStatistics:ST.0/invariants-height-and-eligible-pairs (Δ) and of the Delone-Faddeev normalisation (Disc)
proofSteps: Primitivity: Δ contains 256a^3e^3 and −27a^2d^4, and gcd(256, 27) = 1; Disc contains b^2c^2 with coefficient 1.

No common factor free of e: the e-coefficients of Δ have gcd 1 in ℚ[a, b, c, d], since the leading one is 256a^3 and the constant term is Δ(a, b, c, d, 0) = d^2·Disc(a, b, c, d), which is not divisible by a (it contains b^2c^2d^2). Likewise the d-coefficients of Disc, −27a^2 and b^2c^2 − 4ac^3, are coprime.

No common factor involving e: the resultant Res_e(Δ, ∂Δ/∂e) ∈ ℚ[a, b, c, d] is nonzero because its specialisation at (a, b, c, d) = (1, 0, 0, 1) is Res_e(256e^3 − 27, 768e^2) ≠ 0 (e = 0 is not a root of 256e^3 − 27); by Polynomial.resultant_eq_zero_iff over the field ℚ(a, b, c, d) and Gauss's lemma, Δ and ∂Δ/∂e are coprime. For Disc specialise (a, b, c) = (1, 0, 1): Res_d(−4 − 27d^2, −54d) ≠ 0.
(c) follows from (a), (b) and part (b) of ArithmeticStatistics:ST.2/strong-divisibility-lies-on-a-codimension-two-locus.
acceptance: Independent check: a computer-algebra gcd gives gcd(Δ, ∂Δ/∂e) = 1 and gcd(Disc, ∂Disc/∂d) = 1 over ℚ; both discriminants are moreover irreducible over ℚ, which is not needed.
deg_e Δ = 3, so ∂Δ/∂e has degree 2 in e (not 3 as printed in the proof of Bhargava-Shankar Theorem 2.20; sourceIssue ArithmeticStatistics/E303).

nodes.title: The p-adic density of {p^2 | f} is O(p^{-2})
nodes.statement: Let f ∈ ℤ[x_1, …, x_n] be primitive and coprime to ∂f/∂x_n in ℚ[x_1, …, x_n]. There is C = C(f) such that for every prime p, #{v ∈ (ℤ/p^2ℤ)^n : f(v) ≡ 0 (mod p^2)} ≤ C·p^{2n−2}; equivalently, the Haar measure (total mass 1) of {v ∈ ℤ_p^n : p^2 | f(v)} is at most C·p^{−2}.
hypotheses: Applies to f = Δ on V (n = 5) and f = Disc on U (n = 4) by ArithmeticStatistics:ST.2/discriminant-loci-of-codimension-two
The bound is uniform in p; the constant depends only on f
proofSteps: Group the classes v mod p^2 by a = v mod p with p | f(a).

Classes with a ∈ Y_f(𝔽_p) (p | ∂f/∂x_n(a) as well): there are at most C p^{n−2} such a for p > M_0 (ArithmeticStatistics:ST.2/uniform-bound-for-points-of-a-subscheme-modulo-p, Y_f of codimension 2 by ArithmeticStatistics:ST.2/strong-divisibility-lies-on-a-codimension-two-locus), each with p^n lifts, giving at most C p^{2n−2}; the primes p ≤ M_0 are absorbed into C.

Classes with p ∤ ∂f/∂x_n(a): there are at most deg(f)·p^{n−1} such a, since f mod p is a nonzero polynomial by primitivity (MvPolynomial.schwartz_zippel_totalDegree). For each, f(a + pb) ≡ f(a) + p Σ_i b_i ∂f/∂x_i(a) (mod p^2) is an affine condition on b mod p whose b_n-coefficient is a unit, so exactly p^{n−1} of the p^n lifts satisfy p^2 | f; this gives at most deg(f)·p^{2n−2}.
Divide by p^{2n} for the measure statement (the set is a union of classes mod p^2 in ℤ_p^n).
acceptance: For n = 1 and f = x the density is exactly p^{−2}.

For f = Δ this is the bound (43) of Bhargava-Shankar, 1 − ∫φ_p ≤ ∫_{p^2 | Δ} df ≪ p^{−2}, which the source takes from Poonen's paper; the proof here needs only the codimension-two locus and Schwartz-Zippel.
The bound implies the convergence of ∏_p (1 − μ_p(p^2 | f)) and hence of the Euler products in the sieve theorems.

nodes.title: Functions and sets defined by congruence conditions; acceptable functions
nodes.statement: Fix n ≥ 1 and a primitive polynomial f ∈ ℤ[x_1, …, x_n] (the discriminant: Δ on V_ℤ ≅ ℤ^5, Disc on U_ℤ ≅ ℤ^4). Let μ_p denote the Haar measure on ℤ_p^n of total mass 1. A function φ : ℤ^n → [0, 1] is defined by congruence conditions if there are functions φ_p : ℤ_p^n → [0, 1], one for each prime p, such that (1) for every v ∈ ℤ^n the product ∏_p φ_p(v) converges to φ(v), and (2) each φ_p is locally constant outside a closed set S_p ⊆ ℤ_p^n with μ_p(S_p) = 0. Such φ is acceptable (for f) if there is p_0 such that φ_p(v) = 1 for every prime p > p_0 and every v ∈ ℤ_p^n with p^2 ∤ f(v). A set S ⊆ ℤ^n is defined by congruence conditions (resp. acceptable) if its characteristic function is, with φ_p the characteristic functions of sets S_p ⊆ ℤ_p^n; its p-adic density is μ_p(S) := μ_p(closure of S in ℤ_p^n). S is defined by finitely many congruence conditions if φ_p ≡ 1 for all but finitely many p and each φ_p is the characteristic function of a union of residue classes modulo a power of p.
hypotheses: φ takes values in [0, 1]; the local factors φ_p are part of the data (a function φ can have several presentations)
Acceptability is relative to the polynomial f; for binary quartic forms f = Δ, for binary cubic forms f = Disc
The weights 1/m_p(f) of Bhargava-Shankar Section 3 and the local solubility conditions are functions of this kind; only their acceptability is used in this stage
proofSteps: The data is a family (φ_p)_p with the two conditions; the product in (1) converges for each v because φ_p(v) = 1 for all but finitely many p in the acceptable case (p^2 ∤ f(v) when f(v) ≠ 0 and p is large), and is a condition otherwise.
μ_p is Mathlib's additive Haar measure on the compact group ℤ_p^n (PadicInt), normalised to total mass 1.
For φ_p the characteristic function of a union of classes modulo p^k, ∫φ_p dμ_p = #(classes)/p^{kn}.
acceptance: The characteristic function of {v ∈ ℤ^n : f(v) squarefree} is acceptable, with φ_p = 1_{p^2 ∤ f}.
A set defined by finitely many congruence conditions is acceptable (take p_0 larger than every prime involved).
The characteristic function of {v : f(v) is a perfect square} is defined by congruence conditions (φ_p = 1_{f(v) is a square in ℤ_p}, locally constant off {f = 0}) but is not acceptable.

sources.excerpt: we say that a function φ : VZ → [0, 1] ⊂ R is deﬁned by congruence conditions if, for all primes p, there exist functions φp : VZp → [0, 1] satisfying the following conditions: (1) For all f ∈ VZ, the product Q p φp(f) converges to φ(f).

nodes.title: The loci V_ℝ^(0), V_ℝ^(1), V_ℝ^(2±) of real binary quartic forms by number of real roots and definiteness
nodes.statement: Let V_ℝ be the space of real binary quartic forms f = ax^4 + bx^3y + cx^2y^2 + dxy^3 + ey^4 with the discriminant Δ of ArithmeticStatistics:ST.0/invariants-height-and-eligible-pairs. For f with Δ(f) ≠ 0 the roots of f in ℙ^1(ℂ) are four distinct points permuted by complex conjugation; let r(f) ∈ {0, 2, 4} be the number of real ones (a root at [1 : 0] when a = 0 included). For i = 0, 1, 2 put V_ℝ^(i) := {f : Δ(f) ≠ 0, r(f) = 4 − 2i}; V_ℝ^(2+) (resp. V_ℝ^(2−)) is the set of positive (resp. negative) definite forms, f(x, y) > 0 (resp. < 0) for all (x, y) ≠ (0, 0), so V_ℝ^(2) = V_ℝ^(2+) ⊔ V_ℝ^(2−). The index set is T := {0, 1, 2+, 2−}. For i ∈ T put V_ℤ^(i) := V_ℝ^(i) ∩ V_ℤ.
hypotheses: Only forms with Δ ≠ 0 lie in any locus
The loci are defined for the standard action f ↦ f((x, y)γ) of GL_2(ℝ), which preserves them
proofSteps: The real roots are counted on ℙ^1(ℝ): the number of real roots of f(x, 1) (Polynomial.roots over ℝ) plus 1 when a = 0.
Definiteness: a real binary quartic with Δ ≠ 0 and no real root takes one sign on ℝ^2 \ {0} (connectedness), so V_ℝ^(2) splits into the two definite loci.
acceptance: x^3y − xy^3 = xy(x − y)(x + y) ∈ V_ℝ^(0) with Δ = 4; x^3y + xy^3 = xy(x^2 + y^2) ∈ V_ℝ^(1) with Δ = −4; x^4 + y^4 ∈ V_ℝ^(2+) with Δ = 256.
The sign of Δ does not separate V_ℝ^(0) from V_ℝ^(2): both have Δ > 0.

nodes.title: Real binary quartic forms with given invariants form one or three SL_2^±(ℝ)-orbits
nodes.statement: Let (I_0, J_0) ∈ ℝ^2 with 4I_0^3 − J_0^2 ≠ 0. (a) If 4I_0^3 − J_0^2 < 0, the forms f ∈ V_ℝ with (I(f), J(f)) = (I_0, J_0) form exactly one SL_2^±(ℝ)-orbit, and it lies in V_ℝ^(1). (b) If 4I_0^3 − J_0^2 > 0, they form exactly three SL_2^±(ℝ)-orbits, one contained in each of V_ℝ^(0), V_ℝ^(2+) and V_ℝ^(2−). (c) Consequently, for i ∈ T, two forms f_1, f_2 ∈ V_ℝ^(i) are GL_2(ℝ)-equivalent iff there is λ > 0 with I(f_1) = λ^2 I(f_2) and J(f_1) = λ^3 J(f_2).
hypotheses: SL_2^±(ℝ) = {γ : det γ = ±1} acts by the standard action f ↦ f((x, y)γ), which preserves I and J (weights (det γ)^4 and (det γ)^6)
4I^3 − J^2 = 27Δ, so the two cases are Δ < 0 and Δ > 0
proofSteps: SL_2^±(ℝ)/{±1} = PGL_2(ℝ) acts on ℙ^1(ℝ) simply 3-transitively and on the upper half-plane transitively with stabiliser SO_2(ℝ)/{±1} at i; −1 acts trivially on quartic forms.

Four real roots: move three roots to ∞, 0, 1, so f = c·xy(x − y)(x − μy) with c ≠ 0, μ ∈ ℝ \ {0, 1}; then I = c^2(μ^2 − μ + 1), J = c^3(μ + 1)(2μ − 1)(μ − 2) and 4I^3 − J^2 = 27c^6μ^2(μ − 1)^2 > 0. The ratio J^2/I^3 is a degree-6 function of μ invariant under the anharmonic group generated by μ ↦ 1/μ and μ ↦ 1 − μ (the relabellings of the roots), takes every value in [0, 4) on ℝ \ {0, 1}, and each fibre is one orbit; so (I_0, J_0) determines μ up to relabelling and then c (c^2 = I_0/(μ^2 − μ + 1), the sign from J_0; for J_0 = 0 the forms ±xy(x − y)(x + y) are exchanged by (x, y) ↦ (y, x)).

Two real roots: move them to 0 and ∞ and the conjugate pair onto the unit circle (the diagonal torus fixes 0, ∞ and rescales), so f = c·xy(x^2 + pxy + y^2) with |p| < 2; I = c^2(p^2 − 3), J = c^3 p(9 − 2p^2), 4I^3 − J^2 = 27c^6(p^2 − 4) < 0; the symmetry (x, y) ↦ (−x, y) identifies (c, p) with (−c, −p), and for c > 0 the map p ↦ (I, J) up to the weighted scaling is a bijection from (−2, 2) onto the ratios with 4I^3 < J^2.

No real roots: move one conjugate pair to ±i and rotate by the stabiliser of i so that the other is ±iρ with 0 < ρ < 1, so f = c(x^2 + y^2)(x^2 + ρ^2y^2); I = c^2(ρ^4 + 14ρ^2 + 1), J = −2c^3(1 + ρ^2)(ρ^2 − 6ρ + 1)(ρ^2 + 6ρ + 1), 4I^3 − J^2 = 432c^6ρ^2(1 − ρ^2)^4 > 0; the sign of c is the definiteness, and for fixed sign ρ ↦ (I, J) up to scaling is a bijection from (0, 1) onto the ratios with 4I^3 > J^2.

Assemble: in each root type the normal form is determined by (I, J), which gives (a) and (b) and shows that the invariants map each type onto the stated sign of Δ. (c): I(γf) = (det γ)^4 I(f), J(γf) = (det γ)^6 J(f), so GL_2(ℝ)-equivalent forms have (I, J) related by λ = (det γ)^2 > 0; conversely scale by λ^{1/4}·1 ∈ Λ to equalise the invariants and apply (a)/(b) within the fixed locus.
acceptance: The three normal-form invariant formulas were checked by computer algebra, and uniqueness of the normal forms was checked numerically at several hundred random invariant pairs (i = 1: one p ∈ (−2, 2); i = 2±: one ρ ∈ (0, 1); i = 0: one relabelling class of μ).
x^4 + y^4 and −(x^4 + y^4) have invariants (12, 0) and (12, 0): same (I, J), different orbits (positive versus negative definite), as (b) predicts.
x^3y − (1/3)xy^3 (in V_ℝ^(0)) and (1/16)x^4 − (√2/(3√3))x^3y + (1/2)x^2y^2 + y^4 (in V_ℝ^(2+)) both have invariants (1, 0) and are not GL_2(ℝ)-equivalent.

nodes.title: Lemma 2.2: stabilisers in GL_2(ℝ) of real binary quartic forms, and the weights n_i
nodes.statement: Let f ∈ V_ℝ^(i) (so Δ(f) ≠ 0). Then the stabiliser of f in GL_2(ℝ) for the standard action has order 8 if i ∈ {0, 2+, 2−} and order 4 if i = 1; it contains ±1 and consists of elements of determinant ±1. Define n_i := #Stab_{GL_2(ℝ)}(f)/2, so n_0 = n_{2+} = n_{2−} = 4 and n_1 = 2.
hypotheses: Standard (untwisted) action f ↦ f((x, y)γ)
Δ(f) ≠ 0 is essential: x^2y^2 has an infinite stabiliser
proofSteps: If γ·f = f then I(f) = (det γ)^4 I(f) and J(f) = (det γ)^6 J(f); as (I, J) ≠ (0, 0) (Δ ≠ 0), det γ = ±1.

On matrices of determinant ±1 the standard action agrees with the twisted action γ·f = (det γ)^{−2} f((x, y)γ), which factors through PGL_2(ℝ); every class in PGL_2(ℝ) has a representative of determinant ±1, unique up to ±1. Hence #Stab_{GL_2(ℝ)}(f) = 2·#Stab_{PGL_2(ℝ)}(f).

By ArithmeticStatistics:ST.1/binary-quartic-parametrization-of-two-selmer (second paragraph of Bhargava-Shankar Theorem 3.2, with K = ℝ), Stab_{PGL_2(ℝ)}(f) ≅ E(ℝ)[2] for E : y^2 = x^3 − (I/3)x − J/27.

#E(ℝ)[2] = 1 + (number of real roots of x^3 − (I/3)x − J/27). The discriminant of this cubic is 4(I/3)^3 − 27(J/27)^2 = Δ(f); by Cubic.discr_eq_prod_three_roots it is a positive multiple of ((x − y)(x − z)(y − z))^2, which is positive for three real roots and negative for one real root and a conjugate pair. So #E(ℝ)[2] = 4 if Δ > 0 and 2 if Δ < 0.
Combine with the sign of Δ on the loci (ArithmeticStatistics:ST.2/real-root-types-of-binary-quartic-forms): orders 8, 4, 8, 8.
acceptance: x^4 + y^4 ∈ V_ℝ^(2+): the stabiliser is the group of the eight signed permutation matrices (x, y) ↦ (±x, ±y), (±y, ±x), of order 8.
x^3y + xy^3 ∈ V_ℝ^(1): the stabiliser is {±1, ±[[0, 1], [1, 0]]}, of order 4 (diag(1, −1) sends the form to its negative).
Bhargava-Shankar's Theorem 1.8 uses n_2 = 2 for the definite forms lumped together; this is consistent: V_ℝ^(2) contains two orbits for each (I, J), each with n_{2±} = 4.

nodes.title: The fundamental sets L^(i) of Table 1 and their scalings R^(i) = Λ·L^(i)
nodes.statement: Define bounded sets of real binary quartic forms: L^(0) := {x^3y − (1/3)xy^3 − (J/27)y^4 : −2 < J < 2}; L^(1) := {x^3y − (I/3)xy^3 ± (2/27)y^4 : −1 ≤ I < 1} ∪ {x^3y + (1/3)xy^3 − (J/27)y^4 : −2 < J < 2}; L^(2+) := {(1/16)x^4 − (√(2 − J)/(3√3))x^3y + (1/2)x^2y^2 + y^4 : −2 < J < 2}; L^(2−) := {−f : f ∈ L^(2+)}. Then for each i ∈ T: (a) L^(i) ⊆ V_ℝ^(i) and every f ∈ L^(i) has H(f) = max(|I(f)|^3, J(f)^2/4) = 1; (b) f ↦ (I(f), J(f)) is a bijection from L^(i) onto {(I, J) : H(I, J) = 1, 4I^3 − J^2 > 0} (i ∈ {0, 2±}) or onto {(I, J) : H(I, J) = 1, 4I^3 − J^2 < 0} (i = 1); (c) every GL_2(ℝ)-orbit in V_ℝ^(i) meets L^(i) in exactly one point, and the same holds for h·L^(i) for every h ∈ GL_2(ℝ); (d) all coefficients of all forms in L^(i) have absolute value at most 1. Put R^(i) := Λ·L^(i) = {λ·f : λ > 0, f ∈ L^(i)} (λ·f = f((x, y)λ) = λ^4 f); then f ↦ (I(f), J(f)) is a bijection from R^(i) onto {(I, J) : 4I^3 − J^2 > 0} (resp. < 0), with inverse (I, J) ↦ p^(i)_{I,J}.
hypotheses: The ± in the first family of L^(1) gives J = ∓2
Scaling by λ ∈ Λ multiplies (I, J) by (λ^8, λ^12), i.e. by (μ^2, μ^3) with μ = λ^4
proofSteps: Compute invariants: for x^3y − (1/3)xy^3 − (J/27)y^4, I = −3·1·(−1/3) = 1 and J(f) = −27·(−J/27) = J; for x^3y − (I/3)xy^3 ± (2/27)y^4, (I(f), J(f)) = (I, ∓2); for x^3y + (1/3)xy^3 − (J/27)y^4, (I(f), J(f)) = (−1, J); for the L^(2+) forms, I = 12/16 + 1/4 = 1 and J = 9/4 − 27·(2 − J)/27 − 1/4 = J. Hence H = 1 and the sign of 4I^3 − J^2 is as stated, and the pieces of the curve H = 1 are covered bijectively: for Δ < 0 the curve H(I, J) = 1 is {I = −1, |J| ≤ 2} ∪ {|J| = 2, −1 ≤ I < 1}, matching the two families with the overlap (−1, ±2) assigned to the first.

The root types: x^3 − x/3 − J/27 has discriminant (4 − J^2)/27 > 0 for |J| < 2, so the L^(0) forms (with the root [1 : 0]) have four real roots; the L^(1) forms have 4I^3 − J^2 < 0 and hence two real roots by ArithmeticStatistics:ST.2/real-orbits-of-binary-quartic-forms-with-fixed-invariants; the L^(2+) forms are positive definite (positive at J near 2 and Δ ≠ 0 on the connected parameter interval).

(c) from (b), H(λ^2 I, λ^3 J) = λ^6 H(I, J) (a unique λ > 0 normalises the height to 1) and part (c) of ArithmeticStatistics:ST.2/real-orbits-of-binary-quartic-forms-with-fixed-invariants; h·L^(i) inherits the property since h permutes the GL_2(ℝ)-orbits trivially.
(d): |J| < 2 and −1 ≤ I < 1 bound the listed coefficients by 1 (the largest is |√(2 − J)/(3√3)| < 2/(3√3) < 1).
acceptance: x^3y − (1/3)xy^3 ∈ L^(0) has invariants (1, 0); x^3y + (1/3)xy^3 − (2/27)y^4 ∈ L^(1) has invariants (−1, 2); the point (I, J) = (1, 2) with Δ = 0 is not attained.
Coefficient bound constant: C^4 with C = 1 works for L^(i) itself; for G_0·L the constant C of Proposition 2.7 depends on G_0.

nodes.title: Gauss's fundamental domain for GL_2(ℤ)\GL_2(ℝ) in Iwasawa coordinates, with its Haar measure
nodes.statement: Every g ∈ GL_2(ℝ) with det g > 0 has a unique Iwasawa decomposition g = n(u)a(t)k(θ)λ with n(u) = [[1, 0], [u, 1]] (u ∈ ℝ), a(t) = diag(t^{−1}, t) (t > 0), k(θ) = [[cos θ, sin θ], [−sin θ, cos θ]] (θ ∈ ℝ/2πℤ) and λ = λ·1 (λ > 0). The measure dg = t^{−2} du d^×t dk d^×λ (d^×t = dt/t, d^×λ = dλ/λ, dk = dθ/2π of total mass 1 on SO_2(ℝ)) is a Haar measure on GL_2^+(ℝ). Let ν(t) := {u ∈ [−1/2, 1/2] : u^2 + t^4 ≥ 1}, N′(t) := {n(u) : u ∈ ν(t)}, A′ := {a(t) : t ≥ 3^{1/4}/√2}, K_+ := {k(θ) : 0 ≤ θ < π} and Λ := {λ·1 : λ > 0}. Then F := N′(t)A′K_+Λ is a fundamental domain for the left action of GL_2(ℤ) on GL_2(ℝ) (GL_2(ℝ) = ⋃_{γ ∈ GL_2(ℤ)} γF up to a null set, the translates pairwise almost disjoint), and its image F_PGL2 in PGL_2(ℝ) is a fundamental domain for PGL_2(ℤ). Moreover g ↦ z(g) := −u + it^2 identifies N′(t)A′ with the standard domain fd of the upper half-plane, and t^{−2} du d^×t = (1/2)·dx dy/y^2 under z = x + iy.
hypotheses: K_+ is a set of representatives of SO_2(ℝ)/{±1}; with the full SO_2(ℝ), as printed in the source, F would contain both g and −g ∈ GL_2(ℤ)g and would be a union of two fundamental domains (sourceIssue ArithmeticStatistics/E301)
GL_2(ℤ) acts on the left; F ⊆ GL_2^+(ℝ), which suffices because GL_2(ℤ) contains matrices of determinant −1
ν(t) is a union of one or two intervals depending only on t, and ν(t) = [−1/2, 1/2] for t ≥ 1
proofSteps: Iwasawa: Gram-Schmidt on the rows of g gives g = (lower unitriangular)(positive diagonal)(orthogonal); det g > 0 forces the orthogonal factor into SO_2(ℝ), and the diagonal factor is a(t)λ. Uniqueness from N ∩ AΛ ∩ SO_2 = {1}.
Haar density: the left-invariant form g^{−1}dg in these coordinates has density proportional to t^{−3}λ^{−1} (a direct computation), i.e. t^{−2} du d^×t dθ d^×λ.

Upper half-plane: the positive definite binary quadratic form (x, y)gg^T(x, y)^T equals λ^2 t^{−2}((x + uy)^2 + t^4y^2), whose root in the upper half-plane is z(g) = −u + it^2; left multiplication by γ ∈ SL_2(ℤ) acts on z(g) by the Möbius action of γ (up to the transpose-inverse convention), and k(θ), λ do not change z(g). The conditions u ∈ ν(t), t ≥ 3^{1/4}/√2 say exactly |Re z| ≤ 1/2 and |z| ≥ 1, i.e. z(g) ∈ fd (ModularGroup.fd).

Covering and disjointness: a GL_2(ℤ)-coset meets GL_2^+(ℝ) in one SL_2(ℤ)-coset. By ModularGroup.exists_smul_mem_fd every z is moved into fd, and by ModularGroup.eq_smul_self_of_mem_fdo_mem_fdo (or the measure form ModularGroup.isFundamentalDomain_fdo of Tau Ceti, a MeasureTheory.IsFundamentalDomain for PSL_2(ℤ)) two points of the open domain in one orbit coincide; the kernel {±1} of SL_2(ℤ) → PSL_2(ℤ) acts on the K-coordinate by θ ↦ θ + π, which K_+ resolves.
Measure: with y = t^2, dy = 2t dt, so dx dy/y^2 = 2t^{−3} du dt = 2t^{−2} du d^×t.
acceptance: The identity 1 = n(0)a(1)k(0)·1 lies in F (z = i, on the boundary |z| = 1), and −1 = n(0)a(1)k(π)·1 does not, although −1 ∈ GL_2(ℤ)·1.
For t ≥ 1 the slice N′(t) is the whole interval [−1/2, 1/2].
F contains no matrix of negative determinant.

nodes.title: The standard fundamental domain of SL_2(ℤ) has hyperbolic area π/3
nodes.statement: For the invariant measure on the upper half-plane (Mathlib's volume on ℍ, density 1/(Im z)^2 with respect to Lebesgue measure), volume(ModularGroup.fd) = π/3.
hypotheses: The measure is Mathlib's MeasureSpace instance on ℍ
proofSteps: By UpperHalfPlane.volume_eq_lintegral, volume(fd) = ∫∫ y^{−2} dy dx over {|x| ≤ 1/2, y ≥ √(1 − x^2)}.
The inner integral is ∫_{√(1−x^2)}^∞ y^{−2} dy = (1 − x^2)^{−1/2}.

∫_{−1/2}^{1/2} (1 − x^2)^{−1/2} dx = arcsin(1/2) − arcsin(−1/2) = π/3 by the fundamental theorem of calculus (intervalIntegral.integral_deriv_eq_sub with Real.hasDerivAt_arcsin; the integrand is continuous on [−1/2, 1/2]).
acceptance: The value refines Tau Ceti's ModularGroup.volume_fd_lt_top (finiteness only).
π/3 = 2ζ(2)/π, the form in which the value enters the volume computations.

nodes.title: Vol(PGL_2(ℤ)\PGL_2(ℝ)) = 2ζ(2) for the ℤ-form ω, and the Iwasawa-measure volume of Gauss's domain
nodes.statement: (a) Let ω be the left-invariant top form on PGL_2(ℝ) whose value at the identity is the dual of the ℤ-basis E_11, E_12, E_21 of pgl_2(ℤ) = gl_2(ℤ)/ℤ·1 (well defined up to sign; |ω| is the associated Haar measure). In the coordinates [n(u)a(t)k(θ)] of PGL_2^+(ℝ), |ω| = 2t^{−3} du dt dθ, and Vol_ω(F_PGL2) = Vol_ω(PGL_2(ℤ)\PGL_2(ℝ)) = 2ζ(2) = π^2/3. (b) For the Haar measure dg = t^{−2} du d^×t dk d^×λ of ArithmeticStatistics:ST.2/gauss-fundamental-domain-in-iwasawa-coordinates, the domain N′(t)A′K_+ (λ omitted) has measure π/12 = ζ(2)/(2π); equivalently Vol(GL_2(ℤ)\GL_2^{±1}(ℝ)) = ζ(2)/(2π). (c) On PGL_2^+(ℝ), |ω| = 4π·t^{−2} du d^×t dk.
hypotheses: F is the strict domain with K_+ (θ ∈ [0, π)); with the full circle both volumes double
ω is determined by the ℤ-structure of PGL_2 up to sign, as in the source
proofSteps: (a) Compute g^{−1}dg for g = n(u)a(t)k(θ) and express it modulo scalars in the basis E_11, E_12, E_21 (the E_11-coordinate of X ∈ gl_2 modulo scalars is X_11 − X_22): the determinant of the resulting 3 × 3 matrix of one-forms is −2t^{−3} du dt dθ (a direct computation).

Integrate over F_PGL2: θ ranges over [0, π) and (u, t) over N′(t)A′; with y = t^2, 2t^{−3} du dt = du dy/y^2, so Vol_ω = π·volume(fd) = π·π/3 = π^2/3 by ArithmeticStatistics:ST.2/hyperbolic-area-of-the-modular-fundamental-domain; and 2ζ(2) = π^2/3 by riemannZeta_two.
(b) ∫ t^{−2} du d^×t over N′(t)A′ equals (1/2)·volume(fd) = π/6, and K_+ has dk-mass 1/2; the product is π/12 = ζ(2)/(2π).
(c) Compare the densities: 2t^{−3} du dt dθ = 4π·t^{−2} du d^×t (dθ/2π).
acceptance: Tamagawa check: 2ζ(2)·∏_p (1 − p^{−2}) = 2, the Tamagawa number of PGL_2 used by Bhargava-Shankar at the end of Section 3.6.

Bhargava-Shankar-Tsimerman state Vol(GL_2^{±1}(ℤ)\GL_2^{±1}(ℝ)) = ζ(2)/π; the value here is ζ(2)/(2π), and the factor 2 is compensated by the Jacobian constant of their Proposition 23 (sourceIssue ArithmeticStatistics/E305).
Independent check: the ω-volume π^2/3 was recomputed symbolically from the Maurer-Cartan form.

nodes.title: The multiset F h·L^(i) is n_i fundamental domains: orbit multiplicities m(x) = #Stab_{GL_2(ℝ)}(x)/#Stab_{GL_2(ℤ)}(x)
nodes.statement: Let i ∈ T, h ∈ GL_2(ℝ), and regard F h·L^(i) as a multiset in which x has multiplicity #{g ∈ F : x ∈ gh·L^(i)} (F the strict domain of ArithmeticStatistics:ST.2/gauss-fundamental-domain-in-iwasawa-coordinates). (a) For every x ∈ V_ℝ^(i), the sum of the multiplicities of the points of the GL_2(ℤ)-orbit of x equals m(x) := #Stab_{GL_2(ℝ)}(x)/#Stab_{GL_2(ℤ)}(x), an integer between 1 and n_i. (b) m(x) = n_i for all x outside a null set, and for every x ∈ V_ℤ^(i) whose stabiliser in GL_2(ℤ) is {±1}. (c) Consequently the number of irreducible integral points x ∈ F h·L^(i) with H(x) < X, counted with multiplicity, equals Σ_{[x]} n_i·2/#Stab_{GL_2(ℤ)}(x) over the irreducible GL_2(ℤ)-classes of height < X: it is n_i times the number of these classes when a class whose stabiliser has order 2r is counted with weight 1/r (the weight belongs to the class, not to the point; sourceIssue ArithmeticStatistics/E311).
hypotheses: F must be the strict domain (K_+); with the full SO_2(ℝ) every multiplicity doubles (sourceIssue ArithmeticStatistics/E301)
N(S; X) is the number of GL_2(ℤ)-classes of irreducible elements of S of height < X
proofSteps: Let x_L be the unique point of h·L^(i) in the GL_2(ℝ)-orbit of x (ArithmeticStatistics:ST.2/fundamental-sets-for-real-binary-quartic-orbits) and g with g·x_L = x. Then g′·x_L is GL_2(ℤ)-equivalent to x iff g′ ∈ GL_2(ℤ) g Stab(x_L); since F meets each right GL_2(ℤ)-coset once (up to null sets), the total multiplicity is the number of double cosets GL_2(ℤ)\GL_2(ℤ) g Stab(x_L), which is #[g Stab(x_L) g^{−1}]/#[GL_2(ℤ) ∩ g Stab(x_L) g^{−1}] = m(x).
Both stabilisers contain ±1, so 1 ≤ m(x) ≤ n_i by ArithmeticStatistics:ST.2/stabilizers-of-real-binary-quartic-forms.
(b) For each γ ∈ GL_2(ℤ) \ {±1} the fixed set of γ in V_ℝ is a proper linear subspace, hence null; GL_2(ℤ) is countable, so m(x) = n_i off a null set.
(c) Sum (a) over the irreducible GL_2(ℤ)-classes of height < X: a class with stabiliser of order 2 contributes n_i points, and one with stabiliser of order 2r contributes n_i/r points.
acceptance: For x = x^4 + y^4 all eight elements of Stab_{GL_2(ℝ)}(x) (the signed permutation matrices) are integral, so m(x) = 1: the class of x^4 + y^4 occurs once in F h·L^(2+), not n_{2+} = 4 times.
For x = x^3y − xy^3 ∈ V_ℤ^(0) the rotation (x, y) ↦ (−y, x) lies in its GL_2(ℤ)-stabiliser, which therefore has order at least 4, so m(x) ≤ 2 < n_0: such points are the ones Lemma 2.4 bounds.

nodes.title: The averaged orbit count N(S; X) of binary quartic forms and the regions B(n, t, λ, X)
nodes.statement: Fix a compact semialgebraic set G_0 ⊂ GL_2(ℝ) that is left SO_2(ℝ)-invariant, is the closure of a nonempty open set, and has det h ≥ 1 for h ∈ G_0; let dh be the Haar measure of ArithmeticStatistics:ST.2/gauss-fundamental-domain-in-iwasawa-coordinates and F the strict Gauss domain. For i ∈ T, S ⊆ V_ℤ^(i) (not necessarily GL_2(ℤ)-invariant) and X > 0 define N(S; X) := (1/C_{G_0}^(i)) ∫_{h ∈ G_0} #{x ∈ F h·L^(i) ∩ S^irr : H(x) < X} dh, where C_{G_0}^(i) := n_i ∫_{G_0} dh, S^irr is the set of elements of S irreducible over ℚ, and the count is taken with the multiplicities of the multiset F h·L^(i). For a weight φ : V_ℤ → ℝ, N_φ(S; X) is defined in the same way with each x counted with weight φ(x). For n = n(u), t > 0, λ > 0 put B(n, t, λ, X) := n a(t) λ G_0·L^(i) ∩ {x ∈ V_ℝ^(i) : H(x) < X}, a bounded semialgebraic multiset.
hypotheses: G_0, i and the fundamental set L^(i) are fixed; for GL_2(ℤ)-invariant S the value does not depend on G_0
Only irreducible elements are counted; H is the height max(|I|^3, J^2/4) of ArithmeticStatistics:ST.0/invariants-height-and-eligible-pairs
proofSteps: The integrand h ↦ #{x ∈ F h·L^(i) ∩ S^irr : H(x) < X} is a measurable function bounded on G_0 (finitely many integral points of bounded height lie in each bounded region, and multiplicities are at most n_i), so the integral exists.

For GL_2(ℤ)-invariant S, ArithmeticStatistics:ST.2/orbit-multiplicities-in-fundamental-multisets gives, for every h, #{x ∈ F h·L^(i) ∩ S^irr : H(x) < X} = Σ over irreducible GL_2(ℤ)-classes [x] ⊆ S of height < X of n_i·2/#Stab_{GL_2(ℤ)}(x); averaging over h gives N(S; X) = Σ_{[x]} 2/#Stab_{GL_2(ℤ)}(x), which is the number of classes counted with weight 1 except for the classes with a stabiliser larger than {±1}.
acceptance: For S = V_ℤ^(i), N(S; X) differs from the number of irreducible GL_2(ℤ)-classes in V_ℤ^(i) of height < X by at most the number of classes with stabiliser larger than {±1}, which is O(X^{3/4+ε}) (ArithmeticStatistics:ST.2/orbits-with-large-stabilizer-are-negligible).
N(S_1 ⊔ S_2; X) = N(S_1; X) + N(S_2; X) for disjoint S_1, S_2, invariant or not: the definition (11) of the source extends N to all subsets.

nodes.title: Theorem 2.5: the averaging formula N(S; X) as an integral over N′A′Λ of lattice-point counts in B(n, t, λ, X)
nodes.statement: For every i ∈ T, every S ⊆ V_ℤ^(i) and every X > 0, N(S; X) = (1/(2C_{G_0}^(i))) ∫_{n(u)a(t)λ ∈ N′(t)A′Λ} #{x ∈ S^irr ∩ B(n, t, λ, X)} t^{−2} du d^×t d^×λ, where the count in B is with multiplicity, dk has total mass 1 on SO_2(ℝ), and F is the strict domain N′(t)A′K_+Λ. (If, as printed in the source, the K-factor of F is all of SO_2(ℝ), the same computation gives the identity without the factor 1/2, but then the average (11) with C_{G_0}^(i) = n_i∫_{G_0} dh is twice the orbit count; normalising by 2n_i∫_{G_0} dh instead gives exactly the statement here.)
hypotheses: S arbitrary; the proof uses only the definition of N(S; X), Fubini and the invariance of Haar measure
The factor 1/2 is ∫_{K_+} dk (sourceIssue ArithmeticStatistics/E301)
proofSteps: Write the integrand of the definition as a sum over x ∈ S^irr with H(x) < X of #{g ∈ F : x = gh·x_L}, where x_L is the point of L^(i) in the GL_2(ℝ)-orbit of x (ArithmeticStatistics:ST.2/fundamental-sets-for-real-binary-quartic-orbits).

For fixed x with x = g_j·x_L (finitely many g_j, one for each element of the stabiliser), ∫_{G_0} #{g ∈ F : gh = g_j} dh = Σ_j vol(G_0 ∩ F^{−1}g_j) = Σ_j vol(G_0 g_j^{−1} ∩ F^{−1}) by invariance of dh (GL_2(ℝ) is unimodular), which equals ∫_{g ∈ F} #{h ∈ G_0 : x = gh·x_L} dg.
Exchange sum and integral: N(S; X) = (1/C) ∫_{g ∈ F} #{x ∈ S^irr ∩ gG_0·L : H(x) < X} dg.

Write g = n(u)a(t)kλ with k ∈ K_+: since kG_0 = G_0 (left SO_2(ℝ)-invariance) the integrand does not depend on k, and ∫_{K_+} dk = 1/2, which gives the formula with B(n, t, λ, X) (ArithmeticStatistics:ST.2/averaged-count-of-binary-quartic-orbits).
acceptance: Sanity check of the constant: inserting Vol(B(n, t, λ, X)) for the count and unfolding the integral over the full SO_2(ℝ) gives ∫ Vol(B) t^{−2} du d^×t d^×λ = 2∫_{G_0} Vol(F h·L ∩ {H < X}) dh, hence the main term Vol(R_X(L^(i)))/n_i of (20).
For S invariant under GL_2(ℤ) the right side is independent of G_0, as is the left side.

nodes.title: Lemma 2.3: reducible integral binary quartic forms with a ≠ 0 in R_X(h·L^(i)) number O(X^{2/3+ε})
nodes.statement: Let G_0 ⊂ GL_2(ℝ) be compact and h ∈ G_0. For every ε > 0 the number of integral binary quartic forms f = ax^4 + bx^3y + cx^2y^2 + dxy^3 + ey^4 in the multiset R_X(h·L^(i)) := {w ∈ F h·L^(i) : H(w) < X} (counted with multiplicity) that are reducible over ℚ and have a ≠ 0 is O_ε(X^{2/3+ε}), the implied constant depending only on G_0 and ε.
hypotheses: Only forms with a ≠ 0: the forms with a = 0 in the cusp are reducible and are excluded from the counts by other means (they are never irreducible)
Multiplicities are at most n_i ≤ 4
proofSteps: Coefficient bounds: R_X(h·L) ⊆ N′A′KΛh·L with h·L in a fixed compact set and 0 < λ < X^{1/24} (H(λ·f) = λ^24 H(f) and H = 1 on L). Hence a, b, c = O(X^{1/6}) and ad, bd, ae = O(X^{1/3}); in particular the forms with a ≠ 0 and e = 0 number O(X^{4/6+ε}).

Linear factor, a, e ≠ 0: the quadruple (a, b, d, e) has O(X^{4/6+ε}) possibilities; a linear factor px + qy (p, q coprime) has p | a and q | e, so O(X^ε) choices by the divisor bound d(n) = O_ε(n^ε) (requested from AnalyticNumberTheory:AN.5); then f(−q, p) = 0 determines c.

Product of two irreducible quadratics (px^2 + qxy + ry^2)((a/p)x^2 + sxy + (e/r)y^2): O(X^{2/6+ε}) pairs (a, e) (ae = O(X^{1/3})), O(X^ε) pairs (p, r) by the divisor bound; if the linear system (a/p)q + ps = b, (e/r)q + rs = d is nonsingular, (b, d) determine (q, s) and then c, giving O(X^{4/6+ε}); if singular, d = (r/p)b is determined by b and there are O(X^{1/6}) choices each for b and c, again O(X^{4/6+ε}).
Multiply by the bounded multiplicity.
acceptance: Order check: X^{2/3+ε} is smaller than the main term X^{5/6} and than the error X^{3/4+ε} of Theorem 2.1.
The analogous cubic statement is ArithmeticStatistics:ST.2/reducible-binary-cubic-forms-in-the-main-body, with X^{3/4+ε}.

sources.excerpt: If px + qy is a linear factor of f(x, y), where p, q ∈ Z are relatively prime, then p must be a factor of a, while q must be a factor of e; they are thus both determined up to O(Xǫ) possibilities.

nodes.title: Lemma 2.22: reducible monic integral binary cubic forms of bounded height number O(X^{1/2+ε}) up to unipotent equivalence
nodes.statement: For a monic integral binary cubic form g = x^3 + rx^2y + sxy^2 + ty^3 put I(g) := r^2 − 3s, J(g) := −2r^3 + 9rs − 27t and H(g) := max(|I(g)|^3, J(g)^2/4); these are invariant under the group F_{ℤ,1} of lower unitriangular integer matrices acting by g ↦ g((x, y)γ). For every ε > 0 the number of F_{ℤ,1}-orbits of monic integral binary cubic forms that are reducible over ℚ and have H(g) < X is O_ε(X^{1/2+ε}).
hypotheses: Monic means g(1, 0) = 1
The invariants agree with those of the binary quartic whose monic cubic resolvent is g (ArithmeticStatistics:ST.1/embedding-into-pairs-of-ternary-quadratic-forms)
proofSteps: The substitution x ↦ x + ky changes r by 3k, so every F_{ℤ,1}-orbit has a representative with r ∈ {−1, 0, 1}.
Then |r^2 − 3s|^3 < X gives s = O(X^{1/3}) and J^2/4 < X gives t = O(X^{1/2}).

t = 0 (the factor x): O(X^{1/3}) forms. t ≠ 0: a linear factor x − my has m | t, so O(X^ε) choices of m for each t (divisor bound, requested from AnalyticNumberTheory:AN.5); r, t, m then determine s through g(m, 1) = 0. Total O(X^{1/2+ε}).
acceptance: The count of all monic forms with r ∈ {−1, 0, 1} and H < X is of order X^{1/3}·X^{1/2} = X^{5/6}, so reducibility saves X^{1/3}.
F_{ℤ,1}-invariance: g(x + ky, y) has the same I and J (a direct computation).

nodes.title: Lemma 2.4: GL_2(ℤ)-orbits of binary quartic forms with stabiliser in GL_2(ℚ) of order > 2 number O(X^{3/4+ε})
nodes.statement: For every ε > 0 the number of GL_2(ℤ)-orbits of integral binary quartic forms f with Δ(f) ≠ 0, H(f) < X and #Stab_{GL_2(ℚ)}(f) > 2 is O_ε(X^{3/4+ε}). In particular the same bound holds for the orbits whose stabiliser in GL_2(ℤ) is larger than {±1}.
hypotheses: The stabiliser is for the standard action; its image in PGL_2(ℚ) is nontrivial exactly when #Stab_{GL_2(ℚ)}(f) > 2
proofSteps: A nontrivial element of Stab_{PGL_2(ℚ)}(f) gives, by ArithmeticStatistics:ST.1/binary-quartic-parametrization-of-two-selmer (Stab_{PGL_2(ℚ)}(f) ≅ E(ℚ)[2] for E : y^2 = x^3 − (I/3)x − J/27), a rational 2-torsion point, i.e. a rational root of the monic cubic resolvent g = 4 Det(A_1x − B_f y) of f (ArithmeticStatistics:ST.1/embedding-into-pairs-of-ternary-quadratic-forms), which has I(g) = I(f), J(g) = J(f); so g is reducible over ℚ.

The F_{ℤ,1}-orbit of g is an invariant of the PGL_2(ℤ)-orbit of f (the equivariance of φ in Theorem 2.14), and by ArithmeticStatistics:ST.2/reducible-monic-binary-cubic-forms there are O(X^{1/2+ε}) possibilities for it.

For a fixed reducible g, the number of GL_2(ℤ) × SL_3(ℤ)-orbits on pairs of integral ternary quadratic forms W_ℤ with cubic resolvent g is O(X^{1/4}) (Bhargava, 'The density of discriminants of quartic rings and fields', proof of Lemma 12; recorded as a gap), and each such orbit has at most 12 preimages in PGL_2(ℤ)\V_ℤ (Proposition 2.16, ArithmeticStatistics:ST.1/embedding-into-pairs-of-ternary-quadratic-forms). So O(X^{1/4}) orbits of f per g.
Multiply: O(X^{1/2+ε}·X^{1/4}) = O(X^{3/4+ε}). The GL_2(ℤ)-stabiliser statement follows because a stabiliser in GL_2(ℤ) larger than {±1} has nontrivial image in PGL_2(ℚ).
acceptance: The form x^3y − xy^3 has stabiliser containing the rotation (x, y) ↦ (−y, x), and its resolvent has the rational root corresponding to the 2-torsion point of y^2 = x^3 − x.
Order check: X^{3/4+ε} is below the main term X^{5/6}.

nodes.title: Proposition 2.7: lattice points with a ≠ 0 in B(n, t, λ, X), and its version for translates of mV_ℤ
nodes.statement: Let C > 0 be such that C^4 bounds the absolute values of all coefficients of all forms in G_0·L^(i). Let m ≥ 1 be an integer and L′ = v_0 + mV_ℤ a translate of the lattice mV_ℤ. For u ∈ [−1/2, 1/2], t ≥ 3^{1/4}/√2, λ > 0 and X > 0, the number of points (a, b, c, d, e) ∈ L′ ∩ B(n(u), t, λ, X) with a ≠ 0 (counted with multiplicity) is 0 if Cλ < t, and is m^{−5}·Vol(B(n(u), t, λ, X)) + O(t^4λ^16) if Cλ ≥ t, where the implied constant depends only on G_0 and L^(i) (not on m, v_0, u, t, λ, X).
hypotheses: C exists by the boundedness of L^(i) (ArithmeticStatistics:ST.2/fundamental-sets-for-real-binary-quartic-orbits) and the compactness of G_0
m = 1, v_0 = 0 is Proposition 2.7 itself; the translate version is the one used in Section 2.5
proofSteps: Coefficient ranges: a(t) multiplies the coefficient of x^{4−k}y^k by t^{2k−4}, n(u) with |u| ≤ 1/2 adds to each coefficient a bounded linear combination of the preceding ones (whose ranges are smaller), and λ multiplies all by λ^4; so in B(n, t, λ, X), |a|, |b|, |c|, |d|, |e| are at most C^4λ^4/t^4, C^4λ^4/t^2, C^4λ^4, C^4λ^4t^2, C^4λ^4t^4 respectively.
If Cλ < t then |a| < 1, so a = 0 for every integral point.

If Cλ ≥ t then all five ranges are bounded below by a positive constant and the range of a is the smallest up to a constant; every projection of B onto a coordinate subspace has volume at most a constant times the product of the four largest ranges, O(λ^4/t^2·λ^4·λ^4t^2·λ^4t^4) = O(t^4λ^16), and scaling by 1/m (to pass to the lattice L′) only decreases the projection volumes.

B(n, t, λ, X) is a bounded semialgebraic multiset whose number of defining inequalities, their degrees and its maximum multiplicity are bounded in terms of G_0 and L^(i) (it is a linear image of G_0·L^(i) cut by H < X); apply Davenport's lemma (requested from GeometryOfNumbersAndQuadraticArithmetic:GN.4) to the image of B under v ↦ (v − v_0)/m, whose volume is m^{−5}Vol(B).
acceptance: Cusp mechanism: the region t > Cλ contains no integral point with a ≠ 0, so every integral point there has the factor y and is reducible.
The projection bound drops the smallest range (that of a); for a = 0 slices there is no such saving, which is why the a = 0 points are removed as reducible.

nodes.title: Averaging over the fundamental domain and cutting off the cusp: N(V_ℤ^(i); X) = Vol(R_X(L^(i)))/n_i + O(X^{3/4+ε})
nodes.statement: (a) For i ∈ T and every ε > 0, N(V_ℤ^(i); X) = Vol(R_X(L^(i)))/n_i + O_ε(X^{3/4+ε}), where N(V_ℤ^(i); X) is the number of GL_2(ℤ)-classes of irreducible integral binary quartic forms in V_ℤ^(i) of height < X and R_X(L^(i)) := {w ∈ F·L^(i) : H(w) < X} is the multiset over the strict domain F. (b) Cusp tail: there is c = c(G_0) such that for every S ⊆ V_ℤ^(i), every T ≥ 3^{1/4}/√2 and every X ≥ 1, (1/(2C_{G_0}^(i))) ∫_{t > T} #{x ∈ S^irr ∩ B(n, t, λ, X)} t^{−2} du d^×t d^×λ ≤ c·X^{5/6}/T^2 + O(X^{3/4}).
hypotheses: The error term X^{3/4+ε} is smaller than the main term X^{5/6}
In (b) the bound is uniform in S; it is the form in which the cusp enters the uniformity estimate
proofSteps: By ArithmeticStatistics:ST.2/averaging-formula-for-binary-quartic-forms with S = V_ℤ^(i), and since L^(i) has height 1 and G_0 has determinant ≥ 1, the integrand vanishes unless t ≤ Cλ and λ < X^{1/24} (ArithmeticStatistics:ST.2/binary-quartic-lattice-points-in-the-cusp; points with a = 0 are reducible).

Irreducible points = points with a ≠ 0 minus reducible points with a ≠ 0: the latter contribute O(X^{2/3+ε}) after integration (ArithmeticStatistics:ST.2/reducible-binary-quartic-forms-in-the-main-body, uniform in h ∈ G_0). The averaged count differs from the number of classes by the classes with stabiliser larger than {±1} (ArithmeticStatistics:ST.2/averaged-count-of-binary-quartic-orbits), O(X^{3/4+ε}) of them (ArithmeticStatistics:ST.2/orbits-with-large-stabilizer-are-negligible).
Replace the count of points with a ≠ 0 by Vol(B) + O(t^4λ^16): the error integrates to ∫^{X^{1/24}}∫^{Cλ} t^4λ^16 t^{−2} d^×t d^×λ = O(X^{3/4}).

Main term: ∫ Vol(B(n, t, λ, X)) t^{−2} du d^×t d^×λ over all of N′A′Λ equals 2∫_{G_0} Vol(R_X(h·L)) dh (unfold the integral over the full SO_2(ℝ) and use ∫_{K_+} dk = 1/2), and Vol(R_X(h·L)) = Vol(R_X(L)) for every h, because F h·L is n_i fundamental domains for every h (ArithmeticStatistics:ST.2/orbit-multiplicities-in-fundamental-multisets). Dividing by 2C_{G_0}^(i) = 2n_i∫_{G_0} dh gives Vol(R_X(L))/n_i.
Remove the cuspidal part t > Cλ from the main term: Vol(B) = O(λ^20), so ∫_{λ < X^{1/24}} ∫_{t > Cλ} λ^20 t^{−2} d^×t d^×λ = O(X^{3/4}).

(b) For t > T: the count is at most the number of points with a ≠ 0, i.e. Vol(B) + O(t^4λ^16) with Vol(B) = O(λ^20); ∫_{t > T} t^{−2} d^×t ≤ T^{−2}/2 and ∫^{X^{1/24}} λ^20 d^×λ = X^{5/6}/20, and the error term integrates to O(X^{3/4}).
acceptance: Cusp check: in the region t > Cλ the leading coefficient vanishes, so the cusp contributes only reducible points.
Error-term check: 3/4 < 5/6, so (a) is a genuine asymptotic once Vol(R_X(L^(i))) ≍ X^{5/6} is computed (ArithmeticStatistics:ST.2/volume-of-the-fundamental-region-for-binary-quartic-forms).
Multiplicity check: the division by n_i reflects that F·L^(i) is n_i fundamental domains; with the source's F (full SO_2(ℝ)) both the count and the volume double.

nodes.title: Proposition 2.8 (real case): dv = (1/27)·ω dI dJ under (g, I, J) ↦ g·p_{I,J}
nodes.statement: Let PGL_2(ℝ) act on V_ℝ by the twisted action γ·f := (det γ)^{−2} f((x, y)γ), let ω be the ℤ-normalised invariant form of ArithmeticStatistics:ST.2/covolume-of-pgl2-z, dv = da db dc dd de, and for i ∈ T let p^(i) : (I, J) ↦ p^(i)_{I,J} ∈ R^(i) be the section of ArithmeticStatistics:ST.2/fundamental-sets-for-real-binary-quartic-orbits. Then for every measurable U ⊆ PGL_2(ℝ) and every measurable φ : V_ℝ → [0, ∞], ∫_{U·R^(i)} φ(v) dv = (1/27) ∫_{(I,J)} ∫_{g ∈ U} φ(g·p^(i)_{I,J}) ω(g) dI dJ, the left side over the multiset U·R^(i) (multiplicity #{(g, r) ∈ U × R^(i) : g·r = v}) and the outer integral over {4I^3 − J^2 > 0} (i ∈ {0, 2±}) or {4I^3 − J^2 < 0} (i = 1). In particular this holds for U = F_PGL2.
hypotheses: The constant 1/27 is for the ℤ-basis E_11, E_12, E_21 of pgl_2(ℤ); a different normalisation of ω changes it
Only the real case is planned here; the p-adic analogue (Proposition 3.7, with |1/27|_p) belongs to ArithmeticStatistics:ST.4
proofSteps: Jacobian at the identity: for the polynomial section s_{I,J} = x^3y − (I/3)xy^3 − (J/27)y^4 (which has invariants (I, J), ArithmeticStatistics:ST.0/invariants-height-and-eligible-pairs), the 5 × 5 determinant of the vectors E_11·s, E_12·s, E_21·s, ∂s/∂I, ∂s/∂J (infinitesimal twisted action; E_11 acts by f ↦ x∂_x f − 2f) is −1/27 identically in (I, J) (a direct computation, rechecked by computer algebra).

Independence of the section and of the point: for f with Δ(f) ≠ 0, the orbit tangent vectors E·f span the kernel of (dI, dJ) at f, so det[E_11·f, E_12·f, E_21·f, w_1, w_2] with (dI, dJ)(w_j) = e_j depends only on f; it is invariant under PGL_2(ℂ) (the twisted action has determinant of absolute value 1 on V, and Λ^3 of the adjoint action is trivial). Forms with equal invariants and Δ ≠ 0 are PGL_2(ℂ)-equivalent (ArithmeticStatistics:ST.1/binary-quartic-parametrization-of-two-selmer over ℂ, where every form is soluble and E(ℂ)/2E(ℂ) = 0), and s_{I,J} meets every such level set, so the determinant is −1/27 at every f with Δ(f) ≠ 0 and for every smooth section.
Left translation by g ∈ PGL_2(ℝ) preserves ω and changes dv by |det(g acting on V)| = 1, so the Jacobian of ψ(g, I, J) = g·p^(i)_{I,J} has absolute value 1/27 everywhere.

ψ : U × {(I, J)} → V_ℝ^(i) is a local diffeomorphism (the stabilisers are finite, ArithmeticStatistics:ST.2/stabilizers-of-real-binary-quartic-forms); decompose the domain into countably many measurable pieces on which ψ is injective and apply the change-of-variables formula (MeasureTheory.integral_image_eq_integral_abs_det_fderiv_smul) on each, summing to the multiset integral.
acceptance: Checks of the constant: over each ℤ_p the analogous computation gives |1/27|_p (the source's Section 3.4), and the product formula ∏_v |1/27|_v = 1 is what makes the global Tamagawa computation of ArithmeticStatistics:ST.4 consistent.
The section of L^(i) differs from s_{I,J} by a PGL_2(ℂ)-valued function of (I, J); the determinant does not see the difference.

nodes.title: Lemma 2.9 and Proposition 2.10: eligible invariant pairs form 9 translates of 9ℤ × 27ℤ, and their number up to height X
nodes.statement: (a) The set of eligible pairs (I, J) ∈ ℤ^2 (those occurring as the invariants of an integral binary quartic form) is the union of 9 distinct translates of the lattice 9ℤ × 27ℤ. (b) Let N^±_{I,J}(X) be the number of eligible (I, J) with H(I, J) < X and ±(4I^3 − J^2) > 0. Then N^+_{I,J}(X) = (8/135)X^{5/6} + O(X^{1/2}) and N^−_{I,J}(X) = (32/135)X^{5/6} + O(X^{1/2}).
hypotheses: Eligibility is characterised by the congruences of Theorem 1.7, owned by ArithmeticStatistics:ST.0/invariants-height-and-eligible-pairs
proofSteps: (a) By Theorem 1.7, (I, J) is eligible iff I ≡ 0 (mod 3) and J ≡ 0 (mod 27), or I ≡ 1, 4, 7 (mod 9) with J ≡ ±2, ±16, ±7 (mod 27) respectively. The first condition is 3 classes of I mod 9 times 1 class of J mod 27; the others are 3·2 = 6 classes; 9 classes of (I mod 9, J mod 27) in all.

(b) The region R^±_{I,J}(X) = {(i, j) : |i| < X^{1/3}, |j| < 2X^{1/2}, ±(4i^3 − j^2) > 0} is semialgebraic with bounded complexity and its coordinate projections have length O(X^{1/2}); Davenport's lemma (requested from GeometryOfNumbersAndQuadraticArithmetic:GN.4) applied to each of the 9 translates of 9ℤ × 27ℤ (index 243) gives N^± = (9/243)Vol(R^±_{I,J}(X)) + O(X^{1/2}).

Vol(R^+_{I,J}(X)) = (8/5)X^{5/6} and Vol(R^−_{I,J}(X)) = (32/5)X^{5/6} (the areas of ArithmeticStatistics:ST.2/volume-of-the-fundamental-region-for-binary-quartic-forms, computed there by elementary integration); (1/27)(8/5) = 8/135 and (1/27)(32/5) = 32/135.
acceptance: (I, J) = (−2, ±7) are eligible (I ≡ 7 mod 9, J ≡ ±7 mod 27) with Δ = −3, and they are the eligible pairs with Δ ≠ 0 of smallest height, 49/4; (1, 2) is eligible (realised by x^3y − x^2y^2) but has Δ = 0 and is excluded from both counts; (1, 1) is not eligible.
The density of eligible pairs is 9/243 = 1/27, the factor that turns the areas 8/5 and 32/5 into 8/135 and 32/135.

nodes.title: Theorem 2.11 and (27): counting binary quartic forms satisfying finitely many congruence conditions
nodes.statement: (a) Let m ≥ 1 and let L_j = v_j + mV_ℤ be a translate of mV_ℤ. Then N(L_j ∩ V_ℤ^(i); X) = Vol(R_X(L^(i)))/(n_i m^5) + O_ε(X^{3/4+ε}), the implied constant independent of m and v_j (N the averaged count). (b) If S ⊆ V_ℤ is defined by congruence conditions modulo m, i.e. a union of k translates of mV_ℤ, then N(S ∩ V_ℤ^(i); X) = k·Vol(R_X(L^(i)))/(n_i m^5) + O_{S,ε}(X^{3/4+ε}). (c) If S ⊆ V_ℤ is defined by congruence conditions modulo finitely many prime powers, then N(S ∩ V_ℤ^(i); X) = N(V_ℤ^(i); X)·∏_p μ_p(S) + O_{S,ε}(X^{3/4+ε}), where μ_p(S) is the p-adic density of ArithmeticStatistics:ST.2/functions-defined-by-congruence-conditions.
hypotheses: In (c) the implied constant depends on S (through k)
For GL_2(ℤ)-invariant S the averaged count is the class count up to O(X^{3/4+ε})
proofSteps: (a) Repeat the proof of ArithmeticStatistics:ST.2/averaging-over-the-fundamental-domain-and-cutting-the-cusp with S = L_j: by the translate version of ArithmeticStatistics:ST.2/binary-quartic-lattice-points-in-the-cusp the points with a ≠ 0 number 0 for Cλ < t and m^{−5}Vol(B) + O(t^4λ^16) otherwise, with the constant independent of m; the reducible points and the large-stabiliser classes contribute O(X^{3/4+ε}) as before (they are a subset of those of V_ℤ).
(b) Sum over the k translates.
(c) By the Chinese remainder theorem k·m^{−5} = ∏_p μ_p(S) when m is the product of the prime powers involved; combine with ArithmeticStatistics:ST.2/count-of-binary-quartic-forms-of-bounded-height.
acceptance: S = V_ℤ (m = 1, k = 1) recovers Theorem 2.1.
For S = {f : p | a(f)} (m = p, k = p^4), μ_p(S) = 1/p and the count is N(V_ℤ^(i); X)/p + O(X^{3/4+ε}) for fixed p.

nodes.title: Theorem 2.12: weighted counts of binary quartic forms with weights defined modulo finitely many prime powers
nodes.statement: Let p_1, …, p_k be distinct primes and, for each j, let φ_{p_j} : V_ℤ → ℝ be GL_2(ℤ)-invariant and depend only on f mod p_j^{a_j}. Put φ := ∏_j φ_{p_j} and let N_φ(V_ℤ^(i); X) be the number of irreducible GL_2(ℤ)-orbits in V_ℤ^(i) of height < X, each orbit GL_2(ℤ)·f counted with weight φ(f). Then N_φ(V_ℤ^(i); X) = N(V_ℤ^(i); X)·∏_{j=1}^k ∫_{V_{ℤ_{p_j}}} φ̃_{p_j}(f) df + O(X^{3/4+ε}), where φ̃_{p_j} is the locally constant extension of φ_{p_j} to V_{ℤ_{p_j}}, df is the Haar probability measure, and the implied constant depends only on the φ_{p_j} and ε.
hypotheses: Finitely many primes and finitely many residue conditions
The weights are GL_2(ℤ)-invariant so that N_φ counts orbits
proofSteps: φ is a finite linear combination Σ_c φ(c)·1_{c} of indicator functions of residue classes c modulo m = ∏ p_j^{a_j}; each class is a translate of mV_ℤ.
Apply part (a) of ArithmeticStatistics:ST.2/binary-quartic-counts-with-finitely-many-congruence-conditions to each class and sum; Σ_c φ(c) m^{−5} = ∏_j ∫ φ̃_{p_j} df by the Chinese remainder theorem.
The averaged count of an invariant weighted set equals the weighted class count up to the O(X^{3/4+ε}) large-stabiliser classes.
acceptance: φ ≡ 1 recovers Theorem 2.1; φ = 1_S recovers Theorem 2.11.

nodes.title: Theorem 2.18: forms in a homogeneously expanding region reducing into V(Δ, ∂Δ/∂e) modulo some p > M
nodes.statement: Let B_0 ⊂ V_ℝ be compact and let Y_4 = V(Δ, ∂Δ/∂e) ⊆ 𝔸^5_ℤ. There is C = C(B_0) such that for all X ≥ 1 and M ≥ 2, #{f ∈ X^{1/6}B_0 ∩ V_ℤ : f mod p ∈ Y_4(𝔽_p) for some prime p > M} ≤ C·(X^{5/6}/(M log M) + X^{2/3}). In particular #(X^{1/6}B_0 ∩ ⋃_{p>M} W_p^(1)(V)) ≤ C·(X^{5/6}/(M log M) + X^{2/3}). The source's case is B_0 = F^(ε)_PGL2·R^(i)(1), where F^(ε)_PGL2 ⊂ F_PGL2 is cut off at a height t ≤ T_ε chosen so that Vol(F^(ε)_PGL2) = (1 − ε)Vol(F_PGL2); then X^{1/6}B_0 = F^(ε)_PGL2·R^(i)(X).
hypotheses: B_0 compact; the constant depends on B_0 (for the source's region, on ε)
W_p^(1)(V) ⊆ {f : f mod p ∈ Y_4(𝔽_p)} is the inclusion of ArithmeticStatistics:ST.2/strong-divisibility-lies-on-a-codimension-two-locus; the larger set is what is bounded
proofSteps: Y_4 has codimension 2 in 𝔸^5_ℤ (ArithmeticStatistics:ST.2/discriminant-loci-of-codimension-two).
Apply ArithmeticStatistics:ST.2/quantitative-ekedahl-geometric-sieve with n = 5, k = 2, B = B_0, r = X^{1/6}: r^n/(M^{k−1} log M) = X^{5/6}/(M log M) and r^{n−k+1} = X^{4/6} = X^{2/3}.
The second statement by part (a) of ArithmeticStatistics:ST.2/strong-divisibility-lies-on-a-codimension-two-locus.

F^(ε)_PGL2·R^(i)(X) = X^{1/6}·(F^(ε)_PGL2·R^(i)(1)) because H(c·f) = c^6 H(f) for scalars c > 0, and F^(ε)_PGL2·R^(i)(1) is bounded (t is bounded above on F^(ε) and the coefficients of R^(i)(1) are bounded).
acceptance: The forms with f mod p of splitting type (1^3 1), (1^2 1^2), (2^2), (1^4) or f ∈ pV_ℤ (for p ≥ 3) are the strongly divisible ones; the larger set counted also contains weakly divisible forms whose double root mod p is at [1 : 0], such as 25x^4 + x^2y^2 + y^4 for p = 5.
The bound is used with M fixed and X → ∞: the term X^{2/3} is then negligible against X^{5/6}.

nodes.title: (37): N(W_p^(2)(V); X) = O(X/p^2) uniformly in p, through pairs of ternary quadratic forms
nodes.statement: There is an absolute constant C such that for every prime p and every X ≥ 1, the number of GL_2(ℤ)-classes of irreducible integral binary quartic forms f ∈ W_p^(2)(V) with H(f) < X is at most C·X/p^2.
hypotheses: Rests on Theorem 2.19 (Bhargava, 'The density of discriminants of quartic rings and fields', Proposition 23), which is recorded as a gap
Uniform in both p and X
proofSteps: The map φ of (30) sends f to (A_1, B_f) ∈ W_ℤ, preserves the discriminant, and induces ψ : PGL_2(ℤ)\V_ℤ → (GL_2(ℤ) × SL_3(ℤ))\W_ℤ with fibres of size at most 12 over elements of nonzero discriminant (Theorem 2.14 and Proposition 2.16, ArithmeticStatistics:ST.1/embedding-into-pairs-of-ternary-quadratic-forms).

φ is affine-linear in f with φ(f + pg) − φ(f) = (0, p·B_g), so if Δ(f + pg) is not divisible by p^2 for some g, the same perturbation shows Δ_W(φ(f)) is not strongly divisible: φ maps W_p^(2)(V) into W_p^(2)(W) (definitions of ArithmeticStatistics:ST.2/strongly-and-weakly-divisible-values).
Theorem 2.19: the number of GL_2(ℤ) × SL_3(ℤ)-orbits on W_p^(2)(W) with |Δ| < X is O(X/p^2) with the constant independent of p (gap); multiply by 12.
acceptance: For p > X^{1/2} the bound is below 1 and the set is empty, since p^2 | Δ(f) ≠ 0 forces |Δ(f)| ≥ p^2.
The transport uses only that φ preserves the discriminant and is affine in f; no information about the strongly divisible part of W_ℤ is needed, because W_p^(1)(V) is handled by the geometric sieve.

nodes.title: Theorem 2.20, corrected: forms with p^2 | Δ and p ∤ ∂Δ/∂e in a homogeneously expanding region
nodes.statement: Let W′_p := {f ∈ V_ℤ : p^2 | Δ(f), p ∤ ∂Δ/∂e(f)}, a subset of W_p^(2)(V). Let B_0 ⊂ V_ℝ be compact. (a) There is C = C(B_0) with #(X^{1/6}B_0 ∩ W′_p) ≤ C·(X^{5/6}/p^2 + X^{2/3}) for every prime p and X ≥ 1. (b) If moreover every GL_2(ℤ)-orbit meets X^{1/6}B_0 in at most c_0 points (counted with multiplicity), then #(X^{1/6}B_0 ∩ V_ℤ^irr ∩ ⋃_{p>M} W′_p) ≤ C′·(X^{5/6}/(M log M) + X^{5/6}/log X) for all X ≥ 2 and M ≥ 2, with C′ depending on B_0 and c_0 only. Together with ArithmeticStatistics:ST.2/uniformity-for-strongly-divisible-quartic-discriminants this bounds the whole of X^{1/6}B_0 ∩ ⋃_{p>M} W_p(V), since W_p(V) ⊆ W′_p ∪ {f : f mod p ∈ Y_4(𝔽_p)}.
hypotheses: The source states the bound for W_p^(2)(V) and asserts p ∤ ∂Δ/∂e on it; that assertion is false (sourceIssue ArithmeticStatistics/E302), and the forms of W_p^(2)(V) with p | ∂Δ/∂e are covered by the geometric sieve instead
The orbit-multiplicity hypothesis in (b) holds for the source's region F^(ε)·R^(i)(X) and for the truncated regions used in the proof of Theorem 2.13
proofSteps: W′_p ⊆ W_p^(2)(V): p ∤ ∂Δ/∂e(f) excludes strong divisibility (ArithmeticStatistics:ST.2/strongly-and-weakly-divisible-values, gradient characterisation).

(a) X^{1/6}B_0 has sides of length O(X^{1/6}), so there are O(X^{4/6}) quadruples (a_0, b_0, c_0, d_0). For fixed ones, Δ(a_0, b_0, c_0, d_0, e) mod p is a polynomial in e of degree ≤ 3 (ArithmeticStatistics:ST.2/discriminant-loci-of-codimension-two); the residues e mod p with p | Δ and p ∤ ∂Δ/∂e are simple roots of a nonzero polynomial, at most 3 of them, and each lifts to exactly one class e mod p^2 with p^2 | Δ (Hensel's lemma for a simple root). An interval of length O(X^{1/6}) contains at most O(X^{1/6}/p^2 + 1) integers in a class mod p^2.

(b) For M < p < X^{1/6} use (a): Σ_{p>M} X^{5/6}/p^2 = O(X^{5/6}/(M log M)) and Σ_{p<X^{1/6}} X^{2/3} = O(X^{5/6}/log X) by ArithmeticStatistics:ST.2/chebyshev-bounds-for-prime-sums. For p ≥ X^{1/6} use ArithmeticStatistics:ST.2/weakly-divisible-quartic-discriminants-via-ternary-pairs: the irreducible points of W′_p ⊆ W_p^(2)(V) in the region lie in at most C X/p^2 classes (the region has height ≤ c·X), each contributing at most c_0 points, and Σ_{p ≥ X^{1/6}} X/p^2 = O(X^{5/6}/log X).
acceptance: The source's bound O(X^{5/6}/log M) follows from (b) when M ≤ X^{1/6}, because then 1/log X ≤ 1/(6 log M); for M > X^{1/6} only the second step applies and gives O(X/(M log M)), which is O(X^{5/6}/log M).
The form 25x^4 + x^2y^2 + y^4 lies in W_5^(2)(V) but not in W′_5; it lies in Y_4(𝔽_5) modulo 5.

nodes.title: Theorem 2.13: a uniform tail estimate for binary quartic forms whose discriminant is divisible by p^2 for some p > M
nodes.statement: For a prime p let W_p(V) := {f ∈ V_ℤ : p^2 | Δ(f)}. There are constants c (absolute, given G_0) and C_T (for each T ≥ 3^{1/4}/√2, independent of M) such that for every M ≥ 2 and every T, lim sup_{X→∞} N(⋃_{p>M} W_p(V); X)/X^{5/6} ≤ C_T/(M log M) + c/T^2. Consequently lim_{M→∞} lim sup_{X→∞} N(⋃_{p>M} W_p(V); X)/X^{5/6} = 0: for every δ > 0 there is M_δ with lim sup_{X→∞} N(⋃_{p>M} W_p(V); X)/X^{5/6} < δ for all M ≥ M_δ. Here N is the number of GL_2(ℤ)-classes of irreducible forms of height < X (equivalently the averaged count, up to O(X^{3/4+ε})), summed over i ∈ T.
hypotheses: The source states lim_{X→∞} N(⋃_{p>M} W_p(V); X)/X^{5/6} = O(1/log M) with an implied constant independent of M; its proof does not track how the constants of Theorems 2.18 and 2.20 depend on the cut-off ε, which the rate needs, while the sieve (Theorem 2.21) uses only the limit statement proved here (sourceIssue ArithmeticStatistics/E304)
The statement is about orbit counts, not lattice-point counts; the limits are in X first, then M
proofSteps: Apply ArithmeticStatistics:ST.2/averaging-formula-for-binary-quartic-forms to S := V_ℤ^(i) ∩ ⋃_{p>M} W_p(V) and split the integral at t = T.
t > T: at most c·X^{5/6}/T^2 + O(X^{3/4}) by part (b) of ArithmeticStatistics:ST.2/averaging-over-the-fundamental-domain-and-cutting-the-cusp.

t ≤ T: every B(n, t, λ, X) with t ≤ T lies in Ω_T(X) := X^{1/6}·Ω_T, where Ω_T := ⋃_{|u| ≤ 1/2, t_0 ≤ t ≤ T, λ ≤ 1} n(u)a(t)λG_0·L^(i) is compact (H(λ·f) = λ^24 H(f)). For each x the set {(u, t, λ) : x ∈ B(n(u), t, λ, X)} has measure at most a constant depending on G_0 (it is contained in finitely many translates g_x Stab(x_L)G_0^{−1} of G_0^{−1}, ArithmeticStatistics:ST.2/stabilizers-of-real-binary-quartic-forms), so the t ≤ T part is at most c′·#(S^irr ∩ Ω_T(X)); every GL_2(ℤ)-orbit meets Ω_T(X) in boundedly many points (ArithmeticStatistics:ST.2/orbit-multiplicities-in-fundamental-multisets).

Split S ⊆ {f mod p ∈ Y_4(𝔽_p) for some p > M} ∪ ⋃_{p>M} W′_p (for f ∈ W_p(V) either p | ∂Δ/∂e(f), and then f mod p ∈ Y_4(𝔽_p), or f ∈ W′_p). The first part is O_T(X^{5/6}/(M log M) + X^{2/3}) by ArithmeticStatistics:ST.2/uniformity-for-strongly-divisible-quartic-discriminants with B_0 = Ω_T; the second is O_T(X^{5/6}/(M log M) + X^{5/6}/log X) by ArithmeticStatistics:ST.2/uniformity-for-weakly-divisible-quartic-discriminants.
Divide by X^{5/6}, let X → ∞, sum over the four values of i; then let T → ∞ after M → ∞ (choose T with c/T^2 < δ/2, then M with C_T/(M log M) < δ/2).
acceptance: Interchange check: the acceptance condition of ArithmeticStatistics:ST.2 (an interchange of the sieve limit and the height limit needs a uniform tail theorem) is met by this statement: the bound on lim sup_X is uniform in the set of congruence conditions imposed at primes ≤ M.
Order check: the tail is o(1)·X^{5/6} as M → ∞; for fixed M it is of the same order X^{5/6} as the main term, so it cannot be dropped.
Squarefree-discriminant application: excluding ⋃_p W_p(V) leaves the forms of squarefree discriminant, counted by ArithmeticStatistics:ST.2/squarefree-sieve-for-binary-quartic-forms.

nodes.title: Theorem 2.21: counting binary quartic forms weighted by an acceptable function defined by infinitely many congruence conditions
nodes.statement: Let φ : V_ℤ → [0, 1] be acceptable (for Δ) and defined by congruence conditions via local functions φ_p : V_{ℤ_p} → [0, 1] (ArithmeticStatistics:ST.2/functions-defined-by-congruence-conditions), with each φ_p invariant under GL_2(ℤ). For i ∈ T let N_φ(V_ℤ^(i); X) be the number of irreducible GL_2(ℤ)-orbits in V_ℤ^(i) of height < X, each orbit GL_2(ℤ)·f counted with weight φ(f). Then N_φ(V_ℤ^(i); X) = N(V_ℤ^(i); X)·∏_p ∫_{V_{ℤ_p}} φ_p(f) df + o(X^{5/6}), and the Euler product converges.
hypotheses: Acceptability: φ_p = 1 on {p^2 ∤ Δ} for all large p
GL_2(ℤ)-invariance of the φ_p makes N_φ an orbit count; the source uses it implicitly ('with notation as in Theorem 2.12')
proofSteps: Approximation: since φ_p is locally constant outside a closed null set, there are functions ψ_{p,n} ≤ φ_p ≤ ψ′_{p,n}, defined by congruence conditions modulo p^n, increasing resp. decreasing to φ_p pointwise off the null set, with ψ_{p,0} ≡ 1 ≡ ψ′_{p,0}; by dominated convergence their integrals converge to ∫ φ_p (42).

Convergence of the product: for large p, 1 − ∫ φ_p ≤ μ_p{p^2 | Δ} ≤ C p^{−2} (43) by acceptability and ArithmeticStatistics:ST.2/local-density-of-values-divisible-by-p-squared (Δ is primitive and coprime to ∂Δ/∂e, ArithmeticStatistics:ST.2/discriminant-loci-of-codimension-two).

Upper bound (44): for fixed Y, φ ≤ ∏_p ψ′_{p,⌊Y/p⌋}, a weight defined modulo finitely many prime powers; ArithmeticStatistics:ST.2/weighted-binary-quartic-counts-with-finitely-many-congruence-conditions gives lim sup N_φ/X^{5/6} ≤ lim N(V_ℤ^(i); X)/X^{5/6}·∏_p ∫ ψ′_{p,⌊Y/p⌋}; let Y → ∞ using (42) and (43).

Lower bound (45): for Y large, ∏_p ψ_{p,⌊Y/p⌋} ≤ φ except on ⋃_{p > Y} W_p(V) (acceptability), so N_φ ≥ N_{∏ψ} − N(⋃_{p>Y} W_p(V); X); by the weighted finite count and ArithmeticStatistics:ST.2/uniformity-estimate-for-infinitely-many-congruence-conditions, lim inf N_φ/X^{5/6} ≥ lim N(V_ℤ^(i); X)/X^{5/6}·∏_p ∫ ψ_{p,⌊Y/p⌋} − δ(Y) with δ(Y) → 0; let Y → ∞.
The limit lim N(V_ℤ^(i); X)/X^{5/6} exists by ArithmeticStatistics:ST.2/count-of-binary-quartic-forms-of-bounded-height.
acceptance: Squarefree discriminants: φ = 1_{Δ squarefree}, φ_p = 1_{p^2 ∤ Δ}; the proportion of irreducible classes with squarefree discriminant is ∏_p μ_p{p^2 ∤ Δ}.
For φ defined by finitely many congruence conditions the theorem reduces to Theorem 2.12 with error O(X^{3/4+ε}); for infinitely many conditions only o(X^{5/6}) is claimed.
ArithmeticStatistics:ST.4 applies it with the weight 1/m(f) times local solubility, which is acceptable by Bhargava-Shankar Proposition 3.18.

nodes.title: Real binary cubic forms: the two open GL_2(ℝ)-orbits and their stabilisers (n_0 = 6, n_1 = 2)
nodes.statement: Let U_ℝ be the space of real binary cubic forms f = ax^3 + bx^2y + cxy^2 + dy^3 with the twisted action γ·f := (det γ)^{−1} f((x, y)γ) of GL_2(ℝ) (the action (9) of ArithmeticStatistics:ST.1/delone-faddeev-parametrization-of-cubic-rings), and Disc(f) = b^2c^2 − 4ac^3 − 4b^3d − 27a^2d^2 + 18abcd. (a) Disc(γ·f) = (det γ)^2 Disc(f), and the scalar matrix λ·1 acts by f ↦ λf. (b) U_ℝ^(0) := {Disc > 0}, the forms with three distinct real roots in ℙ^1(ℝ), and U_ℝ^(1) := {Disc < 0}, the forms with one real root and a pair of complex conjugate roots, are each a single GL_2(ℝ)-orbit. (c) The stabiliser in GL_2(ℝ) of f ∈ U_ℝ^(0) has order n_0 := 6 and acts on the three roots as the full symmetric group; the stabiliser of f ∈ U_ℝ^(1) has order n_1 := 2. Put U_ℤ^(i) := U_ℝ^(i) ∩ U_ℤ.
hypotheses: The twisted action (det γ)^{−1} is the one of the Delone-Faddeev correspondence; with the untwisted action the scalars would act by λ^3 and the stabiliser orders would change
Only forms with Disc ≠ 0 are in U_ℝ^(0) ∪ U_ℝ^(1)
proofSteps: (a) Disc is homogeneous of degree 4 and relatively invariant of weight 6 under substitution, Disc(f((x, y)γ)) = (det γ)^6 Disc(f); the factor (det γ)^{−1} multiplies Disc by (det γ)^{−4}. For λ·1: f((x, y)λ)/λ^2 = λf.

(b) Roots: by Cubic.discr_eq_prod_three_roots (after moving a root away from [1 : 0] if a = 0), Disc > 0 iff the three roots are real and distinct, and Disc < 0 iff one is real and two are complex conjugate. PGL_2(ℝ) is simply 3-transitive on ℙ^1(ℝ), and transitive on pairs (real point, conjugate pair) (move the pair to ±i, then rotate by the stabiliser SO_2(ℝ) of i, which is transitive on ℙ^1(ℝ)). A form is determined by its roots up to a nonzero scalar, and the scalars λ·1 realise every scalar factor by (a).

(c) An element of the stabiliser permutes the roots; the map to permutations is injective (an element fixing three points of ℙ^1 is a scalar λ·1, which fixes f only for λ = 1). Every permutation of three real roots is induced by a unique class in PGL_2(ℝ), and exactly one scalar multiple of a representative fixes f; for one real root and a conjugate pair, only the identity and the swap of the pair preserve the real structure, and the swap is realised by a reflection.
acceptance: x^3 − 3xy^2 ∈ U_ℝ^(0) with Disc = 108 and x^3 + xy^2 ∈ U_ℝ^(1) with Disc = −4; the stabiliser of x^3 + xy^2 is {1, diag(−1, 1)} (diag(1, −1) sends it to its negative).
The scalar −1 ∈ GL_2(ℤ) sends f to −f: unlike binary quartic forms, the centre does not act trivially, which is why n_i is the full stabiliser order here and half of it for quartics.

sources.excerpt: Then the action of GL2(R) on VR has two nondegenerate orbits, namely the orbit V(0)R consisting of elements having positive discriminant, and V(1)R consisting of those having negative discriminant.
sources.match: Part (b).

nodes.title: The GL_2(ℤ)-stabiliser of an irreducible integral binary cubic form is trivial or cyclic of order 3
nodes.statement: Let f ∈ U_ℤ be irreducible over ℚ. Then Stab_{GL_2(ℤ)}(f) (twisted action) is trivial or cyclic of order 3, and if it has order 3 then Disc(f) is a positive square.
hypotheses: Irreducibility over ℚ is essential: xy(x − y) has a stabiliser of order 6 in GL_2(ℤ)
proofSteps: As in part (c) of ArithmeticStatistics:ST.2/real-orbits-and-stabilizers-of-binary-cubic-forms, Stab_{GL_2(ℚ)}(f) embeds into the permutations of the three roots of f in ℙ^1(ℚ̄), and the image commutes with the action of Gal(ℚ̄/ℚ) because the elements are rational.
f irreducible: Gal(ℚ̄/ℚ) acts transitively on the roots, through A_3 or S_3. The centraliser of A_3 in S_3 is A_3 and that of S_3 is trivial.

If the stabiliser is A_3 ≅ C_3, the Galois image is A_3, so √Disc(f) = a^2(r_1 − r_2)(r_1 − r_3)(r_2 − r_3) (Cubic.discr_eq_prod_three_roots) is fixed by Galois and rational; a cyclic cubic splits over ℝ as soon as one root is real, so Disc(f) > 0.
acceptance: f = x^3 + x^2y − 2xy^2 − y^3 (the cyclic cubic of conductor 7, Disc = 49) is fixed by the order-3 element γ = [[0, −1], [1, −1]] of SL_2(ℤ), i.e. (x, y) ↦ (y, −x − y); its stabiliser in GL_2(ℤ) is exactly {1, γ, γ^2} (checked by enumeration).
A form with Disc < 0 always has trivial stabiliser in GL_2(ℤ).

sources.excerpt: Now the stabilizer in GL2(Z) of an irreducible element x ∈ VZ is the group of ring automorphisms of the order corresponding to x under the Delone–Faddeev correspondence (see Section 2), and is thus either trivial or C3.
sources.match: The statement; the proof steps give a direct Galois-theoretic argument instead of the Delone-Faddeev detour.

sources.excerpt: No integral binary cubic form having negative discriminant has stabilizer C3 in GL2(Z).
sources.match: The sign statement.

nodes.title: Lemma 21: reducible integral binary cubic forms with a ≠ 0 in R_X(v) number O(X^{3/4+ε})
nodes.statement: Let B ⊂ U_ℝ be compact with |Disc(v)| ≥ 1 for v ∈ B. For v ∈ B with Disc(v) ≠ 0 let R_X(v) := {w ∈ F·v : |Disc(w)| < X} (multiset over the strict Gauss domain F). For every ε > 0 the number of integral forms ax^3 + bx^2y + cxy^2 + dy^3 in R_X(v) that are reducible over ℚ with a ≠ 0 is O_ε(X^{3/4+ε}), the implied constant depending only on B and ε.
hypotheses: Only a ≠ 0; the forms with a = 0 have the factor y
proofSteps: Coefficient bounds: f ∈ N′A′KΛv with λ < X^{1/4} (Disc(λ·v) = λ^4 Disc(v)); the twisted action of a(t) multiplies the coefficients by t^{−3}, t^{−1}, t, t^3, so a = O(λ/t^3) = O(X^{1/4}), ab = O(λ^2/t^4), ac, ad = O(λ^2) = O(X^{1/2}), abc = O(λ^3/t^3) and abd = O(λ^3/t) = O(X^{3/4}).

d = 0 with a ≠ 0: O(X^{3/4+ε}) forms from the bounds on (a, b, c). a, d ≠ 0: O(X^{3/4+ε}) triples (a, b, d); a linear factor rx + sy has r | a and s | d, O(X^ε) choices by the divisor bound (requested from AnalyticNumberTheory:AN.5), and then f(−s, r) = 0 determines c.
acceptance: Order check: X^{3/4+ε} is below the error term X^{5/6} of Theorem 20.
Quartic analogue: ArithmeticStatistics:ST.2/reducible-binary-quartic-forms-in-the-main-body (O(X^{2/3+ε})).

sources.excerpt: Then the number of integral binary cubic forms ax3 + bx2y + cxy2 + dy3 ∈ RX(v) that are reducible with a̸ = 0 is O(X3/4+ǫ), where the implied constant depends only on B.
sources.match: The lemma; the source attributes it to Davenport [15, Lem. 3], [16, Lem. 2] and gives the proof followed here.

nodes.title: Lemma 22: points with stabiliser C_3 are O(X^{3/4+ε})
nodes.statement: The number of GL_2(ℤ)-classes of integral binary cubic forms with 0 < Disc < X whose stabiliser in GL_2(ℤ) is cyclic of order 3 is O_ε(X^{3/4+ε}). Consequently, for every v ∈ U_ℝ^(0), the number of points of U_ℤ ∩ R_X(v) (with multiplicity) with stabiliser C_3 is O_ε(X^{3/4+ε}), with the implied constant independent of v.
hypotheses: Positive discriminant: by ArithmeticStatistics:ST.2/stabilizers-of-irreducible-integral-binary-cubic-forms no irreducible form of negative discriminant has stabiliser C_3
proofSteps: Independence of v: F·v is n_0 = 6 fundamental domains for GL_2(ℤ) on U_ℝ^(0), so a class with stabiliser C_3 has exactly 6/3 = 2 points in R_X(v); the point count is twice the class count.

Take v = x^3 − 3xy^2, whose Hessian covariant H_f = (b^2 − 3ac)x^2 + (bc − 9ad)xy + (c^2 − 3bd)y^2 is 9(x^2 + y^2). The Hessian is SL_2-equivariant, so for g ∈ F the Hessian of g·v is 9 times the positive definite quadratic form attached to g, which is reduced (ArithmeticStatistics:ST.2/gauss-fundamental-domain-in-iwasawa-coordinates): F·v consists of forms with |bc − 9ad| ≤ b^2 − 3ac ≤ c^2 − 3bd.

An element of order 3 (determinant 1) stabilising f stabilises H_f; the only reduced positive definite forms with an automorphism of order 3 are the multiples of x^2 + xy + y^2. Hence b^2 − 3ac = bc − 9ad = c^2 − 3bd, and for fixed (a, b, d) these equations leave O(1) values of c.

The triples (a, b, d) of forms in R_X(v) number O(X^{3/4+ε}) by the coefficient bounds of ArithmeticStatistics:ST.2/reducible-binary-cubic-forms-in-the-main-body (the case a = 0 forces f = b·xy(x + y) up to the constraint and contributes O(X^{1/4})).
acceptance: The source notes that the count is asymptotic to (π√3/18)X^{1/2}; only the upper bound X^{3/4+ε} is needed.
C_3-points are absorbed into the error term O(X^{5/6}) of Theorem 20.

sources.excerpt: Lemma 22 Let v ∈ VR be any point of positive discriminant. Then the number of points in VZ ∩ RX(v) having stabilizer C3 in GL2(Z) is O(X3/4+ǫ), where the implied constant is independent of v.
sources.match: The lemma and the Hessian argument of its proof.

nodes.title: Proposition 23, corrected: |Disc(v)|^{−1} dv is GL_2(ℝ)-invariant, with the Jacobian constant 4π
nodes.statement: Let dg = t^{−2} du d^×t dk d^×λ be the Haar measure on GL_2(ℝ), with dk the invariant probability measure on SO_2(ℝ) extended to the other coset of O_2(ℝ), and dv = da db dc dd on U_ℝ. For i ∈ {0, 1}, v_i ∈ U_ℝ^(i) and every f ∈ C_c(U_ℝ^(i)): ∫_{GL_2(ℝ)} f(g·v_i) dg = (1/4π) ∫_{GL_2(ℝ)·v_i} f(v) |Disc(v)|^{−1} dv = (n_i/4π) ∫_{U_ℝ^(i)} f(v) |Disc(v)|^{−1} dv, where GL_2(ℝ)·v_i is the multiset image (each point covered n_i times). Equivalently, on GL_2^+(ℝ) the map g ↦ g·v_i satisfies dv = 4π|Disc(g·v_i)| dg.
hypotheses: The constant depends on the normalisation of dk; the source's 1/(2π) is off by a factor 2 for its stated normalisation (sourceIssue ArithmeticStatistics/E305)
proofSteps: At g = n(u)a(t)k(θ)λ the Jacobian determinant of (u, t, θ, λ) ↦ g·v with respect to da db dc dd equals ±2|Disc(g·v)|·t^{−3}λ^{−1} (checked symbolically at the forms xy(x − y), x^3 + xy^2, x^3 − 3xy^2 and 2x^3 + x^2y − 5xy^2 + 7y^3); since t^{−3}λ^{−1} du dt dθ dλ = 2π·dg, dv = 4π|Disc(g·v)| dg on GL_2^+(ℝ).
|Disc|^{−1}dv is then GL_2(ℝ)-invariant (Disc(γ·v) = (det γ)^2 Disc(v) and the twisted action has determinant (det γ)^2 on U_ℝ).

The orbit map is n_i-to-one onto U_ℝ^(i) (ArithmeticStatistics:ST.2/real-orbits-and-stabilizers-of-binary-cubic-forms); decompose into injective pieces and apply the change-of-variables formula (MeasureTheory.integral_image_eq_integral_abs_det_fderiv_smul). The component of determinant −1 contributes the same as GL_2^+(ℝ) by right translation.
acceptance: Check against Davenport: with this constant and the strict Gauss domain (covolume π/12), Vol(R_X(v))/n_0 = 4π·(X/4)·(π/12)/6 = π^2X/72, Davenport's constant.
In the source's normalisation the product of the Jacobian constant 2π with the stated covolume ζ(2)/π is 2ζ(2), equal to the product 4π·ζ(2)/(2π) here, so Theorem 20 is unaffected.

sources.excerpt: Proposition 23 For i = 0 or 1, let f ∈ C0(V(i)R ) and let vi be any element of V(i)R . Then ∫g∈GL2(R) f(g · vi) dg = 1/2π ∫v∈GL2(R)·vi f(v) |Disc(v)|−1dv = ni/2π ∫v∈V(i)R f(v) |Disc(v)|−1dv.

nodes.title: The averaged orbit count N(S; X) of binary cubic forms and the regions B(n, t, λ, X)
nodes.statement: Fix C ≥ 1 and the compact SO_2(ℝ)-invariant set B = B(C) := {w ∈ U_ℝ : 3a^2 + b^2 + c^2 + 3d^2 ≤ C, |Disc(w)| ≥ 1}. For i ∈ {0, 1}, S ⊆ U_ℤ^(i) and X > 0 define N(S; X) := ∫_{v ∈ B ∩ U_ℝ^(i)} #{x ∈ F·v ∩ S^irr : |Disc(x)| < X} |Disc(v)|^{−1} dv / (n_i ∫_{B ∩ U_ℝ^(i)} |Disc(v)|^{−1} dv), where F is the strict Gauss domain, F·v is a multiset and S^irr is the set of elements of S irreducible over ℚ. For n = n(u), t > 0, λ > 0 put B(n, t, λ, X) := n a(t) λ (B ∩ U_ℝ^(i)) ∩ {|Disc| < X}, and M_i := (n_i/4π) ∫_{B ∩ U_ℝ^(i)} |Disc(v)|^{−1} dv.
hypotheses: 3a^2 + b^2 + c^2 + 3d^2 is three times the Bombieri norm, invariant under SO_2(ℝ) for the twisted action
Only irreducible elements are counted
proofSteps: The denominator is a positive finite constant (B ∩ U_ℝ^(i) is compact with nonempty interior and |Disc| ≥ 1 on it).

For GL_2(ℤ)-invariant S the integrand is, for every v, Σ over irreducible classes [x] ⊆ S with |Disc(x)| < X of n_i/#Stab_{GL_2(ℤ)}(x) (F·v is n_i fundamental domains), so N(S; X) = Σ_{[x]} 1/#Stab_{GL_2(ℤ)}(x): classes are counted with weight 1, and the classes with stabiliser C_3 with weight 1/3.
acceptance: For S = U_ℤ^(i) the averaged count differs from the number of classes by at most the O(X^{3/4+ε}) classes with stabiliser C_3.
N is additive over disjoint subsets, invariant or not.

sources.excerpt: Then N(S; X) can be expressed as N(S; X) = ∫v∈B∩V(i)R #{x ∈ Fv ∩ Sirr : |Disc(x)| < X} |Disc(v)|−1dv / (ni · ∫v∈B∩V(i)R |Disc(v)|−1dv)
