nodes.title: The averaging formula for binary cubic forms, (20)-(23), with the corrected constants
nodes.statement: For i ∈ {0, 1}, S ⊆ U_ℤ^(i) and X > 0: N(S; X) = (1/M_i) ∫_{g ∈ F} #{x ∈ S^irr ∩ g(B ∩ U_ℝ^(i)) : |Disc(x)| < X} dg = (1/(2M_i)) ∫_{n(u)a(t)λ ∈ N′(t)A′Λ} #{x ∈ S^irr ∩ B(n, t, λ, X)} t^{−2} du d^×t d^×λ, with M_i = (n_i/4π) ∫_{B ∩ U_ℝ^(i)} |Disc(v)|^{−1} dv.
hypotheses: The factor 1/2 is ∫_{K_+} dk; the constant 4π is that of ArithmeticStatistics:ST.2/invariant-measure-on-binary-cubic-forms (the source has M_i with 2π and no 1/2; see sourceIssues ArithmeticStatistics/E305 and E301)
proofSteps: Choose H^(i) ⊆ GL_2(ℝ) maximal with H^(i)·v_i = B ∩ U_ℝ^(i) as an n_i-fold multiset. By ArithmeticStatistics:ST.2/invariant-measure-on-binary-cubic-forms, ∫_{B ∩ U^(i)} Φ(v)|Disc(v)|^{−1} dv = (4π/n_i) ∫_{H^(i)} Φ(h·v_i) dh.

Apply this to Φ(v) = #{g ∈ F : x = g·v}, sum over x, exchange the order (unimodularity of GL_2(ℝ)) as in (18)-(19), and use that the multiset H^(i)·v_i covers B ∩ U^(i) n_i times: the numerator of N(S; X) equals 4π ∫_F #{x ∈ S^irr ∩ gB : |Disc(x)| < X} dg.

Divide by n_i ∫ |Disc|^{−1}: this is the first formula. For the second, write g = n(u)a(t)kλ with k ∈ K_+, use kB = B and ∫_{K_+} dk = 1/2 (ArithmeticStatistics:ST.2/averaged-count-of-binary-cubic-orbits).
acceptance: Inserting Vol(B(n, t, λ, X)) for the count gives Vol(R_X(v))/n_i, independent of v (the computation in the proof of ArithmeticStatistics:ST.2/davenport-count-of-binary-cubic-forms).
For invariant S both sides are independent of C.

nodes.title: Lemma 25 and (28): lattice points with a ≠ 0 in B(n, t, λ, X), for translates of mU_ℤ
nodes.statement: Let C bound the absolute values of all coefficients of all forms in B. Let m ≥ 1 and let L′ = v_0 + mU_ℤ, and let a′ ≥ 1 be the smallest nonzero |a|-coordinate of a point of L′. For u ∈ [−1/2, 1/2], t ≥ 3^{1/4}/√2, λ > 0 and X > 0, the number of points (a, b, c, d) ∈ L′ ∩ B(n(u), t, λ, X) with a ≠ 0 is 0 if Cλ/t^3 < a′, and otherwise m^{−4}Vol(B(n(u), t, λ, X)) + O(C^3t^3λ^3/m^3 + C^2t^4λ^2/m^2 + Ct^3λ/m + 1), the implied constant absolute. For m = 1 the error is O(max(C^3t^3λ^3, 1)).
hypotheses: The x^3-coefficient of a form in B(n, t, λ, X) is at most Cλ/t^3 in absolute value
Davenport's lemma is the input (a request)
proofSteps: Under the twisted action, n(u) with |u| ≤ 1/2 adds to each coefficient a bounded combination of the preceding ones, a(t) multiplies them by t^{−3}, t^{−1}, t, t^3 and λ·1 by λ; so the ranges of (a, b, c, d) are O(Cλ/t^3, Cλ/t, Cλt, Cλt^3).
If Cλ/t^3 < a′ no point of L′ with a ≠ 0 fits.

Otherwise apply Davenport's lemma (requested from GeometryOfNumbersAndQuadraticArithmetic:GN.4) to the image of B(n, t, λ, X) under v ↦ (v − v_0)/m: the projection onto a = 0 has volume O(C^3t^3λ^3/m^3), the 2-dimensional projections O(C^2t^4λ^2/m^2) (the two largest ranges), the 1-dimensional ones O(Ct^3λ/m).
acceptance: Unlike the quartic cusp, the cubic cusp t^3 > Cλ still contains integral points with a = 0 only, but in the range t^3 ≤ Cλ the error C^3t^3λ^3 integrates to X^{5/6}, the size of the error term (and of the second main term of Shintani, which this fragment does not plan).
For m = 1 the terms t^4λ^2 and t^3λ are dominated by t^3λ^3 in the range t^3 ≤ Cλ, t ≥ 3^{1/4}/√2.

nodes.title: Theorem 20 (Davenport): the number of GL_2(ℤ)-classes of irreducible integral binary cubic forms of bounded discriminant
nodes.statement: (a) N(U_ℤ^(0); X) = (π^2/72)X + O(X^{5/6}) and N(U_ℤ^(1); X) = (π^2/24)X + O(X^{5/6}), where N(U_ℤ^(i); X) is the number of GL_2(ℤ)-classes of irreducible integral binary cubic forms f with 0 < (−1)^i Disc(f) < X. (b) For every v ∈ U_ℝ^(i), Vol(R_X(v)) = π^2X/12, where R_X(v) = {w ∈ F·v : |Disc(w)| < X} is the multiset over the strict Gauss domain; so Vol(R_X(v))/n_i = π^2X/(12n_i). (c) Cusp tail: there is c = c(C) such that for every S ⊆ U_ℤ^(i), T ≥ 3^{1/4}/√2 and X ≥ 1, (1/(2M_i)) ∫_{t > T} #{x ∈ S^irr ∩ B(n, t, λ, X)} t^{−2} du d^×t d^×λ ≤ c·X/T^2 + O(X^{5/6}).
hypotheses: Classes under GL_2(ℤ) with the twisted action; the classes with stabiliser C_3 are counted with weight 1 (their number is O(X^{3/4+ε}))
Davenport's original error was O(X^{15/16})
proofSteps: By ArithmeticStatistics:ST.2/averaging-formula-for-binary-cubic-forms with S = U_ℤ^(i), the integrand vanishes unless t^3 ≤ Cλ and λ ≤ X^{1/4} (ArithmeticStatistics:ST.2/binary-cubic-lattice-points-in-the-cusp; B has |Disc| ≥ 1 and points with a = 0 are reducible).

Irreducible points = points with a ≠ 0 minus reducible ones: O(X^{3/4+ε}) by ArithmeticStatistics:ST.2/reducible-binary-cubic-forms-in-the-main-body; the C_3-classes change the count by O(X^{3/4+ε}) (ArithmeticStatistics:ST.2/binary-cubic-forms-with-cyclic-stabilizer).
The error O(max(C^3t^3λ^3, 1)) integrates over t^3 ≤ Cλ, λ ≤ X^{1/4} to O(X^{5/6}); the part of the main term with t^3 > Cλ is O(X^{5/6}) since Vol(B(n, t, λ, X)) ≪ λ^4.

Main term: ∫ Vol(B(n, t, λ, X)) over all of N′A′Λ is 2∫_F Vol(gB ∩ {|Disc| < X}) dg; writing Vol(gB ∩ …) = ∫_{w ∈ B} 1[|Disc(gw)| < X]·|Disc(gw)|/|Disc(w)| dw and applying ArithmeticStatistics:ST.2/invariant-measure-on-binary-cubic-forms gives (1/4π) Vol(R_X(v)) ∫_B |Disc|^{−1}, so the main term is Vol(R_X(v))/n_i (Vol(R_X(w)) does not depend on w ∈ U_ℝ^(i), as F·w is n_i fundamental domains).

(b) For |Disc(v)| = 1, Vol(R_X(v)) = ∫_{g ∈ F} 1[λ^4 < X]·4π|Disc(g·v)| dg = 4π ∫_0^{X^{1/4}} λ^4 d^×λ · ∫_{N′A′K_+} t^{−2} du d^×t dk = 4π·(X/4)·(π/12) = π^2X/12 by ArithmeticStatistics:ST.2/covolume-of-pgl2-z (b); for general v rescale by λ·1.
(a) follows with n_0 = 6, n_1 = 2. (c) Vol(B(n, t, λ, X)) ≪ λ^4, ∫_{t > T} t^{−2} d^×t ≤ T^{−2}/2 and ∫^{X^{1/4}} λ^4 d^×λ = X/4; the error terms integrate to O(X^{5/6}).
acceptance: Davenport's constants: π^2/72 ≈ 0.1371 and π^2/24 ≈ 0.4112.
Delone-Faddeev reading (ArithmeticStatistics:ST.3): these count isomorphism classes of orders in cubic fields of bounded discriminant.
The error O(X^{5/6}) is of the same order as Shintani's second main term, which requires the slicing argument of BST Section 6.

nodes.title: Theorem 26 with (29)-(31): binary cubic forms in lattice translates, uniformly in the modulus
nodes.statement: (a) Let 1 ≤ m ≤ X^{1/6} and L = v_0 + mU_ℤ. Then N(L ∩ U_ℤ^(i); X) = m^{−4}·(π^2/(12n_i))X + O(m^{−3}X^{5/6}) − R_L(X), where the implied constant is independent of m, v_0 and X, and R_L(X) ≥ 0 is at most the number of reducible and C_3-points counted in L, so that Σ_L R_L(X) = O_ε(X^{3/4+ε}) over any family of disjoint translates. (b) If S ⊆ U_ℤ is a union of k translates of mU_ℤ with m ≤ X^{1/6}, then N(S ∩ U_ℤ^(i); X) = (k/m^4)(π^2/(12n_i))X + O(k m^{−3}X^{5/6}) + O_ε(X^{3/4+ε}). (c) If S ⊆ U_ℤ^(i) is defined by finitely many congruence conditions modulo prime powers, then lim_{X→∞} N(S ∩ U_ℤ^(i); X)/X = (π^2/(12n_i))·∏_p μ_p(S).
hypotheses: N is the averaged count, the class count for invariant S
m ≤ X^{1/6} makes the lower-dimensional projection terms of (29) smaller than m^{−3}X^{5/6}
proofSteps: (a) Repeat the proof of ArithmeticStatistics:ST.2/davenport-count-of-binary-cubic-forms with ArithmeticStatistics:ST.2/binary-cubic-lattice-points-in-the-cusp for L: integrating its error terms gives (29), O(C^{10/3}X^{5/6}/(a′^{1/3}m^3) + C^{8/3}X^{2/3}/(a′^{2/3}m^2) + C^{4/3}X^{1/3}/(a′^{1/3}m) + log X), which is O(m^{−3}X^{5/6}) for a′ ≥ 1 and m ≤ X^{1/6}.

The reducible points and C_3-points of L are among those of U_ℤ, bounded in total by ArithmeticStatistics:ST.2/reducible-binary-cubic-forms-in-the-main-body and ArithmeticStatistics:ST.2/binary-cubic-forms-with-cyclic-stabilizer.
(b) Sum (a) over the k translates. (c) Fix S, let X → ∞ in (b), and use k m^{−4} = ∏_p μ_p(S) (Chinese remainder theorem; ArithmeticStatistics:ST.2/functions-defined-by-congruence-conditions).
acceptance: S = U_ℤ recovers Theorem 20 (m = 1).
Uniformity check: for S_p = {f : p | a(f)} (m = p, k = p^3) the error is O(X^{5/6}) + O(X^{3/4+ε}) uniformly for p ≤ X^{1/6}.

nodes.title: Index-p switching: forms with p^2 | a, p | b come from forms of discriminant Disc/p^2 with a marked root modulo p
nodes.statement: Let p be a prime and use the twisted action on U_ℚ. (a) If f = (a, b, c, d) ∈ U_ℤ has p^2 | a and p | b, then f′ := diag(p^{−1}, 1)·f = (a/p^2, b/p, c, pd) ∈ U_ℤ, Disc(f′) = p^{−2}Disc(f), f′(0, 1) ≡ 0 (mod p), and f = diag(p, 1)·f′. (b) Conversely, if g ∈ U_ℤ and α ∈ ℙ^1(𝔽_p) is a root of g mod p, choose γ_α ∈ GL_2(ℤ) whose bottom row reduces to a representative of α; then f_{g,α} := diag(p, 1)·(γ_α·g) ∈ U_ℤ has p^2 | a and p | b, and its GL_2(ℤ)-class depends only on the GL_2(ℤ)-class of g and on α modulo the action of Stab_{GL_2(ℤ)}(g). (c) Consequently every GL_2(ℤ)-class of forms f with Disc(f) ≠ 0 having a translate with p^2 | a and p | b is the class of some f_{g,α} with |Disc(g)| = |Disc(f)|/p^2, and the number of such classes attached to one class [g] is at most the number of roots of g mod p in ℙ^1(𝔽_p): at most 3 if g ≢ 0 (mod p), at most p + 1 otherwise.
hypotheses: This is the form-theoretic content of BST Lemma 13 and Propositions 15-16 (index-p overrings and subrings of cubic rings); no ring theory is used
The twisted action is the one of ArithmeticStatistics:ST.1/delone-faddeev-parametrization-of-cubic-rings
proofSteps: (a) diag(p^{−1}, 1)·f = f(x/p, y)/det(diag(p^{−1}, 1)) = p·f(x/p, y) = (a/p^2)x^3 + (b/p)x^2y + cxy^2 + pdy^3, and Disc(γ·f) = (det γ)^2 Disc(f) with det γ = 1/p (ArithmeticStatistics:ST.2/real-orbits-and-stabilizers-of-binary-cubic-forms (a)).

(b) γ_α·g vanishes at [0 : 1] mod p, i.e. its y^3-coefficient d′ is divisible by p; then diag(p, 1)·(γ_α·g) = (p^2a′, pb′, c′, d′/p) is integral. Two choices γ_α, γ′_α differ by δ ∈ GL_2(ℤ) with p | δ_21, and diag(p, 1)δ diag(p, 1)^{−1} = [[δ_11, pδ_12], [δ_21/p, δ_22]] ∈ GL_2(ℤ); replacing g by ε·g (ε ∈ GL_2(ℤ)) moves α accordingly.

(c) Given f, move it so that p^2 | a and p | b, and take g = f′ from (a), α = [0 : 1]; then f = f_{g,α}. A nonzero binary cubic form over 𝔽_p has at most 3 roots in ℙ^1(𝔽_p) (Polynomial.card_roots' for its dehomogenisation, plus possibly [1 : 0]); the zero form has p + 1.
acceptance: For p = 5 and g = x^3 + xy^2 (which vanishes at [0 : 1]), f_{g,[0:1]} = diag(5, 1)·g = g(5x, y)/5 = 25x^3 + xy^2, and Disc(f) = −100 = 25·Disc(g).
The bound 3 (not p + 1) for g ≢ 0 mod p is what makes the switching estimate O(X/p^2) rather than O(X/p).

nodes.title: Proposition 29 (non-maximal part), for forms: the classes in W_p^DH have O(X/p^2) elements of discriminant < X, uniformly in p
nodes.statement: For a prime p let W_p^DH := {f ∈ U_ℤ : f ∈ pU_ℤ, or some γ ∈ GL_2(ℤ) has γ·f = (a, b, c, d) with p^2 | a and p | b}. There is an absolute constant C such that for every prime p and every X ≥ 1 the number of GL_2(ℤ)-classes of irreducible f ∈ W_p^DH with 0 < |Disc(f)| < X is at most C·X/p^2.
hypotheses: W_p^DH is the complement of the Davenport-Heilbronn set U_p; by BST Theorem 14 (owned with the Delone-Faddeev correspondence) it is the set of forms whose cubic ring is not maximal at p, but only the form definition is used here
proofSteps: Let N(Y) be the number of classes of irreducible integral binary cubic forms with 0 < |Disc| < Y; by ArithmeticStatistics:ST.2/davenport-count-of-binary-cubic-forms, N(Y) ≤ C_0·Y for Y ≥ 1, and N(Y) = 0 for Y ≤ 1.
f ∈ pU_ℤ: f = pf_0 with f_0 irreducible and Disc(f) = p^4 Disc(f_0), at most N(X/p^4) classes.

Otherwise, by ArithmeticStatistics:ST.2/index-p-switching-for-binary-cubic-forms, the classes are among the f_{g,α} with |Disc(g)| < X/p^2 and g irreducible (g is GL_2(ℚ)-equivalent to f): at most 3N(X/p^2) from g ≢ 0 (mod p), and at most (p + 1)N(X/p^6) from g = pg_0.
acceptance: The bound is uniform in p; for p^2 > X the set is empty.

The totally ramified maximal forms (Y_p of BST) are not in W_p^DH; BST bound them by class field theory, while here they are covered by the geometric sieve in ArithmeticStatistics:ST.2/uniformity-estimate-for-binary-cubic-discriminants.

nodes.title: A uniform tail estimate for binary cubic forms whose discriminant is divisible by p^2 for some p > M
nodes.statement: For a prime p let W_p(U) := {f ∈ U_ℤ : p^2 | Disc(f)}. There are constants c and C_T (for each T ≥ 3^{1/4}/√2, independent of M) such that for every M ≥ 3, lim sup_{X→∞} N(⋃_{p>M} W_p(U); X)/X ≤ C_T/(M log M) + c/T^2, where N counts GL_2(ℤ)-classes of irreducible forms with 0 < |Disc| < X. Consequently lim_{M→∞} lim sup_{X→∞} N(⋃_{p>M} W_p(U); X)/X = 0.
hypotheses: Both signs of the discriminant are included
The strongly divisible part (triple root modulo p, which contains the maximal totally ramified forms) is handled by the geometric sieve; BST use class field theory for the totally ramified part
proofSteps: Decomposition for p ≥ 3: if f ∈ W_p(U) and f mod p ∉ Y_3(𝔽_p), where Y_3 = V(Disc, ∂Disc/∂d), then f ∈ W_p^DH. Indeed p ∤ ∂Disc/∂d(f) makes f weakly divisible (gradient characterisation in ArithmeticStatistics:ST.2/strongly-and-weakly-divisible-values), so f ≢ 0 (mod p) and f mod p has no triple root (a triple root moved to [1 : 0] gives p | a, b, c, hence p^2 | Disc(f + pg) for all g); as p | Disc(f), f mod p has a double root α ∈ ℙ^1(𝔽_p) (a repeated root of a cubic is rational). Move α to [1 : 0] by γ ∈ GL_2(ℤ): γ·f = (a, b, c, d) with p | a, p | b and p ∤ c, and Disc(γ·f) ≡ −4ac^3 (mod p^2), so p^2 | Disc forces p^2 | a (p odd).

The W_p^DH part: Σ_{p>M} N(W_p^DH; X) ≤ C X Σ_{p>M} p^{−2} = O(X/(M log M)) by ArithmeticStatistics:ST.2/uniformity-estimate-for-nonmaximal-binary-cubic-forms and ArithmeticStatistics:ST.2/chebyshev-bounds-for-prime-sums.

The Y_3 part: by ArithmeticStatistics:ST.2/averaging-formula-for-binary-cubic-forms split the integral at t = T. For t > T use part (c) of ArithmeticStatistics:ST.2/davenport-count-of-binary-cubic-forms: ≤ cX/T^2 + O(X^{5/6}). For t ≤ T all regions lie in X^{1/4}·Ω_T with Ω_T compact, each point is counted with bounded weight, and ArithmeticStatistics:ST.2/quantitative-ekedahl-geometric-sieve with n = 4, k = 2, r = X^{1/4} (Y_3 of codimension 2 by ArithmeticStatistics:ST.2/discriminant-loci-of-codimension-two; strongly divisible forms reduce into Y_3 by ArithmeticStatistics:ST.2/strong-divisibility-lies-on-a-codimension-two-locus) gives O_T(X/(M log M) + X^{3/4}).
Divide by X, let X → ∞, then choose T and M as in the quartic case.
acceptance: For ArithmeticStatistics:ST.3: every acceptable collection of local specifications in the sense of BST (Σ_p contains the maximal, not totally ramified cubic rings over ℤ_p for large p) corresponds to an acceptable set of forms for Disc, and this theorem is the tail estimate the sieve needs, for Theorems 1, 2 and 8 of BST alike.
The rate C_T/(M log M) + c/T^2 is uniform in the congruence conditions imposed at primes ≤ M.

nodes.title: Counting binary cubic forms weighted by an acceptable function defined by infinitely many congruence conditions
nodes.statement: Let φ : U_ℤ → [0, 1] be acceptable for Disc and defined by congruence conditions via GL_2(ℤ)-invariant local functions φ_p : U_{ℤ_p} → [0, 1] (ArithmeticStatistics:ST.2/functions-defined-by-congruence-conditions). For i ∈ {0, 1} let N_φ(U_ℤ^(i); X) be the number of irreducible GL_2(ℤ)-classes in U_ℤ^(i) with |Disc| < X, each class counted with weight φ. Then N_φ(U_ℤ^(i); X) = (π^2/(12n_i))·∏_p ∫_{U_{ℤ_p}} φ_p(f) df · X + o(X), and the Euler product converges. In particular, for an acceptable set S = ⋂_p S_p, lim_{X→∞} N(S ∩ U_ℤ^(i); X)/X = (π^2/(12n_i))∏_p μ_p(S_p).
hypotheses: Acceptability: φ_p = 1 on {p^2 ∤ Disc} for large p
The cubic-ring translation (maximality, splitting types, local masses Σ 1/(Disc_p(R)|Aut(R)|)) belongs to ArithmeticStatistics:ST.3 and ArithmeticStatistics:ST.1
proofSteps: Approximate φ_p from above and below by functions defined modulo p^n, as in ArithmeticStatistics:ST.2/squarefree-sieve-for-binary-quartic-forms; convergence of the Euler product from 1 − ∫φ_p ≤ μ_p{p^2 | Disc} ≤ Cp^{−2} (ArithmeticStatistics:ST.2/local-density-of-values-divisible-by-p-squared, Disc being primitive and coprime to ∂Disc/∂d by ArithmeticStatistics:ST.2/discriminant-loci-of-codimension-two).

Upper bound: a weight defined modulo finitely many prime powers is a finite linear combination of indicators of translates of mU_ℤ; ArithmeticStatistics:ST.2/binary-cubic-counts-with-congruence-conditions gives its limit; let the truncation grow.

Lower bound: the truncated lower approximation differs from φ only on ⋃_{p>Y} W_p(U), whose contribution is controlled by ArithmeticStatistics:ST.2/uniformity-estimate-for-binary-cubic-discriminants; let Y → ∞.
acceptance: φ ≡ 1 recovers Theorem 20; φ = 1_{U_p} for all p gives Davenport-Heilbronn's count of maximal cubic orders through the Delone-Faddeev and Davenport-Heilbronn correspondences (ArithmeticStatistics:ST.3/davenport-heilbronn-count-of-cubic-fields), with ∏_p μ_p(U_p) = ∏_p (1 − p^{−2})(1 − p^{−3}) and limit 1/(2n_iζ(3)).
With φ_p the indicator of forms maximal and not totally ramified at p, the local densities are (1 − p^{−2})^2 (BST Lemma 19), the input for BST Theorem 2.

nodes.title: The counting function of number fields of fixed degree by discriminant, with signature, Galois-group and local restrictions
nodes.statement: Fix an algebraic closure Q̄ of Q (Mathlib's AlgebraicClosure ℚ). For an integer n ≥ 1, a predicate P on number fields that is invariant under Q-algebra isomorphism, and real numbers ξ < η, let S_n(P; ξ, η) be the set of intermediate fields K of Q̄/Q with [K : Q] = n, ξ < Disc(K) < η and P(K), where Disc(K) = NumberField.discr K ∈ Z is the signed absolute discriminant (its sign is (−1)^{r₂(K)}). S_n(P; ξ, η) is finite by Hermite's theorem. Define N_n(P; ξ, η) as the number of classes of S_n(P; ξ, η) under the relation K ~ K' iff K ≃ₐ[Q] K'; since every number field of degree n embeds into Q̄, N_n(P; ξ, η) is the number of Q-isomorphism classes of degree-n number fields K with ξ < Disc(K) < η and P(K). Abbreviations: N_n^+(P; X) := N_n(P; 0, X), N_n^-(P; X) := N_n(P; −X, 0), and N_n(P; X) := N_n^+(P; X) + N_n^-(P; X) (all fields with 0 < |Disc(K)| < X). The weighted count N_n^{Aut}(P; ξ, η) := Σ_{classes [K]} 1/#Aut(K/Q). The three standard restrictions are pinned as follows. Signature: P(K) is nrComplexPlaces K = r₂. Galois group: for a transitive subgroup Γ ≤ S_n, P(K) says that the image of Gal(Q̄/Q), acting by composition on the n embeddings K → Q̄ (MulAction.toPermHom), is conjugate to Γ under some bijection between the embeddings and {1, …, n}; this is the permutation Galois group of PolynomialGaloisGroups, Layer 0 (the degree-n action of (minpoly ℚ α).Gal for K = Q(α)) with its label predicate of Layer 6. Local specifications: for a collection Σ = (Σ_v) of sets of isomorphism classes of étale algebras of degree n over Q_v (v a prime or ∞), P(K) says K ⊗ Q_v ∈ Σ_v for every v.
hypotheses: n ≥ 1; for the Galois-group restriction Γ is a transitive subgroup of S_n, identified up to conjugacy
P must be invariant under Q-algebra isomorphism; otherwise the count depends on the chosen subfield in the class
The discriminant is Mathlib's signed NumberField.discr; the interval (ξ, η) is open at both ends, matching BST's N₃(ξ, η)
Fields are counted up to isomorphism, not as subfields of Q̄ (a non-Galois cubic field has three conjugate subfields and is counted once)
proofSteps: The set S_n(P; ξ, η) is contained in the set of intermediate fields K of Q̄/Q with |discr K| ≤ ⌈max(|ξ|, |η|)⌉, which is finite by NumberField.finite_of_discr_bdd; take Nat.card of the quotient by the isomorphism relation.

Invariance of P and of finrank and discr under Q-isomorphism makes the quotient well defined; the embedding of every number field of degree n into Q̄ (its minimal polynomial splits in Q̄) shows that every isomorphism class is represented.

The subfield formula: the members of S_n(P; ξ, η) isomorphic to a fixed K are the images of the n embeddings K → Q̄, two embeddings having the same image iff they differ by an automorphism of K, so the class of K has n/#Aut(K/Q) members and N_n(P; ξ, η) = Σ_{K ∈ S_n(P; ξ, η)} #Aut(K/Q)/n.

The family of degree-n number fields up to isomorphism, ordered by |Disc|, with weight 1 (or 1/#Aut(K/Q) for the weighted count), is an instance of the arithmetic family of ArithmeticStatistics:ST.0/arithmetic-family; its counting function is N_n(P; X), and its bounded-height finiteness is Hermite's theorem.
acceptance: N₂(⊤; −5, 0) = 2 (Q(√−3) and Q(i)), N₃(⊤; −24, 0) = 1 (the field of x³ − x − 1, discriminant −23) and N₃(⊤; 0, 50) = 1 (the cyclic field Q(ζ₇)⁺, discriminant 49).
For n = 3, the set S₃(⊤; −24, 0) has three elements but N₃(⊤; −24, 0) = 1: the subfield count and the isomorphism-class count differ by the factor 3/#Aut.
Sign check: N_n(P; −X, 0) counts exactly the fields with r₂ odd (NumberField.sign_discr).

nodes.title: The number h_m(K) of m-torsion elements of the class group of a number field
nodes.statement: For a number field K and an integer m ≥ 1, h_m(K) := #{c ∈ Cl(K) : c^m = 1} = Nat.card {c : ClassGroup (𝓞 K) // c ^ m = 1}, the order of the m-torsion subgroup Cl(K)[m] of the ideal class group. For a quadratic field K₂ of discriminant D this is BST's h*_3(K₂) = #Cl₃(D) when m = 3. For a prime p, h_p(K) = p^{rk_p Cl(K)} where rk_p A = dim_{F_p} A/pA.
hypotheses: m ≥ 1; the class group is Mathlib's ClassGroup (𝓞 K) of the ring of integers (the wide class group); narrow class groups, where used, are named explicitly
Cl(K) is finite (NumberField.classNumber), so h_m(K) is a positive integer dividing the class number
proofSteps: Define h_m(K) as Nat.card of the subtype {c : ClassGroup (𝓞 K) // c ^ m = 1}; it is the kernel of the m-th power endomorphism of the finite abelian group Cl(K).
For a finite abelian group A, #A[m] = #(A/mA) = #Hom(A, Z/mZ) (duality of finite abelian groups), and for m = p prime #A[p] = p^{rk_p A}.
For coprime m, m': A[mm'] ≅ A[m] × A[m'], so h_{mm'} = h_m h_{m'}; and h_m(K) divides h(K) = NumberField.classNumber K by Lagrange.
acceptance: For K = Q(√−23), Cl(K) ≅ Z/3Z, so h₃(K) = 3 and h₂(K) = 1.
For K = Q(√−5), Cl(K) ≅ Z/2Z, so h₂(K) = 2 = 2^{t−1} with t = 2 ramified primes (genus theory, Tau Ceti).
The number of index-3 subgroups of Cl(K) is (h₃(K) − 1)/2, the quantity of BST (59).

nodes.title: The splitting symbol (f, p) of an integral binary cubic form and the local sets T_p(σ), V_p, Y_p, Z_p
nodes.statement: Let V_Z be the space of integral binary cubic forms f(x, y) = a x³ + b x² y + c x y² + d y³ (coefficients (a, b, c, d) ∈ Z⁴, the carrier of ArithmeticStatistics:ST.1/delone-faddeev-parametrization-of-cubic-rings) and p a prime. If f ≢ 0 (mod p), f mod p has exactly three zeros in P¹(F̄_p) counted with multiplicity; the splitting symbol (f, p) = (f₁^{e₁} f₂^{e₂} …) lists the degrees f_i over F_p of the fields of definition of the distinct zeros and their multiplicities e_i, and takes one of the five values (111), (12), (3), (1²1), (1³). For each symbol σ, T_p(σ) := {f ∈ V_Z : f ≢ 0 (mod p), (f, p) = σ}. With U_p ⊆ V_Z the set of forms f such that the cubic ring R(f) is maximal at p (the Davenport-Heilbronn set of ArithmeticStatistics:ST.1: f ∉ U_p iff f ≡ 0 (mod p), or some GL₂(Z)-translate of f has a ≡ 0 (mod p²) and b ≡ 0 (mod p)), put U_p(σ) := U_p ∩ T_p(σ), V_p := U_p \ T_p(1³) (maximal at p and not totally ramified at p), Y_p := U_p ∩ T_p(1³) (maximal and totally ramified at p), W_p := V_Z \ U_p and Z_p := V_Z \ V_p = W_p ⊔ Y_p. Over Z_p and F_p the same definitions apply to V_{Z_p} = Z_p⁴ and V_{F_p} = F_p⁴.
hypotheses: p is prime; the symbol is undefined for f ≡ 0 (mod p), and such f lie in W_p
All the sets depend only on f mod p² (T_p(σ) only on f mod p), so they are finite unions of translates of p²V_Z and have well-defined p-adic densities
The symbol is invariant under the twisted GL₂(Z)-action (γf)(x, y) = det(γ)^{-1} f((x, y)γ) of ST.1, since GL₂ permutes the zeros in P¹ preserving degrees and multiplicities
Z_p is BST's set of forms 'whose discriminants are not fundamental'; W_p and Y_p are its two parts
proofSteps: Factor f mod p over F_p into irreducible binary forms (homogeneous factorisation in F_p[x, y]); the pairs (degree, multiplicity) of the distinct irreducible factors, as a multiset, is the symbol; the five values are the multisets with Σ f_i e_i = 3.

GL₂(F_p) acts on binary forms over F_p by linear substitution and scaling by det^{-1}, which maps irreducible factors to irreducible factors of the same degree with the same multiplicities; reduction mod p commutes with the action, so T_p(σ), U_p and hence V_p, Y_p, W_p, Z_p are GL₂(Z)-invariant.
U_p is imported from ST.1 (Davenport-Heilbronn's maximality criterion, BST Theorem 14); the remaining sets are Boolean combinations.
acceptance: x y (x − y) has symbol (111) at every p, x (x² + y²) has symbol (12) at p = 3, and x²y has symbol (1²1) at every p.
y³ + p x³ has symbol (1³), lies in U_p (a ≢ 0 mod p²) and hence in Y_p; y³ + p² x³ has symbol (1³) but lies in W_p.
V_Z = W_p ⊔ V_p ⊔ Y_p as a disjoint union.

nodes.title: The splitting symbol determines R(f)/(p), and for f ∈ U_p it is the splitting type of p in R(f)
nodes.statement: For an integral binary cubic form f with f ≢ 0 (mod p) and cubic ring R(f) (ArithmeticStatistics:ST.1/delone-faddeev-parametrization-of-cubic-rings): (f, p) = (f₁^{e₁} f₂^{e₂} …) iff R(f)/pR(f) ≅ F_{p^{f₁}}[t₁]/(t₁^{e₁}) ⊕ F_{p^{f₂}}[t₂]/(t₂^{e₂}) ⊕ …. Consequently, if f ∈ U_p (R(f) maximal at p) and f is irreducible with R(f) ⊗ Q = K a cubic field, then (f, p) is the splitting type of p in K: (111) split, (12) one degree-1 and one degree-2 prime, (3) inert, (1²1) partially ramified, (1³) totally ramified.

Both sides depend only on the GL₂(F_p)-orbit of f mod p; check the five orbits on representatives: xy(x − y) gives F_p³, x·q(x, y) with q irreducible gives F_p ⊕ F_{p²}, an irreducible cubic gives F_{p³}, x²y gives F_p[t]/(t²) ⊕ F_p, x³ gives F_p[t]/(t³); these are pairwise non-isomorphic algebras.

If R(f) ⊗ Z_p is the maximal order of K ⊗ Q_p, then R(f)/pR(f) = O_K/pO_K ≅ ⊕_{𝔭 | p} O_K/𝔭^{e(𝔭)}, and O_K/𝔭^{e} ≅ F_{p^{f(𝔭)}}[t]/(t^e) (Dedekind–Kummer; NumberFieldArithmetic Layer 1 splitting dictionary), so the symbol records (f(𝔭), e(𝔭)).

The second half needs f ∈ U_p: a form p·g has no symbol at all, and f = y³ + 4x³ has (f, 2) = (1³) while R(f) is not maximal at 2 (f ∈ W₂), so R(f)/2R(f) is not O_K/2O_K.

nodes.title: Lemma 17: the p-adic densities of the sets T_p(σ)
nodes.statement: Let μ_p be the p-adic density on V_Z (the Haar measure of the p-adic closure in V_{Z_p} = Z_p⁴, total mass 1; for a set defined modulo p it is (number of residue classes mod p)/p⁴). Then μ_p(T_p(111)) = (1/6)(p − 1)² p (p + 1)/p⁴, μ_p(T_p(12)) = (1/2)(p − 1)² p (p + 1)/p⁴, μ_p(T_p(3)) = (1/3)(p − 1)² p (p + 1)/p⁴, μ_p(T_p(1²1)) = (p − 1) p (p + 1)/p⁴ and μ_p(T_p(1³)) = (p − 1)(p + 1)/p⁴.
hypotheses: p prime
μ_p is the normalised additive Haar measure on Z_p⁴ (the density used in BST Theorem 26, supplied with that theorem by ArithmeticStatistics:ST.2)
proofSteps: Membership in T_p(σ) depends only on f mod p, so μ_p(T_p(σ)) = #{f ∈ F_p⁴ : (f, p) = σ}/p⁴.
A nonzero binary cubic form over F_p is determined up to the p − 1 nonzero scalars by its zero divisor in P¹(F̄_p), a Frobenius-stable effective divisor of degree 3.

Count the divisors of each shape: unordered triples of distinct points of P¹(F_p): (p + 1)p(p − 1)/6; a point of P¹(F_p) plus a conjugate pair from P¹(F_{p²}) \ P¹(F_p): (p + 1)(p² − p)/2; a conjugate triple from P¹(F_{p³}) \ P¹(F_p): (p³ − p)/3; a double point and a different single point, both rational: (p + 1)p; a rational triple point: p + 1.
Multiply each count by p − 1 and divide by p⁴.
acceptance: The five densities sum to (p⁴ − 1)/p⁴, the density of forms not ≡ 0 mod p: (p − 1)(p + 1)[(p − 1)p + p + 1] = (p² − 1)(p² + 1).
At p = 2 the counts of forms are 1, 3, 2, 6, 3 (sum 15 = 2⁴ − 1).

sources.excerpt: The number of unordered triples of distinct points in P1 Fp is 1 6(p + 1)p(p −1). Furthermore, given such a triple of points, there is a unique binary cubic form, up to scaling, having this triple of points as its roots.
sources.match: The counting method of the proof; the five formulas of the lemma are those stated in the node.

nodes.title: Lemma 18: the p-adic densities of the sets U_p(σ)
nodes.statement: U_p(111) = T_p(111), U_p(12) = T_p(12), U_p(3) = T_p(3); and μ_p(U_p(1²1)) = (p − 1)²(p + 1)/p⁴, μ_p(U_p(1³)) = (p − 1)²(p + 1)/p⁵. Equivalently, a proportion (p − 1)/p of the forms in T_p(1²1) and in T_p(1³) lie in U_p.
hypotheses: p prime; U_p is the Davenport-Heilbronn set of ST.1 (R(f) maximal at p iff f ∈ U_p)
proofSteps: For σ ∈ {(111), (12), (3)} the discriminant is prime to p (f mod p is squarefree), so R(f) is maximal at p (an overring of index divisible by p would force p² | Disc); hence U_p(σ) = T_p(σ).

For σ ∈ {(1²1), (1³)} move the unique multiple zero of f mod p to (1 : 0) by an element of GL₂(Z); then a ≡ b ≡ 0 (mod p), and by the criterion of ST.1 the form fails to be maximal exactly when additionally a ≡ 0 (mod p²).

Among the forms of T_p(σ) put in this position, the condition a ≡ 0 (mod p²) cuts out a proportion 1/p (a mod p² is uniformly distributed among the p residues ≡ 0 mod p), and the normalisation is GL₂(Z)-equivariant, so μ_p(U_p(σ)) = ((p − 1)/p) μ_p(T_p(σ)); insert Lemma 17.

sources.locator: Lemma 18 and the paragraph before it, p. 9
sources.excerpt: Of all f ∈Tp(121) or Tp(13) that have been rendered in such a form, a proportion of 1/p actually satisfy the congruence a ≡0 (mod p2) of condition (ii). Thus a proportion of (p −1)/p of forms in Tp(121) and in Tp(13) correspond to cubic rings maximal at p.
sources.match: The proof of the two nontrivial densities, verbatim.

nodes.title: Lemma 19: μ_p(U_p) = (p³ − 1)(p² − 1)/p⁵ and μ_p(V_p) = (p² − 1)²/p⁴
hypotheses: p prime
proofSteps: U_p is the disjoint union of the U_p(σ) over the five symbols (a form ≡ 0 mod p is not in U_p) and V_p is the union over σ ≠ (1³).
Sum the densities of Lemma 18: (p − 1)²(p + 1)[p² + p + 1]/p⁵ = (p² − 1)(p³ − 1)/p⁵, and without the (1³) term (p − 1)²(p + 1)(p² + p)/p⁵ = (p² − 1)²/p⁴.
acceptance: At p = 2: μ₂(U₂) = 21/32 and μ₂(V₂) = 9/16.

sources.excerpt: Using the fact that Up is simply the union of the Up(σ)’s, while Vp is the union of the Up(σ)’s where σ̸ = (13), we obtain from Lemma 18: Lemma 19 We have µ(Up) = (p3 −1)(p2 −1) / p5 µ(Vp) = (p2 −1)2 / p4 .

nodes.title: Maximal cubic domains are the rings of integers of cubic fields; the orbits in ∩_p U_p count cubic fields
nodes.statement: Let f be an irreducible integral binary cubic form, so that R(f) is an order in the cubic field K = R(f) ⊗ Q (ArithmeticStatistics:ST.1/delone-faddeev-parametrization-of-cubic-rings). (a) R(f) is maximal (contained in no strictly larger cubic ring inside K) iff R(f) = O_K, iff R(f) is maximal at every prime p, iff f ∈ U := ∩_p U_p. (b) The map f ↦ R(f) ⊗ Q induces a bijection between GL₂(Z)-orbits of irreducible forms in U and Q-isomorphism classes of cubic fields, with Disc(f) = Disc(R(f)) = Disc(K); hence for every interval, N(U ∩ V_Z^{(i)}; X) (the number of irreducible GL₂(Z)-orbits in U with 0 < (−1)^i Disc < X) equals N₃(⊤; 0, X) for i = 0 and N₃(⊤; −X, 0) for i = 1. (c) For f ∈ U, p is totally ramified in K iff f ∈ T_p(1³); hence the irreducible orbits in V := ∩_p V_p correspond to the cubic fields in which no prime is totally ramified.
hypotheses: f irreducible over Q (equivalently R(f) is a domain, ST.1)
V_Z^{(0)} and V_Z^{(1)} are the forms of positive and negative discriminant
proofSteps: Every element of an order R ⊆ K is integral over Z (R is a finitely generated Z-module), so R ⊆ O_K; O_K is itself a cubic ring (free of rank 3), so a maximal order equals O_K, and conversely O_K is contained in no larger order.

R ⊆ O_K has finite index, and R = O_K iff no prime p divides [O_K : R], iff R ⊗ Z_p = O_K ⊗ Z_p for all p, i.e. R is maximal at every p; by the Davenport-Heilbronn criterion of ST.1 this holds iff f ∈ U_p for all p.

By Delone-Faddeev (ST.1), GL₂(Z)-orbits of forms correspond to isomorphism classes of cubic rings with Disc(f) = Disc(R(f)); restricting to orbits with R(f) ≅ O_K for a cubic field K gives a bijection with isomorphism classes of cubic fields (K ≅ K' iff O_K ≅ O_{K'}), and Disc(O_K) = NumberField.discr K.
Part (c) is ArithmeticStatistics:ST.3/splitting-symbol-determines-the-reduction-mod-p applied to f ∈ U_p.
acceptance: The form x³ − x y² − y³ lies in U (its discriminant −23 is squarefree) and corresponds to the cubic field of discriminant −23.
The form 4x³ + y³ lies in W₂ (a ≡ 0 mod 4, b ≡ 0 mod 2): R(f) = Z[∛4], of index 2 in O_{Q(∛2)} = Z[∛2], with Disc −432 = 2²·(−108); its orbit is not counted by N(U; X).
The irreducible orbits in U with |Disc| < 50 are exactly four, of discriminants −23, −31, −44 and 49, matching the four cubic fields with |Disc| < 50.

sources.excerpt: Now a cubic ring R is maximal if and only if the cubic Zp-algebra Rp = R ⊗Zp is maximal for every p (this is because R is a maximal ring if and only if it is isomorphic to a product of rings of integers in number ﬁelds).
sources.match: Parts (a) and (b); the domain case is the ring of integers of the cubic field.

sources.excerpt: Let U = ∩pUp. Then U is the set of v ∈VZ corresponding to maximal cubic rings R.
sources.match: The identification of U used in the proof of Theorem 1.

nodes.title: The Davenport-Heilbronn theorem: N₃(0, X) ~ X/(12ζ(3)) and N₃(−X, 0) ~ X/(4ζ(3))
nodes.statement: Let N₃(ξ, η) = N₃(⊤; ξ, η) be the number of cubic fields K up to isomorphism with ξ < Disc(K) < η (ArithmeticStatistics:ST.3/number-field-counting-function, n = 3, no Galois-group restriction: cyclic cubic fields are included). Then N₃(0, X) = X/(12ζ(3)) + o(X) and N₃(−X, 0) = X/(4ζ(3)) + o(X) as X → ∞. More precisely, for i ∈ {0, 1} with n₀ = 6 = #Aut_R(R³) and n₁ = 2 = #Aut_R(R ⊕ C), lim_{X→∞} N(U ∩ V_Z^{(i)}; X)/X = (π²/(12 n_i)) ∏_p (1 − p^{−2})(1 − p^{−3}) = 1/(2 n_i ζ(3)). The same method gives, for any finite set of primes and prescribed splitting types at them, the count multiplied by the product of the corresponding relative local densities (the finite-condition case of ArithmeticStatistics:ST.3/density-of-cubic-orders-with-local-specifications).
hypotheses: The count is by isomorphism classes of fields, ordered by the signed discriminant; the total is N₃(X) ~ X/(3ζ(3))
Cyclic cubic fields are included but number O(X^{1/2}) (every ramified prime is totally ramified, so Disc = f² with f the conductor), so the same asymptotic holds for S₃-cubic fields
The error term is only o(X); power savings are in the second-order node ArithmeticStatistics:ST.3/roberts-second-order-term-for-cubic-fields
proofSteps: By ArithmeticStatistics:ST.3/maximal-irreducible-cubic-rings-are-rings-of-integers-of-cubic-fields, N₃(0, X) = N(U ∩ V_Z^{(0)}; X) and N₃(−X, 0) = N(U ∩ V_Z^{(1)}; X), where N(S; X) counts irreducible GL₂(Z)-orbits in S with |Disc| < X and U = ∩_p U_p.

Upper bound: for every Y, ∩_{p<Y} U_p is defined by congruence conditions modulo ∏_{p<Y} p², so the congruence-condition count of binary cubic forms (BST Theorem 26, supplied by ArithmeticStatistics:ST.2) gives lim_{X} N(∩_{p<Y} U_p ∩ V_Z^{(i)}; X)/X = (π²/(12 n_i)) ∏_{p<Y} μ_p(U_p); since U ⊆ ∩_{p<Y} U_p, limsup_X N(U ∩ V_Z^{(i)}; X)/X ≤ (π²/(12 n_i)) ∏_{p<Y} (1 − p^{−2})(1 − p^{−3}) (ArithmeticStatistics:ST.3/densities-of-maximal-and-nowhere-totally-ramified-forms); let Y → ∞.

Lower bound: ∩_{p<Y} U_p ⊆ U ∪ ∪_{p≥Y} W_p with W_p = V_Z \ U_p, so N(U ∩ V_Z^{(i)}; X) ≥ N(∩_{p<Y} U_p ∩ V_Z^{(i)}; X) − Σ_{p≥Y} N(W_p; X); the uniformity estimate N(W_p; X) = O(X/p²) with a constant independent of p (BST Proposition 29, nonmaximal part, supplied by ArithmeticStatistics:ST.2) bounds the tail by O(X Σ_{p≥Y} p^{−2}) = O(X/Y). Hence liminf ≥ (π²/(12 n_i)) ∏_{p<Y} (1 − p^{−2})(1 − p^{−3}) − O(1/Y); let Y → ∞.

Evaluate the constant: ∏_p (1 − p^{−2}) = 1/ζ(2) = 6/π² and ∏_p (1 − p^{−3}) = 1/ζ(3) (Euler product, riemannZeta_eulerProduct_tprod; ζ(2) = π²/6, riemannZeta_two), so (π²/(12 n_i)) · (6/π²)/ζ(3) = 1/(2 n_i ζ(3)); with n₀ = 6, n₁ = 2 this is 1/(12ζ(3)) and 1/(4ζ(3)). The values n₀, n₁ are the orders of the GL₂(R)-stabilizers of forms of positive and negative discriminant (Aut_R(R³) = S₃ and Aut_R(R ⊕ C) = Z/2), supplied with the count of ST.2.
acceptance: Ratio: asymptotically three times as many complex cubic fields as totally real ones (n₀/n₁ = 3).
The count is by fields, not orders: the order count of BST Theorem 6 has the larger constants π²/72 and π²/24; the ratio (π²/(12 n_i))/(1/(2n_i ζ(3))) = ζ(2)ζ(3) = ∏_p μ_p(U_p)^{−1}.

nodes.title: A cubic field is nowhere totally ramified iff its Galois closure is unramified over the quadratic resolvent field; then Disc(K₃) = Disc(K₂)
nodes.statement: Let K₃ be a cubic field. (a) If K₃ is nowhere totally ramified (no prime p has p O_{K₃} = 𝔭³), then K₃ is not Galois (an S₃-cubic field). (b) For an S₃-cubic field K₃ with Galois closure K₆ and quadratic resolvent K₂ ⊆ K₆ (the fixed field of A₃ = Gal(K₆/K₂); K₂ = Q(√Disc(K₃))), the extension K₆/K₂ is unramified at all finite primes iff K₃ is nowhere totally ramified, and in that case Disc(K₃) = Disc(K₂). (c) Conversely, if K₂ is a quadratic field and L/K₂ is an unramified cyclic cubic extension that is Galois over Q with Gal(L/Q) ≅ S₃, then each of the three conjugate cubic subfields of L is nowhere totally ramified and has discriminant Disc(K₂). (The archimedean places impose no condition: a cubic extension is unramified at infinity.)
hypotheses: 'Unramified' is at finite primes; the degree 3 of K₆/K₂ is odd, so infinite places are automatically unramified
K₂ is Q(√Disc(K₃)): √Disc(K₃) generates the fixed field of A₃ in K₆
Disc(K₃) ∈ Disc(K₂)·(Q^×)² always; equality needs the nowhere-totally-ramified hypothesis
proofSteps: (a) A cyclic cubic field has Disc = f² with f its conductor and every ramified prime totally ramified (inertia groups are subgroups of Z/3Z); a field with no ramified prime would be an unramified extension of Q, which does not exist (Minkowski, |Disc| > 1: NumberField.abs_discr_gt_two); so a nowhere totally ramified cubic field is S₃.

(b) For a prime 𝔓 of K₆ over p with inertia group I ≤ S₃ acting on the three embeddings of K₃: the ramification indices of the primes of K₃ above p are the orbit lengths of I on {1, 2, 3} (Galois correspondence for inertia groups; NumberFieldArithmetic Layer 6 and LocalFieldsRamification Layer 3). p is totally ramified in K₃ iff I acts transitively iff 3 divides #I iff I ∩ A₃ ≠ 1 iff 𝔓 ∩ K₂ ramifies in K₆/K₂ (the inertia group of K₆/K₂ at 𝔓 is I ∩ A₃).

Discriminant equality: at a prime p not totally ramified in K₃, K₃ ⊗ Q_p is either unramified (both discriminants prime to p; in the case (12) p is inert in K₂ but unramified) or Q_p × F with F/Q_p a ramified quadratic extension, and then K₂ ⊗ Q_p ≅ F (the discriminant algebra of Q_p × F is F), so v_p(Disc K₃) = v_p(disc F) = v_p(Disc K₂); the signs agree because Disc(K₃)/Disc(K₂) is a square. Hence Disc(K₃) = Disc(K₂).
(c) The three cubic subfields of L are the fixed fields of the three transpositions; they are conjugate, and by (b) applied to L = K₆ they are nowhere totally ramified with discriminant Disc(K₂).
acceptance: For K₃ the field of x³ − x − 1 (Disc −23): K₂ = Q(√−23), and K₆ is the Hilbert class field of Q(√−23) (class number 3); 23 is partially ramified in K₃.
The cyclic cubic field of discriminant 49 is totally ramified at 7 and is excluded, consistent with (a).
Q(∛2) (Disc −108 = −2²·3³) is totally ramified at 2 and 3, K₂ = Q(√−3) with Disc −3 ≠ −108.

sources.excerpt: Then one checks that the Galois cubic extension K6/K2 is unramiﬁed precisely when the cubic ﬁeld K3 is nowhere totally ramiﬁed. Conversely, if K2 is a quadratic ﬁeld, and K6 is any unramiﬁed cubic extension of K2, then as an extension of the base ﬁeld Q, the ﬁeld K6 is Galois with Galois group S3
sources.match: Parts (b) and (c); the source says 'one checks', and the proof steps supply the inertia-group argument.

sources.excerpt: Now given a nowhere totally ramiﬁed cubic ﬁeld K3, we have observed earlier that in the Galois closure K6 is contained a quadratic ﬁeld K2 and K6/K2 is unramiﬁed. In addition, the discriminant of K2 is equal to the discriminant of K3.
sources.match: The discriminant equality of (b).

nodes.title: Hasse's correspondence: the nowhere totally ramified cubic fields with resolvent K₂ number (h₃(K₂) − 1)/2
nodes.statement: For every quadratic field K₂, the number of isomorphism classes of cubic fields K₃ that are nowhere totally ramified and whose quadratic resolvent is K₂ (equivalently, by ArithmeticStatistics:ST.3/nowhere-totally-ramified-cubic-fields-and-unramified-cubic-extensions-of-the-resolvent, with Disc(K₃) = Disc(K₂)) equals (h₃(K₂) − 1)/2, where h₃(K₂) = #Cl(K₂)[3]. Consequently, for i ∈ {0, 1}, Σ_{0<(−1)^i Disc(K₂)<X} (h₃(K₂) − 1)/2 = N(V ∩ V_Z^{(i)}; X), the number of irreducible GL₂(Z)-orbits in V = ∩_p V_p with 0 < (−1)^i Disc < X.
hypotheses: The count is of fields up to isomorphism; each such field has three conjugate embeddings, all with the same resolvent
h₃ is the wide class group's 3-torsion (Mathlib ClassGroup); for p = 3 wide and narrow class groups have the same 3-part
The sign condition matches: Disc(K₃) = Disc(K₂), so real quadratic resolvents correspond to totally real cubic fields (positive discriminant)
proofSteps: Class field theory (ClassFieldTheory Layer 13, gal_hilbertClassField_equiv_classGroup): unramified abelian extensions of K₂ inside a fixed algebraic closure correspond to subgroups of Cl(K₂), and unramified cyclic cubic extensions L/K₂ to subgroups of index 3; a finite abelian group A has (#A[3] − 1)/2 subgroups of index 3 (they correspond to the lines of the F₃-vector space Hom(A, Z/3Z), which has #A[3] elements).

Each such L is Galois over Q (its norm subgroup is stable under Gal(K₂/Q), whose generator σ acts on Cl(K₂) by c ↦ c^{−1}, because c·σ(c) is the class of the ideal norm to Q, which is principal), and Gal(L/Q) ≅ Z/3Z ⋊ Z/2Z with σ acting by inversion, i.e. S₃.

By the resolvent lemma, the three cubic subfields of such an L form one isomorphism class of nowhere totally ramified cubic fields with resolvent K₂, and conversely the Galois closure of such a K₃ is such an L; distinct L give non-isomorphic cubic fields (L is the Galois closure). Hence the count is (h₃(K₂) − 1)/2.

Summing over K₂ with 0 < (−1)^i Disc(K₂) < X and using ArithmeticStatistics:ST.3/maximal-irreducible-cubic-rings-are-rings-of-integers-of-cubic-fields (c) (irreducible orbits in V ↔ nowhere totally ramified cubic fields, Disc preserved) gives the displayed identity (BST (59)).
acceptance: K₂ = Q(√−23): h₃ = 3, so exactly one nowhere totally ramified cubic field has discriminant −23 (the field of x³ − x − 1).
K₂ = Q(√−3), Q(i): h₃ = 1, so no cubic field has discriminant −3 or −4.
K₂ = Q(√229) (class number 3): exactly one cubic field of discriminant 229, the totally real field of x³ − 4x + 1.

sources.excerpt: Furthermore, by class ﬁeld theory the number of triplets of cubic ﬁelds K3 corresponding to a given K2 in this way equals (h∗ 3(K2) −1)/2, where h∗ 3(K2) denotes the number of 3-torsion elements in the class group of K2.
sources.match: The count and the summed identity (59); the source cites class field theory without further proof.

sources.excerpt: Let K be an imaginary quadratic ﬁeld. Then surjections from Cl(K) to Z/3Z, by class ﬁeld theory, correspond to unramiﬁed Z/3Z-extensions L of K with an isomorphism Gal(L/K) ≃Z/3Z. Also by class ﬁeld theory, we can show that such an L is necessarily Galois over Q, with Galois group S3.
sources.match: The class-field-theoretic steps (stated for imaginary K there; the argument is the same for real K).

nodes.title: Uniformity for totally ramified primes: the cubic fields with |Disc| < X totally ramified at p number O(X/p²), uniformly in p
nodes.statement: There is an absolute constant C such that for every prime p and every X ≥ 1, the number of cubic fields K (up to isomorphism) with |Disc(K)| < X in which p is totally ramified is at most C X/p². Equivalently N(Y_p ∩ U; X) ≤ C X/p², where U = ∩_q U_q. This is the part of BST Proposition 29 (N(Z_p; X) = O(X/p²)) concerning totally ramified primes, restricted to maximal forms, which is all the sieve for the mean of 3-torsion uses: ∩_{p<Y} V_p ⊆ V ∪ ∪_{q≥Y} W_q ∪ ∪_{p≥Y} (Y_p ∩ U).
hypotheses: The constant is uniform in p; this is what licenses the sieve over infinitely many primes in the proof of the mean of 3-torsion
Only the maximal (field) part of Y_p is bounded here; a form in Y_p that is not maximal at another prime q lies in W_q and is covered by the nonmaximal estimate of ST.2
proofSteps: Cyclic cubic fields: Disc(K) = f² with p | f when p is totally ramified, and a cyclic cubic field is determined by its conductor f up to at most 2^{ω(f)} choices, so there are O(X^{1/2+ε}/p) of them with |Disc| < X; this is O(X/p²) for p² ≤ X, and there are none for p² > X.

S₃-cubic fields: for K with quadratic resolvent K₂ of discriminant D₂, the Galois closure K₆ is a cyclic cubic extension of K₂ on whose group Gal(K₂/Q) acts by inversion, hence K₆ lies in the ring class field of an order O_f of K₂ (ClassFieldTheory Layer 13, ringClassField and gal_ringClassField_equiv_pic), and Disc(K) = D₂ f² with f the conductor; by the inertia argument of the resolvent lemma a prime p ≥ 5 is totally ramified in K iff p | f.

For fixed K₂ and f, the cubic fields with resolvent K₂ and conductor f correspond to some of the index-3 subgroups of Pic(O_f) (quadratic orders and their Picard groups: GlobalNumberFields Layer 11), so there are at most #Pic(O_f)[3]; from the exact sequence 1 → (O_{K₂}/f)^×/((Z/f)^× O_{K₂}^×) → Pic(O_f) → Cl(K₂) → 1, whose kernel has 3-rank at most ω(f) + 2, #Pic(O_f)[3] ≤ 3^{ω(f)+2} h₃(K₂).

Σ_{0<|D₂|<Y} h₃(K₂) = O(Y): by ArithmeticStatistics:ST.3/three-torsion-of-quadratic-class-groups-counts-cubic-fields, Σ (h₃(K₂) − 1)/2 counts nowhere totally ramified cubic fields with |Disc| < Y, which is at most the number M₃(Y) = O(Y) of orders in cubic fields (BST Theorem 6, from ST.2), and the number of K₂ is O(Y).

Summing over f divisible by p and K₂ with |D₂| < X/f²: the count is O(X Σ_{p|f} 3^{ω(f)} f^{−2}) ≤ O(3X p^{−2} Σ_{g≥1} 3^{ω(g)} g^{−2}) = O(X/p²), the series converging. The primes p = 2, 3 are covered by the trivial bound N₃(X) = O(X) with a fixed constant.
acceptance: Summed over p ≥ Y the bound is O(X/Y), the tail estimate used in the sieve for V = ∩_p V_p.
For p = 5 the fields counted include Q(∛5) (Disc −675 = −3³·5², O = Z[∛5]) in which 5 is totally ramified.
The bound is sharp in order: by the congruence count of ST.2 and Lemma 18, a proportion μ_p(U_p(1³))/μ_p(U_p) ≍ p^{−2} of cubic fields is totally ramified at p.

sources.locator: Section 8.2, Proposition 29 and the last sentence of its proof, pp. 23-24
sources.excerpt: Proposition 29 N(Zp; X) = O(X/p2), where the implied constant is independent of p. ... Finally, that N(Yp; X) = O(X/p2) follows easily from class ﬁeld theory. A nice, short exposition of this may be found in, e.g., [13, p. 15].
sources.match: The statement for Y_p; the source gives no proof and cites Datskovsky-Wright [13], which is not public. The proof steps reconstruct the standard ring-class-field argument for the maximal part, which is recorded as a gap.

nodes.title: Squarefree integers in each nonzero residue class modulo 4 have density 2/π²
nodes.statement: For a ∈ {1, 2, 3} and x ≥ 1, #{1 ≤ n ≤ x : n squarefree, n ≡ a (mod 4)} = (2/π²) x + O(√x), with an absolute implied constant.
hypotheses: The residue class a = 0 contains no squarefree integers
The error O(√x) is not optimised
proofSteps: Squarefree detection: for n ≥ 1, write n = b² m with m squarefree (Nat.sq_mul_squarefree_of_pos); then d² | n iff d | b, so Σ_{d² | n} μ(d) = Σ_{d | b} μ(d) = [b = 1] = [n squarefree] (ArithmeticFunction.coe_zeta_mul_coe_moebius).

For odd a: an n ≡ a (mod 4) is odd, so only odd d contribute, and #{n ≤ x : n ≡ a (4), d² | n} = x/(4d²) + O(1) for odd d (CRT, d² and 4 coprime). Summing over odd d ≤ √x: (x/4) Σ_{d odd} μ(d)/d² + O(√x) + O(x Σ_{d>√x} d^{−2}) = (x/4) ∏_{p>2} (1 − p^{−2}) + O(√x).

∏_{p>2} (1 − p^{−2}) = (1/ζ(2))/(1 − 1/4) = (6/π²)(4/3) = 8/π² (ArithmeticFunction.LSeries_zeta_mul_Lseries_moebius and ArithmeticFunction.LSeries_zeta_eq_riemannZeta at s = 2, riemannZeta_two, and the Euler factor at 2), so the count is (2/π²) x + O(√x).
For a = 2: n = 2m with m ≤ x/2 odd squarefree; the odd squarefree m ≤ y number (4/π²) y + O(√y) (sum of the two odd classes), giving (2/π²) x + O(√x).
acceptance: Sum over a = 1, 2, 3: (6/π²) x + O(√x), the classical density of squarefree integers.
Numerical check: there are 608 squarefree n ≤ 1000 (200, 204 and 204 in the classes 1, 2 and 3 mod 4), and 6000/π² ≈ 607.9, 2000/π² ≈ 202.6.

nodes.title: The number of quadratic fields with 0 < ±Disc < X is 3X/π² + O(√X)
nodes.statement: N₂(⊤; 0, X) = (3/π²) X + O(√X) and N₂(⊤; −X, 0) = (3/π²) X + O(√X). Equivalently, the number of fundamental discriminants D ≠ 1 (Int.IsFundamentalDiscr) with 0 < D < X, respectively −X < D < 0, is (3/π²) X + O(√X).
hypotheses: Quadratic fields are counted up to isomorphism (each has one subfield of Q̄ and #Aut = 2); the weighted count of BSW is half of this
D = 1 (the discriminant of Q) is excluded
proofSteps: Quadratic fields up to isomorphism correspond bijectively to fundamental discriminants D ≠ 1 via K ↦ Disc(K): every quadratic field is Q(√d) with d ≠ 1 squarefree, Disc(Q(√d)) = d if d ≡ 1 (mod 4) and 4d otherwise (Tau Ceti NumberField.discr_eq_of_squarefree_of_mod_four_eq_one and NumberField.discr_eq_four_mul_of_mod_four_ne_one), these values are exactly the fundamental discriminants ≠ 1 (Int.isFundamentalDiscr_iff_squarefree), and Q(√d) ≅ Q(√d') iff d = d' for squarefree d, d'.

Count positive fundamental discriminants: D = n ≡ 1 (mod 4) squarefree, n < X (n ≠ 1): (2/π²) X + O(√X); D = 4m with m ≡ 2, 3 (mod 4) squarefree, m < X/4: (4/π²)(X/4) + O(√X). Total (3/π²) X + O(√X) (ArithmeticStatistics:ST.3/squarefree-integers-in-residue-classes-modulo-four).
Negative: D = −n with n ≡ 3 (mod 4) squarefree, n < X: (2/π²) X; D = −4m with m ≡ 1, 2 (mod 4) squarefree (so −m ≡ 3, 2), m < X/4: (4/π²)(X/4). Total (3/π²) X + O(√X).
acceptance: Small values: the negative fundamental discriminants in (−25, 0) are −3, −4, −7, −8, −11, −15, −19, −20, −23, −24, i.e. N₂(⊤; −25, 0) = 10, against 3·25/π² ≈ 7.6.
Both signs together: (6/π²) X, agreeing with Wood's Tauberian count N_{S₂}(X) ~ (6/π²) X.
This is the denominator of the Davenport-Heilbronn mean of 3-torsion; it is 3/π², not 6/π², per sign (sourceIssue ArithmeticStatistics/E402).

nodes.title: The Davenport-Heilbronn theorem on 3-torsion: the mean of #Cl(K)[3] is 4/3 over real and 2 over imaginary quadratic fields
nodes.statement: Σ_{0<Disc(K)<X} h₃(K) = (4/3) Σ_{0<Disc(K)<X} 1 + o(X) and Σ_{−X<Disc(K)<0} h₃(K) = 2 Σ_{−X<Disc(K)<0} 1 + o(X), the sums over quadratic fields K up to isomorphism ordered by discriminant, h₃(K) = #Cl(K)[3]. Equivalently lim_{X→∞} (Σ_{0<±Disc(K)<X} h₃(K)) / N₂(⊤; 0 < ±Disc < X) = 4/3 (real) and 2 (imaginary).
hypotheses: Quadratic fields are ordered by |Disc| and weighted equally; the averages are over all quadratic fields of the given sign
The proof sieves to V = ∩_p V_p, defined by infinitely many congruence conditions, and needs the uniform tail bound for Z_p = W_p ⊔ Y_p
No Cohen-Lenstra hypothesis is used; the theorem is the case p = 3, α = 1 of the moment prediction ArithmeticStatistics:ST.3/cohen-lenstra-moment-prediction, which it confirms
proofSteps: By ArithmeticStatistics:ST.3/three-torsion-of-quadratic-class-groups-counts-cubic-fields, Σ_{0<(−1)^i Disc(K)<X} (h₃(K) − 1)/2 = N(V ∩ V_Z^{(i)}; X).

The sieve of the proof of ArithmeticStatistics:ST.3/davenport-heilbronn-count-of-cubic-fields with V_p in place of U_p: the upper bound from the congruence count over ∩_{p<Y} V_p (ST.2) and μ_p(V_p) = (1 − p^{−2})² (ArithmeticStatistics:ST.3/densities-of-maximal-and-nowhere-totally-ramified-forms); the lower bound from ∩_{p<Y} V_p ⊆ V ∪ ∪_{p≥Y} (W_p ∪ Y_p), the nonmaximal bound N(W_p; X) = O(X/p²) (ST.2) and ArithmeticStatistics:ST.3/cubic-fields-totally-ramified-at-large-primes-are-sparse. Hence lim N(V ∩ V_Z^{(i)}; X)/X = (π²/(12 n_i)) ∏_p (1 − p^{−2})² = (π²/(12 n_i))(36/π⁴) = 3/(n_i π²).
By ArithmeticStatistics:ST.3/count-of-quadratic-fields, Σ_{0<±Disc<X} 1 ~ 3X/π².
Therefore the mean of h₃ is 1 + 2 · (3/(n_i π²))/(3/π²) = 1 + 2/n_i: 1 + 2/6 = 4/3 for i = 0 (positive discriminant, real quadratic) and 1 + 2/2 = 2 for i = 1 (imaginary).
acceptance: Imaginary: mean h₃ = 2, i.e. the mean number of surjections Cl(K) → Z/3Z (which is h₃ − 1) is 1; real: mean 4/3, i.e. 1/3 surjections on average — the Cohen-Lenstra predictions |A|^0 and |A|^{−1} for A = Z/3Z.
Small-range sanity check (not a test of the limit): among the 10 imaginary quadratic fields with |Disc| < 25 only Q(√−23) has h₃ = 3, giving an average 6/5.
The sieve cannot be run with a pointwise density at each prime alone: without the uniform bound for Y_p (totally ramified primes, via class field theory) only the upper bound follows.

nodes.title: Local specifications Σ = (Σ_p) ∪ Σ_∞ for cubic orders, acceptable and strongly acceptable collections, and local masses
nodes.statement: A local specification for cubic orders is a collection Σ = (Σ_p)_p ∪ Σ_∞ where, for each prime p, Σ_p is a set of isomorphism classes of nondegenerate cubic rings over Z_p (orders in étale cubic Q_p-algebras; by Delone-Faddeev over Z_p, equivalently a GL₂(Z_p)-invariant set of binary cubic forms over Z_p of nonzero discriminant), and Σ_∞ ⊆ {R³, R ⊕ C}. An order R in a cubic field is a Σ-order if R ⊗ Z_p ∈ Σ_p for all p and R ⊗ R ∈ Σ_∞. Σ is acceptable if for all sufficiently large p, Σ_p contains every maximal cubic Z_p-order that is not totally ramified; it is strongly acceptable if for all sufficiently large p, Σ_p is one of: all nondegenerate cubic Z_p-orders, all maximal ones, or all maximal ones not totally ramified. The local mass of Σ_p is m_p(Σ_p) := Σ_{R ∈ Σ_p} 1/(Disc_p(R) · #Aut(R)), where Disc_p(R) = p^{v_p(Disc R)}; the archimedean mass is m_∞(Σ_∞) := Σ_{R ∈ Σ_∞} 1/#Aut(R) with #Aut(R³) = 6 and #Aut(R ⊕ C) = 2.
hypotheses: Isomorphism classes over Z_p, not over Q_p: several orders can lie in the same étale algebra
Nondegenerate means nonzero discriminant; degenerate rings never occur as R ⊗ Z_p for an order R in a cubic field
The infinite sum m_p over all nondegenerate orders converges (BST (57))
proofSteps: Represent Σ_p as a GL₂(Z_p)-invariant subset of V_{Z_p} of forms of nonzero discriminant (Delone-Faddeev over Z_p, ST.1) and Σ_∞ as a subset of the two real orbits; the predicates are statements about all but finitely many p.

The three standard specifications: 'all orders' (Σ_p = everything, Σ_∞ = both), 'maximal' (Σ_p = the image of U_p, i.e. forms in U_p ⊗ Z_p) and 'maximal and not totally ramified' (Σ_p = the image of V_p); each is strongly acceptable, and strongly acceptable implies acceptable.
acceptance: The maximal specification recovers Theorem 1 and the nowhere-totally-ramified one Theorem 2 in the density theorem.
m_p(all maximal) = 1 + 1/p + 1/p² (BST (58)) and m_p(all nondegenerate) = (1 − 1/p)^{−1}(1 − 1/p²)^{−1} (BST (57)).
A specification with Σ_p = {totally ramified maximal orders} for infinitely many p is not acceptable.

nodes.title: Lemma 32: the p-adic density of the forms whose ring lies in Σ_p is #GL₂(F_p)/p⁴ · Σ_{R ∈ Σ_p} 1/(Disc_p(R) #Aut(R))
nodes.statement: For a prime p and a set Σ_p of isomorphism classes of nondegenerate cubic rings over Z_p, the set S_p(Σ_p) := {x ∈ V_{Z_p} : R(x) ∈ Σ_p} has Haar measure μ_p(S_p(Σ_p)) = (#GL₂(F_p)/p⁴) Σ_{R ∈ Σ_p} 1/(Disc_p(R) · #Aut_{Z_p}(R)) = (1 − p^{−2})(1 − p^{−1}) m_p(Σ_p), with μ_p normalised to give V_{Z_p} measure 1.
hypotheses: p prime; Σ_p consists of nondegenerate rings (each GL₂(Z_p)-orbit then has positive measure)
Aut is the automorphism group of R as a Z_p-algebra, equal to the GL₂(Z_p)-stabilizer of a corresponding form (Delone-Faddeev over Z_p, ST.1)
proofSteps: By Delone-Faddeev over Z_p, S_p(Σ_p) is the disjoint union over R ∈ Σ_p of the GL₂(Z_p)-orbits GL₂(Z_p)·v_R, with Stab(v_R) ≅ Aut(R).

|Disc(x)|_p^{−1} dx is a GL₂(Q_p)-invariant measure on V_{Z_p}; with Haar measure dg on GL₂(Z_p) normalised to total mass #GL₂(F_p), the orbit map g ↦ g·v_R is #Aut(R)-to-1 and the Jacobian identity ∫_{GL₂(Z_p)·v_R} dx = c · |Disc(v_R)|_p · #GL₂(F_p)/#Aut(R) holds with c = p^{−4} independent of v_R (a Jacobian computation with an indeterminate v_R). This p-adic change of variables is requested from AnalyticNumberTheory:AN.8.
Sum over R ∈ Σ_p; #GL₂(F_p) = (p² − 1)(p² − p) (Matrix.card_GL_field).
acceptance: Σ_p = all maximal orders: (p² − 1)(p² − p)p^{−4}(1 + 1/p + 1/p²) = (p³ − 1)(p² − 1)/p⁵ = μ_p(U_p), agreeing with Lemma 19.
Σ_p = all nondegenerate orders: the density is 1, which gives BST (57).
Σ_p = {Z_p³}: #Aut = 6, Disc_p = 1, density (p² − 1)(p² − p)/(6p⁴) = μ_p(T_p(111)) (Lemma 17).

nodes.title: BST Theorem 8: the number of Σ-orders of bounded discriminant for an acceptable Σ
nodes.statement: Let Σ = (Σ_p) ∪ Σ_∞ be an acceptable collection of local specifications (ArithmeticStatistics:ST.3/acceptable-local-specifications-for-cubic-orders) and N₃(Σ; X) the number of isomorphism classes of orders R in cubic fields with R ⊗ Z_p ∈ Σ_p for all p, R ⊗ R ∈ Σ_∞ and |Disc(R)| < X. Then N₃(Σ; X) = (1/2)(Σ_{R∈Σ_∞} 1/#Aut(R)) · ∏_p ((p − 1)/p · Σ_{R∈Σ_p} 1/(Disc_p(R) #Aut(R))) · X + o(X). Equivalently (BST Theorem 31), for S(Σ, i) the irreducible forms of V_Z^{(i)} whose ring is a Σ-order, lim_X N(S(Σ, i); X)/X = (1/(2 n_i)) ∏_p (p − 1)/p · m_p(Σ_p).
hypotheses: Σ must be acceptable; the condition at p is on R ⊗ Z_p (the printed Theorem 8 says R ⊗ Q_p, a misprint: sourceIssue ArithmeticStatistics/E406)
The count is of orders, not fields; fields are the case Σ_p = maximal for all p
The Euler product converges because Σ is acceptable (the p-factor is 1 + O(p^{−2}) for large p)
proofSteps: For each Y, ∩_{p<Y} S_p(Σ_p) is defined by finitely many congruence conditions (each Σ_p-condition is determined modulo a power of p because orbits of nondegenerate forms are open), so the congruence-condition count of ST.2 (BST Theorem 26) gives the limit (π²/(12 n_i)) ∏_{p<Y} μ_p(S_p(Σ_p)) for the forms satisfying the conditions at p < Y.

Acceptability: for p ≥ Y (Y large) the forms violating Σ_p lie in Z_p = W_p ⊔ Y_p, whose count is O(X/p²) uniformly (BST Proposition 29: W_p from ST.2; the maximal part of Y_p from ArithmeticStatistics:ST.3/cubic-fields-totally-ramified-at-large-primes-are-sparse; the remaining non-maximal part of Y_p from the uniform tail estimates of ST.2), so the sieve of the proof of Theorem 1 applies verbatim.
Sum over i ∈ Σ_∞ with 1/n_i = 1/#Aut(R) for R = R³ (i = 0) or R ⊕ C (i = 1).
acceptance: Σ_p = all nondegenerate orders: (1/(2n_i)) ∏_p (1 − p^{−2})^{−1} = ζ(2)/(2 n_i) = π²/(12 n_i), i.e. π²/72 and π²/24 (BST Theorem 6 main term).
Σ_p = maximal not totally ramified: (1/(2n_i)) ∏_p (1 − 1/p)(1 + 1/p) = 3/(n_i π²), the count used for Theorem 2.

nodes.title: BST Theorem 3 (Roberts' conjecture): the second main term in the count of cubic fields
hypotheses: The second main term has order X^{5/6}; the error O_ε(X^{5/6−1/48+ε}) is a power saving over it

The proof (BST Sections 6, 7 and 9: slicing and smoothing in the cusp, second-order p-adic densities, and a refined sieve over three ranges of n) is not decomposed in this packet; see the gap on second-order terms
proofSteps: Count forms in dyadic ranges of the discriminant with the second-order count of binary cubic forms satisfying finitely many congruence conditions (BST Theorem 27, the congruence version of the Davenport-Shintani count; uniform lattice counts of ST.2).
Compute the second-order p-adic densities μ₂(σ, p), μ₂(p), μ₂'(p) (BST Section 7) and the second-order local masses (BST Lemma 37).

Sieve with the Möbius identities (61)-(62) over squarefree n, splitting n into three ranges: Theorem 27 with the identities of BST Proposition 33 for small n, the uniformity estimates of Belabas-Bhargava-Pomerance for large n, and an equidistribution argument (BST Section 9.4) for n near X^{1/6}.

nodes.title: Mertens: the number of SL₂(Z)-classes of positive definite binary quadratic forms with 0 < −D < X is (π/18) X^{3/2} + O(X log X)
nodes.statement: For D < 0 let h⁺(D) be the number of SL₂(Z)-equivalence classes of positive definite integral binary quadratic forms a x² + b x y + c y² (a > 0) of discriminant b² − 4ac = D, all forms counted (primitive or not). Then Σ_{−X<D<0} h⁺(D) = (π/18) X^{3/2} + O(X log X).
hypotheses: Positive definite forms only: counting the negative definite classes as well doubles the sum (sourceIssue ArithmeticStatistics/E401 on the printed statement)
Non-primitive forms are included (they are irreducible over Q); the primitive count has constant (π/18)/ζ(3)
Classes, not weighted classes: the forms x² + y² and x² + xy + y² and their multiples are counted with weight 1 (Hurwitz's weights 1/2, 1/3 change only lower-order terms)
proofSteps: Reduction: every positive definite form is SL₂(Z)-equivalent to exactly one reduced form (|b| ≤ a ≤ c, with b ≥ 0 if |b| = a or a = c). Write f = a(x − τy)(x − τ̄y) with τ in the upper half plane; SL₂(Z) acts on τ by Möbius transformations, and f is reduced iff τ lies in the closed fundamental domain ModularGroup.fd with the boundary identified (ModularGroup.exists_smul_mem_fd, ModularGroup.eq_smul_self_of_mem_fdo_mem_fdo). The canonical representatives are those pinned in ModularForms Layer 11.

Counting: h⁺ summed over −X < D < 0 is the number of integer triples (a, b, c) with |b| ≤ a ≤ c, 4ac − b² < X and the boundary convention. Slice by a: a ≤ √(X/3), and for each (a, b) the number of c is (X + b²)/(4a) − a + O(1); summing over |b| ≤ a and a ≤ √(X/3) gives the integral V(X) plus O(X log X) (the O(1) terms contribute O(X), the Riemann-sum error in b and a contributes O(X log X)).

Volume: in coordinates (a, τ = x + iy), b = −2ax, c = a|τ|², the Jacobian is 4a²y and the discriminant condition is 4a²y² < X, so V(X) = ∫_{fd} ∫_0^{√X/(2y)} 4a²y da dx dy = (X^{3/2}/6) ∫_{fd} dx dy / y² = (X^{3/2}/6)(π/3) = (π/18) X^{3/2}, using the hyperbolic area ∫_{−1/2}^{1/2} ∫_{√(1−x²)}^∞ dy dx / y² = 2 arcsin(1/2) = π/3.
acceptance: Numerical check: the number of reduced positive definite forms with 4ac − b² < X is 172131, 5494441, 44054144 for X = 10⁴, 10⁵, 4·10⁵, i.e. 0.17213, 0.17375, 0.17414 times X^{3/2}, against π/18 ≈ 0.17453.
Small values: h⁺(−3) = h⁺(−4) = 1, h⁺(−12) = 2 (x² + 3y² and 2x² + 2xy + 2y²), h⁺(−16) = 2 (x² + 4y² and 2x² + 2y²).
The constant is (1/6) × area(SL₂(Z)\H) = (1/6)(π/3).

nodes.title: Siegel: Σ_{0<D<X} h_D log ε_D ~ (π²/18) X^{3/2} for indefinite binary quadratic forms
nodes.statement: For D > 0 not a square let h_D be the number of SL₂(Z)-equivalence classes of integral binary quadratic forms of discriminant D (all forms, primitive or not), and ε_D = (t + u√D)/2 with (t, u) the smallest positive solution of t² − D u² = 4. Then Σ_{0<D<X, D non-square} h_D log ε_D = (π²/18) X^{3/2} + o(X^{3/2}).
hypotheses: D ranges over positive non-square discriminants D ≡ 0, 1 (mod 4); for D a square the forms are reducible and excluded
The weight log ε_D is the regulator of the order of discriminant D computed with the smallest unit of norm +1; the theorem is about h_D log ε_D, not h_D alone
proofSteps: Geometry of numbers: SL₂(Z) acts on indefinite forms with stabilizer (in SL₂(R)) a copy of SO(1, 1) ≅ R^×, and the stabilizer in SL₂(Z) of a form of discriminant D is infinite cyclic, generated by the automorph attached to ε_D; the fundamental domain for this stabilizer in the real orbit has invariant volume proportional to log ε_D, so the averaged count of BST type over V_R^{indef} counts classes with weight log ε_D.

Alternatively, for fundamental D the primitive part of h_D log ε_D equals √D · Res_{s=1} ζ_{Q(√D)}(s) (Dirichlet's class number formula; in the library NumberField.dedekindZeta_residue with the right-limit theorem NumberField.tendsto_sub_one_mul_dedekindZeta_nhdsGT), and Siegel averages these residues.
No public source read proves this theorem; it is recorded as the gap 'Siegel's indefinite count has no public proof in the sources read'.

D = 5: one class (x² + xy − y²), ε₅ = (3 + √5)/2, log ε₅ ≈ 0.9624.

nodes.title: The quadratic and cubic predecessors (Mertens/Siegel and Davenport), with the imaginary quadratic count corrected
nodes.statement: (Theorem 1.4, Mertens 1874 / Siegel 1944, corrected) With h⁺(D) the number of SL₂(Z)-classes of positive definite integral binary quadratic forms of discriminant D < 0 and h_D the number of SL₂(Z)-classes of integral binary quadratic forms of non-square discriminant D > 0: Σ_{−X<D<0} h⁺(D) ~ (π/18) X^{3/2}, and Σ_{0<D<X} h_D log ε_D ~ (π²/18) X^{3/2}, where ε_D = (t + u√D)/2 with t, u the smallest positive integral solutions of t² − D u² = 4. (Theorem 1.5, Davenport 1951) With h(D) the number of GL₂(Z)-classes of irreducible integral binary cubic forms of discriminant D: Σ_{−X<D<0} h(D) ~ (π²/24) X and Σ_{0<D<X} h(D) ~ (π²/72) X. Via Delone-Faddeev, classes of irreducible integral binary cubic forms correspond to orders in cubic fields, so Theorem 1.5 counts cubic orders by discriminant.
hypotheses: h⁺(D) counts positive definite classes only: the printed h_D ('irreducible forms of discriminant D') would include the negative definite classes and give (π/9) X^{3/2} (sourceIssue ArithmeticStatistics/E401)
h_D log ε_D in the real case is a class-number-times-regulator statement, NOT a class-number statement
The cubic statement is about GL₂(Z)-classes, and irreducibility is required; reducible forms are excluded
The Delone-Faddeev correspondence is with ORDERS in cubic fields (including non-maximal ones), not with cubic fields
proofSteps: Imaginary quadratic part: ArithmeticStatistics:ST.3/mertens-count-of-positive-definite-binary-quadratic-forms, with error O(X log X).
Real quadratic part: ArithmeticStatistics:ST.3/siegel-count-of-indefinite-binary-quadratic-forms (recorded with a gap: no public proof in the sources read).

Cubic part: Davenport's theorem is the main term of BST Theorem 20 / Theorem 5, N(V_Z^{(0)}; X) = (π²/72) X + O(X^{5/6}) and N(V_Z^{(1)}; X) = (π²/24) X + O(X^{5/6}), proved by the averaging method of BST Section 5 and supplied by ArithmeticStatistics:ST.2 (uniform arithmetic lattice/orbit counts); the order interpretation is Delone-Faddeev (ArithmeticStatistics:ST.1/delone-faddeev-parametrization-of-cubic-rings) with irreducible forms ↔ domains (BST Proposition 11).

These are the exact low-degree cases with which ST.3's field counts must agree: sieving Davenport's order count to maximal orders gives the Davenport-Heilbronn theorem, and the ratio of the constants is ζ(2)ζ(3).
acceptance: Consistency check: Theorem 1.6 (quartic) has main term of order X^{5/6} in the height, while Theorems 1.4 and 1.5 have X^{3/2} and X in the discriminant; the orderings are by different invariants and must not be compared directly.
Weight check: the quadratic count is by SL₂(Z)-classes, the cubic and quartic counts by GL₂(Z)-classes; the group must be recorded.
Regulator check: in the real quadratic case the sum is weighted by log ε_D, and no unweighted asymptotic for h_D alone is asserted.
Sign check: numerically, the reduced positive definite forms with 4ac − b² < 4·10⁵ number 0.17414 X^{3/2}, against π/18 ≈ 0.17453; including the negative definite classes would double this.

nodes.title: Bhargava: the mean of #Cl(K)[2] over S₃-cubic fields is 5/4 (totally real) and 3/2 (complex)
nodes.statement: Over S₃-cubic fields K ordered by |Disc(K)|: the average of h₂(K) = #Cl(K)[2] is 5/4 over totally real fields and 3/2 over complex cubic fields; the average of #Cl⁺(K)[2] (narrow class group) is 2 over totally real fields and 3/2 over complex ones. More generally (BSW Theorem 6(b) over a number field F with an acceptable, archimedean-pure Σ): the mean of h₂(L/F) is 1 + 2^{−r₁−2r₂−α₃(Σ)} and of h₂⁺(L/F) is 1 + 2^{−r₁−2r₂+α₃(Σ)}, α₃(Σ) being the number of real places of F at which Σ prescribes R³; for F = Q, r₁ = 1, r₂ = 0 and α₃ = 1 (totally real) or 0 (complex).

nodes.title: Fouvry-Kluners: all moments of 2^{rk₄} of narrow class groups of quadratic fields, and the 4-rank distribution
nodes.statement: Let C_D be the narrow class group of the quadratic field of fundamental discriminant D and rk₄(C_D) = rk₂(C_D²) its 4-rank. For every integer k ≥ 0 and ε > 0, with N(k, 2) the number of F₂-subspaces of F₂^k and R(X, ε, k) = X(log X)^{−2^{−k}+ε}: Σ_{0<−D<X} 2^{k·rk₄(C_D)} = N(k, 2) Σ_{0<−D<X} 1 + O_{ε,k}(R(X, ε, k)) and Σ_{0<D<X} 2^{k·rk₄(C_D)} = 2^{−k}(N(k + 1, 2) − N(k, 2)) Σ_{0<D<X} 1 + O_{ε,k}(R(X, ε, k)) (and the same within each of the classes D ≡ 1 (mod 4), 0 (mod 8), 4 (mod 8)). nodes.title: The Cohen-Lenstra(-Gerth) moment prediction for p-ranks of class groups of quadratic fields, as an explicit conjectural hypothesis
nodes.statement: For a prime p and an integer α ≥ 0, the propositions Conj^−(p, α) and Conj^+(p, α) are: M^−(∏_{0≤i<α} (p^{rk_p(C_D²)} − p^i)) = 1 and M^+(∏_{0≤i<α} (p^{rk_p(C_D²)} − p^i)) = p^{−α}, where C_D is the narrow class group of the quadratic field of discriminant D, C_D² its subgroup of squares, and M^±(f) := lim_{X→∞} (Σ_{0<±D<X} f(D))/(Σ_{0<±D<X} 1) over fundamental discriminants D (the limit is asserted to exist). For odd p, rk_p(C_D²) = rk_p(Cl_D) and p^{rk_p} = h_p (ArithmeticStatistics:ST.3/torsion-count-of-class-groups), so the moment is the average of ∏_{i<α}(h_p(K) − p^i), i.e. of the number of injections (Z/pZ)^α → Cl(K)[p]. These are CONJECTURES: every theorem of this packet that uses one takes it as an explicit hypothesis, and none is assumed.
hypotheses: For odd p this is Cohen-Lenstra's conjecture (C6), (C10); for p = 2 Gerth's modification replaces C_D by C_D² (genus theory fixes rk₂(C_D) = ω(D) − 1)
The mean over fundamental discriminants of one sign ordered by |D|
A proposition with content (a limit statement), never a hypothesis-free axiom

Define the proposition as the statement that this limit equals 1, resp. p^{−α}.

Conj^±(3, 1) is the Davenport-Heilbronn theorem (means 2 and 4/3 of h₃); Conj^±(2, α) for all α is Fouvry-Kluners.
Conj^−(p, 1) says the mean of h_p over imaginary quadratic fields is 2, i.e. the mean number of surjections Cl → Z/pZ is 1.

nodes.title: Malle's invariants ind(g), a(G) and b(k, G) of a transitive permutation group
nodes.statement: Let 1 ≠ G ≤ S_n be transitive on Ω = {1, …, n}. For g ∈ G, ind(g) := n − (number of orbits of ⟨g⟩ on Ω) = Σ over the cycles of g of (length − 1). ind(G) := min{ind(g) : 1 ≠ g ∈ G} and a(G) := ind(G)^{−1}. For a number field k, the absolute Galois group of k acts on the set of conjugacy classes of G through the cyclotomic character: σ sends the class C of g to the class of g^{χ(σ)}, χ(σ) ∈ (Z/eZ)^× the action on e-th roots of unity, e the exponent of G; the orbits are the k-conjugacy classes, and b(k, G) := the number of k-conjugacy classes C with ind(C) = ind(G). Equivalently, with H_k ≤ (Z/eZ)^× the image of Gal(k(ζ_e)/k), b(k, G) is the number of orbits of H_k acting by powering on the conjugacy classes of minimal index.
hypotheses: G ≠ 1 and transitive
ind is a class function, so ind(C) is well defined
b depends on k only through H_k; H_Q = (Z/eZ)^× and H_k = 1 when ζ_e ∈ k
proofSteps: ind(g) = #support(g) − #cycles(g) (cycle type of the permutation).
The powering action of (Z/eZ)^× on conjugacy classes is well defined because g^e = 1, preserves ind (⟨g^u⟩ = ⟨g⟩ for u a unit), and b counts orbits of H_k on the minimal-index classes.
acceptance: S_n (n ≥ 2): transpositions have index 1, so a(S_n) = 1 and b(Q, S_n) = 1.
C₃ ≀ C₂ ≤ S₆: a = 1/2, b(Q, G) = 1 and b(Q(ζ₃), G) = 2 (Kluners).
S₃ ≤ S₆ (regular): a = 1/3, b(Q) = 1.

nodes.title: Malle's conjecture (strong and weak forms), as explicit conjectural hypotheses
nodes.statement: For a number field k and a transitive 1 ≠ G ≤ S_n, let Z(k, G; x) be the number of extensions K/k inside a fixed algebraic closure k̄ of degree n whose Galois group (the normal closure's group acting on the n embeddings over k) is permutation-isomorphic to G, with N_{k/Q}(d_{K/k}) ≤ x. The strong Malle conjecture MalleStrong(k, G) is the proposition: there is c(k, G) > 0 with Z(k, G; x) ~ c(k, G) x^{a(G)} (log x)^{b(k,G)−1} as x → ∞. The weak Malle conjecture MalleWeak(k, G) is: there is c₁ > 0 with Z(k, G; x) ≥ c₁ x^{a(G)} for x large, and for every ε > 0 there is c₂(ε) with Z(k, G; x) ≤ c₂(ε) x^{a(G)+ε}. For k = Q, counting isomorphism classes instead of subfields of Q̄ changes Z by the constant factor n/#Aut(K/Q) (which depends only on G), so the statements are unchanged when Z(Q, G; x) is replaced by N_n(Gal = G; −x, x) of ArithmeticStatistics:ST.3/number-field-counting-function. These are CONJECTURES: MalleStrong is false in general (Kluners), and theorems using either form take it as an explicit hypothesis.
hypotheses: The invariants a(G) and b(k, G) are those of ArithmeticStatistics:ST.3/malle-invariants-of-a-permutation-group
Z counts subfields of k̄, not isomorphism classes; the conversion factor is constant for fixed G
MalleStrong(Q, G) is refuted for G = C₃ ≀ C₂ ≤ S₆; MalleWeak has no known counterexample
proofSteps: Define Z(k, G; x) as a finite count (Hermite's theorem over k) and the two propositions by the displayed asymptotic statements.
Record the known cases as tests: abelian G (Wright), S₃ ≤ S₃ (Davenport-Heilbronn), S₄, S₅ (Bhargava), and the failure for C₃ ≀ C₂.
acceptance: MalleStrong(Q, S₂) holds: N₂(X) ~ (6/π²) X with a(S₂) = 1, b = 1 (ArithmeticStatistics:ST.3/count-of-quadratic-fields).
MalleStrong(Q, S₃) holds by Davenport-Heilbronn (a = 1, b = 1, constant 1/(3ζ(3)) for isomorphism classes).
MalleStrong(Q, C₃ ≀ C₂) fails (ArithmeticStatistics:ST.3/kluners-counterexample-to-malle-conjecture).

nodes.title: Kluners' counterexample: the strong Malle conjecture fails for C₃ ≀ C₂ ≤ S₆ over Q
nodes.statement: For G = C₃ ≀ C₂ = C₃² ⋊ C₂ ≤ S₆ (order 18), a(G) = 1/2 and b(Q, G) = 1, but Z(Q, G; x) ≫ x^{1/2} log x; hence MalleStrong(Q, C₃ ≀ C₂) is false. More precisely Z̃(Q, G; x) ≥ Z(Q(ζ₃), C₃; x/27) ~ c(Q(ζ₃), C₃) x^{1/2} log x, where Z̃ counts towers L/K/Q with Gal(L/K) = C₃, [K : Q] = 2, |d_L| ≤ x, and the C₆ and S₃(6) contributions are O(x^{1/3}).
hypotheses: The failure is caused by the cyclotomic intermediate field K = Q(ζ₃): excluding it restores the predicted order x^{1/2}
The lower bound uses the abelian case of Malle's conjecture (Wright) over K = Q(ζ₃), where b(K, C₃) = 2
proofSteps: Compute a(G) = 1/2 (the elements of order 3 with three fixed points have index 2) and b(Q, G) = 1 (the two classes of such elements are fused by the cyclotomic action over Q), but b(Q(ζ₃), C₃) = 2.

Lower bound: every cyclic cubic extension L/K of K = Q(ζ₃) with Galois group of L/Q equal to G gives a sextic field with |d_L| = d_K³ N(d_{L/K}) = 27 N(d_{L/K}); by Wright's theorem Z(K, C₃; y) ~ c y^{1/2} log y (b(K, C₃) = 2).

The other groups arising from towers, C₆ and S₃(6), contribute O(x^{1/3}) (abelian case; Davenport-Heilbronn and discriminant comparison), so Z(Q, G; x) ≫ x^{1/2} log x, contradicting x^{1/2} (log x)^{0}.
Wright's theorem for abelian groups over number fields is quoted (not decomposed): gap 'Wright's theorem (Malle's conjecture for abelian groups) is quoted'.
acceptance: Kluners also shows Ẑ (towers avoiding Q(ζ₃)) ~ c x^{1/2}, as Malle predicts, using the Davenport-Heilbronn 3-rank averages.
The same mechanism gives counterexamples C_ℓ ≀ C_m for primes ℓ > 2 with gcd(m, ℓ − 1) > 1.

nodes.title: The orbit weights m(f) and m_p(f)
nodes.statement: Let a group G act on a set V, let Γ ≤ G be a subgroup and Y ⊆ V a Γ-stable subset. For v ∈ V put G_{v,Y} := {g ∈ G : g·v ∈ Y}; it is a union of right cosets Γg. The orbit weight of v is w_{Γ,Y}(v) := #(Γ\G_{v,Y}), the number of right cosets Γg contained in G_{v,Y} (a natural number when the coset set is finite; the value 0 marks an infinite set, following Nat.card), and the orbit count is n_{Γ,Y}(v) := #(Γ\(G·v ∩ Y)). For binary quartic forms, with PGL_2 acting through the twisted action γ·f(x,y) = (det γ)^{-2} f((x,y)·γ) of ST.0: the global weight of f ∈ V_Z is m(f) := w_{PGL_2(Z),V_Z}(f) for G = PGL_2(Q) acting on V_Q, and the local weight of f ∈ V_{Z_p} is m_p(f) := w_{PGL_2(Z_p),V_{Z_p}}(f) for G = PGL_2(Q_p) acting on V_{Q_p}; PGL_2(Z) and PGL_2(Z_p) are the images of GL_2(Z) and GL_2(Z_p). Equivalently m(f) = #[PGL_2(Z)\PGL_2(Q)_f] and m_p(f) = #[PGL_2(Z_p)\PGL_2(Q_p)_f] with PGL_2(Q)_f := {γ : γ·f ∈ V_Z}, the description used in the proof of Proposition 3.6.
hypotheses: Y is Γ-stable, so that membership g·v ∈ Y depends only on the right coset Γg.

The action is the twisted action (21)/(32): the centre acts trivially and I, J are invariant. With the untwisted action every scalar would stabilise the invariants only up to a power, and G_{v,Y} would not descend to PGL_2.

The source defines m(f) as the stabilizer sum Σ_{f'∈B(f)} #Aut_Q(f')/#Aut_Z(f'); the coset count is equal to it whenever Aut_Q(f) is finite (lemma orbit-weight-as-a-stabilizer-sum), in particular whenever Δ(f) ≠ 0.
proofSteps: Form G_{v,Y} ⊆ G and its image in the right-coset space Γ\G; w_{Γ,Y}(v) is the cardinality of that image.
Γ-stability of Y gives (γg)·v ∈ Y ⟺ g·v ∈ Y, so G_{v,Y} is a union of right Γ-cosets.
Specialise to (G, Γ, Y) = (PGL_2(Q), PGL_2(Z), V_Z) and (PGL_2(Q_p), PGL_2(Z_p), V_{Z_p}), using the twisted action of ST.0/binary-quartic-form descended to PGL_2 (the scalar matrices act trivially).
acceptance: For v ∈ Y the identity coset lies in Γ\G_{v,Y}, so w_{Γ,Y}(v) ≥ 1 whenever it is finite.
w is G-invariant: w(g·v) = w(v), through the bijection Γh ↦ Γhg^{-1} of coset sets.
For S_3 acting on {0,1,2}, Γ = 1 and Y = {0}: w(0) = 2 while n(0) = 1, so the weight is not the orbit count.
