nodes.title: The weighted sets S(F), S_p(F) and S_∞(F) of locally soluble binary quartic forms
nodes.statement: Let F be a family of elliptic curves over Q defined by congruence conditions (ST.0), with invariant set Inv(F) = {(I(E), J(E)) : E ∈ F} ⊆ Z², local sets Inv_p(F) ⊆ Z_p² and sign set Inv_∞(F) ⊆ R². Define S(F) := {f ∈ V_Z : f is locally soluble and (I(f), J(f)) = (2⁴I, 2⁶J) for some (I, J) ∈ Inv(F)}, each PGL_2(Z)-orbit weighted by 1/m(f); for every prime p, S_p(F) := {f ∈ V_{Z_p} : f is Q_p-soluble, 2⁴ | I(f) and 2⁶ | J(f) in Z_p, and (2^{-4}I(f), 2^{-6}J(f)) ∈ Inv_p(F)}, weighted by 1/m_p(f); and S_∞(F) := {f ∈ V_R : f is R-soluble and (I(f), J(f)) ∈ Inv_∞(F)}. Here a form over a field K is K-soluble when z² = f(x, y) has a solution with x, y, z ∈ K and (x, y) ≠ (0, 0), and locally soluble means R-soluble and Q_p-soluble for every p (ST.1). The set S_p(F) is the local condition set; the source calls S_p(F) the p-adic closure of S(F) and then uses exactly this description (sourceIssue ArithmeticStatistics/E508).
hypotheses: F is presented as F_Σ by closed local sets Σ_p with null boundary (ST.0), so that Inv_p(F) ⊆ Σ_p is closed.
The scaling (2⁴, 2⁶) is forced by Theorem 3.5 (ST.1): Selmer elements of E^{I,J} are classes of integral forms with invariants (2⁴I, 2⁶J), not (I, J).
Because Inv_∞(F) is a union of sign conditions, it is invariant under (I, J) ↦ (λ²I, λ³J) for λ > 0; in particular (2⁴I, 2⁶J) ∈ Inv_∞(F) iff (I, J) ∈ Inv_∞(F).
proofSteps: Define the three sets as subsets of V_Z, V_{Z_p} and V_R through the invariants I, J of ST.0/binary-quartic-invariants and the solubility predicates of ST.1.
Attach the weights 1/m and 1/m_p of rational-orbit-weight.
Record PGL_2(Z)- (resp. PGL_2(Z_p)-, PGL_2(R)-) stability: solubility and the invariants are preserved by the twisted action.
acceptance: x³y − 16xy³ = xy(x − 4y)(x + 4y) has invariants (48, 0) = (2⁴·3, 2⁶·0) and a rational root, so it lies in S(F) for the family of all curves (it is the identity class for E: y² = x³ − x).
−x⁴ − y⁴ is negative definite, hence not R-soluble, hence in no S_∞(F).
x³y − xy³ has I = 3, not divisible by 2⁴, so it lies in no S(F).

nodes.title: The Selmer-weighted local masses M_p(V, F), M_∞(V, F; X) and the archimedean mass M_∞(F; X)
nodes.statement: For (I, J) in a field K ⊇ Q with Δ(I, J) = (4I³ − J²)/27 ≠ 0 let E^{I,J}: y² = x³ − (I/3)x − J/27. For a family F defined by congruence conditions define, with dIdJ the Haar probability measure on Z_p² and the Lebesgue measure on R²: M_p(V, F) := ∫_{Inv_p(F)} #(E^{I,J}(Q_p)/2E^{I,J}(Q_p)) / #E^{I,J}(Q_p)[2] dIdJ; M_∞(F; X) := ∫_{(I,J) ∈ Inv_∞(F), H(I,J) < X} dIdJ; M_∞(V, F; X) := ∫_{(I,J) ∈ Inv_∞(F), H(I,J) < X} #(E^{I,J}(R)/2E^{I,J}(R)) / #E^{I,J}(R)[2] dIdJ. The unweighted local mass M_p(F) = ∫_{Inv_p(F)} dIdJ is the local density of the family at p supplied by ST.0/family-defined-by-local-conditions.
hypotheses: The integrands are finite: E^{I,J}(K)[2] has at most 4 elements, and E(Q_p)/2E(Q_p), E(R)/2E(R) are finite (local-two-descent-index, archimedean-selmer-ratio-is-one-half).
The measure on Z_p² is the Haar probability measure, so M_p(F) ≤ 1; the archimedean measure is Lebesgue measure in the coordinates (I, J), with the height H(I, J) = max{|I|³, J²/4} of ST.0.
The curve E^{I,J} is written in the source's normalisation (Theorem 3.2); for integral (I, J) = (−3A, −27B) it is E_{A,B}.
proofSteps: Define the integrands as functions of (I, J) on {Δ ≠ 0} and integrate over the local invariant sets of ST.0.
Measurability: the integrands are locally constant on {Δ ≠ 0} (they take finitely many values determined by the sign of Δ at ∞, and by local-two-descent-index at p).
acceptance: M_p(V, F) = M_p(F) for odd p and M_2(V, F) = 2M_2(F); M_∞(V, F; X) = M_∞(F; X)/2 (local-selmer-mass-ratios).

nodes.title: Averages of arithmetic functions over a height-ordered family
nodes.statement: Let F be an arithmetic family in the sense of ST.0 (a set with a height h having finite sublevel sets) and φ a real function on F. For X ∈ R let N(F; X) := #{E ∈ F : h(E) < X} and Avg_F(φ; X) := (Σ_{E ∈ F, h(E) < X} φ(E)) / N(F; X) (with value 0 when N(F; X) = 0). φ has average c over F if Avg_F(φ; X) → c as X → ∞; its upper average is limsup_{X→∞} Avg_F(φ; X). For elliptic curves over Q the height is H(E) = max{4|A|³, 27B²} or H'(E) = max{|I(E)|³, J(E)²/4}; since 27H = 4H' (ST.0) the two orderings give the same averages and upper averages. The average size of the 2-Selmer group over F is the average of E ↦ #S_2(E).
hypotheses: The average is a limit of ratios of finite sums; its existence is part of any theorem asserting it.
Upper averages (limsup) are used for statements, such as the rank bound, that assert no limit.
Rescaling the height by a positive constant changes N(F; X) into N(F; cX) and does not change limits or limsups as X → ∞.
proofSteps: Define N(F; X) and the partial sums with the counting API of ST.0/arithmetic-family (strict inequality h < X, as in the source).
Define the average as a filter limit at X → ∞ and the upper average as the limsup.
acceptance: The constant function c has average c over any infinite family.
Over all elliptic curves the indicator of {B = 0} has average 0 (#{A : 4|A|³ < X} ≍ X^{1/3} while N ≍ X^{5/6}).
Changing H to H' leaves every average unchanged.

sources.excerpt: When all elliptic curves E/Q are ordered by height, the average size of the 2-Selmer group S2(E) is 3.

nodes.title: The orbit weight as a sum of stabilizer ratios
nodes.statement: In the setting of rational-orbit-weight let v ∈ Y with Stab_G(v) finite and Γ\(G·v ∩ Y) finite. Then w_{Γ,Y}(v) = Σ_{Γv' ∈ Γ\(G·v ∩ Y)} #Stab_G(v') / #Stab_Γ(v'), and #Stab_G(v') = #Stab_G(v) for every v' ∈ G·v. Consequently n_{Γ,Y}(v) ≤ w_{Γ,Y}(v) ≤ #Stab_G(v)·n_{Γ,Y}(v), and w_{Γ,Y}(v) = n_{Γ,Y}(v) iff Stab_Γ(v') = Stab_G(v') for every v' ∈ G·v ∩ Y; in particular w = n when Stab_G(v) = 1. For binary quartic forms: m(f) = Σ_{f' ∈ B(f)} #Aut_Q(f)/#Aut_Z(f') and m_p(f) = Σ_{f' ∈ B_p(f)} #Aut_{Q_p}(f)/#Aut_{Z_p}(f'), and for the PGL_2(Z_p)-orbits f_1, …, f_k inside one PGL_2(Q_p)-class, Σ_i 1/#Aut_{Z_p}(f_i) = m_p(f)/#Aut_{Q_p}(f).
hypotheses: Stab_G(v) finite; for binary quartic forms with Δ(f) ≠ 0 the stabilizer in PGL_2(K) is isomorphic to E^{I,J}(K)[2] (ST.1, Theorem 3.2), of order at most 4.
Stab_Γ(v') = Γ ∩ Stab_G(v') is a subgroup of Stab_G(v'), so each ratio is a positive integer.
proofSteps: The orbit map G_{v,Y} → G·v ∩ Y, g ↦ g·v, is surjective and Γ-equivariant, so it induces a surjection Γ\G_{v,Y} → Γ\(G·v ∩ Y).

The fibre over Γv' with v' = g'·v is {Γg : g·v ∈ Γ·v'} = Γ\(Γg'Stab_G(v)), in bijection with (g'^{-1}Γg' ∩ Stab_G(v))\Stab_G(v) ≅ Stab_Γ(v')\Stab_G(v'), of size #Stab_G(v')/#Stab_Γ(v') by Lagrange (mathlib:Subgroup.card_mul_index).
Stabilizers along one G-orbit are conjugate, so #Stab_G(v') = #Stab_G(v); sum over the fibres.
The ratio is ≥ 1 with equality iff Stab_Γ(v') = Stab_G(v'), which gives the comparison with n and the equality criterion.
For the last formula apply the first one inside the class of f and use m_p(f_i) = m_p(f).
acceptance: For S_3 acting on {0,1,2} with Γ = 1 and Y = {0}: the sum has one term #S_2/1 = 2 = w(0).
If Γ = G the sum is Σ 1 over the single orbit, giving w = 1.
The identity Σ_i φ(f_i)/(m_p(f_i)#Aut_{Z_p}(f_i)) = φ(f)/#Aut_{Q_p}(f) in the proof of Corollary 3.8 is the last formula.

nodes.title: The Cartan decomposition of GL_2(Q_p) and PGL_2(Q_p)
nodes.statement: For every prime p and every γ ∈ GL_2(Q_p) there are k_1, k_2 ∈ GL_2(Z_p) and integers a ≤ b with γ = k_1·diag(p^a, p^b)·k_2, and (a, b) is uniquely determined by γ (a = min of the valuations of the entries, a + b = v_p(det γ)). Consequently every element of PGL_2(Q_p) outside PGL_2(Z_p) lies in PGL_2(Z_p)·diag(1, p^k)·PGL_2(Z_p) for a unique integer k ≥ 1, and each such double coset is a finite union of p^{k−1}(p + 1) right cosets PGL_2(Z_p)·g.
hypotheses: Z_p is a principal ideal domain (a discrete valuation ring).
The statement is about GL_2 and its image PGL_2 = GL_2/Q_p^×; scaling by p^m shifts (a, b) to (a + m, b + m), so the PGL_2 invariant is k = b − a.
proofSteps: Multiply γ by a power of p so that it has entries in Z_p; then the Z_p-lattice Z_p²·γ is a submodule of Z_p².

Apply the Smith normal form over the PID Z_p (mathlib:Submodule.smithNormalForm): there is a basis of Z_p² in which the submodule is spanned by d_1e_1, d_2e_2 with d_1 | d_2; write d_i = u_i p^{a_i} with units u_i.
The change-of-basis matrices lie in GL_2(Z_p); absorb the units into k_1 to obtain γ = k_1 diag(p^a, p^b) k_2.
Uniqueness: the minimum valuation of the entries and v_p(det) are invariant under multiplication by GL_2(Z_p) on either side.
The coset count: the right cosets in PGL_2(Z_p) diag(1, p^k) PGL_2(Z_p) correspond to the sublattices of Z_p² of index p^k with cyclic quotient, of which there are p^{k−1}(p + 1).
acceptance: diag(p, p) is scalar, hence trivial in PGL_2(Q_p): k = 0.
diag(1, p) has (a, b) = (0, 1) and k = 1; there are p + 1 right cosets in its double coset.

sources.excerpt: If mp(f) ≠ 1, then there exists γ ∈ PGL2(Qp)\PGL2(Zp) such that γ · f ∈ VZp. By replacing f with a PGL2(Zp)-translate if necessary, we may assume that γ = diag(p^a, p^b), with a > b = 0.

nodes.title: A non-integral translate of an integral form forces p² | Δ
nodes.statement: Let p be any prime and f ∈ V_{Z_p} with Δ(f) ≠ 0. If γ·f ∈ V_{Z_p} for some γ ∈ PGL_2(Q_p) \ PGL_2(Z_p) (twisted action), then p² | Δ(f). Equivalently: if p² ∤ Δ(f) then PGL_2(Q_p)_f = PGL_2(Z_p) and m_p(f) = 1; in particular m_p(f) = 1 whenever p ∤ Δ(f). More precisely, if γ·f ∈ V_{Z_p} with γ ∈ PGL_2(Z_p) diag(1, p^k) PGL_2(Z_p) then p^{2k} | Δ(f); hence PGL_2(Q_p)_f is a finite union of right PGL_2(Z_p)-cosets and m_p(f) is finite.
hypotheses: Valid for every prime p, including p = 2 and p = 3 (only the solubility half of Proposition 3.18 needs p odd).
The twisted action preserves I, J and Δ, and elements of PGL_2(Z_p) preserve integrality.
proofSteps: By cartan-decomposition-of-pgl2-over-qp write γ = k_1 δ k_2 with δ = diag(1, p^k) or diag(p^k, 1), k ≥ 1; since k_1 preserves V_{Z_p}, δ·(k_2·f) ∈ V_{Z_p}, and Δ(k_2·f) = Δ(f) (ST.0/relative-invariance-of-i-and-j). Replace f by k_2·f.

For δ = diag(1, p^k) the twisted action sends the coefficients (a, b, c, d, e) to (p^{-2k}a, p^{-k}b, c, p^{k}d, p^{2k}e); integrality forces p^{2k} | a and p^{k} | b. For diag(p^k, 1) the roles of (a, b) and (e, d) are exchanged.

Δ lies in the ideal (a, b²) of Z[a, b, c, d, e]: Δ(0, b, c, d, e) = −b²(27b²e² − 18bcde + 4bd³ + 4c³e − c²d²) = b²·disc(bx³ + cx² + dx + e); and Δ(a, b, c, d, e) = Δ(e, d, c, b, a). Every monomial of Δ is therefore divisible by a or by b², hence p^{2k} | Δ(f).
Since v_p(Δ(f)) is finite, k ≤ v_p(Δ(f))/2, and each double coset contains finitely many right cosets; so PGL_2(Z_p)\PGL_2(Q_p)_f is finite.
acceptance: For f = p²x⁴ + y⁴ (Δ = 256p⁶), δ = diag(1, p) gives δ·f = x⁴ + p²y⁴ ∈ V_{Z_p}, so m_p(f) ≥ 2, consistent with p² | Δ.
For p odd and f = x⁴ − y⁴ (Δ = −256), PGL_2(Q_p)_f = PGL_2(Z_p).

sources.excerpt: It then follows that the x⁴-coefficient of f is divisible by p² and the x³y-coefficient of f is divisible by p, implying that p² | ∆(f).
sources.match: The divisibility argument; the node adds the ideal-membership identity that justifies the last implication.

nodes.title: PGL_2 over Q has class number one
nodes.statement: The diagonal map τ: PGL_2(Z)\PGL_2(Q) → ∏'_p PGL_2(Z_p)\PGL_2(Q_p), into the families (σ_p)_p with σ_p the identity coset for all but finitely many p, is a bijection. Equivalently: PGL_2(Q) ∩ ∏_p PGL_2(Z_p) = PGL_2(Z) inside ∏_p PGL_2(Q_p), and for every such family (σ_p) there is γ ∈ PGL_2(Q) with PGL_2(Z_p)γ = σ_p for all p.
hypotheses: The restricted product condition (σ_p trivial for almost all p) is necessary: the image of any γ ∈ PGL_2(Q) is integral at all p not dividing the entries' denominators and det.
Right cosets PGL_2(Z)γ correspond to homothety classes of lattices Z²γ ⊆ Q².
proofSteps: Right cosets GL_2(Z)γ ↔ lattices L = Z²γ ⊆ Q² (free of rank 2, as submodules of Q² over the PID Z: mathlib:Submodule.smithNormalForm); likewise GL_2(Z_p)γ_p ↔ Z_p-lattices in Q_p².

Local–global principle for lattices: L ↦ (Z_p L)_p is a bijection from lattices in Q² onto families (L_p) of Z_p-lattices with L_p = Z_p² for almost all p, with inverse (L_p) ↦ Q² ∩ ⋂_p L_p (clear denominators and use the Chinese remainder theorem).

Pass to PGL_2: homothety classes. The map Q^× → ⊕_p Z, t ↦ (v_p(t))_p (mathlib:padicValRat), is surjective with kernel {±1}, so homothety classes of global lattices correspond bijectively to families of local homothety classes.
Injectivity in group form: if γ ∈ PGL_2(Q) lies in PGL_2(Z_p) for every p, take a primitive integral representative g; then det g is a p-adic unit for all p, so det g = ±1 and γ ∈ PGL_2(Z).
acceptance: The family (σ_p) with σ_ℓ = PGL_2(Z_ℓ) diag(1, ℓ) and σ_p trivial for p ≠ ℓ is the image of diag(1, ℓ).
A non-restricted family (σ_p nontrivial for infinitely many p) is not in the image.

nodes.title: Global weights are products of local weights (Proposition 3.6)
nodes.statement: For every f ∈ V_Z with Δ(f) ≠ 0: m_p(f) = 1 for every p ∤ Δ(f), each m_p(f) is finite, and m(f) = ∏_p m_p(f).
hypotheses: Δ(f) ≠ 0; the product is finite because m_p(f) = 1 for p ∤ Δ(f).
proofSteps: By rational-orbit-weight, m(f) = #PGL_2(Z)\PGL_2(Q)_f and m_p(f) = #PGL_2(Z_p)\PGL_2(Q_p)_f.

The diagonal map τ: PGL_2(Z)\PGL_2(Q)_f → ∏_p PGL_2(Z_p)\PGL_2(Q_p)_f is well defined; the product is finite by nonintegral-local-translates-force-square-discriminant (PGL_2(Q_p)_f = PGL_2(Z_p) for p ∤ Δ(f)), and each factor is finite by the same lemma.
τ is injective by class-number-one-for-pgl2-over-q (PGL_2(Q) ∩ ∏_p PGL_2(Z_p) = PGL_2(Z)).
τ is surjective: class-number-one-for-pgl2-over-q gives γ ∈ PGL_2(Q) with prescribed local cosets; then γ·f ∈ V_{Z_p} for all p, so γ·f ∈ V_Z and γ ∈ PGL_2(Q)_f.
acceptance: For f = 4x⁴ + y⁴ one has Δ(f) = 2^{14}, so m_p(f) = 1 for every odd p and m(f) = m_2(f) ≥ 2 (diag(1, 2) maps f to x⁴ + 4y⁴).
For f = x⁴ − y⁴ (Δ = −2⁸) one has m(f) = m_2(f).

nodes.title: The number of squarefree monic polynomials over a finite field
nodes.statement: For a finite field F_q the number s_n of squarefree monic polynomials of degree n over F_q is s_0 = 1, s_1 = q and s_n = q^n − q^{n−1} for n ≥ 2.
hypotheses: Squarefree in the sense of Mathlib's Squarefree in the monoid F_q[X] (no square of a nonunit divides it).
proofSteps: Every monic g has a unique factorisation g = e²·d with e monic and d monic squarefree (existence: mathlib:exists_sq_mul_squarefree, normalised to monic factors; uniqueness from unique factorisation).
Counting monic polynomials of degree n by the degree k of e gives q^n = Σ_{0 ≤ k ≤ n/2} q^k s_{n−2k}.
The generating functions satisfy (1 − qt)^{-1} = (1 − qt²)^{-1} S(t), so S(t) = (1 − qt²)/(1 − qt), whose coefficients are 1, q, q^n − q^{n−1}.
acceptance: q = 2, n = 2: the squarefree monic quadratics over F_2 are x² + x and x² + x + 1, so s_2 = 2 = 4 − 2.

sources.excerpt: An element of S̄ is determined, up to scaling by elements in F×p, by its roots in P1Fp. ... An elementary computation then yields the following equality: #S̄ = p²(p + 1)(p − 1)².

nodes.title: The number of binary quartic forms with nonzero discriminant over F_q
nodes.statement: For every finite field F_q, #{f ∈ V_{F_q} : Δ(f) ≠ 0} = q²(q + 1)(q − 1)², where Δ is the integral discriminant polynomial of ST.0 reduced to F_q.
hypotheses: Holds for every finite field, including characteristic 2 and 3 (verified by exhaustive count for q = 2, 3, 5, 7, 11).
Δ(f) is the discriminant of the dehomogenisation f(x, 1) when a ≠ 0 (ST.0/quartic-discriminant-is-the-polynomial-discriminant), and Δ(0, b, c, d, e) = b²·disc(bx³ + cx² + dx + e).
proofSteps: Case a ≠ 0: Δ(f) = disc(f(x, 1)) ≠ 0 iff f(x, 1) is separable (mathlib:Polynomial.resultant_deriv with mathlib:Polynomial.resultant_eq_zero_iff) iff it is squarefree (mathlib:PerfectField.separable_iff_squarefree, finite fields being perfect); scaling out a gives (q − 1)(q⁴ − q³) forms by count-of-squarefree-monic-polynomials-over-a-finite-field.
Case a = 0: Δ(f) = b²·disc(bx³ + cx² + dx + e) ≠ 0 iff b ≠ 0 and the cubic is squarefree: (q − 1)(q³ − q²) forms.
Sum: (q − 1)(q⁴ − q²) = q²(q + 1)(q − 1)².
acceptance: q = 3: 144 forms; q = 5: 2400; q = 2: 12 (checked by exhaustive enumeration).
The count equals #PGL_2(F_q) · #{(I, J) ∈ F_q² : Δ(I, J) ≠ 0} = q(q² − 1)·q(q − 1) for q ≥ 5, as the proof of nonsingular-binary-quartic-forms-over-finite-fields-are-soluble requires.

nodes.title: Every nonsingular binary quartic form over F_p (p odd) is soluble
nodes.statement: Let p be an odd prime and f ∈ V_{F_p} with Δ(f) ≠ 0. Then f is F_p-soluble: there are x, y, z ∈ F_p with (x, y) ≠ (0, 0) and z² = f(x, y). Consequently, for p ≥ 5 and (I, J) ∈ F_p² with Δ(I, J) ≠ 0, Σ_{f ∈ PGL_2(F_p)\V_{F_p}(I, J)} 1/#Aut_{F_p}(f) = 1 (the second assertion of Lemma 3.15).
hypotheses: p odd. For p ≥ 5 the proof is uniform; p = 3 is a finite verification; p = 2 is excluded (squares are not a proper subgroup of F_2^×).
The PGL_2(F_p)-action is the twisted action, which preserves (I, J).
proofSteps: (p ≥ 5) For (I, J) with Δ(I, J) ≠ 0 let E = E^{I,J}. By ST.1 (Theorem 3.2 over K = F_p, characteristic ≠ 2, 3) the F_p-soluble PGL_2(F_p)-orbits in V(I, J) := {f : (I(f), J(f)) = (I, J)} correspond to E(F_p)/2E(F_p), and every stabilizer is isomorphic to E(F_p)[2].

E(F_p) is finite (tauceti:WeierstrassCurve.Affine.finite_point), and for a finite abelian group #(G/2G) = #G[2] (mathlib:Subgroup.index_ker with mathlib:Subgroup.card_mul_index applied to multiplication by 2).
Orbit–stabilizer (mathlib:MulAction.card_orbit_mul_card_stabilizer_eq_card_group): the number of soluble f ∈ V(I, J) is #PGL_2(F_p)·#(E/2E)/#E[2] = #PGL_2(F_p) = p(p² − 1).

There are p² − p pairs (I, J) with Δ(I, J) ≠ 0 (the curve J² = 4I³ has the p points (t², 2t³)), so the number of soluble nonsingular forms is (p² − p)p(p² − 1) = p²(p + 1)(p − 1)², which is the number of all nonsingular forms by count-of-nonsingular-binary-quartic-forms-over-a-finite-field. Hence every nonsingular form is soluble, and the mass formula follows.
(p = 3) Exhaustive check of the 3⁵ = 243 forms over F_3: each of the 144 forms with Δ ≠ 0 vanishes at a point of P¹(F_3) or takes the nonzero square value 1 there.
acceptance: Over F_5 all 2400 nonsingular forms are soluble; over F_7 all 14112 (exhaustive check).
Over F_p with p ≥ 5 and Δ(I, J) ≠ 0 the fibre V(I, J) has exactly p(p² − 1) elements.
The hypothesis Δ ≠ 0 is needed: 2(x² + y²)² over F_3 (Δ = 0) takes only the non-square value 2 on P¹(F_3) and is not F_3-soluble.

nodes.title: An insoluble form at an odd prime has discriminant divisible by p²
nodes.statement: Let p be an odd prime and f ∈ V_{Z_p} with Δ(f) ≠ 0. If f is not Q_p-soluble then p² | Δ(f). In particular every f ∈ V_{Z_p} with p ∤ Δ(f) is Q_p-soluble.
hypotheses: p odd: the Hensel lifting of a square root of a unit uses that 2 is a unit.
Splitting types refer to the factorisation of the reduction f̄ ∈ V_{F_p} into irreducible binary forms, as in the source.
proofSteps: If p ∤ Δ(f): by nonsingular-binary-quartic-forms-over-finite-fields-are-soluble there are (x̄, ȳ, z̄) with z̄² = f̄(x̄, ȳ). If z̄ ≠ 0, lift z by Hensel's lemma (mathlib:hensels_lemma for Z² − f(x, y), derivative 2z a unit). If z̄ = 0, (x̄ : ȳ) is a simple root of f̄ and lifts to a root of f in P¹(Q_p), giving a solution with z = 0.
If f ≡ 0 (mod p) then p⁶ | Δ(f).
If p | Δ(f) and f̄ ≠ 0, f̄ has a repeated factor; its splitting type is (1²11), (1²2), (1³1), (1²1²), (2²) or (1⁴). Types (1²11) and (1³1) have a simple F_p-rational root, which lifts as above.

Type (1²2): after a PGL_2(Z_p)-change of variables and a Hensel factorisation, f = a(x² − kp y²)(x² − n y²) with n a non-residue unit; if a is a square, f(1, 0) is a nonzero square; otherwise take the first residue (c + 1)n̄ in n̄, 2n̄, …, (p − 1)n̄, set x̄_0² = (c + 1)n̄, so x̄_0² − n̄ = cn̄ is a non-residue and f(x_0, 1) is a nonzero square.
Types (1²1²), (2²), (1⁴) mean f̄ = c·ḡ² for a binary quadratic form ḡ. Δ and its gradient vanish identically on forms c·g² (polynomial identity), so Δ(c g² + p h) ≡ 0 (mod p²) for all lifts.
acceptance: Every f ∈ V_{Z_5} with 5 ∤ Δ(f) is Q_5-soluble (exhaustive check over F_5 and Hensel lifting).

f = 2(x² + y²)² + 3xy³ = 2x⁴ + 4x²y² + 3xy³ + 2y⁴ has Δ(f) = 28116 = 2²·3²·781 and is not Q_3-soluble: for primitive (x, y), f(x, y) ≡ 2 (mod 3) is a non-square unit. Its type at 3 is (2²) and 3² | Δ(f), as the lemma requires.
Forms of type (1²2) are soluble although p | Δ(f): the lemma is not the converse statement.

nodes.title: The local weight m_p and Q_p-solubility are locally constant off Δ = 0
nodes.statement: Let p be a prime. On the open set {f ∈ V_{Z_p} : Δ(f) ≠ 0} the functions f ↦ m_p(f) and f ↦ 1[f is Q_p-soluble] are locally constant; precisely, m_p is constant on f + p^{δ+1}V_{Z_p} where δ = v_p(Δ(f)). The set {f ∈ V_{Z_p} : Δ(f) = 0} is closed and has Haar measure zero. Consequently, for a family F defined by congruence conditions, φ_p := 1_{S_p(F)}/m_p is a function V_{Z_p} → [0, 1] that is locally constant outside the closed null set {Δ = 0} ∪ {f : (2^{-4}I(f), 2^{-6}J(f)) ∈ ∂Inv_p(F)}.
hypotheses: The boundary of Inv_p(F) has measure zero (ST.0: the local sets Σ_p are closed with null boundary), and the map f ↦ (I(f), J(f)) pulls null sets of Z_p² back to null sets of V_{Z_p} (it is a submersion off Δ = 0, change-of-measure formula).
proofSteps: m_p: by nonintegral-local-translates-force-square-discriminant only double cosets PGL_2(Z_p) diag(1, p^k) PGL_2(Z_p) with 2k ≤ δ can meet PGL_2(Q_p)_f; whether δ_k·(κ·f) is integral (κ ∈ PGL_2(Z_p)) depends only on f modulo p^{2k}; f' ≡ f (mod p^{δ+1}) has v_p(Δ(f')) = δ, so the same cosets occur for f and f'.

Solubility is open: a solution (x, y, z) with z ≠ 0 persists because Q_p^{×2} is open (Hensel's lemma, mathlib:hensels_lemma); a solution with z = 0 is a simple root of f (Δ(f) ≠ 0) and persists under perturbation by Hensel's lemma.

Insolubility is open: if f is insoluble, f(x, y) lies in the open set Q_p^× \ Q_p^{×2} for all primitive (x, y) ∈ Z_p², a compact set; by continuity of (f, x, y) ↦ f(x, y) and compactness (tube lemma) the same holds on a neighbourhood of f.

{Δ = 0} is null: for fixed (a, b, c, d) with (a, b) ≠ (0, 0), Δ is a nonzero polynomial of degree at most 3 in e, so it has at most 3 roots; Fubini on Z_p⁴ × Z_p with the Haar measure (mathlib:MeasureTheory.Measure.haarMeasure) gives measure zero.
φ_p takes values in [0, 1] because m_p ≥ 1 (rational-orbit-weight) and is locally constant off the displayed closed null set.
acceptance: m_p(x⁴ − y⁴) = 1 on the whole ball (x⁴ − y⁴) + p V_{Z_p} for odd p.
The indicator of Q_3-solubility is 0 on the ball f_0 + 3V_{Z_3} with f_0 = 2x⁴ + 4x²y² + 3xy³ + 2y⁴ (all values ≡ 2 mod 3).

nodes.statement: A form f ∈ V_R with Δ(f) ≠ 0 is R-soluble if and only if f is not negative definite, i.e. iff f ∉ V_R^{(2−)}. Hence S_∞(F) ∩ {Δ ≠ 0} is the union of the components V_R^{(0)} and V_R^{(2+)} over {Δ > 0} ∩ Inv_∞(F) and the component V_R^{(1)} over {Δ < 0} ∩ Inv_∞(F).

nodes.title: The Jacobian of the orbit map (PGL_2 × A², ω ∧ dI ∧ dJ) → (V, dv) is the constant −1/27
nodes.statement: Let s_{I,J} := x³y − (I/3)xy³ − (J/27)y⁴, so that I(s_{I,J}) = I and J(s_{I,J}) = J, and let ψ: PGL_2 × A² → V, ψ(g, I, J) := g·s_{I,J} (twisted action). Let ω be the left-invariant top-degree form on PGL_2 whose value at the identity on the images of E_{11}, E_{12}, E_{21} in pgl_2 = gl_2/(scalars) is 1 (these images form a Z-basis of gl_2(Z)/Z·1, so ω generates the invariant top-degree forms of PGL_2 over Z, as in the source's Proposition 2.8), and let dv = da ∧ db ∧ dc ∧ dd ∧ de. Then ψ*(dv) = −(1/27)·ω ∧ dI ∧ dJ identically on PGL_2 × A², over every commutative ring in which 3 is invertible. At g = 1 the Jacobian matrix (rows a, …, e; columns E_{11}, E_{12}, E_{21}, ∂_I, ∂_J) is [[0,1,0,0,0],[1,0,0,0,0],[0,−I,3,0,0],[I/3,−4J/27,0,−1/3,0],[2J/27,0,−I/3,0,−1/27]], of determinant −1/27.
hypotheses: The action is the twisted action, whose determinant on the 5-dimensional space V is 1 (for the untwisted action it would be (det g)^{10}).
The sign of ω is fixed by the ordered basis (E_{11}, E_{12}, E_{21}); only |−1/27| enters the measure statements.
proofSteps: The twisted action of g on V has determinant 1 (polynomial identity), and ω is left-invariant, so the Jacobian of ψ at (g, I, J) equals its value at (1, I, J).

At g = 1 the derivative of t ↦ (1 + tE)·s_{I,J} for E ∈ {E_{11}, E_{12}, E_{21}} and the partial derivatives ∂_I s, ∂_J s give the displayed matrix; its determinant (mathlib:Matrix.det) is −1/27, independent of (I, J).
The identity is a polynomial identity with coefficients in Z[1/3], hence valid after base change to R, Q_p and every Z[1/3]-algebra.
acceptance: |−1/27|_p = 1 for p ≠ 3 and |−1/27|_3 = 27, the values the source obtains in §3.4 by counting points modulo p (p ≠ 3) and modulo 9 (p = 3).
|−1/27|_∞ = 1/27 is the constant of the source's Proposition 2.8.

nodes.title: The local mass formula (Proposition 3.9)
nodes.statement: For every family F defined by congruence conditions and every prime p, ∫_{S_p(F)} m_p(f)^{-1} df = |2^{10}/27|_p (1 − p^{-2}) M_p(V, F).

proofSteps: Apply weighted-p-adic-change-of-measure to φ = 1_{S_p(F)}: every f ∈ S_p(F) has Δ(f) ≠ 0, is Q_p-soluble, and has invariants (2⁴I, 2⁶J) with 3 | I, 27 | J, so 2⁴·3 | I(f) and 2⁶·3³ | J(f); φ is PGL_2(Q_p)-invariant.

For (I, J) = (2⁴I', 2⁶J') the curves E^{I,J} and E^{I',J'} are isomorphic over Q_p ((x, y) ↦ (4x, 8y)), so the Selmer ratio is unchanged, and every soluble class is counted exactly when (I', J') ∈ Inv_p(F).
The substitution (I, J) = (2⁴I', 2⁶J') has Jacobian |2^{10}|_p, giving |2^{10}|_p·|1/27|_p(1 − p^{-2}) M_p(V, F).

The product over all p of |2^{10}/27|_p is 27/2^{10}, which cancels the archimedean factor 2^{10}/27 in selmer-average-as-product-of-local-masses.

nodes.title: #(G/2G) = |2|_p^{-1}·#G[2] for an abelian group with a finite-index subgroup isomorphic to Z_p
nodes.statement: Let G be an abelian group and U ≤ G a subgroup of finite index with U ≅ (Z_p, +) as abstract groups, p prime. Then G[2] and G/2G are finite and #(G/2G) = |2|_p^{-1}·#G[2]: #(G/2G) = #G[2] for p odd and #(G/2G) = 2·#G[2] for p = 2.
hypotheses: Only the abstract group structure is used; G is written additively and 2G is the image of multiplication by 2.
proofSteps: For an abelian group M with M[2] and M/2M finite put q(M) = #(M/2M)/#M[2]. For finite M, q(M) = 1: #M = #M[2]·#2M by the first isomorphism theorem (mathlib:Subgroup.index_ker, mathlib:Subgroup.card_mul_index).
Multiplication by 2 on 0 → U → G → G/U → 0 gives the exact sequence 0 → U[2] → G[2] → (G/U)[2] → U/2U → G/2G → (G/U)/2(G/U) → 0 (snake lemma), so G[2], G/2G are finite and q(G) = q(U)·q(G/U) = q(U).

Consequently, for f ∈ V_Z with Δ(f) ≠ 0 and φ_p := 1_{S_p(F)}/m_p: 1_{S_∞(F)}(f)·Π_p φ_p(f) = 1_{S(F)}(f)/m(f).

nodes.title: Nonidentity 2-Selmer elements as a weighted count of integral orbits
nodes.statement: Let F be a family of elliptic curves defined by congruence conditions. For every ε > 0 and X ≥ 1, Σ_{E ∈ F, H'(E) < X} (#S_2(E) − 1) = Σ_{PGL_2(Z)·f ⊆ S(F), f irreducible over Q, H(f) < 2^{12}X} 1/m(f) + O_ε(X^{3/4+ε}), where S_2(E) is the (finite) 2-Selmer group and the implied constant is independent of F.
hypotheses: S_2(E) is finite (Tau Ceti EllipticCurves layer 7) and is identified with the locally soluble 2-coverings of ST.1.
The weights 1/m(f) and 1/n(f) lie in (0, 1]; the error comes only from orbits with a nontrivial stabilizer in PGL_2(Q) and from forms that are products of two irreducible quadratic forms.
proofSteps: By ST.1 (Theorem 3.5), the nonidentity elements of S_2(E^{I,J}) correspond bijectively to the PGL_2(Q)-classes of locally soluble integral forms with invariants (2⁴I, 2⁶J) and no rational linear factor; distinct curves have distinct invariants, and H(2⁴I, 2⁶J) = 2^{12}H(I, J) (ST.0).
Each such class C meets V_Z in n(f) PGL_2(Z)-orbits, and Σ_{orbits in C} 1/n(f) = 1.

By orbit-weight-as-a-stabilizer-sum, m(f) = n(f) unless some orbit in C has a nontrivial stabilizer in PGL_2(Q); by ST.2 (Lemma 2.4) the PGL_2(Z)-orbits of height < Y with nontrivial PGL_2(Q)-stabilizer number O_ε(Y^{3/4+ε}), and each weight is at most 1.

Forms with no rational linear factor are irreducible or products of two irreducible quadratic forms; the latter have a ≠ 0 and are reducible, so by ST.2 (Lemma 2.3 and Proposition 2.7: the cusp contains only forms with a = 0) they number O_ε(Y^{2/3+ε}).
acceptance: For E: y² = x³ − x (A = −1, B = 0), S_2(E) has order 4 (E(Q) = E(Q)[2] and Ш[2] = 0), so E contributes 3 to the left side; since E(Q)[2] ≠ 0 its forms have nontrivial PGL_2(Q)-stabilizers and may be weighted differently on the right, which is why the error term is needed.
The identity class (forms with a rational linear factor, e.g. x³y − 16xy³ for y² = x³ − x) is excluded from the right side.

nodes.title: The weighted count of locally soluble orbits is a product of local densities
nodes.statement: Let F be a large family of elliptic curves defined by congruence conditions. Then, as Y → ∞, Σ_{PGL_2(Z)·f ⊆ S(F), f irreducible, H(f) < Y} 1/m(f) = N(V_Z ∩ S_∞(F); Y)·Π_p ∫_{S_p(F)} m_p(f)^{-1} df + o(Y^{5/6}), where N(V_Z ∩ S_∞(F); Y) is the number of irreducible GL_2(Z)-orbits of integral forms that are R-soluble with invariants in Inv_∞(F) and height < Y, and the Euler product converges absolutely.
hypotheses: F large: for all but finitely many p, Inv_p(F) contains every (I, J) ∈ Z_p² with p² ∤ Δ(I, J) (ST.0).
The sieve of ST.2 (Theorem 2.21) is applied separately to each component V^{(i)}, i ∈ {0, 1, 2+, 2−}; only the R-soluble components with invariants in Inv_∞(F) contribute.
proofSteps: Local weights: φ_p := 1_{S_p(F)}/m_p: V_{Z_p} → [0, 1] is locally constant outside a closed null set (local-weights-and-solubility-are-locally-constant).

Product: for f ∈ V_Z with Δ(f) ≠ 0 in an R-soluble component with invariants in Inv_∞(F), Π_p φ_p(f) = 1_{S(F)}(f)/m(f) (locally-soluble-set-is-cut-out-by-local-conditions, global-weight-is-product-of-local-weights); the product converges because φ_p(f) = 1 for p ∤ 6Δ(f) outside the exceptional primes of largeness.

Acceptability (ST.0/acceptable-weight-function): for p ≥ 5 outside the finite exceptional set, if p² ∤ Δ(f) then f is Q_p-soluble and m_p(f) = 1 (bad-forms-have-square-discriminant), and (2^{-4}I(f), 2^{-6}J(f)) ∈ Inv_p(F) by largeness since Δ(2^{-4}I, 2^{-6}J) = 2^{-12}Δ(f); so φ_p(f) = 1.
Apply Theorem 2.21 (ST.2) on each R-soluble component and add; the Euler product converges because 1 − ∫φ_p ≤ μ_p{p² | Δ} = O(p^{-2}) for large p.

Replacing the weight 1/m by 1 would count PGL_2(Z)-orbits rather than Selmer elements and change every local factor at the primes dividing the discriminants.

nodes.title: The number of R-soluble integral orbits of bounded height
nodes.statement: For a family F defined by congruence conditions and every ε > 0, N(V_Z ∩ S_∞(F); X) = (1/27)·Vol(PGL_2(Z)\PGL_2(R))·M_∞(V, F; X) + O_ε(X^{3/4+ε}).

nodes.title: Lattice points (I, J) of bounded height in residue classes
nodes.statement: Let L ⊆ Z² be a union of k cosets of mZ² (m ≥ 1). Then, uniformly in X ≥ 1, #{(I, J) ∈ L : H(I, J) < X, 4I³ − J² > 0} = (k/m²)·(8/5)X^{5/6} + O_m(X^{1/2}) and #{(I, J) ∈ L : H(I, J) < X, 4I³ − J² < 0} = (k/m²)·(32/5)X^{5/6} + O_m(X^{1/2}).

nodes.title: Uniform tail estimate: curves whose discriminant is divisible by p² for some large p
nodes.statement: There is an absolute constant C such that for all M ≥ 5 and X ≥ 2, #{(A, B) ∈ Z² : 4|A|³ < X, 27B² < X, 4A³ + 27B² ≠ 0, p² | 4A³ + 27B² for some prime p > M} ≤ C(X^{5/6}/M + X^{5/6}/log X). In particular limsup_{X→∞} X^{-5/6}·#{E : H(E) < X, p² | Δ(E) for some p > M} = O(1/M).
hypotheses: Pairs (A, B), not only minimal pairs, are counted; H(E_{A,B}) = max{4|A|³, 27B²}.
Δ(E_{A,B}) = −16(4A³ + 27B²); for p ≥ 5 the conditions p² | Δ and p² | 4A³ + 27B² agree.
proofSteps: If p² | D := 4A³ + 27B² ≠ 0 then p² ≤ |D| ≪ X, so only primes p ≪ X^{1/2} occur.

Multiplicative case p ∤ A (p ≥ 5): then p ∤ B, and for fixed A the congruence B² ≡ −4A³/27 (mod p²) has at most 2 solutions modulo p², so the number of pairs is ≪ (X^{1/3} + 1)(X^{1/2}/p² + 1) ≪ X^{5/6}/p² + X^{1/3}.
Additive case p | A: then p | B, and the number of pairs is ≪ (X^{1/3}/p + 1)(X^{1/2}/p + 1) ≪ X^{5/6}/p² + X^{1/2}/p + 1.
acceptance: Pairs with p | A and p | B satisfy p² | 4A³ + 27B² and have density p^{-2}, so the tail is ≫ X^{5/6}/(M log M): the bound O(X^{5/6}/M) is sharp up to the logarithm.
The per-prime bound O(X^{5/6}/p² + X^{1/3}) is not uniform in p for p > X^{1/3}; the sum over p is what the sieve needs.

proofSteps: Embed x³ + Ax + B ↦ the binary cubic form x³ + Axy² + By³; a GL_2(Z)-class has at most 12 preimages, since each preimage gives a distinct integral solution of v(a, b) = 1 and a cubic Thue equation of nonzero discriminant has at most 12 solutions (Delone, Evertse; gap).

By Davenport–Heilbronn's Proposition 1 (equivalently Bhargava–Shankar–Tsimerman's Proposition 29 for Z_p = W_p ∪ Y_p) the GL_2(Z)-classes of integral binary cubic forms with |disc| < CX and p² | disc number O(X/p²): the forms nonmaximal at p are ST.2's uniformity estimate, the maximal forms totally ramified at p are ST.3's cubic-fields-totally-ramified-at-large-primes-are-sparse (stated there for forms maximal at every prime; gap). Hence the curves with p² | Δ number O(X/p²).
Additive reduction (p | A, p | B): O(X^{5/6}/p² + X^{1/2}/p + 1), combined with O(X/p²) gives O(X^{5/6}/p^{5/3}).
Multiplicative reduction with p² | Δ: O(X^{1/3}(X^{1/2}/p² + 1)), combined with O(X/p²) gives O(X^{5/6}/p^{3/2}).
acceptance: For p > X^{1/2} the count is 0: H'(E) < X gives |4A³ + 27B²| ≤ 8X/27, and p² | Δ ≠ 0 forces p² ≤ 8X/27.
Summing the bound over p > M gives O(X^{5/6}/M^{1/2}), a weaker tail than the elementary tail estimate but uniform in X.

nodes.title: The number of elliptic curves of bounded height in a large family (Theorem 3.17)
nodes.statement: Let F be a large family of elliptic curves defined by congruence conditions and N(F; X) := #{E ∈ F : H'(E) < X}. Then N(F; X) = M_∞(F; X)·Π_p M_p(F) + o(X^{5/6}), and the product converges: 1 − M_p(F) = O(p^{-2}) for all but finitely many p.
hypotheses: Curves are counted up to Q-isomorphism, through their invariants (I, J) = (−3A, −27B) for the unique minimal pair (A, B) (ST.0, from Tau Ceti EllipticCurves layer 8).
The main term may vanish (if some M_p(F) = 0); the statement is still true, and theorems dividing by N(F; X) assume Π_p M_p(F) > 0.
proofSteps: Finite approximation: for a finite set of primes P and closed-open sets U_p ⊆ Z_p² that are finite unions of cosets of p^kZ_p², lattice-points-of-bounded-invariant-height gives #{(I, J) ∈ Z² : (I, J) ∈ U_p ∀p ∈ P, (I, J) ∈ Inv_∞(F), H < X} = M_∞(F; X)Π_{p∈P} μ_p(U_p) + O_P(X^{1/2}).
Upper bound: since ∂Inv_p(F) is null (ST.0), choose U_p ⊇ Inv_p(F) with μ_p(U_p \ Inv_p(F)) small; letting P grow gives limsup N(F; X)/X^{5/6} ≤ M_∞(F; 1)Π_p M_p(F).

Lower bound: choose U_p ⊆ Inv_p(F) for p ≤ Y; a pair in all U_p (p ≤ Y) but outside Inv(F) fails Inv_p(F) at some p > Y, and for Y beyond the exceptional primes of largeness this forces p² | Δ(I, J); by tail-estimate-for-square-divisors-of-the-discriminant these number O(X^{5/6}/Y + X^{5/6}/log X).
Convergence: for p ≥ 5 outside the exceptional set, Inv_p(F) ⊇ {p² ∤ Δ}, and μ_p{p² | Δ(I, J)} ≤ 3p^{-2} (at most 2 residues of J modulo p² for each unit I, and p² classes with p | I, p | J).
Let Y → ∞.
acceptance: Family of all curves: N(F; X) ~ 8X^{5/6}/(81ζ(10)); in terms of H(E) < T this is (2^{4/3}/(3^{3/2}ζ(10)))T^{5/6}.
For the large family of example E501 (a measure-zero Cantor-type condition at 5) the main term is 0 and N(F; X) = o(X^{5/6}).

nodes.statement: Let F be a large family of elliptic curves defined by congruence conditions with M_p(F) > 0 for every prime p. Then lim_{X→∞} (Σ_{E ∈ F, H'(E) < X} (#S_2(E) − 1)) / N(F; X) = Vol(PGL_2(Z)\PGL_2(R))·(M_∞(V, F; X)/M_∞(F; X))·Π_p ((1 − p^{-2})·M_p(V, F)/M_p(F)), where the archimedean ratio M_∞(V, F; X)/M_∞(F; X) does not depend on X.

By count-of-real-soluble-integral-orbits and homogeneity (M_∞(V, F; 2^{12}X) = 2^{10}M_∞(V, F; X)), N(V_Z ∩ S_∞(F); 2^{12}X) = (2^{10}/27)Vol(PGL_2(Z)\PGL_2(R))M_∞(V, F; X) + O(X^{3/4+ε}).
By local-mass-formula-for-locally-soluble-forms, ∫_{S_p(F)} m_p^{-1} = |2^{10}/27|_p(1 − p^{-2})M_p(V, F); the product formula gives (2^{10}/27)·Π_p |2^{10}/27|_p = 1.
Denominator: count-of-curves-in-a-large-family, with M_∞(F; X)Π_p M_p(F) ≍ X^{5/6} by the positivity hypothesis.
Take the ratio; M_∞(V, F; X)/M_∞(F; X) is constant by homogeneity (local-masses-of-a-family).

The limit is a product over all places, with the archimedean factor 2ζ(2)·(1/2).

nodes.title: Theorem 3.1: the average size of S_2(E) over a large family is 3
nodes.statement: Let F be a large family of elliptic curves over Q defined by congruence conditions (ST.0) with M_p(F) > 0 for every prime p. When the curves in F are ordered by height H (equivalently H'), the average size of the 2-Selmer group is 3: lim_{X→∞} Σ_{E ∈ F, H(E) < X} #S_2(E) / #{E ∈ F : H(E) < X} = 3. The average of #S_2(E) − 1 equals Vol(PGL_2(Z)\PGL_2(R))·Π_p vol(PGL_2(Z_p)) = 2, the Tamagawa number of PGL_2.
hypotheses: F must be large, not merely defined by congruence conditions: largeness allows infinitely many conditions but requires that at all but finitely many p nothing is excluded away from p² | Δ.
M_p(F) > 0 for every p: an added hypothesis without which the source's proof does not apply (sourceIssue ArithmeticStatistics/E501).
The ordering is by the naive height; a different ordering (by conductor or discriminant) is a different theorem.
S_2(E) is the 2-Selmer group Sel_2(E/Q) of Tau Ceti EllipticCurves layer 7, identified by ST.1 with the locally soluble 2-coverings; it is finite.
proofSteps: By selmer-average-as-product-of-local-masses the average of #S_2(E) − 1 is Vol(PGL_2(Z)\PGL_2(R))·(M_∞(V, F; X)/M_∞(F; X))·Π_p (1 − p^{-2})M_p(V, F)/M_p(F).
By local-selmer-mass-ratios the ratios are 1/2 at ∞, 2 at p = 2 and 1 at odd p.
By tamagawa-number-of-pgl2-is-two the value is 2ζ(2)·(1/2)·2·Π_p(1 − p^{-2}) = 2.
Add the constant 1 (average-over-a-height-ordered-family: averages add) and pass from H' to H (27H = 4H').
acceptance: Largeness check: the families of all curves, of finitely many congruence conditions, and of semistable curves are large (ST.0); the semistable family excludes a positive-density set at every p (the additive pairs, all with p² | Δ) and is still large. What largeness forbids is excluding, at infinitely many p, pairs with p² ∤ Δ(I, J).
Local-mass check: the ratio is 2 at p = 2 and 1 at the other primes; an implementation that treats p = 2 like the others obtains the average 2.
Tamagawa check: 2ζ(2)Π_p(1 − p^{-2}) = 2ζ(2)/ζ(2) = 2; verify the cancellation explicitly.
Averaging check: the theorem computes the average of #S_2(E), a size, not of the 2-Selmer rank; the passage to ranks costs the inequality 2k ≤ 2^k of rank-bound-from-the-selmer-average.
Consistency: the value 3 agrees with the heuristic predictions of Poonen–Rains and of Delaunay combined with Goldfeld–Katz–Sarnak (source p. 2); those models are statements of ST.5, not inputs here.

nodes.title: The families of Theorems 1.1 and 1.3 and the semistable family satisfy the hypotheses of Theorem 3.1
nodes.statement: Each of the following families of elliptic curves over Q is defined by congruence conditions, is large, and has M_p(F) > 0 for every prime p: (a) all elliptic curves; (b) every nonempty family {E_{A,B} : (A, B) ∈ U} where U ⊆ Z² is a union of residue classes modulo some m ≥ 1, possibly with a sign condition on Δ; (c) all semistable elliptic curves (good or multiplicative reduction at every prime).
hypotheses: Nonemptiness in (b): a union of residue classes containing no minimal pair with Δ ≠ 0 (e.g. p⁴ | A and p⁶ | B) defines the empty family.
In (c) semistability at 2 and 3 is a condition on the minimal model, not on the short model (A, B), which is never minimal at 2 when it has good reduction.
proofSteps: Largeness: (a) is ST.0/all-elliptic-curves-form-a-large-family; (b) and (c) contain, at every p ∤ 6m, all pairs with p² ∤ Δ (for p ≥ 5 the minimal-pair model is minimal at p, and E_{A,B} is semistable at p iff not both p | A and p | B, pairs with p² | Δ) — ST.0/elliptic-families-defined-by-congruence-conditions.

Local sets: Σ_p = {(−3A, −27B) : A, B ∈ Z_p, not (p⁴ | A and p⁶ | B), Δ ≠ 0}, intersected with the residue conditions at p | m in (b), and with semistability at p in (c); the semistability locus at p is open and closed in {Δ ≠ 0} because the reduction type of a minimal model is locally constant in the coefficients off Δ = 0 (Mathlib's reduction predicates WeierstrassCurve.HasGoodReduction, HasMultiplicativeReduction; local constancy from Tau Ceti EllipticCurves layer 4).
Inv_p(F) = Σ_p: minimal pairs satisfying the global conditions are p-adically dense in Σ_p (CRT, and pairs failing minimality at some prime q ∉ P have density at most Σ_q q^{-10} < 1).

Positivity: each Σ_p contains a nonempty open set (a residue class of a member of F), hence M_p(F) = μ_p(Σ_p) > 0; for (c) at p = 2, 3 use a curve with good reduction there, e.g. y² + y = x³ − x (conductor 37).
acceptance: The family {B = 0} (j = 1728) is not large (ST.0), and the Cantor-type family of E501 is large with M_5(F) = 0: both fail the hypotheses.

nodes.title: The 2-Selmer rank identity (2)
nodes.statement: For every elliptic curve E over Q: r_2(S_2(E)) = r(E) + r_2(E(Q)[2]) + r_2(Ш_E[2]), where r(E) is the rank of E(Q) and r_2(G) = dim_{F_2} G for an elementary abelian 2-group G. In particular r(E) ≤ r_2(S_2(E)) and 2^{r(E)}·#E(Q)[2] ≤ #S_2(E).

S_2(E) is finite (Tau Ceti EllipticCurves layer 7); Ш_E[2] is its quotient by the image of E(Q)/2E(Q), finite as well. Nothing here controls Ш_E.
proofSteps: The exact sequence 0 → E(Q)/2E(Q) → S_2(E) → Ш_E[2] → 0 of F_2-vector spaces (Tau Ceti EllipticCurves layer 7).

#(E(Q)/2E(Q)) = 2^{r(E)}·#E(Q)[2] (tauceti:WeierstrassCurve.Affine.card_range_μ, with E(Q) finitely generated by tauceti:WeierstrassCurve.Affine.fg_point_of_numberField), transported to the cohomological carrier by the comparison of explicit and cohomological 2-Selmer groups (layer 7 milestone, used through ST.1).

Take F_2-dimensions. The inequality 2^{r}·#E(Q)[2] ≤ #S_2(E) is also tauceti:WeierstrassCurve.Affine.pow_rank_le_card_of_range_μ_le for the explicit 2-Selmer group tauceti:WeierstrassCurve.Affine.selmerGroup₂.

nodes.title: 0% of elliptic curves have rational 2-torsion
nodes.statement: #{(A, B) ∈ Z² : max{4|A|³, 27B²} < X, x³ + Ax + B has a rational root} = O(X^{1/2}). Consequently, for every large family F with M_p(F) > 0 for all p, the proportion of E ∈ F with E(Q)[2] ≠ 0 tends to 0 and the average of r_2(E(Q)[2]) over F is 0.

With |A| ≤ α := (X/4)^{1/3}: if r² ≥ 4α then |r³ + Ar| ≥ (3/4)|r|³ ≥ 6α^{3/2} > (X/27)^{1/2}, so |r| < 2α^{1/2} ≪ X^{1/6}; each pair (A, r) determines B, giving O(X^{1/3}·X^{1/6}) = O(X^{1/2}) pairs.
By count-of-curves-in-a-large-family, N(F; X) ≫ X^{5/6} when Π_p M_p(F) > 0; divide.

The bound is a density statement, not an inequality between ranks.

nodes.title: Corollary 1.2: average 2-Selmer rank and average rank at most 1.5
nodes.statement: Let F be a large family with M_p(F) > 0 for every prime p (for Corollary 1.2 itself, the family of all elliptic curves), ordered by height. Then limsup_{X→∞} Avg_F(r_2(S_2(E)); X) ≤ 3/2 and limsup_{X→∞} Avg_F(r(E); X) ≤ 3/2: the average 2-Selmer rank, and hence the average rank, of elliptic curves in F is bounded by 1.5. This bounds the Mordell–Weil rank; it does not compute it, since r(E) and r_2(S_2(E)) differ by r_2(E(Q)[2]) + r_2(Ш_E[2]), which is not controlled.
hypotheses: The conclusion is about the upper average (limsup); no lower bound and no limit is asserted.
The inequality 2k ≤ 2^k for k ∈ N, an equality exactly at k = 1, 2, is where the loss from average size 3 to average rank 1.5 occurs.
The rank bound needs E(Q) finitely generated and S_2(E) finite (two-selmer-rank-identity).
proofSteps: Pointwise, 2·r_2(S_2(E)) ≤ 2^{r_2(S_2(E))} = #S_2(E) (mathlib:Nat.mul_le_pow with a = 2: 2k ≤ 2^k).
Average: Avg_F(r_2(S_2); X) ≤ Avg_F(#S_2; X)/2 → 3/2 by average-size-of-the-2-selmer-group-is-three, so the upper average is at most 3/2.
r(E) ≤ r_2(S_2(E)) (two-selmer-rank-identity), so the upper average of r(E) is at most 3/2 (upperFamilyAverage_mono).
acceptance: ST.4's acceptance condition is met here: the Selmer average bounds the rank through the proved inequality 2k ≤ 2^k, and the Selmer rank is not equated with the Mordell–Weil rank; the difference r_2(E(Q)[2]) + r_2(Ш_E[2]) is not controlled.

Check the loss: #S_2(E) is always a power of 2, and 2k ≤ 2^k is an equality only at k = 1, 2. Mean size 3 gives mean 2-Selmer rank ≤ 3/2 through this inequality (Jensen's inequality would give only log₂3 ≈ 1.585). The conjectured average rank 1/2 (Goldfeld, Katz–Sarnak, p. 1) is a separate statement about Mordell–Weil ranks.
Check the direction: Theorem 1.1 is an equality (average exactly 3); Corollary 1.2 is only an upper bound for ranks.
Check that the 2-torsion term is handled by a density statement (rational-two-torsion-has-density-zero), not by an inequality.

nodes.title: Higher height moments in an arithmetic family
nodes.statement: Let F be an arithmetic family ordered by a height (ArithmeticStatistics:ST.0/arithmetic-family): a set F with h : F → ℝ such that F(X) := {x ∈ F : h(x) < X} is finite for every X, and N_F(X) := #F(X) → ∞. For f : F → [0, ∞] and an integer m ≥ 1 put S_m(f; X) := Σ_{x ∈ F(X)} f(x)^m. The upper and lower m-th height moments of f are M⁺_m(f) := limsup_{X→∞} S_m(f;X)/N_F(X) and M⁻_m(f) := liminf_{X→∞} S_m(f;X)/N_F(X), both in [0, ∞]; the m-th moment exists when they agree. nodes.title: Isomorphism classes of finite abelian p-groups, indexed by partitions
nodes.statement: The carrier L of isomorphism classes of finite abelian p-groups is the type of pairs (n, λ) with n ∈ ℕ and λ a partition of n (Mathlib Nat.Partition n). For a prime p the class (n, λ) is realised by the standard representative A_λ = ⊕_i ℤ/p^{λ_i} (parts in decreasing order), a group of order p^n. Attached data: the conjugate partition λ'_i = #{j : λ_j ≥ i} (so λ'_1 is the p-rank and p^{λ'_1} = |A_λ[p]|), the multiplicity m_i(λ) = #{j : λ_j = i}, the automorphism count |Aut A_λ|, and the trivial class (0, ∅). Every finite abelian p-group is isomorphic to A_λ for exactly one λ.
hypotheses: p prime (for the realisation and the classification)
proofSteps: Define the carrier as the dependent pair type Σ n, Nat.Partition n; sort the parts decreasingly and take the product of ZMod (p^{λ_i}) as representative, with its AddCommGroup structure from the Pi instance.
Order: |A_λ| = ∏ p^{λ_i} = p^{Σλ_i} = p^n (ZMod.card and Fintype.card of a Pi type).

Existence of a class for a finite abelian p-group G: apply AddCommGroup.equiv_directSum_zmod_of_finite to get G ≅ ⊕ ℤ/q_i^{e_i}; since G is p-primary every q_i = p (or e_i = 0), so the exponents form a partition of log_p|G|.
Uniqueness: the conjugate partition is recovered from the invariants |p^{i-1}G/p^iG| = p^{λ'_i}, which are isomorphism invariants, and a partition is determined by its conjugate.
The p-torsion count |A_λ[p]| = p^{λ'_1}: each cyclic factor ℤ/p^{λ_j} with λ_j ≥ 1 contributes a factor p.
acceptance: |A_{(1)}| = p, |Aut A_{(1)}| = p − 1; the trivial class has one automorphism.
ℤ/p² and (ℤ/p)² both have order p² and are different classes (conjugate partitions (1,1) and (2)).

nodes.statement: For p prime and a partition λ with conjugate partition λ' and part multiplicities m_i, |Aut(A_λ)| = p^{Σ_i (λ'_i)²} · ∏_i ∏_{s=1}^{m_i} (1 − p^{−s}). nodes.title: Exact count of surjections between finite abelian p-groups
nodes.statement: Let p be prime, X = A_ξ and A = A_α finite abelian p-groups with conjugate partitions x_i = ξ'_i and a_i = α'_i. If x_i < a_i for some i then |Sur(X, A)| = 0. Otherwise |Sur(X, A)| = ∏_{i ≥ 1} p^{x_i a_{i+1}} ∏_{j = a_{i+1}}^{a_i − 1} (p^{x_i} − p^j).
hypotheses: p prime
X, A finite abelian p-groups
proofSteps: Surjectivity of f : X → A is equivalent to surjectivity on each layer: by induction on i, f is onto iff the induced maps p^{i−1}X/p^iX → p^{i−1}A/p^iA are onto (Nakayama over ℤ_p applied to the filtration).

Count homomorphisms layer by layer: choosing the image of a basis of the i-th layer of X amounts to choosing an x_i-tuple in the corresponding layer of A, and the factor p^{x_i a_{i+1}} counts the free choices in deeper layers.

The surjectivity condition on layer i is that the x_i chosen vectors span an a_i-dimensional F_p-space containing the fixed a_{i+1}-dimensional image from deeper layers: the number of such tuples is ∏_{j=a_{i+1}}^{a_i−1}(p^{x_i} − p^j).
If x_i < a_i the layer map cannot be onto, so there is no surjection.
acceptance: |Sur(ℤ/p², ℤ/p)| = p − 1, |Sur(ℤ/p², ℤ/p²)| = p(p − 1) = |Aut(ℤ/p²)|, |Sur(ℤ/p × ℤ/p², ℤ/p²)| = p²(p − 1).

nodes.title: The Cohen–Lenstra measure μ_{p,u}
nodes.statement: For a prime p and an integer u ≥ 0 put c_{p,u} = ∏_{i ≥ u+1} (1 − p^{−i}). The Cohen–Lenstra measure μ_{p,u} is the probability measure on the isomorphism classes L of finite abelian p-groups with μ_{p,u}(A) = c_{p,u} / (|A|^u · |Aut A|). The case u = 0 is the Cohen–Lenstra distribution of EVW §8.1 (imaginary quadratic fields); u = 1 is the real-quadratic distribution. Total mass one is the mass formula (ST.5/cohen-lenstra-mass-formula), which the construction takes as input.
hypotheses: p prime
u ∈ ℕ
proofSteps: Define c_{p,u} as the convergent infinite product ∏_{i≥0} (1 − p^{−(i+u+1)}) (tprod), positive and < 1 because Σ p^{−i} < ∞.
Define the weight w(A) = c_{p,u}/(|A|^u |Aut A|) in [0, ∞] using the carrier's order p^{A.1} and autCard.
By the mass formula the weights sum to 1, so they define a probability mass function (Mathlib PMF).
acceptance: μ_{p,0}(0) = c_{p,0}; c_{3,0} ≈ 0.5601 is the predicted proportion of imaginary quadratic fields with 3 ∤ h (EVW §1.1 prints this as the indivisibility probability 1 − c_3 ≈ 0.440, a misprint recorded as ArithmeticStatistics/E624).

nodes.title: Partitions with parts at least u+1 versus partitions by largest part
nodes.statement: For u, m ≥ 0 let a_m be the number of partitions of m with every part ≥ u + 1 and b_{i,j} the number of partitions of i with largest part exactly j. Then a_m = Σ_{i + uj = m} b_{i,j}; equivalently, as formal power series, ∏_{j ≥ u+1} (1 − q^j)^{−1} = Σ_{n ≥ 0} f_n(q) q^{nu} with f_n(q) = Σ_N b_{N,n} q^N.
hypotheses: u ∈ ℕ
proofSteps: Adding u columns of height j to the Young diagram of a partition of i with largest part j gives a partition of i + uj whose largest part occurs at least u + 1 times, and this is a bijection.
Conjugation exchanges 'largest part occurs at least u + 1 times' with 'every part is at least u + 1'.

nodes.title: Hall's partition identity
nodes.statement: For every n ≥ 0 and a prime p, with q = p^{−1}: f_n(q) := Σ_{N≥0} b_{N,n} q^N = Σ_{λ ⊢ n} 1/|Aut A_λ|, where b_{N,n} counts partitions of N with largest part exactly n. Equivalently f_n(q) = Σ_{μ ⊢ n} q^{Σ μ_i²} ∏_i ψ_{μ_i, μ_{i−1} − μ_i}(q) with ψ_{a,b}(q) = ∏_{i=1}^{a+b}(1 − q^i)/(∏_{i=1}^{a}(1 − q^i) ∏_{i=1}^{b}(1 − q^i)), ψ_{a,∞}(q) = 1/∏_{i=1}^{a}(1 − q^i) and μ_0 = ∞.
hypotheses: p prime
n ∈ ℕ
proofSteps: Given a partition ν of N with largest part n, take the Young diagram D of ν' (height n) and cut out the Durfee-type squares μ_1 × μ_1, μ_2 × μ_2, … along the diagonal (μ_1 largest with (μ_1, μ_1) ∈ D, μ_i largest with (μ_1+…+μ_i, μ_i) ∈ D); then |μ| = n.
The cells to the right of the i-th square form a partition of height ≤ μ_i and width ≤ μ_{i−1} − μ_i, counted by ψ_{μ_i, μ_{i−1}−μ_i}(q); the construction is reversible.

Substitute the automorphism count (ST.5/automorphism-count-of-finite-abelian-p-groups): 1/|Aut A_λ| = q^{Σ(λ'_i)²}∏_i 1/(q)_{λ'_i−λ'_{i+1}}, and the product ∏_i ψ_{μ_i, μ_{i−1}−μ_i}(q) telescopes to ∏_i 1/(q)_{μ_i−μ_{i+1}}; with μ = λ' the right side is Σ_{λ⊢n} 1/|Aut A_λ|.

nodes.title: The groupoid of extensions of finite abelian groups has cardinality one
nodes.statement: For finite abelian groups G and K, consider exact sequences 0 → K →ι B →f G → 0 with B abelian, and isomorphisms of such sequences that are the identity on K and on G. Then Σ over isomorphism classes of sequences of 1/|Aut(sequence)| = 1. Equivalently, Σ_{[B]} #{f ∈ Sur(B, G) : ker f ≅ K}/|Aut B| = 1/|Aut K|.
hypotheses: G, K finite abelian groups
proofSteps: Write G = ⊕_i ℤ/n_i (Mathlib AddCommGroup.equiv_directSum_zmod_of_finite, after splitting into cyclic factors). An extension is determined up to isomorphism by choosing lifts b_i ∈ B of the generators: n_i b_i lies in ι(K), and its class in K/n_iK does not depend on the lift; conversely every tuple (k_i) ∈ ∏_i K/n_iK arises (B = (K ⊕ ℤ^r)/⟨n_i e_i − k_i⟩). So the isomorphism classes are in bijection with ∏_i K/n_iK.
The automorphisms of a sequence are φ = id + ι∘h∘f with h ∈ Hom(G, K) ≅ ∏_i K[n_i].
|K/n_iK| = |K[n_i]| (kernel and cokernel of multiplication by n_i on the finite group K have the same order), so the groupoid cardinality is ∏|K/n_iK| / ∏|K[n_i]| = 1.
For the second form: a fixed B contributes #{(ι, f)}/|Aut B| by orbit counting, and #{(ι, f)} = #{f ∈ Sur(B, G) : ker f ≅ K}·|Aut K|.

G = 0: only B ≅ K contributes, with 1/|Aut K|.

nodes.title: The Cohen–Lenstra constant exceeds one half for odd primes
nodes.statement: For an odd prime ℓ, c_ℓ = ∏_{i≥1}(1 − ℓ^{−i}) > 1/2; hence β = c_ℓ^{−1} − 1 < 1. For ℓ = 2, c_2 ≈ 0.2888 < 1/2 and β > 1.

proofSteps: c_ℓ is increasing in ℓ (each factor increases), so c_ℓ ≥ c_3.
Bound c_3 from below: ∏_{i≥1}(1 − 3^{−i}) ≥ (1 − 1/3)(1 − 1/9)(1 − Σ_{i≥3} 3^{−i}) = (2/3)(8/9)(1 − 1/18) = 0.5597… > 1/2 (using ∏(1 − x_i) ≥ 1 − Σ x_i for the tail, Mathlib geometric series).

nodes.statement: Let ℓ be an odd prime and ν a probability measure on L with ⟨Sur(−, A)⟩_ν = 1 for every A ∈ L. Then ν = μ_{ℓ,0}.

all surjection moments of ν equal 1
proofSteps: Put u_A = |Aut A|·ν(A) ≥ 0. The moment identity reads u_A + Σ_{B ≠ A} (|Sur(B, A)|/|Aut B|) u_B = 1 (EVW (8.2.1)).
By ST.5/cohen-lenstra-moments with u = 0 the same identity holds for u_B = c_ℓ, so β_A := Σ_{B≠A}|Sur(B, A)|/|Aut B| = c_ℓ^{−1} − 1 =: β for every A.
If L ≤ u_B ≤ U for all B then 1 − βU ≤ u_A ≤ 1 − βL; starting from 0 ≤ u ≤ 1 the bounds are alternating partial sums of Σ(−β)^k.
Since β < 1 (ST.5/cohen-lenstra-contraction-constant) both bounds converge to 1/(1 + β) = c_ℓ, so ν(A) = c_ℓ/|Aut A| = μ_{ℓ,0}(A).

nodes.title: Enlargements of a finite abelian ℓ-group
nodes.statement: For finite abelian ℓ-groups A, A' and s ≥ 0, A' is an s-enlargement of A if some surjection A' ↠ A has kernel of order ℓ^s (a 1-enlargement is an enlargement). Equivalently |A'| = ℓ^s|A| and the Young diagram of A is contained in that of A' (a_i ≤ a'_i for the conjugate partitions). The set E_s(A) of isomorphism classes of s-enlargements is finite, with at most p(s + m) elements where ℓ^m = |A|. The surjection is data separate from the isomorphism class.
hypotheses: ℓ prime
proofSteps: Define IsEnlargement ℓ s A' A by the existence of a surjective homomorphism of the representatives with kernel of cardinality ℓ^s.

Characterisation: a finite abelian ℓ-group A' has a quotient isomorphic to A iff α ⊆ α' as Young diagrams (the type of a quotient is contained in the type of the group, and every contained type occurs); the order condition fixes s.
Hence E_s(A) is the image of the partitions of m + s containing α, a finite set of size ≤ p(m + s).
Composition: an s-enlargement of a t-enlargement is an (s+t)-enlargement (compose the surjections, orders multiply).
acceptance: (ℤ/ℓ)² and ℤ/ℓ² are the two 1-enlargements of ℤ/ℓ.

nodes.title: The aggregate enlargement inequality (EVW (8.4.1), corrected proof)
nodes.statement: Let ℓ be prime and X, A finite abelian ℓ-groups with Sur(X, A) ≠ ∅ and |X| > |A|. Then there is a 1-enlargement A' of A with |Sur(X, A')| ≥ (ℓ − 1)|Sur(X, A)|. One may take A' with conjugate partition a'_j = a_j + 1 at the least j with x_j > a_j, and a'_i = a_i otherwise.
hypotheses: ℓ prime
Sur(X, A) ≠ ∅
proofSteps: Since X ↠ A, x_i ≥ a_i for all i (ST.5/exact-surjection-count-formula), and |X| > |A| gives some i with x_i > a_i; let j be the least.
For i < j, x_i = a_i; hence a_{j−1} = x_{j−1} ≥ x_j ≥ a_j + 1, so a' is a conjugate partition, contains α, and A' is a 1-enlargement (ST.5/enlargement-of-finite-abelian-p-groups).

Compare the products of the exact formula for (X, A') and (X, A): the factor at index j − 1 changes by ℓ^{x_{j−1}}/(ℓ^{x_{j−1}} − ℓ^{a_j}) ≥ 1, and index j gains the factor ℓ^{x_j} − ℓ^{a_j} ≥ ℓ^{a_j}(ℓ − 1) ≥ ℓ − 1; all other factors agree.

nodes.title: Tails of surjection counts are dominated by enlargements (EVW Lemma 8.4)
nodes.statement: Let ℓ be an odd prime, ε > 0 and A ∈ L with |A| = ℓ^m. There are c(A) and a finite nonempty M ⊂ L such that for every X ∈ L with |X| > c(A): |Sur(X, A)| ≤ ε · (Σ_{A'∈M} |Sur(X, A')|)/|M|. One may take M = E_s(A) and c(A) = ℓ^s|A| for any s with p(s + m)(ℓ − 1)^{−s} ≤ ε.
hypotheses: ℓ odd prime
proofSteps: Pick s by ST.5/partition-tail-domination; put M = E_s(A) (nonempty: ℤ/ℓ^s ⊕ A).

If Sur(X, A) = ∅ the inequality is trivial. Otherwise iterate ST.5/aggregate-enlargement-inequality s times (possible while |X| > ℓ^t|A|): there is A' ∈ E_s(A) (by IsEnlargement.trans) with |Sur(X, A')| ≥ (ℓ − 1)^s|Sur(X, A)|.
Hence |Sur(X, A)| ≤ (ℓ − 1)^{−s} Σ_{A'∈M}|Sur(X, A')| = (ℓ − 1)^{−s}|M| · (average) ≤ p(s + m)(ℓ − 1)^{−s} · (average) ≤ ε · (average), using |M| ≤ p(s + m) (card_enlargements_le).

nodes.title: Finitely many approximate moments control finitely many masses (EVW Proposition 8.3)
nodes.statement: Let ℓ be an odd prime, ε_0 > 0 and L_0 ⊂ L finite. There exist δ > 0 and a finite L' ⊂ L such that every probability measure ν on L with ⟨Sur(−, A)⟩_ν ∈ [1 − δ, 1 + δ] for all A ∈ L' satisfies |ν(A) − μ_{ℓ,0}(A)| ≤ ε_0 for all A ∈ L_0.

L_0 finite

The masses ν_k(B) lie in [0, 1]; by compactness of [0, 1]^L (Tychonoff, countable index, sequential compactness: Mathlib CompactSpace.tendsto_subseq) pass to a pointwise convergent subsequence ν_k → ν_∞.

Fatou (ENNReal.tsum_eq_liminf_sum_nat) gives ⟨Sur(−, A)⟩_{ν_∞} ≤ 1. For the reverse, split the moment at |B| ≤ c(A) (finitely many B, limits commute) and bound the tail Σ_{|B|>c}ν_k(B)|Sur(B, A)| ≤ ε · max_{A'∈M}⟨Sur(−, A')⟩_{ν_k} ≤ ε(1 + 1/k) by ST.5/finite-enlargement-domination-of-tails; hence ⟨Sur(−, A)⟩_{ν_∞} = 1 for all A.
A = 0 shows ν_∞ is a probability measure; ST.5/moments-determine-the-cohen-lenstra-measure gives ν_∞ = μ, contradicting |ν_k(A) − μ(A)| > ε_0 in the limit.

nodes.statement: Let p be prime, n, u ≥ 0 and M ∈ M_{n×(n+u)}(ℤ_p) Haar-random, viewed as ℤ_p^{n+u} → ℤ_p^n. For every finite abelian p-group A: E|Sur(coker M, A)| = |Sur(ℤ_p^n, A)| · |A|^{−(n+u)} = |A|^{−u} ∏_{i=0}^{r−1}(1 − p^{i−n}), r the p-rank of A. hypotheses: p prime
M Haar-distributed on M_{n×(n+u)}(ℤ_p)
proofSteps: A surjection coker M ↠ A is a surjection F : ℤ_p^n ↠ A with F∘M = 0; so E|Sur(coker M, A)| = Σ_{F ∈ Sur(ℤ_p^n, A)} P(F M = 0) (finite sum, homomorphisms factor through (ℤ/p^e)^n).

|Sur(ℤ_p^n, A)| = |A|^n ∏_{i=0}^{r−1}(1 − p^{i−n}) (a map is onto iff it is onto modulo p; count F_p-surjections F_p^n → F_p^r by Matrix.card_GL_field-type counting and lift).

u = 0, A = ℤ/p: E(p^{rk coker} − 1) = 1 − p^{−n}.

nodes.title: The number of matrices of given rank over a finite field
nodes.statement: For a finite field F with q elements and r ≤ min(m, n), #{M ∈ M_{m×n}(F) : rank M = r} = ∏_{i=0}^{r−1} (q^m − q^i)(q^n − q^i)/(q^r − q^i) = [m choose r]_q ∏_{i=0}^{r−1}(q^n − q^i). Hence P_F(m, n, j) = q^{−mn} ∏_{i=0}^{n−j−1} (q^m − q^i)(q^n − q^i)/(q^{n−j} − q^i).
hypotheses: F finite field with q elements
r ≤ min(m, n)
proofSteps: A rank-r matrix is determined by its column space W ⊆ F^m (dim r) and a surjective linear map F^n ↠ W.
The number of r-dimensional subspaces is the Gaussian binomial [m choose r]_q (ST.5/gaussian-binomial-coefficient, owned by part S of this stage).
Surjections F^n ↠ F^r are counted by choosing r linearly independent rows: ∏_{i<r}(q^n − q^i) (as in Mathlib Matrix.card_GL_field / card_linearIndependent).
acceptance: r = n = m: |GL_n(F_q)|.

nodes.statement: For a finite field F and r, n ≥ 0, P_Sym,F(r, n) is the probability that a uniformly random symmetric r × r matrix over F has kernel of dimension n: #{M = M^T ∈ M_r(F) : dim ker M = n}/|F|^{r(r+1)/2}. Koymans–Pagano's P_Sym(r, n) is P_Sym,F_2(r, n).
hypotheses: F finite field
proofSteps: Symmetric matrices are determined by their r(r+1)/2 entries on and above the diagonal, so there are |F|^{r(r+1)/2} of them.
Define the ratio; the events for n = 0, …, r partition the symmetric matrices.
acceptance: P_Sym,F_2(r, r) = 2^{−r(r+1)/2} (only the zero matrix).

nodes.title: MacWilliams' count of symmetric matrices of given rank
nodes.statement: For a finite field F with q elements and 0 ≤ k ≤ s, writing k = 2h or 2h + 1, the number of symmetric s × s matrices of rank k is N(s, k) = ∏_{i=1}^{h} q^{2i}/(q^{2i} − 1) · ∏_{i=0}^{k−1} (q^{s−i} − 1).
hypotheses: F finite field with q elements
k ≤ s
proofSteps: Recursion on s: a symmetric (s+1) × (s+1) matrix is determined by a symmetric s × s block S, a column v and a corner entry; the rank of the extension is rank S, rank S + 1 or rank S + 2 according to whether v lies in the column space of S and the value of the corner against v^T S^+ v.

Solve the recursion N(s+1, k) = q^k N(s, k) + (q^{s} − q^{k−1})·N(s, k − 1)·(…) + … in closed form and verify it matches the product formula (MacWilliams, Theorem 2); the count is the same for all q (odd q and characteristic 2 give the same totals).
Check: Σ_k N(s, k) = q^{s(s+1)/2}.
acceptance: Exhaustive enumeration over F_2 for s ≤ 4 agrees with the formula (carried out in this blueprint's preparation).

nodes.statement: Over F_2, for every n ≥ 0: lim_{r→∞} P_Sym(r, n) = P_Sym(∞, n) := ∏_{j≥0}(1 − 2^{−(2j+1)}) / ∏_{i=1}^{n}(2^i − 1), and |P_Sym(r, n) − P_Sym(∞, n)| ≤ 2^{n+1−r} for all r ≥ 1. The limits sum to 1.

proofSteps: By ST.5/macwilliams-symmetric-rank-count with k = r − n = 2h or 2h + 1: P_Sym(r, n) = 2^{−n(n+1)/2} ∏_{i=1}^{h}(1 − 2^{−2i})^{−1} ∏_{j=n+1}^{r}(1 − 2^{−j}) (the exponent kr − k(k−1)/2 − r(r+1)/2 simplifies to −n(n+1)/2).

nodes.title: The Koymans–Pagano identity (A.2)
hypotheses: m ∈ ℕ
proofSteps: Probability space: pairs (T, U), T a uniform surjection F_2^{m+1} ↠ F_2^m and U a uniform bilinear pairing F_2^{m+1} × F_2^m → F_2; fix x ≠ 0 in F_2^{m+1}.
P(x ∈ ker T) = 1/(2^{m+1} − 1): ker T is a uniform line.
Let A_{n,x} be the event 'x ∈ leftker U and dim leftker U = n + 1'; P(A_{n,x}) = P(m, m, n)/2^m (x ∈ leftker U has probability 2^{−m}, and then U on a complement is a uniform m × m matrix).

Conditionally on A_{n,x} and T(leftker U) = V (dim V = n), T restricted to leftker U is a uniform surjection onto V, so P(x ∈ ker T | A_{n,x}) = 1/(2^{n+1} − 1); summing gives the identity (the events A_{n,x} for n = 0…m cover the conditioning needed in KP's (A.7)).
acceptance: Verified exactly for m ≤ 11 in this blueprint's preparation.

nodes.title: The Cohen–Lenstra–Martinet predicted surjection moment
nodes.statement: For a finite group G, a prime p, a finite F_p[G]-module Z (representation ρ) and elements σ_v ∈ G (one for each infinite place v of the base field k, σ_v in the conjugacy class of complex conjugation over v), the predicted moment is M(Z, σ) = ∏_v |Z^{σ_v}|^{−1}, where Z^{σ} = {z : ρ(σ)z = z}.
hypotheses: G finite group
p prime
Z a finite F_p[G]-module
proofSteps: Define the product over the list σ of |ker(ρ(σ_v) − 1)|, then invert.
Since Z^{σ} is an F_p-subspace, M(Z, σ) = p^{−Σ_v dim Z^{σ_v}}.
acceptance: G = C_2 acting on F_p (p odd) by −1, σ the generator (a complex place of an imaginary quadratic field): M = 1, the Cohen–Lenstra u = 0 moment.
σ = 1 (a real place): M = 1/p, the u = 1 moment.

nodes.title: The Cohen–Lenstra–Martinet average conjecture (LOWW (1.1))
nodes.statement: Conjecture (a proposition). For a number field k, a transitive permutation group G and a prime p ∤ |G|, there is c_{k,G,p} > 0 with lim_{X→∞} |E_k(G, X)|^{−1} Σ_{K∈E_k(G,X)} |Cl_K[p]| = c_{k,G,p}, where E_k(G, X) is the set of extensions K/k (in a fixed algebraic closure) with Galois-closure group G and Disc(K) ≤ X. Cohen, Lenstra and Martinet fix the enriched signature; (1.1) additionally assumes that the frequencies of enriched signatures exist. Proved cases: (S_2, 3) (Davenport–Heilbronn, Datskovsky–Wright), (S_3, 2) (Bhargava) and, by LOWW, every transitive 2-group with a transposition and p = 3; these proofs are ST.3's.
hypotheses: k a number field
G a transitive permutation group
p a prime not dividing |G|
proofSteps: Take the family E_k(G, X) from ST.3 (G-extension families ordered by discriminant) as a finite set of subfields of an algebraic closure.
State the existence of a positive limit of the average of |Cl_K[p]| (the p-torsion of the class group of the ring of integers).
acceptance: For (G, p) = (S_2, 3), k = ℚ the proved constants are 2 (imaginary) and 4/3 (real) per signature; the conjecture (1.1) averages over both signatures.
The constant is not determined by (1.1) alone; the Cohen–Martinet framework predicts it per enriched signature (ST.5/cohen-martinet-surjection-moment-conjecture).

nodes.title: The Cohen–Martinet surjection-moment conjecture (Wang–Wood form)
nodes.statement: Conjecture (a proposition). For a family of Galois G-extensions K̃/k with fixed decomposition data σ_v at the infinite places, ordered by discriminant, and a finite F_p[G]-module V with no trivial constituent (p ∤ |G|), the average of |Sur_G(Cl_{K̃/k}, V)| tends to ∏_v |V^{σ_v}|^{−1}. p ∤ |G|

fixed decomposition groups at infinity

nodes.title: Relative 3-torsion as a count of equivariant maps to an irreducible module
nodes.statement: Let G = C_2 ≀ H be a transitive 2-group with a transposition, S_K the stabilizer of a point, S_F = C_2^d ⋊ Stab_H(1), U the sign representation of S_F/S_K over F_3 and V = Ind_{S_F}^G U. Then V is irreducible, and for a G-extension K̃/k with index-2 subfield F of K: h_3(K/F) = |Hom_{S_F}(Cl_{K̃/k}, U)| = |Hom_G(Cl_{K̃/k}, V)| = 1 + |Sur_G(Cl_{K̃/k}, V)|.
hypotheses: G = C_2 ≀ H transitive with a transposition
proofSteps: With e = |S_K|^{−1}Σ_{g∈S_K} g, multiplication by e maps Cl_{K̃/k}/3 onto Cl_{K/k}/3 and every S_F-map to U factors through it; Cl_{K/F}/3 is the −1 eigenspace of S_F/S_K, so h_3(K/F) = |Hom_{S_F}(Cl, U)|.
Frobenius reciprocity: Hom_{S_F}(Cl, U) ≅ Hom_G(Cl, Ind U).
V is irreducible: its basis e_i = (1 ⋊ h_i)e_1 is permuted by H and each sign can be changed independently by C_2^d, so any nonzero vector generates V.
Every nonzero G-map to an irreducible module is onto (image is a nonzero submodule), so |Hom_G| = 1 + |Sur_G|.
acceptance: G = D_4 (H = C_2): V is 2-dimensional over F_3 and h_3(K/F) = 1 + |Sur_{D_4}(Cl, V)|.

nodes.title: The Cohen–Lenstra–Martinet prediction 1 + 3^{−u} for h_3(K/F) (LOWW Proposition 7.1)
nodes.statement: In the setting of ST.5/relative-three-torsion-as-irreducible-hom-count, for a family of C_2 ≀ H-extensions K/k with relative unit rank u = rk O_K^× − rk O_F^×: Σ_v dim V^{σ_v} = u, so the Cohen–Martinet moment conjecture for V predicts that the average of h_3(K/F) tends to 1 + 3^{−u}. This is the value LOWW prove (Theorem 1.2 = 6.11, at ST.3), so their theorem confirms a new case of the heuristics.
hypotheses: G = C_2 ≀ H transitive with a transposition
a family with fixed relative unit rank u
the Cohen–Martinet moment conjecture for V
proofSteps: By ST.5/relative-three-torsion-as-irreducible-hom-count, h_3(K/F) = 1 + |Sur_G(Cl, V)|; average and apply the conjecture: the limit is 1 + ∏_v |V^{σ_v}|^{−1}.

σ_v = x_v ⋊ r_v permutes the basis lines F_3 e_i: a fixed point of r_v with trivial x_v-coordinate gives a trivial line (an infinite place of F split in K), a 2-cycle gives a regular representation of σ_v with one trivial dimension (a place of F ramified over k); a fixed point with nontrivial coordinate contributes 0.
Hence Σ_v dim V^{σ_v} is the number of infinite places of F not ramified in K, which is the relative unit rank u; so ∏_v|V^{σ_v}|^{−1} = 3^{−u} (cohenMartinetPredictedMoment_eq_pow).
acceptance: G = C_2 (H trivial), k = ℚ: h_3(K/ℚ) = h_3(K), u = 0 for imaginary and 1 for real quadratic K: predictions 2 and 4/3 (Davenport–Heilbronn).
The prediction depends only on u, not on the individual decomposition groups.

nodes.title: The Cohen–Lenstra–Martinet prediction for h_3(K/k) (LOWW §7.2)
nodes.statement: For G = C_2 ≀ H with W = Ind_{S_F}^G F_3 the permutation representation of H and W' = W/F_3: under the Cohen–Martinet moment conjectures for V and for the irreducible constituents V_i (multiplicity a_i) of W' = ∏_i V_i^{a_i}, the predicted average of h_3(K/k) over G-extensions with given behaviour at infinity is (1 + x_V) ∏_i Σ_{j=0}^{a_i} [a_i choose j]_{q_i} x_i^j, where x_Z = ∏_v|Z^{σ_v}|^{−1}, x_i = x_{V_i} and q_i = |End_G(V_i)| (Gaussian binomial). When W' is irreducible this is (1 + 3^{−u(K/F)})(1 + 3^{−u(F/k)}), u(·/·) the relative unit ranks. (The printed general factor 1 + x_i + … + x_i^{a_i} is wrong for a_i ≥ 2; ArithmeticStatistics/E623.)
hypotheses: G = C_2 ≀ H transitive with a transposition
the Cohen–Martinet moment conjectures for V and the constituents of W'
proofSteps: Ind_{S_K}^G F_3 = W × V and h_3(K/k) = |Hom_{S_K}(Cl_{K̃/k}, F_3)| = |Hom_G(Cl_{K̃/k}, W' × V)| (Cl_{K̃/k} has no trivial quotient).

Split Hom_G into the V-part and the W'-part (Hom_G of a product is the product of Hom_G's). For Z = V_i^{a_i}: |Hom_G(Cl, Z)| = Σ_{W ≤ Z} |Sur_G(Cl, W)|, the submodules W ≅ V_i^j number [a_i choose j]_{q_i}, and the predicted moment of V_i^j is x_i^j (|(V_i^j)^{σ}| = |V_i^{σ}|^j); so the predicted average is Σ_j [a_i choose j]_{q_i} x_i^j.
Count fixed points: ∏_v|W^{σ_v}| = 3^{r_1(F)+r_2(F)} and ∏_v|(W')^{σ_v}| = 3^{u(F/k)}; with Proposition 7.1 for V the irreducible case gives the product formula.
acceptance: Example 7.2 (k = ℚ, G = D_4): predicted averages of h_3(K) are 40/27, 16/9, 8/3, 8/3 for the four group signatures (), (24), (13)(24), (12)(34).
The same families have proven averages ≈ 1.12, 1.34, 2.01, 1.41 (ST.5/dihedral-quartic-proven-average-versus-prediction).

nodes.title: The finite-level enhanced Cohen–Lenstra laws
nodes.statement: For a prime ℓ, g ≥ 0 and a tuple n = (n_1, …, n_k) of positive integers, the finite-level law on k-tuples of classes is CL^{(g)}_{n,ℓ}(H_1, …, H_k) = Haar_g(F ∈ End_g(ℤ_ℓ) : coker(1 − F^{n_j}) ≅ H_j for all j). The enhanced law CL_{n,ℓ} (Lipnowski–Tsimerman Definition 5.16, distinct n_j) is its limit as g → ∞, defined only where the limit exists (EnhancedCohenLenstraLimitExists); CL_{n,S} is the product over ℓ ∈ S.
hypotheses: ℓ prime
n_j ≥ 1
proofSteps: Define the finite-g law as the Haar measure of the set of F with the prescribed cokernels (padicMatrixHaar on M_g(ℤ_ℓ)).

nodes.title: The probability that 1 − F² is invertible modulo 2
hypotheses: g ∈ ℕ
proofSteps: In characteristic 2, 1 − F² = (1 − F)², which is invertible iff 1 − F is.
F ↦ 1 − F is a bijection of M_g(F_2), so the count equals |GL_g(F_2)| (Matrix.card_GL_field) out of 2^{g²} matrices.

For the ℓ-adic law: coker(1 − F) = coker(1 − F²) = 0 iff 1 − F² is invertible over ℤ_2 iff it is invertible mod 2 (enhancedCokernelLaw_zero_zero), and Haar measure pushes forward to the uniform measure mod 2.

The limit c_{2,0} is positive, as Lipnowski–Tsimerman need.

g ∈ ℕ
proofSteps: 1 − F² = (1 − F)(1 + F) is invertible iff neither 1 nor −1 is an eigenvalue of F (1 ≠ −1 since ℓ is odd).

nodes.statement: Conjecture (a proposition about one family). Let p be a prime, S a finite set of primes not containing p, n = (n_1, …, n_k) distinct positive integers, and (F_g)_g a family of g-dimensional abelian varieties over F_p with sampling laws P_g. nodes.title: Maximal isotropic subspaces of a quadratic space over 𝔽_p
nodes.statement: Let K be a field, V a finite-dimensional K-vector space and Q : V → K a quadratic form (Mathlib QuadraticForm, any characteristic), with polar form b_Q(x, y) = Q(x + y) − Q(x) − Q(y). For a subspace W let W^⊥ be its b_Q-orthogonal. W is maximal isotropic if Q|_W = 0 and W^⊥ = W; I_V denotes the set of maximal isotropic subspaces. (V, Q) is nondegenerate if b_Q is nondegenerate, and weakly metabolic if moreover I_V ≠ ∅. For K = 𝔽_p this is Poonen–Rains' definition for a quadratic form with values in (1/p)ℤ/ℤ ≅ 𝔽_p. nodes.title: Reduction of maximal isotropic subspaces to X^⊥/X
nodes.statement: Let (V, Q) be a nondegenerate quadratic space over a field K and X ⊆ V an isotropic subspace (Q|_X = 0). Then X ⊆ X^⊥, the quotient X^⊥/X carries the induced quadratic form Q_X(v + X) := Q(v), which is well defined and has nondegenerate polar form, and dim X^⊥/X = dim V − 2 dim X. For W ∈ I_V, the subspace (W ∩ X^⊥) + X lies in I_V and its image π_X(W) := ((W ∩ X^⊥) + X)/X lies in I_{X^⊥/X}. The map π_X : I_V → I_{X^⊥/X} is the isotropic reduction map; if X ⊆ W then π_X(W) = W/X, and for X ⊆ Y isotropic, π_{Y/X} ∘ π_X = π_Y.
hypotheses: (V, Q) nondegenerate, finite-dimensional
X isotropic: Q|_X = 0
proofSteps: Well-definedness of Q_X: for x ∈ X and v ∈ X^⊥, Q(v + x) = Q(v) + Q(x) + b_Q(v, x) = Q(v).

Nondegeneracy of Q_X: if v ∈ X^⊥ pairs to zero with X^⊥ then v ∈ (X^⊥)^⊥ = X (double orthogonal for a nondegenerate form, from mathlib:LinearMap.BilinForm.finrank_add_finrank_orthogonal and inclusion).
Dimension: dim X^⊥ = dim V − dim X by nondegeneracy, so dim X^⊥/X = dim V − 2 dim X (mathlib:Submodule.finrank_quotient_add_finrank).
W' := (W ∩ X^⊥) + X is isotropic: Q vanishes on W ∩ X^⊥ ⊆ W and on X, and b_Q(W ∩ X^⊥, X) = 0.

dim W' = n when dim V = 2n: dim(W ∩ X^⊥) = 2n − dim(W + X) = n − dim X + dim(W ∩ X) (orthogonal of a sum, W^⊥ = W), so dim W' = dim(W ∩ X^⊥) + dim X − dim(W ∩ X) = n; an isotropic subspace of dimension n in a nondegenerate 2n-space equals its orthogonal, so W' ∈ I_V. Its image in X^⊥/X is maximal isotropic by the lattice correspondence between subspaces of X^⊥ containing X and subspaces of X^⊥/X.
Compatibility π_{Y/X} ∘ π_X = π_Y: unwind the definitions using the third isomorphism theorem.
acceptance: X = 0: π_0 is the identity of I_V.
V the hyperbolic plane and X = K × 0: X^⊥/X = 0 and π_X is the constant map to {0}.
dim X^⊥/X = 2n − 2 dim X when dim V = 2n.

nodes.title: Every fibre of the isotropic reduction map has ∏(p^{n−i} + 1) elements
nodes.statement: Let (V, Q) be a weakly metabolic quadratic space of dimension 2n over 𝔽_p and X ⊆ V an isotropic subspace. Then every fibre of π_X : I_V → I_{X^⊥/X} has exactly ∏_{i=1}^{dim X} (p^{n−i} + 1) elements.

Then X_n is distributed as a sum of independent Bernoulli variables B_1, …, B_n with Prob(B_i = 1) = 1/(p^{i−1} + 1); equivalently Σ_{d≥0} a_{d,n} z^{d} = ∏_{i=0}^{n−1} (z + p^{i})/(1 + p^{i}), i.e. Σ_{Z ∈ I_V} z^{dim(Z ∩ W)} = ∏_{i=0}^{n−1} (z + p^{i}) as polynomials in z.

nodes.title: The Poonen–Rains distribution X_{Sel_p}
nodes.statement: For a prime p, the Poonen–Rains distribution is the probability measure on ℤ_{≥0} with Prob(X_{Sel_p} = d) = a_d := c_p ∏_{j=1}^{d} p/(p^{j} − 1), where c_p := ∏_{j≥0} (1 + p^{−j})^{−1} = (1/2) ∏_{i≥0} (1 − p^{−(2i+1)}). (The j = 0 factor is 1/2.) That the a_d sum to 1 is the theorem ArithmeticStatistics:ST.5/intersection-law-converges-to-poonen-rains, which is used to package the weights as a probability mass function.
hypotheses: p prime

nodes.title: Proportion of invertible alternating matrices over 𝔽_p
nodes.statement: Let M_m(𝔽_p)^alt be the set of alternating m × m matrices over 𝔽_p (zero diagonal, Aᵗ = −A), of cardinality p^{m(m−1)/2}, and GL_m(𝔽_p)^alt its subset of invertible ones. If m is odd, GL_m(𝔽_p)^alt = ∅. If m is even, #GL_m(𝔽_p)^alt / #M_m(𝔽_p)^alt = ∏_{i=1}^{m/2} (1 − p^{1−2i}).
hypotheses: p prime
proofSteps: #M_m(𝔽_p)^alt = p^{m(m−1)/2}: an alternating matrix is determined freely by its strictly upper triangular entries.

Odd m: det A = det Aᵗ = det(−A) = −det A in odd dimension, and for p = 2 an alternating (zero-diagonal symmetric) form of odd rank does not exist; in all characteristics the rank of an alternating form is even (symplectic basis), so A is singular.

Even m, induction on m: the first column of an invertible alternating A is any of the p^{m−1} − 1 nonzero vectors with zero first entry; the number of completions does not depend on it (a change of basis in GL_m(𝔽_p) fixing e_1 moves any admissible column to any other), and splitting off the hyperbolic plane spanned by e_1 and a partner leaves p^{m−2} free coupling entries times an invertible alternating (m − 2)-matrix: #GL_m^alt = (p^{m−1} − 1) p^{m−2} #GL_{m−2}^alt.
Divide by p^{m(m−1)/2} = p^{2m−3} p^{(m−2)(m−3)/2}: the factor is (p^{m−1} − 1)/p^{m−1} = 1 − p^{1−m}; with m = 2i this is 1 − p^{1−2i}.
acceptance: m = 2: the invertible alternating 2 × 2 matrices are [[0, a], [−a, 0]] with a ≠ 0: ratio (p − 1)/p = 1 − p^{−1}.
p = 2, m = 4: 28 of the 64 alternating matrices are invertible, and (1 − 2^{−1})(1 − 2^{−3}) = 7/16 = 28/64.

nodes.title: Symplectic finite abelian p-groups and their symplectic automorphism groups
nodes.statement: A symplectic p-group is a finite abelian p-group G with a nondegenerate alternating bilinear pairing [ , ] : G × G → ℚ_p/ℤ_p; Sp(G) is the group of automorphisms preserving [ , ]. G admits such a pairing if and only if G ≅ H × H for a finite abelian p-group H, and any two symplectic structures on the same group are isomorphic; hence isomorphism classes of symplectic p-groups are the classes of groups H × H, indexed by partitions all of whose parts occur with even multiplicity (ArithmeticStatistics:ST.5/isomorphism-classes-of-finite-abelian-p-groups), and #Sp(G) depends only on the class of G.
hypotheses: p prime
G finite abelian p-group
proofSteps: Define the pairing condition (bilinear into ℚ_p/ℤ_p, alternating [x, x] = 0, nondegenerate: the adjoint G → Hom(G, ℚ_p/ℤ_p) is bijective).

Normal form: a nondegenerate alternating pairing on a finite abelian p-group has a symplectic basis {e_i, f_i} with ⟨e_i⟩ ≅ ⟨f_i⟩ ≅ ℤ/p^{a_i} and [e_i, f_i] = p^{−a_i}; induct on the exponent by splitting off a hyperbolic pair generated by an element of maximal order and a partner of equal order (routine).
Existence on H × H: the standard pairing [(h, χ), (h', χ')] := χ'(h) − χ(h') on H × H^∨ with H^∨ ≅ H; uniqueness follows from the normal form.
acceptance: G = (ℤ/p)²: Sp(G) = SL_2(𝔽_p), of order p(p² − 1).
G = ℤ/p has no symplectic structure.
G = 0: Sp(G) is trivial.
