nodes.title: Imaginary discriminant slices over F_q(t) are monic squarefree polynomials of odd degree
nodes.statement: Let q be odd and n ≥ 1. The quadratic extensions K of F_q(t) whose completion at ∞ is F_q((t^{−1}))(√(t)) (Wood's imaginary infinity type) and whose discriminant has norm q^{2n} (Wood's slice IQ_{=q^{2n}}) are exactly the fields F_q(t)(√f) for f monic squarefree of degree 2n − 1, each obtained from exactly one f. Consequently #IQ_{=q^{2n}} = q^{2n−1} − q^{2n−2} for n ≥ 2 and = q for n = 1.
hypotheses: q odd
Wood's imaginary infinity type fixes the square class of the leading coefficient (the completion at ∞ is the one generated by √t)
proofSteps: A quadratic extension of F_q(t) is F_q(t)(√f) with f ∈ F_q[t] squarefree, unique up to (F_q^×)² (ST.5/odd-degree-quadratic-function-field-family).

The place ∞ ramifies iff deg f is odd; for odd deg f the completion at ∞ is F_q((t^{−1}))(√(a t)) with a the leading coefficient, and it equals the prescribed one iff a is a square; choosing the square-class representative with a = 1 gives a unique monic f.
The discriminant divisor is the zero divisor of f plus the ramified place ∞, of degree deg f + 1, so norm q^{2n} ⇔ deg f = 2n − 1.
The count is ST.4/count-of-squarefree-monic-polynomials-over-a-finite-field in degree 2n − 1.
acceptance: n = 1: IQ_{=q²} consists of the q fields F_q(t)(√(t − c)), c ∈ F_q.
The other ramified square class at ∞ (leading coefficient a nonsquare) is excluded from IQ; it belongs to neither IQ nor RQ (Wood §2 p.5).

nodes.title: Real discriminant slices over F_q(t) are monic squarefree polynomials of even degree
nodes.statement: Let q be odd and n ≥ 1. The quadratic extensions K of F_q(t) split completely at ∞ and with discriminant of norm q^{2n} (Wood's slice RQ_{=q^{2n}}) are exactly the fields F_q(t)(√f) for f monic squarefree of degree 2n, each from exactly one f. Hence #RQ_{=q^{2n}} = q^{2n} − q^{2n−1}. The place ∞ contributes nothing to the discriminant.
hypotheses: q odd
proofSteps: ∞ splits in F_q(t)(√f) iff deg f is even and the leading coefficient is a square in F_q; normalise it to 1.
∞ is then unramified, so the discriminant divisor is the zero divisor of f, of degree deg f; norm q^{2n} ⇔ deg f = 2n.
Count by ST.4/count-of-squarefree-monic-polynomials-over-a-finite-field in degree 2n ≥ 2.
acceptance: n = 1: q² − q fields.
The discriminant exponent is Σ n_i = 2n, not Σ n_i + 1 (Wood p.25 copies the imaginary sentence; sourceIssues ArithmeticStatistics/E671).

nodes.title: The generalized dihedral group A ⋊ Z/2 and its involution class
nodes.statement: Let A be a finite abelian group of odd order. Put G_A := A ⋊ Z/2, where the generator τ of Z/2 acts on A by inversion, and let c_A ⊂ G_A be the set of elements with nontrivial image in Z/2, i.e. c_A = {aτ : a ∈ A}. Then (i) c_A is exactly the set of involutions of G_A; (ii) c_A is a single conjugacy class, stable under invertible powers (hence a rational class); (iii) c_A generates G_A; (iv) if A ≠ 0 the centre of G_A is trivial; (v) (G_A, c_A) is nonsplitting: for every subgroup H ≤ G_A, c_A ∩ H is empty or a single H-conjugacy class. For A of order a power of an odd prime ℓ and q prime to 2ℓ, the Hurwitz scheme X_n := Hn^{c_A}_{G_A,n} ⊗ F_q of tame G_A-covers of A¹ branched at n points with all finite inertia in c_A is the scheme of EVW §8.6.
hypotheses: |A| odd (for (i), (ii), (v))
A ≠ 0 for (iv); for A = 0, G_A = Z/2 has full centre and is treated separately as the trivial moment
proofSteps: Construct the inversion action Z/2 → Aut(A) and the semidirect product (Mathlib SemidirectProduct); c_A is the preimage of the nontrivial element under rightHom.
(i) (aτ)² = a·τaτ^{−1} = a − a = 0, while an element a ≠ 0 of A has odd order; so involutions are exactly c_A.
(ii) b(aτ)b^{−1} = (a + 2b)τ and 2 is invertible on A, so A acts transitively on c_A; invertible powers of an involution are itself.
(iii) (aτ)(0τ) = a, so ⟨c_A⟩ contains A and τ.
(iv) a central element commutes with τ, forcing 2a = 0 hence a = 0 on the A-part, and aτ is not central when A ≠ 0.

(v) For H ≤ G_A meeting c_A, H = (H ∩ A) ⋊ ⟨a₀τ⟩ and c_A ∩ H = {(h + a₀)τ : h ∈ H ∩ A} = one (H ∩ A)-orbit by (ii) applied to the odd group H ∩ A. This is the instance of EVW Lemma 3.2 used in §8.6; the general odd-index lemma belongs to the Hurwitz homological-stability roadmap.
acceptance: A = Z/3: G_A ≅ S_3 and c_A is the class of transpositions.
A = 0: G_A = Z/2 is not centre-free.
A = Z/2 (even order): c_A = {τ, aτ} consists of two central involutions of the Klein group, so (ii) and (iv) fail.

nodes.title: Pairs (L, α) of a quadratic extension and a class-group surjection
nodes.statement: Let q be odd, n odd, L ∈ S_n with ring O_L (integral closure of F_q[t] in L), and A a finite abelian group. A pair (L, α) consists of L and a surjective homomorphism α : Cl(O_L) → A. Two pairs (L, α), (L', α') are isomorphic if there is a K-isomorphism φ : L → L' with α' ∘ φ_* = α. The nontrivial automorphism σ of L/K acts on Cl(O_L) by −1, so (L, α) ≅ (L, β) iff β = ±α. The moment m_A(L) := |Sur(Cl(O_L), A)| counts pairs with fixed L before identification.
hypotheses: q odd; n odd
A finite abelian (in the application an ℓ-group, ℓ odd)
proofSteps: Define the class group of O_L (Mathlib ClassGroup of the integral closure), the set of surjections and the involution α ↦ −α.
σ acts by −1 on Cl(O_L): for a fractional ideal I, I·σ(I) is the extension of the norm ideal from F_q[t], a principal ideal domain, hence principal.
For |A| odd and A ≠ 0, −α ≠ α for every surjection α (else 2α = 0, forcing α = 0), so the sign action on Sur(Cl(O_L), A) is free.
acceptance: A = 0: m_A(L) = 1 for every L (the unique map is surjective).
For A ≠ 0 of odd order, m_A(L) is even.

nodes.title: The σ-anti-invariant quotient of the unramified pro-ℓ group is the ℓ-part of the class group
nodes.statement: Let q be odd, ℓ an odd prime not dividing q, n odd and L ∈ S_n with nontrivial automorphism σ over K = F_q(t). Let J_L be the Galois group of the maximal abelian everywhere unramified pro-ℓ extension of L, and J'_L := J_L/(1 + σ)J_L its largest quotient on which σ acts by −1. Class field theory gives an exact sequence 0 → Cl(O_L)_ℓ → J_L → Ẑ_ℓ → 0 on which σ acts trivially on Ẑ_ℓ and by −1 on Cl(O_L)_ℓ, and the snake lemma yields a canonical isomorphism J'_L ≅ Cl(O_L)_ℓ. Here Cl(O_L)_ℓ is the ℓ-primary part, and Cl(O_L) ≅ Pic⁰(C_L)(F_q) because C_L has a unique point over ∞.
hypotheses: q odd, ℓ odd prime, ℓ ∤ q
n odd (so ∞ is ramified and has a unique, rational point above it)
proofSteps: Import from the function-field class field theory owner (FunctionFieldArithmetic:FA.4): the unramified abelian pro-ℓ quotient sits in 0 → Pic⁰(C_L)(F_q)_ℓ → J_L → Ẑ_ℓ → 0 with the degree map to Gal(F̄_q/F_q)_ℓ.
Identify Pic⁰(C_L)(F_q) with Cl(O_L) via I ↦ D_I − deg(D_I)·∞ (unique rational point ∞ over ∞ of P¹).
σ acts by −1 on Cl(O_L) (ST.5/class-group-surjection-pair) and trivially on the constant-field quotient.

Apply the snake lemma to multiplication by 1 + σ on the sequence; since ℓ is odd, (1 + σ) is invertible on Ẑ_ℓ (acts by 2) and zero on Cl(O_L)_ℓ, giving J_L/(1+σ)J_L ≅ Cl(O_L)_ℓ/(1+σ)Cl(O_L)_ℓ = Cl(O_L)_ℓ.
acceptance: Surjections onto an ℓ-group A factor through the ℓ-primary part, so Sur(Cl(O_L), A) = Sur(J'_L, A).
For ℓ = 2 the quotient J_L/(1 + σ)J_L is not the 2-part of the class group (2 is not invertible).

nodes.title: F_q-points of the dihedral Hurwitz scheme classify class-group surjections up to sign
nodes.statement: Let q be odd, ℓ an odd prime with ℓ ∤ q, A a nontrivial finite abelian ℓ-group, (G_A, c_A) the generalized dihedral datum and X_n = Hn^{c_A}_{G_A,n} ⊗ F_q, n odd. There is a bijection between X_n(F_q) and the set of isomorphism classes of pairs (L, α) with L ∈ S_n and α : Cl(O_L) → A surjective. Given (L, α), compose α with J'_L ≅ Cl(O_L)_ℓ, extend to Gal(F_L/K) = J'_L ⋊ ⟨τ⟩ → G_A (unique up to A-conjugacy), and take the fixed field F_α: a tame G_A-cover of P¹ over F_q, geometrically connected, branched exactly where L/K is (the n roots of f and ∞, since F_α/L is unramified), a point of Hn^{c_A}_{G_A,n}: n branch points in A¹ with inertia generated by elements of c_A, plus ramification at ∞; conversely a tame G_A-cover with inertia in c_A branched at n points of A¹ has X/A → P¹ ramified at ∞ (odd number of finite branch points) and X → X/A étale, giving (L, α) by class field theory.
hypotheses: q odd; ℓ odd prime, ℓ ∤ q
A nontrivial finite abelian ℓ-group
n odd
G_A centre-free, so F_q-points of the Hurwitz scheme are covers defined over F_q (not only Galois-stable geometric classes)
proofSteps: Import the Hurwitz scheme Hn^c_{G,n}, finite étale over Conf_n over Z[1/|G|], and, for centre-free G and any field k of characteristic prime to |G|, the bijection between Hn^c_{G,n}(k) and isomorphism classes of tame G-covers of P¹_k branched at n points of A¹ with finite inertia in c (InverseGaloisAndArithmeticFundamentalGroups:IG.5; EVW §§7.1, 7.3; PAPER-ELLENBERG-VENKATESH-WESTERLAND-16 items /63–/65).

Forward map: by ST.5/involution-quotient-of-the-unramified-pro-l-group and the splitting (8.7.1) of 1 → J'_L → Gal(F_L/K) → Z/2 → 1 (ℓ odd), α gives g_α : Gal(F_L/K) → G_A, well defined up to A-conjugacy since all involutions of G_A are A-conjugate (ST.5/generalized-dihedral-cover-datum (ii)).
Ramification: F_α/L is unramified, so the branch points are those of L/K; each inertia group maps onto an order-2 subgroup generated by an element of c_A; F_q is algebraically closed in F_α.

Inverse: for a tame G_A-cover X → P¹ with inertia in c_A branched at n points of A¹, X → X/A is étale over A¹ (local computation: inertia meets A trivially); X/A → P¹ has an odd number of finite branch points, hence is ramified at ∞, where the inertia is cyclic of order 2 mapping onto Z/2, so X → X/A is étale everywhere; class field theory (FunctionFieldArithmetic:FA.4) turns the étale A-cover into α.
Check the two constructions are mutually inverse on isomorphism classes, using that (L, α) ≅ (L, β) iff β = ±α (ST.5/class-group-surjection-pair).
acceptance: A = Z/3: the points of X_n(F_q) are S_3-covers whose quadratic resolvent is in S_n.
The bijection is with isomorphism classes of pairs, i.e. with pairs modulo α ~ −α; the marked count is twice the point count (ST.5/factor-two-point-count-identity).

nodes.title: The moment sum is twice the number of Hurwitz points
nodes.statement: In the setting of ST.5/hurwitz-points-classify-class-group-surjections (q odd, ℓ odd, ℓ ∤ q, A a nontrivial finite abelian ℓ-group, n odd): Σ_{L ∈ S_n} m_A(L) = 2|X_n(F_q)|. For A = 0 the average of m_A over S_n is exactly 1.
hypotheses: as in ST.5/hurwitz-points-classify-class-group-surjections
proofSteps: Σ_{L ∈ S_n} m_A(L) counts pairs (L, α) with α surjective, L running over S_n (each field once).
Isomorphism classes of pairs with fixed L are the orbits of α ↦ −α; for A ≠ 0 of odd order this action is free (ST.5/class-group-surjection-pair), so every class has exactly 2 elements.
Distinct L ∈ S_n are non-isomorphic over K, so the classes over different L are distinct; apply the bijection of ST.5/hurwitz-points-classify-class-group-surjections.
acceptance: A = 0 is excluded from the factor 2: m_0 ≡ 1 and the sign action is trivial.
Dividing by |S_n| = 2(q^n − q^{n−1}) (n ≥ 3) turns the identity into average m_A = |X_n(F_q)|/(q^n − q^{n−1}).

nodes.title: The empirical law of ℓ-primary class groups in S_n
nodes.statement: Let q be odd, ℓ prime and n odd. The empirical law ν_n = ν_{q,ℓ,n} is the probability measure on the set of isomorphism classes of finite abelian ℓ-groups with ν_n(A) := #{L ∈ S_n : Cl(O_L)_ℓ ≅ A}/|S_n|, where Cl(O_L)_ℓ is the ℓ-primary part of the (finite) class group. Its A-moment Σ_B ν_n(B)|Sur(B, A)| equals the average of m_A(L) = |Sur(Cl(O_L), A)| over S_n, because surjections onto an ℓ-group factor through the ℓ-primary part.
hypotheses: q odd, ℓ prime, n odd
classes of finite abelian ℓ-groups as in ST.5/isomorphism-classes-of-finite-abelian-p-groups
proofSteps: Class groups Cl(O_L) are finite (function-field class number finiteness, via Pic⁰(C_L)(F_q) finite); their ℓ-primary parts are finite abelian ℓ-groups, each isomorphic to exactly one class.
Define ν_n(A) as the proportion; computing it over polynomials P_n instead of S_n gives the same value since every class of S_n has (q − 1)/2 representatives.
Total mass one: the events Cl(O_L)_ℓ ≅ A partition S_n.
Moment identity: Sur(Cl(O_L), A) = Sur(Cl(O_L)_ℓ, A) for A an ℓ-group (restriction to the primary part is a bijection, the prime-to-ℓ part mapping to 0).
acceptance: ν_1 is the Dirac mass at the trivial group (genus 0: Cl(O_L) = 0).
Using the whole class group Cl(O_L) ≅ A instead of the ℓ-part does not define a probability measure on ℓ-groups (EVW p.777 prints Cl(O_L) ≃ A; sourceIssues ArithmeticStatistics/E666).

nodes.title: Upper and lower densities along odd degrees
nodes.statement: For a real sequence u : ℕ → ℝ, its upper (lower) odd-degree density is limsup (liminf) of u(n) as n → ∞ through odd n. For q odd, ℓ prime and A a finite abelian ℓ-group, δ^+(q, A) and δ^−(q, A) are the upper and lower odd-degree densities of n ↦ ν_{q,ℓ,n}(A). For fixed q they need not coincide; the degree limit n → ∞ is taken before q → ∞.
hypotheses: u bounded (for ν_n(A) ∈ [0, 1] automatically)
proofSteps: Define δ^± via Mathlib Filter.limsup (and its order dual liminf) of u(2m + 1) along m → ∞.
For bounded u, δ^− ≤ δ^+, with equality iff u converges along odd n, in which case both equal the limit.
acceptance: For u constant, δ^+ = δ^− = that constant.
For u(n) = (−1)^{(n−1)/2}, δ^+ = 1 and δ^− = −1 along odd n.

nodes.title: Top compactly supported cohomology counts Frobenius-fixed components
nodes.statement: Let X be a smooth separated scheme of finite type and pure dimension n over F_q, and λ a prime not dividing q. Then H^{2n}_c(X_{F̄_q}, Q_λ) ≅ Q_λ(−n)^{π₀(X_{F̄_q})}, the permutation representation on geometric connected components twisted by Q_λ(−n); hence Tr(Frob_q | H^{2n}_c(X_{F̄_q}, Q_λ)) = q^n · #{geometric components fixed by Frobenius}. In particular the trace is q^n exactly when one geometric component is defined over F_q.
hypotheses: X smooth, separated, finite type, pure dimension n over F_q
λ ∤ q
proofSteps: Decompose X_{F̄_q} into its connected components, which are smooth irreducible of dimension n and permuted by Frobenius.
For each geometrically connected smooth component C, Poincaré duality (EtaleDualityAndPerverseSheaves:EDC.2) gives H^{2n}_c(C, Q_λ) ≅ H^0(C, Q_λ)^∨(−n) = Q_λ(−n).
Frobenius permutes the summands; only fixed components contribute to the trace, each contributing q^n (geometric Frobenius acts on Q_λ(−n) by q^n).
acceptance: X = A^n: trace q^n.
X = two conjugate copies of A^n over F_{q²} viewed over F_q (non-split): no fixed component, trace 0.

sources.excerpt: By Poincar´e duality, this is equivalent to the statement that there is exactly one Fq-rational connected component of ¯Xn.
sources.match: Top-degree trace versus rational components.

sources.excerpt: Also, if Z is n-dimensional, then Tr(Frob |H2n c,ét(ZFq, Qℓ)) is qn times the number of Frobenius ﬁxed n-dimensional components of ZFq.
sources.match: The general form used by LWZB.

nodes.title: Uniform point-count error from a geometric Betti bound
nodes.statement: Let X be smooth of pure dimension n over F_q, λ ∤ q a prime, and C ≥ 1 a real number with dim H^i(X_{F̄_q}, Q_λ) ≤ C^{i+1} for all i ≥ 1. If exactly one geometric connected component of X is fixed by Frobenius and √q > C, then |q^{−n}|X(F_q)| − 1| ≤ Σ_{i ≥ 1} C^{i+1} q^{−i/2} = C²/(√q − C). The numerical core: for reals t_j (0 ≤ j < 2n) with |t_j| ≤ q^{j/2} C^{2n−j+1}, |q^{−n} Σ_{j<2n} (−1)^j t_j| ≤ C²/(√q − C).
hypotheses: X smooth of pure dimension n over F_q
Betti bound dim H^i ≤ C^{i+1} for i ≥ 1
exactly one Frobenius-fixed geometric component
proofSteps: Grothendieck–Lefschetz: |X(F_q)| = Σ_j (−1)^j Tr(Frob | H^j_c(X_{F̄_q}, Q_λ)) (SchemeAndStackFoundations:SF.2).
The j = 2n term is q^n (ST.5/top-cohomology-counts-rational-components).

Deligne's weight bound (DeligneWeightsAndPurity:DWP.7): every Frobenius eigenvalue on H^j_c has absolute value ≤ q^{j/2}; with Poincaré duality dim H^j_c = dim H^{2n−j} (EtaleDualityAndPerverseSheaves:EDC.2), |Tr(Frob | H^j_c)| ≤ q^{j/2} C^{2n−j+1}.
Sum the finite range j < 2n first, then bound by the geometric series Σ_{i≥1} (C/√q)^i · C = C²/(√q − C) (put i = 2n − j).
acceptance: C = 1, q = 16: the bound is 1/3.
Only finitely many j occur; the infinite series is used only as an upper bound after the finite sum.

sources.excerpt: Deligne has proven [19] that every eigenvalue of the geometric Frobenius Frobq (i.e., if we ﬁx a projective embedding of Xn over Fq, this is the opera- tion that raises coordinates to the qth power) on compactly supported Hj c of a smooth variety is bounded above, in absolute value, by qj/2.

nodes.title: EVW Theorem 8.8: uniform moment estimate over F_q(t)
nodes.statement: Let ℓ be an odd prime and A a finite abelian ℓ-group. There is a constant B(A) such that for every odd prime power q with ℓ ∤ q(q − 1) and √q > B(A), and every odd n > B(A), | (Σ_{L ∈ S_n} m_A(L))/|S_n| − 1 | ≤ B(A)/√q, where m_A(L) = |Sur(Cl(O_L), A)|. For A = 0 the left side is 0.
hypotheses: ℓ odd prime
A finite abelian ℓ-group (abelian is a standing hypothesis; sourceIssues ArithmeticStatistics/E661)
q odd prime power, ℓ ∤ q(q − 1) (domain as corrected: sourceIssues ArithmeticStatistics/E663)
n odd, n > B(A), √q > B(A)
proofSteps: A = 0 is immediate (m_0 ≡ 1). Assume A ≠ 0 and let G = G_A, c = c_A (ST.5/generalized-dihedral-cover-datum), X_n = Hn^c_{G,n} ⊗ F_q.

By ST.5/factor-two-point-count-identity and ST.5/size-of-the-odd-degree-quadratic-family (n ≥ 3), the average equals |X_n(F_q)|/(q^n − q^{n−1}); so it suffices to bound |q^{−n}|X_n(F_q)| − 1| (then absorb the factor (1 − 1/q)^{−1}).

Stated input, not planned in ST.5 (gap 'EVW homological stability and uniform Betti bound'; owner: the accepted Part II InverseGaloisPartIIHurwitzHomologicalStability): EVW Proposition 7.8 — if (G, c) is nonsplitting, G centre-free and c a rational conjugacy class generating G, there is C(G, c) with dim H^i_ét(Hn^c_{G,n} ⊗ F̄_q, Q_λ) ≤ C(G, c)^{i+1} for all i, n and all q prime to |G|, for primes λ > max(|G|, q, n); it rests on EVW Theorem 6.1 (for (G, c) nonsplitting and k a field with |G| invertible there are A, B with U : H_p(Hur^c_{G,n}, k) → H_p(Hur^c_{G,n+deg U}, k) an isomorphism for n > Ap + B, also on the connected loci CHur) and Corollary 6.2 (the same for the quotients by G when G is centre-free).

Proposition 7.8 gives the Betti hypothesis of ST.5/uniform-trace-error-estimate with C = C(G_A, c_A) (EVW write C(A) = C(G, c)² to put the bound as C(A)^i), for a prime λ > max(|G|, q, n) chosen for each (q, n); the trace formula and the weight bound hold for every prime λ ∤ q, so this choice costs nothing.
For n larger than a bound depending only on A, exactly one geometric component of X_n is Frobenius-fixed (ST.5/one-rational-geometric-component).
Combine to get |q^{−n}|X_n(F_q)| − 1| ≤ 2C(A)/√q for √q ≥ 2C(A), and take B(A) = 2C(A) enlarged to cover the (1 − 1/q) factor and the degree threshold.
acceptance: A = Z/3, q = 7 (ℓ = 3 divides q − 1 = 6): excluded; the method gives a different (Malle-type) answer there.
Averages over ⊔_{m ≤ n} S_m follow from the same bound.

nodes.title: EVW: the Cohen–Lenstra distribution over F_q(t) as q → ∞
nodes.statement: Let ℓ be an odd prime and A a finite abelian ℓ-group. As q → ∞ through odd prime powers with ℓ ∤ q(q − 1), both the upper density δ^+(q, A) and the lower density δ^−(q, A) — taken over odd n → ∞ of the proportion of L ∈ S_n (imaginary quadratic extensions of F_q(t), ramified at ∞) with Cl(O_L)_ℓ ≅ A — converge to the Cohen–Lenstra mass μ(A) = ∏_{i≥1}(1 − ℓ^{−i})/|Aut A|. Precisely: for every ε > 0 there is Q such that |δ^±(q, A) − μ(A)| ≤ ε for all such q > Q.
hypotheses: ℓ odd prime
A finite abelian ℓ-group
q odd, ℓ ∤ q, ℓ ∤ q − 1 (the printed domain 'q ≢ 1 mod ℓ' also allows q even and q a power of ℓ, which the proof does not cover: sourceIssues ArithmeticStatistics/E663)
proofSteps: Fix A₀ and ε > 0. Apply finite moment control (ST.5/finite-moment-control-of-masses, EVW Proposition 8.3) with the finite set {A₀}: it yields δ > 0 and a finite set L' of finite abelian ℓ-groups such that any probability measure ν with |⟨Sur(−, A)⟩_ν − 1| ≤ δ for all A ∈ L' satisfies |ν(A₀) − μ(A₀)| ≤ ε.
The measures ν_n (ST.5/empirical-l-primary-class-group-law) are probability measures whose A-moments are the averages of m_A over S_n.
By ST.5/uniform-function-field-surjection-moment-estimate, choose Q > max_{A ∈ L'} B(A) with B(A)/√Q < δ for all A ∈ L'; then for q > Q allowed and odd n > Q, |ν_n(A₀) − μ(A₀)| ≤ ε.

Hence every limit point of ν_n(A₀) along odd n lies in [μ(A₀) − ε, μ(A₀) + ε], i.e. δ^±(q, A₀) are within ε of μ(A₀) (ST.5/lower-and-upper-degree-densities). The quantifiers are in this order: finitely many moments first, then uniform thresholds in q and n.
acceptance: ℓ = 3, A = 0: δ^±(q, 0) → ∏_{i≥1}(1 − 3^{−i}) ≈ 0.560, the limiting proportion of class numbers prime to 3 (EVW §1.1 calls 0.440 the indivisible proportion; it is the divisible one: sourceIssues ArithmeticStatistics/E665).
The theorem asserts nothing for fixed q: equality δ^+(q, A) = δ^−(q, A) is not proved (EVW Remark 7.9).
q ≡ 1 mod ℓ is excluded; there the method gives a different limiting distribution.

nodes.title: Positive proportions of class numbers divisible and not divisible by ℓ
nodes.statement: Let ℓ be an odd prime. There is Q₀(ℓ) such that for every odd prime power q > Q₀(ℓ) with ℓ ∤ q(q − 1), the lower odd-degree density of the proportion of L ∈ S_n with ℓ ∤ |Cl(O_L)| is positive, and the lower odd-degree density of the proportion with ℓ | |Cl(O_L)| is positive. Quantitatively both lower densities tend to c_ℓ = ∏_{i≥1}(1 − ℓ^{−i}) > 0 and 1 − c_ℓ > 0 respectively as q → ∞.
hypotheses: ℓ odd prime

nodes.title: The ℓ^k-torsion local system of the odd-degree hyperelliptic family
nodes.statement: Let k be a field with 2ℓ invertible (ℓ an odd prime), n = 2g + 1 odd, and over Conf_n ⊗ k (monic squarefree degree-n polynomials f) let C_f be the smooth projective curve birational to y² = f(x), of genus g, with its unique point at ∞. For each m ≥ 1 the ℓ^m-torsion V_m := Jac(C_f)[ℓ^m] forms a locally constant étale sheaf of free Z/ℓ^m-modules of rank 2g on Conf_n ⊗ k, the Tate module T = lim V_m is a lisse Z_ℓ-sheaf of rank 2g, and the Weil pairing (from the canonical principal polarization) is a perfect alternating pairing V_m × V_m → μ_{ℓ^m}. Consequently geometric monodromy lies in Sp(V_m) and, over k = F_q, a Frobenius element acts in GSp_q(V_m) (similitude multiplier q).
hypotheses: ℓ odd prime, 2ℓ invertible on the base
k arbitrary (F_q or the function field of Conf_n)
proofSteps: The Jacobian of the relative smooth proper curve y² = f(x) over Conf_n ⊗ k (completed at the unique point over ∞) is an abelian scheme of relative dimension g (tauceti JacobianChallenge Layer D: Pic⁰ and the Jacobian).
[ℓ^m] is finite étale of degree ℓ^{2mg} when ℓ is invertible, so V_m is a locally constant sheaf, free over Z/ℓ^m of rank 2g (AbelianSchemesAndArithmeticModuli:A3).

The canonical principal polarization induces the Weil pairing V_m × V_m → μ_{ℓ^m}, perfect and alternating (AbelianSchemesAndArithmeticModuli:A3); monodromy preserves it up to the cyclotomic character, which is trivial on the geometric fundamental group and equals q on Frobenius over F_q.
acceptance: n = 1: g = 0 and V_m = 0.
n = 3: V_m has rank 2 (elliptic curves y² = f(x) with the point at ∞).
The Frobenius multiplier is q, not 1: over F_q the monodromy image is in GSp, not Sp.

nodes.title: The geometric generic fibre of X_n → Conf_n is Sur(V, A) modulo sign
nodes.statement: Let ℓ be odd, A a nontrivial finite abelian ℓ-group, m ≥ 1 with ℓ^m A = 0, and n = 2g + 1 odd. Over the function field K of Conf_n ⊗ F_q (or any field of characteristic prime to 2ℓ), the geometric generic fibre Σ of the finite étale cover X_n = Hn^{c_A}_{G_A,n} → Conf_n is identified, Gal(K̄/K)-equivariantly, with Sur(V_m, A)/{±1}, where V_m = Jac(C)[ℓ^m](K̄) with its monodromy action. The marked set Sur(V_m, A) has twice as many elements, and since −I ∈ Sp(V_m), the Sp(V_m)-orbit sets of Sur(V_m, A) and of Sur(V_m, A)/{±1} correspond bijectively.
hypotheses: ℓ odd prime; A ≠ 0 a finite abelian ℓ-group with ℓ^m A = 0
n odd
characteristic prime to 2ℓ

Pairs (C, α) and (C, −α) give isomorphic G_A-covers (the hyperelliptic involution acts by −1), so the fibre of the unmarked cover is Sur(V_m, A)/{±1}, not Sur(V_m, A) (EVW print Sur(V, A): sourceIssues ArithmeticStatistics/E662).
Equivariance: the identification is canonical, hence commutes with Gal(K̄/K).
−I ∈ Sp(V_m) acts as the sign, so each Sp-orbit on Sur(V_m, A) is a union of sign classes; orbit sets correspond.

nodes.title: Degeneration of labelled hyperelliptic moduli to the boundary Δ_{1,1}
nodes.statement: Let k be algebraically closed with 2ℓ invertible, g ≥ 3. The moduli space H̃_g of labelled hyperelliptic (Z/2-)curves of genus g degenerates to the boundary stratum Δ_{1,1}: there are clutching maps κ_L : H̃_{g−1} × H̃_1 → H̃_g, κ_R : H̃_1 × H̃_{g−1} → H̃_g and κ : H̃_1 × H̃_{g−2} × H̃_1 → H̃_g factoring through both, whose images meet the closure of H̃_g. Along a clutching map the ℓ-torsion of Pic⁰ splits: κ^*Pic⁰(C_γ)[ℓ] ≅ Pic⁰(C_{γ1})[ℓ] × Pic⁰(C_{γ2})[ℓ] as symplectic local systems, and the monodromy group of the image contains the product of the factors' monodromy groups.
hypotheses: k algebraically closed, 2ℓ invertible
g ≥ 3 (class vector (1, …, 1) of length 2g + 2 split as (1,1,1,1), (1,…,1) of length 2g − 2, (1,1,1,1))
proofSteps: Achter–Pries Lemma 2.5: the class vector of H̃_g splits into γ1 = γ3 = (1,1,1,1) and γ2 of length 2g − 2, giving the Δ_{1,1} degeneration.
Achter–Pries Lemma 3.1(a): for a stable curve C = C1 ∪ C2 meeting in one section, restriction gives Pic⁰(C) ≅ Pic⁰(C1) × Pic⁰(C2) on stalks, hence an isomorphism of ℓ-torsion sheaves.
Achter–Pries Lemma 3.1(b): the Galois cover trivialising the product local system has group H1 × H2, so the monodromy of the image of κ is the product.

For g ≤ 2 there is no such degeneration; the base cases use full curve moduli.

nodes.title: Two overlapping symplectic block subgroups generate Sp(V)
nodes.statement: Let F be a finite field of odd characteristic and V = V1 ⊕ V2 ⊕ V3 a nondegenerate symplectic F-space with the V_i pairwise orthogonal and all nonzero. If a subgroup H ≤ Sp(V) contains Sp(V1 ⊕ V2) × Sp(V3) and Sp(V1) × Sp(V2 ⊕ V3), then H = Sp(V).
hypotheses: F finite, char F odd
V_i ≠ 0, pairwise orthogonal, V nondegenerate
proofSteps: Sp(V) over a field is generated by the symplectic transvections t_{v,a}(x) = x + a⟨x, v⟩v (v ∈ V, a ∈ F): classical input recorded as the gap 'Generation of Sp(V) by symplectic transvections'.
Transvections along vectors of V1 ⊕ V2 or of V2 ⊕ V3 lie in H by hypothesis (they are the transvections of those nondegenerate summands, extended by the identity).

For v = v1 + v2 + v3 with v1 + v2 ≠ 0: Sp(V1 ⊕ V2) acts transitively on nonzero vectors of V1 ⊕ V2 and V2 ≠ 0, so some h ∈ Sp(V1 ⊕ V2) ⊂ H sends v1 + v2 into V2; then h(v) ∈ V2 ⊕ V3, t_{h(v),a} ∈ H and t_{v,a} = h^{−1} t_{h(v),a} h ∈ H. If v1 + v2 = 0 then v ∈ V3.

Hence H contains all transvections and H = Sp(V). This elementary argument replaces Achter–Pries's appeal to the maximality of Sp(V1 ⊕ V2) × Sp(V3) in Sp(V) (Kleidman–Liebeck), which needs V1 ⊕ V2 and V3 of different dimensions.
acceptance: dim V1 = dim V3 = 2, dim V2 = 2g − 4 is the case used for g ≥ 3.
The hypothesis V2 ≠ 0 is used: for V = V1 ⊕ V3, the subgroup Sp(V1) × Sp(V3) contains both block subgroups and is proper.

sources.excerpt: If the pairing is symplectic, and if H ⊆Sp(V) contains both Sp(V1 ⊕V2) and Sp(V2 ⊕V3), then H = Sp(V).

nodes.title: Achter–Pries: the mod-ℓ monodromy of hyperelliptic curves is Sp_{2g}(F_ℓ)
nodes.statement: Let ℓ be an odd prime and k an algebraically closed field in which 2ℓ is invertible. For every g ≥ 1 the mod-ℓ monodromy groups of the labelled hyperelliptic moduli space H̃_g ⊗ k and of the hyperelliptic moduli space H_g ⊗ k (tautological curves, ℓ-torsion of Pic⁰) are both Sp_{2g}(F_ℓ).
hypotheses: ℓ odd prime
k algebraically closed, char k ∤ 2ℓ
proofSteps: H_g ⊗ k is open dense in its closure, which is dominated by H̃_g ⊗ k, so it suffices to treat H̃_g (restriction to a dense open does not change the image: InverseGaloisAndArithmeticFundamentalGroups:IG.0).

Base cases g = 1, 2: every curve of genus g is hyperelliptic, so M_ℓ(H_g) = M_ℓ(M_g) = Sp_{2g}(F_ℓ) (Deligne–Mumford 5.15–5.16; gap 'Full mod-ℓ monodromy of M_1 and M_2'); pass to H̃_g by Achter–Pries Lemma 3.3, since the Galois group Sym(2g + 2) of H̃_g → H_g and Sp_{2g}(F_ℓ) have no common nontrivial quotient (PSp_{2g}(F_ℓ) simple except PSp_2(F_3) ≅ A_4).

Induction for g ≥ 3: by ST.5/hyperelliptic-boundary-degeneration the image contains Sp(V1) × Sp(V2 ⊕ V3) and Sp(V1 ⊕ V2) × Sp(V3) with dim V1 = dim V3 = 2 (induction hypothesis for genera 1 and g − 1).
Conclude by ST.5/overlapping-symplectic-subgroups-generate.
acceptance: For ℓ = 2 the image is smaller (EVW p.780 footnote remark); ℓ odd is essential.

nodes.title: A closed subgroup of Sp_{2g}(Z_ℓ) with full mod-ℓ image is everything (outside (g, ℓ) = (1, 3))
nodes.statement: Let ℓ be an odd prime, g ≥ 1 and H ≤ Sp_{2g}(Z_ℓ) a closed subgroup whose reduction mod ℓ is all of Sp_{2g}(F_ℓ). If g ≥ 2 or ℓ ≥ 5, then H = Sp_{2g}(Z_ℓ). For (g, ℓ) = (1, 3) the conclusion needs the extra condition that H mod 9 meets the kernel of SL_2(Z/9) → SL_2(F_3) nontrivially; without it the implication fails: the order-24 subgroup of SL_2(Z/9) generated by [[0, 1], [8, 0]] and [[1, 7], [6, 7]] maps isomorphically onto SL_2(F_3), and its inverse image in SL_2(Z_3) is a proper closed subgroup (of index 27) with full mod-3 image.
hypotheses: ℓ odd prime, g ≥ 1
H closed in Sp_{2g}(Z_ℓ) (images of profinite groups are compact, hence closed)
(g, ℓ) ≠ (1, 3), or the congruence-kernel condition at (1, 3)
proofSteps: Sp_{2g} is simply connected, so Vasiu's Main Theorem 1.3 applies with c(G) = 1: case (a) ℓ ≥ 5; case (b) ℓ = 3, where the extra condition concerns only normal SL_2/PGL_2 factors, i.e. only g = 1.

The mechanism (Vasiu §§3.7.1, 4.1.2, 4.5, 4.7; Serre's lifting argument): H mod ℓ² surjects onto Sp_{2g}(F_ℓ); the extension 0 → sp_{2g}(F_ℓ) → Sp_{2g}(Z/ℓ²) → Sp_{2g}(F_ℓ) → 1 does not split and the adjoint module is irreducible, so H mod ℓ² contains the whole congruence kernel; then powering lifts congruence kernels level by level and H = Sp_{2g}(Z_ℓ) by closedness. This proof is recorded as the gap 'Vasiu's surjectivity criterion for Sp_{2g}'.

The (1, 3) witness: check by finite computation that the two matrices generate a group of order 24 mapping bijectively to SL_2(F_3) (whose order is 24), so its preimage in SL_2(Z_3) misses the nontrivial level-2 congruence kernel.
acceptance: The (1, 3) subgroup of index 27 is a closed proper subgroup with full mod-3 image.
Achter–Pries Corollary 3.5 invokes 'a standard group theory argument' at all (g, ℓ), which is insufficient at (1, 3) (sourceIssues ArithmeticStatistics/E667).

nodes.statement: Let ℓ be an odd prime and k algebraically closed with 2ℓ invertible. For g ≥ 2, or g = 1 and ℓ ≥ 5, the ℓ-adic monodromy groups of H̃_g ⊗ k and of H_g ⊗ k are Sp_{2g}(Z_ℓ). The case (g, ℓ) = (1, 3) is not covered by this argument.

nodes.title: Full symplectic monodromy for y² = ∏(x − a_i) over Conf_n
nodes.statement: Let ℓ be odd, k algebraically closed with 2ℓ invertible and n = 2g + 1 ≥ 5 (or n = 3 with ℓ ≥ 5). The geometric ℓ-adic monodromy of the Jacobian of y² = ∏_{i=1}^n (x − a_i) over Conf_n(A¹_k) is Sp_{2g}(Z_ℓ).
hypotheses: ℓ odd, char k ∤ 2ℓ
n = 2g + 1 ≥ 5, or n = 3 and ℓ ≥ 5
proofSteps: The family over the ordered configuration space PConf_n is a torsor under the smooth connected group B_n of affine changes (a, b, d) with d² = a^n, and [PConf_n/B_n] ≅ H̃_g^{sm} keeps the hyperelliptic involution (InverseGaloisAndArithmeticFundamentalGroups:IG.1; PAPER-ELLENBERG-VENKATESH-WESTERLAND-16 items /128–/131).

A representable smooth surjection with geometrically connected fibres induces a surjection on étale π₁ (IG.0; EVW items /132); restriction from the compact-type locus to the smooth locus does not change the image (IG.0; item /133).

Hence the image over PConf_n equals that over H̃_g, which is Sp_{2g}(Z_ℓ) by ST.5/integral-hyperelliptic-monodromy; PConf_n → Conf_n is finite étale Galois with group S_n, and the image over Conf_n contains the image over PConf_n and is contained in Sp_{2g}(Z_ℓ).
acceptance: n = 3, ℓ = 3 is excluded (genus 1).
The statement is geometric: over F_q the arithmetic image lies in GSp with multiplier q.

nodes.title: Symplectic similitudes of a lattice with a perfect alternating pairing
nodes.statement: Let R be a commutative ring and V a free R-module of rank 2g with a perfect alternating pairing ω (in matrix form, V = R^{2g} with ω(x, y) = xᵀJy, J the standard alternating matrix). The similitude group GSp(V) consists of the R-linear automorphisms h with ω(hx, hy) = m(h)·ω(x, y) for a unit m(h) ∈ R^×, the multiplier; m : GSp(V) → R^× is a homomorphism with kernel Sp(V). For a unit m, GSp_m(V) := m^{−1}(m) is a coset of Sp(V). In matrices: h ∈ GSp_m ⇔ h J hᵀ = m J.

ω perfect and alternating
proofSteps: Define the multiplier coset {h : h J hᵀ = m J} and GSp as their union over units m; closure under products and inverses is a computation (multipliers multiply).
The multiplier is well defined because J is invertible; m = 1 recovers Mathlib's symplecticGroup.

−I ∈ Sp.

nodes.title: Components of X_n are symplectic orbits; rational ones are GSp_q-stable orbits
nodes.statement: In the range of ST.5/monodromy-of-the-odd-degree-polynomial-family (A a nontrivial finite abelian ℓ-group, ℓ odd, q odd with ℓ ∤ q, ℓ^m A = 0): the geometric connected components of X_n ⊗ F̄_q correspond bijectively to Sp(V_m)-orbits on Sur(V_m, A), and an orbit O gives a component defined over F_q iff the stabilizer in GSp(V_m) of some (equivalently every) x ∈ O meets GSp_q(V_m). The fibre is Sur(V_m, A)/{±1} (ST.5/geometric-generic-fibre-of-the-unmarked-hurwitz-cover); since −I ∈ Sp, the orbit sets agree with those on Sur(V_m, A).

The geometric image is Sp(V_m) (ST.5/finite-level-monodromy-of-the-polynomial-family) and a Frobenius element lies in GSp_q(V_m); Frobenius fixes the orbit of x iff some element of Sp·F = GSp_q ∩ (image) fixes x, i.e. the stabilizer of x meets GSp_q.
Lift to T using surjectivity GSp_q(T) → GSp_q(V_m) and Sur(V_m, A) = Sur(T, A).

The equivalence 'some x' ⇔ 'every x' holds because stabilizers along an orbit are Sp-conjugate and Sp is normal in GSp.

nodes.title: Primary decomposition of a similitude with multiplier q
nodes.statement: Let ℓ be odd, V free of rank 2g over Z_ℓ with a perfect alternating pairing, q ∈ Z_ℓ^× with q − 1 ∈ Z_ℓ^×, and h ∈ GSp_q(V). Let V_1 (resp. V_q) be the set of v ∈ V with (h − 1)^N v → 0 (resp. (h − q)^N v → 0) ℓ-adically, and W := ⋂_N (h − 1)^N (h − q)^N V. Then V = V_1 ⊕ V_q ⊕ W as Z_ℓ-modules, each summand is h-stable, h − 1 is invertible on V_q ⊕ W and h − q is invertible on V_1 ⊕ W.
hypotheses: ℓ odd prime
q and q − 1 units of Z_ℓ
h ∈ GSp_q(V)
proofSteps: Factor the characteristic polynomial of h mod ℓ into its (x − 1)-primary part, (x − q)-primary part and a coprime remainder (1 ≠ q in F_ℓ); lift the coprime factorisation by Hensel's lemma to Z_ℓ[x].

The corresponding idempotents in Z_ℓ[h] give an h-stable decomposition V = V_1 ⊕ V_q ⊕ W with the stated invertibility (a polynomial coprime mod ℓ to the char. poly. of h on a summand acts invertibly on it).
Identify the idempotent summands with the limit descriptions (EVW's definitions): on V_1, h − 1 is topologically nilpotent; on the complement it is invertible.
acceptance: h = diag(I, q I): V_1 = V_−, V_q = V_+, W = 0.
If q ≡ 1 mod ℓ the decomposition V_1 ⊕ V_q fails (the primary parts coincide mod ℓ); this is why q − 1 must be a unit.

sources.excerpt: Then, since q and 1 are distinct in Fℓ, we have (8.9.3) V = V1 ⊕Vq ⊕W.
sources.match: The decomposition (8.9.3).

nodes.title: Isotropy of the primary parts and a Lagrangian in ker f
nodes.statement: In ST.5/primary-decomposition-for-a-multiplier-q-similitude: V_1 and V_q are isotropic, V_1 ⊕ V_q is orthogonal to W, and W is nondegenerate; W = W_+ ⊕ W_− with W_± isotropic, and then W_+ ⊕ V_1 and W_− ⊕ V_q are complementary maximal isotropic (Lagrangian) direct summands of V. If f : V → A satisfies f ∘ h = f, then the Lagrangian W_− ⊕ V_q lies in the image of h − 1, hence in ker f.
hypotheses: as in ST.5/primary-decomposition-for-a-multiplier-q-similitude
f : V → A a homomorphism with f ∘ h = f
proofSteps: For x ∈ V_1 and y ∈ V_1 ⊕ W write y = (h − q)^N z_N; using ω(hx, hy) = q ω(x, y), ω(x, y) ∈ ω((h − 1)^N x, V) for all N, hence 0 (EVW's iteration). Symmetrically for V_q.
W is nondegenerate as an orthogonal summand of a perfect pairing (EVW fact (ii)); decompose W into two isotropic summands (EVW fact (iii), a symplectic basis: ST.5/symplectic-normal-forms-over-z-l).
(V_1 ⊕ W_+) ⊕ (V_q ⊕ W_−) = V with both summands isotropic, so both are maximal isotropic (fact (iv)).
h − 1 is invertible on V_q ⊕ W, so V_q ⊕ W_− ⊆ im(h − 1); f ∘ (h − 1) = 0 gives V_q ⊕ W_− ⊆ ker f.
acceptance: h = diag(I, qI) with f factoring through the projection to V_−: the killed Lagrangian is V_+.
Without q − 1 invertible the conclusion fails for h = I.

sources.excerpt: In particular, W−⊕Vq is a maximal isotropic submodule of V , which furthermore lies in the image of h −1, and thus belongs to ker(f).
sources.match: The killed Lagrangian.

nodes.title: Symplectic bases and Lagrangians over Z_ℓ
nodes.statement: Let M be a finite free Z_ℓ-module with a perfect alternating pairing. (i) M has a symplectic basis; any basis x_1, …, x_g of a Lagrangian direct summand extends to one; hence Sp(M) acts transitively on Lagrangian direct summands. (ii) An orthogonal direct summand of M is nondegenerate. (iii) M = M_+ ⊕ M_− with M_± Lagrangian. (iv) If M = P ⊕ Q with P, Q isotropic, both are Lagrangian (of rank half of M). (v) Every automorphism of a Lagrangian M_+ extends, by inverse transpose on a complementary Lagrangian M_−, to an element of Sp(M).
hypotheses: ℓ prime (odd in the application)
M finite free over Z_ℓ, pairing perfect and alternating
proofSteps: (i) Given a basis x_i of a Lagrangian summand, choose y_j with ω(x_i, y_j) = δ_ij by perfectness, then correct y_j by combinations of the x_i to make ⟨y_i, y_j⟩ = 0 (EVW's argument); transitivity follows by mapping one symplectic basis to another.
(ii) A degenerate vector of an orthogonal summand would be degenerate in M.
(iii) Take the spans of the two halves of a symplectic basis.
(iv) Reduce mod ℓ and use the field statement (isotropic subspaces have dimension at most half).
(v) With respect to a symplectic basis adapted to M_+ ⊕ M_−, the block matrix diag(a, (aᵀ)^{−1}) is symplectic.
acceptance: M = Z_ℓ²: every primitive vector spans a Lagrangian.
Over Z_ℓ the summand condition matters: ℓZ_ℓ·e₁ is isotropic but not a direct summand.

sources.excerpt: (i) any two maximal isotropic Zℓ-submodules of V are conjugate to one an- other under Sp(V );
sources.match: Fact (i); facts (ii)–(iv) follow in the text.

sources.excerpt: Since every automorphism of GL(V+) is induced by an element of Sp(V ), we are reduced to checking that any two surjections V+ →A are conjugate under GL(V+).

nodes.title: GL_g(Z_ℓ) acts transitively on surjections Z_ℓ^g → A
nodes.statement: Let A be a finite abelian ℓ-group generated by at most g elements. Then GL_g(Z_ℓ) acts transitively (by precomposition) on the set of surjective homomorphisms Z_ℓ^g → A.
hypotheses: A finite abelian ℓ-group with dim_{F_ℓ}(A/ℓA) = k ≤ g
proofSteps: Fix x_1, …, x_k ∈ A whose classes form a basis of A/ℓA; by Nakayama they generate A.

For a surjection f, lift x_i to y_i ∈ Z_ℓ^g; the y_i are independent mod ℓ, so extend to a Z_ℓ-basis y_1, …, y_g, and replace y_i for k < i ≤ g by y_i − Σ_{j ≤ k} c_{ij} y_j so that f(y_i) = 0 (possible since the x_j generate A). (EVW print 'i > g' for 'k < i ≤ g': sourceIssues ArithmeticStatistics/E664.)
Doing the same for f_2 gives a basis y'_i; the automorphism y_i ↦ y'_i carries f_1 to f_2.
acceptance: A = 0: the unique map; transitivity is trivial.
g < dim A/ℓA: there are no surjections.

nodes.title: EVW Lemma 8.9: a unique Sp-orbit of surjections fixed by a multiplier-q similitude
nodes.statement: Let ℓ be odd, V a free Z_ℓ-module of rank 2g with a perfect alternating pairing, A a finite abelian ℓ-group and q ∈ Z_ℓ^× with q − 1 ∈ Z_ℓ^×. Let O be the set of surjections f : V → A such that f ∘ h = f for some h ∈ GSp_q(V). If g ≥ dim_{F_ℓ}(A/ℓA), then O is nonempty and Sp(V) acts transitively on O.
hypotheses: ℓ odd prime; q, q − 1 ∈ Z_ℓ^×
A finite abelian ℓ-group
g ≥ dim_{F_ℓ}(A/ℓA)
proofSteps: Nonempty: write V = V_+ ⊕ V_− with Lagrangians (ST.5/symplectic-normal-forms-over-z-l (iii)); h := q on V_+ and 1 on V_− lies in GSp_q; any surjection factoring through the projection to V_− (exists as rank V_− = g ≥ dim A/ℓA) is fixed by h.
Given f ∈ O with h, ker f contains a Lagrangian direct summand (ST.5/orthogonality-and-a-killed-lagrangian).
By transitivity on Lagrangians (normal forms (i)) move it to V_+, so f factors through V → V_−.
Automorphisms of V_− extend to Sp(V) (normal forms (v)), reducing to GL_g(Z_ℓ)-transitivity on surjections Z_ℓ^g → A (ST.5/linear-group-transitive-on-lattice-surjections).
acceptance: Without q − 1 ∈ Z_ℓ^× the conclusion fails: for q = 1, V = Z_ℓ², A = F_ℓ², the identity fixes every surjection, and Sur(V, A) splits into ℓ − 1 orbits of Sp_2(Z_ℓ) = SL_2(Z_ℓ), indexed by the determinant in F_ℓ^×.

nodes.title: Exactly one geometric component of X_n is defined over F_q
nodes.statement: Let ℓ be odd, A a nontrivial finite abelian ℓ-group and q an odd prime power with ℓ ∤ q(q − 1). For every odd n larger than a bound depending only on A (n ≥ 5 and g = (n − 1)/2 ≥ dim_{F_ℓ}(A/ℓA)), exactly one geometric connected component of X_n = Hn^{c_A}_{G_A,n} ⊗ F̄_q is fixed by Frobenius.
hypotheses: ℓ odd; A ≠ 0 finite abelian ℓ-group
q odd, ℓ ∤ q(q − 1)
n odd with n ≥ 5 and (n − 1)/2 ≥ dim_{F_ℓ}(A/ℓA)
proofSteps: By ST.5/monodromy-orbits-and-rational-components, Frobenius-fixed components correspond to Sp(T)-orbits of surjections T → A whose stabilizer meets GSp_q(T).
Since ℓ ∤ q(q − 1), q and q − 1 are units of Z_ℓ; ST.5/unique-similitude-stable-symplectic-orbit gives exactly one such orbit (nonempty and transitive).
acceptance: q ≡ 1 mod ℓ: excluded; several orbits may be rational, giving a different limit.
The bound on n depends only on A, not on q.

sources.excerpt: We claim that, for suﬃciently large n, there is a unique Sp(V )-orbit on Sur(V, A) deﬁned over Fq.
sources.match: The claim.

nodes.title: The convergence mode 'fixed large degree, q → ∞'
nodes.statement: For m ≥ 1 let A_m be the filter on N of prime powers q coprime to m, tending to infinity. For a function E(q, n) of a prime power q and a degree n, and a target c(n), say E has eventual-degree large-q limit c if there is n₀ such that for every fixed n ≥ n₀, E(q, n) → c(n) as q → ∞ along A_m. This is the mode in which the function-field moment theorems of Wood (2019) and Ellenberg–Venkatesh–Westerland (degree densities first, then q) are proved; it is not the fixed-q, large-degree limit of the direct function-field analogue of the number-field conjectures, and the two limits may not be interchanged without a new uniform estimate.
hypotheses: m ≥ 1 (the moduli excluded from q)
E : prime powers × N → R, c : N → R
proofSteps: Define A_m := atTop ⊓ principal{q : q a prime power, gcd(q, m) = 1}; it is a proper filter (infinitely many primes are coprime to m).
Define the predicate ∃ n₀, ∀ n ≥ n₀, Tendsto (q ↦ E(q, n)) A_m (nhds c(n)).
Limits are unique along the proper filter A_m, so c(n) is determined for n ≥ n₀.
acceptance: E(q, n) = n/(n + q): the eventual-degree large-q limit is 0 at every n, while for each fixed q, E(q, n) → 1 as n → ∞.
Constant functions have their constant as limit.

sources.locator: §1 after Theorem 1.2, p.3 (arXiv v2; Duke 168, p.380)
sources.excerpt: The limits in Theorem 1.2 are not the same as the limits in the direct function ﬁeld analog of Conjecture 1.1. In particular, in the analog of Conjecture 1.1 there should be a ﬁxed q and a limit in n. In Theorem 1.2, we have a ﬁxed n and a limit in q.
sources.match: The convergence mode, and its difference from the fixed-q limit.

nodes.title: Wood Theorem 4.8, imaginary good case: unit moment per component invariant
nodes.statement: Let G be a finite group, G′ ≤ G ≀ S₂ admissible, good and centre-free, c the set of order-2 elements of G′ outside ker(G′ → S₂). For each prime power q coprime to |G′| choose a Frobenius-fixed component invariant f_q with f_q(u_q) = (x, 2n − 1), x ↦ (1, 1, σ) in G′. Then for n sufficiently large, the number of pairs (K, ρ) with K ∈ IQ_{=q^{2n}} and ρ ∈ Sur(G_K^{un,∞}, G) of type G′ and component invariant f_q, divided by #IQ_{=q^{2n}}, tends to 1 as q → ∞ with (q, |G′|) = 1. The invariant f_q may vary with q; n is fixed before q → ∞; it is a rigid average (no |Aut_{G′}(G)| factor).
hypotheses: G′ admissible, good (c is one G′-class), Z(G′) = 1
q prime to |G′| (hence odd)
n ≥ n₀(G′)
proofSteps: Proposition 4.4 (InverseGaloisAndArithmeticFundamentalGroups:IG.4; PAPER-WOOD-19 /73, /75): pairs (K, ρ) of the given type correspond to marked (G′, c)-extensions of F_q(t) of imaginary infinity type, with Disc M = Disc K^{|G′|/2}, so discriminant norm q^{2n} ⇔ Σ n_i = 2n − 1.

Theorem 4.5(2)–(3) (IG.5; PAPER-WOOD-19 /79, /80): these marked extensions are the F_q-points of CHur^{c,(1,1,σ)}_{G′,2n−1}, and for n ≥ N₀ the points with component invariant f_q are those of one Frobenius-fixed geometric component C.
Theorem 4.7 (IG.5; PAPER-WOOD-19 /88): |#C(F_q) − q^{2n−1}| ≤ K_{2n−1} q^{2n−3/2} uniformly in q.
#IQ_{=q^{2n}} = q^{2n−1} − q^{2n−2} (ST.5/imaginary-exact-slice-parametrization); the ratio is 1 + O_n(q^{−1/2}).
acceptance: G = C_3, G′ = C_3 ⋊ C_2 (the dihedral case): recovers the unit 3-moment of the imaginary Cohen–Lenstra heuristic in this mode.
The limit is in the mode of ST.5/eventual-degree-large-q-limit.

nodes.title: Wood Theorem 1.2, good imaginary case
nodes.statement: Let G be finite and G′ ≤ G ≀ S₂ admissible, good and centre-free, c its outside involutions. For n sufficiently large, E⁻_{F_q(t), q^{2n}}(G, G′)/|H₂(G′, c)[q − 1]| → 1/|Aut_{G′}(G)| as q → ∞ with (q, |G′|) = 1, where E⁻ is the average number of unramified G-extensions L/K split at ∞ with Gal(L̃/F_q(t)) of type G′, over K ∈ IQ_{=q^{2n}}, and H₂(G′, c) is the reduced Schur multiplier. The torsion count |H₂(G′, c)[q − 1]| varies with q and is divided out inside the limit.
hypotheses: G′ admissible, good, Z(G′) = 1
q coprime to |G′|
n ≥ n₀(G, G′)
proofSteps: The Frobenius-fixed component invariants of the imaginary slice number exactly |H₂(G′, c)[q − 1]| (Wood Theorem 4.5(3) with Proposition 4.1; gap 'Reduced Schur multiplier inputs': PAPER-WOOD-19 /68–/70, owner InductionRestrictionPartIIReducedSchur).

Sum ST.5/imaginary-per-component-unit-moment over them: along q with |H₂(G′, c)[q − 1]| = d fixed, Ẽ⁻ → d; since d takes finitely many values the normalised ratio Ẽ⁻/|H₂(G′, c)[q − 1]| → 1 along all allowed q.
Convert rigid to unrigid: E⁻ = Ẽ⁻/|Aut_{G′}(G)| (ArithmeticStatistics:ST.3, PAPER-WOOD-19 /13).

nodes.title: Exact count of stable parity multidegrees (stars and bars)
nodes.statement: Let N ≥ 1, N₀ ≥ 0, d ≥ 0 and ε ∈ {0, 1}^N. Let a_i be the least integer ≥ N₀ with a_i ≡ ε_i (mod 2). The number of m ∈ Z_{≥0}^N with m_i ≥ N₀, m_i ≡ ε_i (mod 2) and Σ m_i = d is the binomial coefficient C(L + N − 1, N − 1) if L := (d − Σ a_i)/2 is a nonnegative integer, and 0 otherwise.
proofSteps: The map m_i = a_i + 2z_i is a bijection between such m and z ∈ Z_{≥0}^N with Σ z_i = L.
Weak compositions of L into N parts number C(L + N − 1, N − 1) (Mathlib Nat.choose and the stars-and-bars count); when d − Σ a_i is odd or negative the set is empty.
acceptance: N = 1: the count is 1 if d ≥ N₀ and d ≡ ε₁ (mod 2), else 0.

nodes.title: Many large parity vectors
nodes.statement: For N ≥ 2, N₀ ≥ 0 and ε ∈ {0,1}^N there is v > 0 (depending only on N, N₀) such that for all sufficiently large d with d ≡ Σ ε_i (mod 2), the number of m ∈ Z^N with m_i ≥ N₀, m_i ≡ ε_i (mod 2) and Σ m_i = d is at least v·d^{N−1}.

nodes.title: Wood Theorem 4.8, bad types: a liminf lower bound
nodes.statement: Let G′ ≤ G ≀ S₂ be admissible and centre-free but not good, with N_{G′} ≥ 2 classes of outside involutions. There is w > 0 depending only on G, G′ such that for n sufficiently large, liminf_{q→∞, (q,|G′|)=1} Ẽ^±_{F_q(t), q^{2n}}(G, G′)/|H₂(G′, c)[q − 1]| ≥ w·n^{N_{G′}−1}. The printed statement asserts a limit; only this liminf bound is proved (sourceIssues ArithmeticStatistics/E668).
hypotheses: G′ admissible, centre-free, not good
q coprime to |G′|
n large
proofSteps: Keep only multidegrees m with Σ m_i = 2n − 1 (imaginary; 2n real), every m_i ≥ N₀ and the parities of Wood Proposition 4.1 (m_1 odd, others even, imaginary; all even, real): at least v n^{N−1} of them (ST.5/many-large-parity-vectors).

nodes.title: The whole fixed-degree component profile
nodes.statement: Fix a centre-free admissible F = G′ with outside involution classes c_1, …, c_N, a sign ± and n ≥ 2; put d = 2n − 1 and g = (1, 1, σ) in the imaginary case, d = 2n and g = 1 in the real case. The profile is P_n^±(q) := C_n^±(q)/M(q) ∈ Q_{≥0}. It includes every multidegree, not only the stable range m_i ≥ N₀. In the suggested formalisation the geometric counts are carried as data: a function m ↦ C_m(q) and the normaliser M.

nodes.title: The complete stable-range component sum
nodes.statement: Let F = G′, c = ⊔_{i ≤ N} c_i its outside involution classes, A = H₂(F, c), g ∈ c ∪ {1}, q odd coprime to |F| and N₀ a stable threshold. For a set S ⊆ {0,1}^N of surviving parity vectors (those compatible with [g] in F^ab and with v₂(q − 1) ≥ t_A(b(g, ε)) + 1, Wood Proposition 4.1/Remark 4.2 as refined in PAPER-WOOD-19 /301, /304), define Σ_stable(d) := Σ_{ε ∈ S} #{m : m_i ≥ N₀, m_i ≡ ε_i (mod 2), Σ m_i = d}. Then C_{stable,d}^g(q)/|A[q − 1]| = Σ_stable(d): each surviving parity class of stable multidegrees contributes exactly |A[q − 1]| Frobenius-fixed components per multidegree, the others none. The boundary remainder is not included.
hypotheses: F centre-free admissible, q odd coprime to |F|
N₀ a stable threshold
S the surviving parity vectors determined by the reduced-Schur-multiplier criterion
proofSteps: Define the parity-class count (ST.5/stable-parity-multidegree-count) and sum it over S.

For each stable m, the Frobenius-fixed components are the q^{−1}-fixed lifting invariants over (g, m) (Theorem 4.5(3), IG.5); their number is |A[q − 1]| if the parity vector of m survives and 0 otherwise (PAPER-WOOD-19 /301, /304; gap 'Reduced Schur multiplier inputs').
The survival criterion depends only on m mod 2, so the stable count is |A[q − 1]| times Σ_stable(d).

nodes.title: The normalised rigid moment differs from the component profile by O(q^{−1/2})
nodes.statement: In ST.5/whole-fixed-degree-component-profile, let B_n bound the total number of geometric components (uniformly in q) and K_d be the uniform component error of Wood Theorem 4.7. Then |Ẽ_n^±(q)/M(q) − P_n^±(q)| ≤ B_n(K_d q^{−1/2} + q^{−1})/(1 − q^{−1}); in particular the difference is O_n(q^{−1/2}). One may take B_n = D_d, the degree of the finite étale map CHur_{F,d} → Conf_d.
hypotheses: as in ST.5/whole-fixed-degree-component-profile
B_n a q-uniform bound on the number of geometric components
proofSteps: A rational point lies on a Frobenius-fixed component; non-fixed open and closed components contribute no F_q-points.
Each fixed component C has |#C(F_q) − q^d| ≤ K_d q^{d−1/2} (Theorem 4.7, IG.5; PAPER-WOOD-19 /88); the rigid moment numerator is Σ_C #C(F_q) (Proposition 4.4, IG.4).
The denominator is q^d(1 − q^{−1}) (ST.5/imaginary-exact-slice-parametrization, ST.5/real-exact-slice-parametrization); divide by it and by M(q) ≥ 1, using C_n(q) ≤ B_n.
B_n = D_d is q-independent because the degree of CHur_{F,d} → Conf_d is constant over the connected base (IG.5; PAPER-WOOD-19 /314).
acceptance: If no component is fixed, the moment is O_n(q^{−1/2}).
The bound is uniform in q at fixed n only.

nodes.title: The ordinary q-limit exists iff the component profile is eventually constant
nodes.statement: Under ST.5/moment-minus-component-profile-vanishes (with M(q) ≤ K uniformly, as M(q) divides |H₂(F, c)|), the limit of Ẽ_n^±(q)/M(q) as q → ∞ along allowed prime powers exists iff P_n^±(q) is eventually equal to a single rational value, and then that value is the limit. A convergent function with values in a finite subset of R is eventually constant: a finite subset of a T1 space is discrete (Mathlib Finite.instDiscreteTopology) and convergence to a point of a discrete subtype is eventual equality (Mathlib Filter.tendsto_pure).

nodes.title: Surjections onto H ⋊ Γ as tuples (ρ, N, s, φ)
nodes.statement: Let Γ be a finite group, H a Γ-group and G a profinite group. There is a bijection between Sur(G, H ⋊ Γ) (continuous surjections) and tuples (ρ, N, s, φ) with ρ ∈ Sur(G, Γ), N ⊆ ker ρ a closed normal subgroup of G, s : Γ → G/N a homomorphic section of the induced map ρ : G/N → Γ, and φ : ker ρ/N → H a Γ-isomorphism, where Γ acts on ker ρ/N through s and conjugation. The bijection sends ψ to (projection of ψ to Γ, ker ψ, ψ^{−1} restricted to Γ, ψ|_{ker ρ/N}).
hypotheses: Γ finite; H a Γ-group (finite in the application)
G profinite; homomorphisms continuous, N closed
proofSteps: Forward map as stated; ψ^{−1}(Γ) makes sense on G/N ≅ H ⋊ Γ.
Inverse: from 1 → ker ρ/N → G/N → Γ → 1 and the section s get G/N ≅ ker ρ/N ⋊ Γ; extend φ to ker ρ/N ⋊ Γ ≅ H ⋊ Γ (Mathlib SemidirectProduct and its universal properties) and compose with G → G/N.
The two constructions are mutually inverse (direct check).
acceptance: H = 1: surjections G → Γ correspond to (ρ, ker ρ, the unique section, the unique map).
Γ = 1: Sur(G, H) ↔ (N, φ) with φ : G/N ≅ H.

sources.excerpt: Lemma 9.1. Let Γ be a ﬁnite group, H a Γ-group, and G a proﬁnite group. We have a bijection from Sur(G, H ⋊Γ) to
sources.match: Statement of Lemma 9.1 (the tuple set (9.2) follows).

nodes.title: Complements of a coprime abelian normal subgroup are conjugate
nodes.statement: Let E be a finite group and H ⊴ E an abelian normal subgroup with gcd(|H|, [E : H]) = 1. Then H has a complement in E and any two complements are conjugate by an element of H. Consequently, for Γ finite and H a finite abelian Γ-group with gcd(|H|, |Γ|) = 1, the sections of H ⋊ Γ → Γ form one H-conjugacy orbit, and there are exactly [H : H^Γ] of them.
hypotheses: E finite; H abelian normal; |H| and [E : H] coprime
proofSteps: Existence is Mathlib's Schur–Zassenhaus theorem (Subgroup.exists_right_complement'_of_coprime).

Two complements K, K' ≅ Γ := E/H give a 1-cocycle c : Γ → H with k' = c(γ)k; H¹(Γ, H) is killed by |Γ| (corestriction–restriction) and by |H|, hence is 0 when they are coprime, so c is a coboundary c(γ) = γ(h)h^{−1} and K' = h K h^{−1}.
Sections of H ⋊ Γ → Γ correspond to complements; H acts on them by conjugation transitively, with stabiliser of the standard section Γ equal to H^Γ.
acceptance: H = 1: one section.
Γ = Z/2 acting by −1 on H = Z/3: [H : H^Γ] = 3 sections, the three involutions' subgroups of S_3.

sources.excerpt: the Schur–Zassenhaus theorem says that all sections s: Γ →G/N of ρ: G/N →Γ diﬀer by conjugation of elements of ker ρ/N. Since the stabilizer of the action of ker ρ/N on these sections is (ker ρ/N)Γ, we have that the number of sections is [ker ρ/N : (ker ρ/N)Γ] = [H : HΓ].
sources.match: The section count, proved here for abelian ker ρ/N.

nodes.notes: Conjugacy of complements for nonabelian coprime H (Schur–Zassenhaus in general, which needs Feit–Thompson or a solvability hypothesis) is planned by the accepted Part II ArithmeticStatisticsPartIIRandomGammaGroups, which imports ST.5; ST.5 therefore states LWZB Lemma 9.3 and Theorem 1.4 with an explicit section-conjugacy hypothesis and proves that hypothesis here only in the abelian case needed by Corollary 1.5.

nodes.title: LWZB Lemma 9.3: moments of unramified H-extensions as counts of H ⋊ Γ-extensions
nodes.statement: Let Γ be finite, Q = Q or F_q(t), and H a finite Γ-group with gcd(|H|, |Γ|) = 1 such that (SZ) all sections of H ⋊ Γ → Γ are H-conjugate (true when H is abelian: ST.5/complements-of-a-coprime-abelian-normal-subgroup-are-conjugate). Let N(H, Γ, D, Q) be the number of surjections Gal(Q̄/Q) → H ⋊ Γ whose H ⋊ Γ-extension K has rDisc K = D, whose H-extension K/K^H is unramified everywhere and split completely above ∞, and whose Γ-extension K^H/Q is split completely at ∞. Then Σ_ρ |Sur_Γ(Gal(K_ρ^{un,∞}/K_ρ)^{(|Γ|′)}, H)| = [H : H^Γ]^{−1} N(H, Γ, D, Q), where ρ runs over surjections Gal(Q̄/Q) → Γ split completely at ∞ with rDisc = D (Γ-extensions with their identification, not isomorphism classes) and the Γ-action is that of the chosen section on the maximal pro-|Γ|′ quotient. Summing instead over isomorphism classes E_Γ(D, Q), the right side acquires the factor |Z(Γ)|/|Γ|.
hypotheses: Γ finite; H finite Γ-group with gcd(|H|, |Γ|) = 1
(SZ): sections of H ⋊ Γ → Γ are H-conjugate
left side summed over surjections ρ (see the correction for isomorphism classes)
proofSteps: Apply ST.5/surjections-onto-a-semidirect-product with G = Gal(Q̄/Q).

For each ρ, the maximal pro-|Γ|′ quotient ker ρ/M carries a distinguished section s_ρ (LWZB Definition 2.1); tuples with s = s_ρ correspond to Γ-surjections ker ρ/M → H; the local conditions and rDisc = D match on both sides.
By (SZ), all sections of G/N → Γ are ker ρ/N-conjugate with stabiliser (ker ρ/N)^Γ, so there are [H : H^Γ] sections, each with the same number of φ's.

Isomorphism classes of Γ-extensions are orbits of Inn(Γ) of size [Γ : Z(Γ)] on surjections, and |Sur_Γ(…, H)| is constant on orbits; this gives the factor |Z(Γ)|/|Γ| (sourceIssues ArithmeticStatistics/E673).

nodes.title: LWZB Theorem 1.4: moments of Gal(K^#/K) over F_q(t) as q → ∞
nodes.statement: Let Γ be finite and H a finite admissible Γ-group satisfying (SZ). For prime powers q with gcd(q, |Γ||H|) = 1 and gcd(q − 1, |H|) = 1 put R_b(q) := Σ_{n ≤ b} Σ_{K ∈ E_Γ(q^n, F_q(t))} |Sur_Γ(Gal(K^#/K), H)| / Σ_{n ≤ b} |E_Γ(q^n, F_q(t))|, where E_Γ(D, F_q(t)) is the set of Γ-extensions of F_q(t) split completely at ∞ with radical discriminant norm D and K^# is the maximal unramified extension of K split completely above ∞ with all finite subextensions of degree prime to q(q − 1)|Γ|. Then lim_{b→∞} limsup_{q→∞} R_b(q) = lim_{b→∞} liminf_{q→∞} R_b(q) = [H : H^Γ]^{−1}. For each b every limit point of R_b(q) in q lies within O_G(1/b) of [H : H^Γ]^{−1}; the existence of lim_{q→∞} R_b(q) is not proved.
hypotheses: Γ finite; H finite admissible Γ-group; (SZ)
q prime power, gcd(q, |Γ||H|) = 1, gcd(q − 1, |H|) = 1 (these force |H| odd)
proofSteps: By ST.5/counting-unramified-h-extensions-via-semidirect-extensions (the normalisation factor cancels in the ratio) the numerator is [H : H^Γ]^{−1} Σ_{n ≤ b} N(H, Γ, q^n, F_q(t)); the Γ-surjections from Gal(K^{un,∞}/K) onto H factor through Gal(K^#/K) because |H| is prime to q(q − 1)|Γ|.
N(H, Γ, q^n, F_q(t)) = #Hur^n_{G,c}(F_q) with G = H ⋊ Γ and c the elements of the order of their image in Γ; the denominator is Σ_n #Hur^n_{Γ,Γ∖1}(F_q) (LWZB Lemma 10.2, IG.5).

Grothendieck–Lefschetz (SF.2), Deligne's bound (DWP.7) and the Betti comparison (LWZB Lemma 10.3, IG.5) give |#Hur^b(F_q) − π(q, b) q^b| ≤ B(b) Σ_{j<2b} q^{j/2}, with the top-degree trace counting Frobenius-fixed components (ST.5/top-cohomology-counts-rational-components); lower n contribute O_b(q^{b−1/2}).

LWZB Theorem 10.4 (IG.5): π_{G,c}(q, b) = π_Γ(q, b) + O_G(b^{d_Γ(q)−2}) and π_Γ(q, b) ≥ C_G b^{d_Γ(q)−1} on the residues where it is nonzero; so R_b(q) = [H : H^Γ]^{−1}(1 + O_G(b^{−1}) + O_b(q^{−1/2})) along each residue class of q mod |G|², hence every limit point in q lies in [H : H^Γ]^{−1}(1 + O_G(1/b)).

Let b → ∞. The printed lim_q is replaced by limsup/liminf (sourceIssues ArithmeticStatistics/E672); the value is the μ_Γ-moment of the random-group model, whose identification (LWZB Theorem 6.2) belongs to ArithmeticStatisticsPartIIRandomGammaGroups and is not used here.
acceptance: Γ = Z/2, H = Z/3 with inversion: [H : H^Γ]^{−1} = 1/3, the real-quadratic Cohen–Lenstra 3-moment, in the q → ∞ mode.
Even |H| is excluded by the hypotheses (q or q − 1 is even).

nodes.title: LWZB Corollary 1.5: Cohen–Lenstra–Martinet moments over F_q(t)
nodes.statement: Let Γ be finite and H a finite abelian Γ-group with gcd(|H|, |Γ|) = 1 and H^Γ = 1. Then with q running over prime powers with gcd(q, |Γ||H|) = 1 and gcd(q − 1, |H|) = 1, lim_{b→∞} limsup_q and lim_{b→∞} liminf_q of Σ_{n ≤ b} Σ_{K ∈ E_Γ(q^n, F_q(t))} |Sur_Γ(Cl(O_K), H)| / Σ_{n ≤ b} |E_Γ(q^n, F_q(t))| both equal |H|^{−1}.
hypotheses: Γ finite; H finite abelian Γ-group, gcd(|H|, |Γ|) = 1, H^Γ = 1
q as in ST.5/liu-wood-zureick-brown-function-field-moments
proofSteps: An abelian Γ-group is admissible iff gcd(|H|, |Γ|) = 1 and H^Γ = 1 (LWZB §7.1); (SZ) holds by ST.5/complements-of-a-coprime-abelian-normal-subgroup-are-conjugate.
By class field theory for function fields (FunctionFieldArithmetic:FA.4), Gal(K^#/K)^{ab} is the prime-to-q(q − 1)|Γ| part of Cl(O_K), so Γ-surjections onto the abelian H coincide.
Apply ST.5/liu-wood-zureick-brown-function-field-moments: [H : H^Γ]^{−1} = |H|^{−1}.
acceptance: Γ = Z/2 acting by −1 on H = Z/ℓ^k (ℓ odd): the real-quadratic Cohen–Lenstra moment |H|^{−1}.
Fields are ordered by radical discriminant, not discriminant.

These are Layer 8's stated targets; ST.0 composes them with the invariant map (I, J) = (−3a₄, −27a₆) and does not restate them.

Hasse-Minkowski for ternary forms over a number field: if K is a number field and Q a regular ternary quadratic form over K that is isotropic over every finite completion K_v and every real completion, then Q is isotropic over K (the Layer 5.1 ternary case, with localization by QuadraticForm.baseChange along the actual maps into the completions).

Functoriality of the explicit 2-descent (built in TauCeti/AlgebraicGeometry/EllipticCurve/MordellWeil) under a variable change of short Weierstrass curves: for W, W' over a field K with W' obtained by x' = u^2 x, y' = u^3 y (u in K^x), the K-algebra isomorphism W.A = W'.A, T |-> u^2 T, induces a group isomorphism W.M = W'.M that intertwines μ with the induced isomorphism of point groups, commutes with localRes for every field extension L/K, maps localCondition to localCondition, and maps selmerGroup₂ R Loc of W onto that of W'.

The Layer 7 identification of the explicit etale-algebra 2-Selmer group selmerGroup₂ (Layer 6) with the cohomological Sel_2(E/K) in H^1(K, E[2]), under which μ becomes the Kummer connecting map, together with the exact sequence 0 -> E(K)/2E(K) -> Sel_2(E/K) -> Sha(E/K)[2] -> 0.

A uniform bound for cubic Thue equations: there is an absolute constant N such that for every binary cubic form g in Z[x, y] with nonzero discriminant, #{(x, y) in Z^2 : g(x, y) = 1} <= N (N = 12 by Delone-Nagell for negative and Evertse (Invent. Math. 73, 1983) for positive discriminant; N = 10 by Bennett (Trans. AMS 353, 2001)). A uniform N of any size suffices (for example via Siegel's identity and the uniform bound for nondegenerate solutions of unit equations, DiophantineApproximationAndTranscendence:DT.2/uniform-bound-nondegenerate-solutions, with the unit rank of the splitting field bounded by 5).

Davenport's lemma for bounded semialgebraic multisets (Bhargava-Shankar, Proposition 2.6; Bhargava-Shankar-Tsimerman, Proposition 24), with its projection-volume error and uniform constants: for all n, m, k, ℓ there is a constant C = C(n, m, k, ℓ) such that for every bounded semialgebraic multiset R ⊂ ℝ^n of maximum multiplicity at most m, defined by at most k polynomial inequalities of degree at most ℓ, and for every image R′ of R under an upper or lower triangular unipotent linear map, |#(R′ ∩ ℤ^n) − Vol(R)| ≤ C·max(Vol(R̄), 1), where the lattice points are counted with multiplicity and Vol(R̄) is the largest d-dimensional volume (1 ≤ d ≤ n − 1) of a projection of R onto a coordinate subspace obtained by setting n − d coordinates to 0. The consumers apply it to the affine images (R − v_0)/m to count points of translates v_0 + mℤ^n; the constant must not depend on R beyond (n, m, k, ℓ).

The divisor bound: for every ε > 0 there is a constant C_ε such that the number d(n) of positive divisors of n satisfies d(n) ≤ C_ε·n^ε for every integer n ≥ 1 (Hardy-Wright, Theorem 315). Mathlib has only d(n) ≤ n (Nat.card_divisors_le_self).

The p-adic orbital volume identity for binary cubic forms: for a prime p and a binary cubic form v0 over Z_p with Disc(v0) != 0, with dx the Haar measure on V_{Z_p} = Z_p^4 of total mass 1 and the twisted GL2(Z_p)-action, vol(GL2(Z_p) . v0) = p^{-4} |Disc(v0)|_p #GL2(F_p) / #Stab_{GL2(Z_p)}(v0). Equivalently, |Disc(x)|_p^{-1} dx is GL2(Q_p)-invariant and the orbit map g -> g . v0 has Jacobian p^{-4}|Disc(v0)|_p with respect to the Haar measure of GL2(Z_p) of total mass #GL2(F_p). This is the local density of an orbit of the prehomogeneous space of binary cubic forms (BST Lemma 32).

For a number field K = Q(alpha) of degree n inside a fixed algebraic closure: the permutation Galois group of K, the image of Gal(Qbar/Q) acting on the n embeddings K -> Qbar, identified with the degree-n action of (minpoly Q alpha).Gal on its roots (Layer 0 comparison milestone), independent of the choice of alpha and of numbering up to conjugacy in S_n.

The label predicates TransitiveGroupLabel for n <= 5 (in particular 3T1 = C3, 3T2 = S3, 4T5 = S4, 5T5 = S5), invariant under conjugation and renumbering, to restrict counts of cubic, quartic and quintic fields by Galois group.

(1) For a quadratic field K2: the Hilbert class field and gal_hilbertClassField_equiv_classGroup, giving a bijection between index-3 subgroups of Cl(K2) and unramified cyclic cubic extensions of K2 inside a fixed algebraic closure. (2) For the order O_f of conductor f in K2: ringClassField and gal_ringClassField_equiv_pic, and the characterisation that a cyclic extension L/K2 Galois over Q on which Gal(K2/Q) acts by inversion lies in the ring class field of some O_f, with conductor-discriminant formula Disc(K3) = Disc(K2) f^2 for the cubic subfields K3 of L when L/Q has group S3.

For an order O_f of conductor f in a quadratic field K2: the exact sequence 1 -> (O_K/fO_K)^x / ((Z/fZ)^x O_K^x) -> Pic(O_f) -> Cl(K2) -> 1 (the congruence description of Pic for quadratic orders), from which #Pic(O_f)[3] <= 3^{omega(f)+2} #Cl(K2)[3].

For a Galois extension L/Q with group G and a prime P of L over p with inertia group I: the ramification indices of the primes of a subfield L^H above p are the lengths of the orbits of I on G/H (equivalently on the embeddings of L^H), and the inertia group of L/L^N at P is I intersect N for a normal subgroup N; with the tame discriminant exponent v_P(different) = e - 1.
For an etale cubic Q_p-algebra of the form Q_p x F with F/Q_p a ramified quadratic extension: its discriminant ideal equals that of F, and the discriminant algebra (Q_p(sqrt(disc))) is F.

For a number field K and prime p: O_K/pO_K is isomorphic to the product over primes P | p of O_K/P^{e(P)}, and O_K/P^e is isomorphic to F_{p^{f(P)}}[t]/(t^e) (Dedekind-Kummer splitting dictionary), so the splitting type of p is read off from O_K/pO_K.
The tower formula for discriminants: for number fields F subset L, |Disc(L)| = |Disc(F)|^{[L:F]} N_{F/Q}(Disc(L/F)).

Reduced positive definite integral binary quadratic forms with the pinned canonical representatives (|b| <= a <= c, and b >= 0 whenever |b| = a or a = c): every positive definite form is SL2(Z)-equivalent to exactly one reduced form (the matrix-orbit to binary-quadratic-form correspondence of Layer 11, item (ix)).
Every quadratic field is isomorphic to Q(sqrt d) for a unique squarefree integer d != 0, 1 (Q(sqrt d) and Q(sqrt d') are isomorphic iff d = d' for squarefree d, d').

For every elliptic curve E over Q: the 2-Selmer group Sel_2(E/Q) ⊆ H¹(Q, E[2]) is finite (AEC X.4.2); the Shafarevich–Tate group Ш(E/Q) with the exact sequence 0 → E(Q)/2E(Q) → Sel_2(E/Q) → Ш(E/Q)[2] → 0 of F_2-vector spaces; and the named comparison of Sel_2(E/Q) with the explicit étale-algebra 2-Selmer group selmerGroup₂ of Layer 6, compatible with the descent maps.

Mordell–Weil for elliptic curves over Q and the explicit 2-descent rank bound: E(Q) finitely generated, #(im μ) = 2^{rank}·#E(Q)[2], and 2^{rank}·#E(Q)[2] ≤ #S for every finite subgroup S of the square classes containing im μ (built at the pin as fg_point_of_numberField, card_range_μ and pow_rank_le_card_of_range_μ_le).

(i) For an elliptic curve E over Q_p, E(Q_p) has a subgroup of finite index isomorphic to (Z_p, +): E_1(Q_p) ≅ Ê(pZ_p) for a minimal model (AEC VII.2.2 with Layer 1's formal group), Ê(p^rZ_p) ≅ (p^rZ_p, +) through the formal logarithm for r > 1/(p − 1) (AEC IV.6.4), E_0(Q_p)/E_1(Q_p) ≅ Ẽ_ns(F_p) finite (AEC VII.2.1) and [E(Q_p) : E_0(Q_p)] finite. (ii) For a Weierstrass equation over Z_p with Δ ≠ 0, the reduction type (good, multiplicative, additive) of its minimal model is locally constant in the coefficients on {Δ ≠ 0}.

Every elliptic curve over Q is isomorphic to E_{A,B} for a unique minimal pair (A, B) (IsMinimalPairNF with exists_minimalPairModel and minimalPairModel_unique), so that Q-isomorphism classes of naive height < X correspond to minimal pairs with max{4|A|³, 27B²} < X.

For an elliptic curve E over a number field F and a prime p: the discrete p^∞-Selmer group Sel_{p^∞}(E/F) (direct limit of the Kummer Selmer groups Sel_{p^k}), its structure (ℚ_p/ℤ_p)^c ⊕ (finite) and the corank c = corank_{ℤ_p} Sel_{p^∞}(E/F) = dim_{ℚ_p} Hom(Sel_{p^∞}, ℚ_p/ℤ_p) ⊗ ℚ_p; the exact sequence 0 → E(F)[p^∞]/p^k → Sel_{p^k}(E/F) → Sel_{p^∞}(E/F)[p^k] → 0; and, per the confirmed fix of RT-PAPER-BURUNGALE-TIAN-26/15 (item isogeny-selmer-corank), for an F-isogeny φ : E → E' the equality corank_{ℤ_p} Sel_{p^∞}(E/F) = corank_{ℤ_p} Sel_{p^∞}(E'/F) for every p (φ and φ̂ induce maps whose composites are [deg φ]).

Per the confirmed fix of RT-PAPER-BURUNGALE-TIAN-26/14 (item congruent-2-parity): for E : y² = x³ − x and every positive squarefree n ≡ 1, 2, 3 (mod 8), corank_{ℤ_2} Sel_{2^∞}(E^(n)/ℚ) is even, where E^(n) : ny² = x³ − x. Source route: 2-parity (−1)^{corank_{ℤ_2} Sel_{2^∞}(E^(n)/ℚ)} = w(E^(n)/ℚ) (Monsky, Math. Z. 221 (1996); T. Dokchitser, Notes on the parity conjecture, Theorem 5.1, for curves with a rational 2-torsion point) together with the root numbers w(E^(n)/ℚ) = +1 exactly for positive squarefree n ≡ 1, 2, 3 mod 8 (Birch–Stephens; item congruent-root-number at RankZeroOneBSD:BSD.0).

For an isogeny φ : E → E' of elliptic curves over a number field and every place v: the images of the local Kummer maps E'(F_v)/φE(F_v) → H¹(F_v, E[φ]) and E(F_v)/φ̂E'(F_v) → H¹(F_v, E'[φ̂]) are exact annihilators of each other under local Tate duality for the Weil pairing E[φ] × E'[φ̂] → μ_{deg φ}, so that Sel_φ(E) and Sel_φ̂(E') are dual Selmer structures.

The Greenberg–Wiles (Poitou–Tate) Euler characteristic formula for a finite Galois module M over a number field F with a Selmer structure L and its dual structure L^* on M^∨(1): #Sel_L(M)/#Sel_{L^*}(M^∨(1)) = (#H⁰(F, M)/#H⁰(F, M^∨(1))) · ∏_v #L_v/#H⁰(F_v, M).

Per the confirmed finding RT-PAPER-BURUNGALE-TIAN-26/16, for elliptic curves over a number field F containing an imaginary quadratic K with End_F(E) an order O ⊆ O_K: the order and ideal action; for an invertible ideal 𝔭 of norm 3 the ideal-kernel isogeny E → E/E[𝔭] of degree 3 with End(E/E[𝔭]) ≅ O_K when End(E) ≅ O_K; existence, for each ideal class, of a prime ideal representative of norm ℓ ≠ 3 and the corresponding ℓ-isogeny E' → E; the normalised action of O_K on the invariant differential (a ∈ O_K acts on the formal group with derivative a at the origin, so |a'(0)|_v = |a|_v); a K-isogeny from a curve with CM by an order to one with CM by O_K (Rubin, Cetraro notes, Prop. 5.3); and invariance of End under quadratic twist.
The j-invariant of an elliptic curve with complex multiplication is an algebraic integer.

Counting form of Hilbert irreducibility for ℚ(A, B): a thin subset of ℤ² has o(X^{5/6}) points in the box |A| ≤ X^{1/3}, |B| ≤ X^{1/2} (more precisely O(X^{5/6 − δ}) for some δ > 0, after Cohen–Serre).

Large-sieve bounds for bilinear sums of quadratic symbols (a/p)(p/q) over squarefree integers with prescribed prime factors, as used by Kane §§5–7 to bound the non-principal 'character' terms in the moments of #Sel_2(E_b).

Isogenies of elliptic curves, the dual isogeny, the invariant differential and formal groups, with the derivative at the origin of the formal-group map induced by an isogeny (used in the Schaefer formula c(φ) = c(E')/c(E)·|φ'(0)|^{−1}) and Vélu's formula for 2-isogenies.

Over a p-adic field: minimal models, reduction types (Tate's algorithm, Kodaira types), the filtration E(F) ⊇ E_0(F) ⊇ E_1(F) and the Tamagawa number c = #E(F)/E_0(F); the Néron–Ogg–Shafarevich criterion and potential good reduction for integral j.

The quadratic twist E^s of an elliptic curve by F(√s)/F (WeierstrassCurve.quadraticTwist), its points as the (−1)-eigenspace for the twisting character, twists of isogenies, and the isomorphism ny² = x³ − x ≅ y² = x³ − n²x.
Mordell–Weil: E(ℚ) finitely generated, so rank E(ℚ) ≥ 2 gives (ℤ/n)² ↪ E(ℚ)/nE(ℚ).

Selmer structures on finite Galois modules and the elliptic Selmer groups Sel_m(E/F) and Sel_φ(E/F) for isogenies φ (Kummer local conditions), the Kummer injection E(F)/mE(F) ↪ Sel_m(E/F), Ш(E/F) and the m-descent exact sequence.

The absolute local Artin map for a p-adic field F_v, identifying the image of inertia in G_{F_v}^{ab} with the image of O_v^×, so that every finite-order character of inertia with values in an abelian group and trivial on commutators extends to G_{F_v}.

Browning–Le Boudec–Sawin, Lemma 3.9 (PAPER-BROWNING-LEBOUDEC-SAWIN-23/congruence-det, routed to GN.0): for N ≥ 2, Q ≥ 1 and linearly independent primitive c, d ∈ ℤ^N, the lattice Λ^{(Q)}_c ∩ Λ^{(Q)}_d, where Λ^{(Q)}_c = {y ∈ ℤ^N : ⟨c, y⟩ ≡ 0 mod Q}, has determinant (index in ℤ^N) Q²/gcd(G(c, d), Q), G(c, d) being the gcd of the 2×2 minors of (c, d).

The model ring with positive involution R_{L,n} = ∏_i M_{n_i}(O_{L_i}) of Lipnowski–Tsimerman Definition 5.1 (L_i distinct CM fields, ∗ = conjugate transpose; PAPER-LIPNOWSKI-TSIMERMAN-18/model-ring), and its quaternionic analogue M_m(O_D) for a maximal order O_D of the definite quaternion algebra D over ℚ(√p) ramified exactly at the two infinite places, with the canonical involution composed with transpose.

(a) The orbit count n_{L,n} of R_{L,n}^× on positive symmetric units under a ↦ γ*aγ (PAPER-LIPNOWSKI-TSIMERMAN-18/model-orbit-count) and the corrected bound (55) (model-count-source, E13): log n_{L,n} ≤ (1/2)Σ_i [K_i:ℚ]n_i² log n_i + O_p(g²) where Σ_i [K_i:ℚ]n_i = g and the L_i arise from p-Weil numbers. (b) For the quaternionic model: the number n_D(m) of GL_m(O_D)-orbits on positive definite quaternion-hermitian matrices in GL_m(O_D) satisfies log n_D(m) ≤ 2m² log m + O_p(m²) (from the mass of unimodular quaternion-hermitian lattices, ∏_{i≤m}|ζ_{ℚ(√p)}(1 − 2i)| up to exp(O(m²)), and the automorphism-group bound).

Principal polarizations of abelian varieties over a field, isomorphisms of polarized abelian varieties, and the count n_A of isomorphism classes of principal polarizations on A as Aut(A)-orbits (PAPER-LIPNOWSKI-TSIMERMAN-18/polarization, polarized-isomorphism, polarization-orbits).

Poincaré complete reducibility up to isogeny and the semisimple rational endomorphism algebra End⁰(A) = ∏ M_{n_i}(End⁰(A_i)) (PAPER-LIPNOWSKI-TSIMERMAN-18/poincare-decomposition, rational-endomorphism).
The Hasse bound |#E(𝔽_q) − q − 1| ≤ 2√q for an elliptic curve over a finite field 𝔽_q, used for q = p and q = p².

Arithmetic Hurwitz schemes and their point counts, as used by EVW §§7–8, Wood 2019 §4 and LWZB §§10–12: (a) for a finite group G and a rational union of classes c generating G, the scheme Hn^c_{G,n} of tame G-covers of P¹ branched at n points of A¹ (and possibly ∞) with finite inertia in c, finite étale over Conf_n over Z[1/|G|], whose k-points for G centre-free and any field k of characteristic prime to |G| are the isomorphism classes of such covers defined over k (EVW §§7.1, 7.3; PAPER-ELLENBERG-VENKATESH-WESTERLAND-16 /63–/65); (b) the tame cohomological specialization of EVW Proposition 7.7 with Z/λ^k and Q_λ coefficients (/68) and Lemma 10.3 of LWZB; (c) Wood's marked scheme CHur^{c,g}_{F,m} with Theorem 4.5(1)–(3) (points = marked (F, c)-extensions of the prescribed infinity type; stable Frobenius-fixed components ↔ fixed lifting invariants) and the uniform component estimate |#C(F_q) − q^n| ≤ K_n q^{n−1/2} of Theorem 4.7, and the q-uniform component bound D_d (PAPER-WOOD-19 /77–/80, /86, /88, /314); (d) LWZB's Hur^n_{G,c} with Lemma 10.2 (points count N(H, Γ, q^n, F_q(t))), Lemma 10.3 and Theorem 10.4 (Frobenius-fixed components of G- and Γ-schemes agree up to O_G(n^{d_Γ(q)−2}) with a lower bound C_G n^{d_Γ(q)−1}) (PAPER-LIU-WOOD-ZUREICKBROWN-24 /30–/34, /37, /38, /40, /41).

Galois-category dictionary for finite étale covers of connected (Deligne–Mumford) bases: connected components of a finite étale cover are orbits of the geometric fundamental group on the geometric generic fibre; over F_q a component is defined over F_q iff Frobenius preserves the orbit; a dense open immersion into a connected normal base and a representable smooth surjection with geometrically connected fibres induce surjections on étale π₁ (PAPER-ELLENBERG-VENKATESH-WESTERLAND-16 /127, /132, /133).

The arithmetic/geometric fundamental-group exact sequence for geometrically connected schemes over F_q; the labelled odd-degree hyperelliptic family adapter: the lifted affine group B_n, its connectedness, and the quotient presentation [PConf_n/B_n] ≃ H̃_g^{sm} keeping the hyperelliptic involution (PAPER-ELLENBERG-VENKATESH-WESTERLAND-16 /128–/131, /136); and the corrected Achter–Pries exact sequence 1 → (A ∩ Sp)/G → A/G → χ_λ(G_F) → 1 for the arithmetic and geometric images (/137).
