Class field theory of global function fields: for a quadratic extension L of F_q(t) ramified at ∞ with a unique rational point above ∞, Cl(O_L) ≅ Pic⁰(C_L)(F_q), and the Galois group J_L of the maximal abelian unramified pro-ℓ extension (ℓ ∤ q) sits in 0 → Cl(O_L)_ℓ → J_L → Ẑ_ℓ → 0 compatibly with Gal(L/K); étale abelian A-covers of a curve over an algebraically closed field of characteristic prime to |A| correspond to surjections from Jac[ℓ^k]; for a Γ-extension K of F_q(t), Gal(K^#/K)^{ab} is the prime-to-q(q − 1)|Γ| part of Cl(O_K) (PAPER-ELLENBERG-VENKATESH-WESTERLAND-16 /85; LWZB §1).

The Grothendieck–Lefschetz trace formula |X(F_q)| = Σ_j (−1)^j Tr(Frob | H^j_c(X_{F̄_q}, Q_λ)) for separated schemes of finite type over F_q and primes λ ∤ q, with compactly supported cohomology (PAPER-ELLENBERG-VENKATESH-WESTERLAND-16 /93).

Poincaré duality for smooth separated schemes of pure dimension n over F̄_q with Q_λ coefficients, Frobenius-compatibly: H^j_c ≅ H^{2n−j}(−n)^∨, in particular H^{2n}_c of a geometrically connected smooth component is Q_λ(−n) (PAPER-ELLENBERG-VENKATESH-WESTERLAND-16 /91).

Deligne's weight bound: for X separated of finite type over F_q and λ ∤ q, every eigenvalue of geometric Frobenius on H^j_c(X_{F̄_q}, Q_λ) has all complex absolute values ≤ q^{j/2} (Weil II, Théorème 1) (PAPER-ELLENBERG-VENKATESH-WESTERLAND-16 /92).

For a principally polarized abelian scheme (the Jacobian of the relative curve y² = f(x)) over a base where ℓ is invertible: [ℓ^m] is finite étale of rank ℓ^{2mg}, the ℓ^m-torsion is a locally constant sheaf of free Z/ℓ^m-modules of rank 2g, and the Weil pairing induced by the polarization is perfect and alternating with values in μ_{ℓ^m}; the Tate-module pairing with its Tate twist.

gaps.title: Bhargava's uniformity estimate for weakly divisible discriminants of pairs of ternary quadratic forms (Theorem 2.19 = [4, Proposition 23])
gaps.detail: Needed: for W_ℤ = pairs (A, B) of integral ternary quadratic forms with GL_2(ℤ) × SL_3(ℤ) acting and the discriminant Δ(A, B) = Disc(4 Det(Ax − By)), the number of GL_2(ℤ) × SL_3(ℤ)-orbits on W_p^(2)(W) (Δ divisible by p^2 but not strongly) with |Δ| < X is O(X/p^2), the constant independent of p and X. Source: M. Bhargava, 'The density of discriminants of quartic rings and fields', Annals of Mathematics 162 (2005), 1031-1063, Proposition 23; not read (not publicly accessible to this job). Its proof uses the geometry of numbers for GL_2 × SL_3 on the 12-dimensional space W (reduction theory, the cusp analysis and the count of quartic rings of bounded discriminant) together with a switching map γ ∈ G(ℚ) dividing Δ by p^2 (Bhargava's geometric-sieve paper, Section 1.5, Condition 6). By RS-07, uniform orbit counts and tail estimates belong to ArithmeticStatistics:ST.2, so this geometry of numbers is ST.2 work; a public route is Bhargava-Shankar-Wang, 'Geometry-of-numbers methods over global fields I' (arXiv:1512.03035), which reproves the quartic counts over global fields. Resolution: add that source (or the Annals paper) to ST.2 and plan the count of GL_2(ℤ) × SL_3(ℤ)-orbits on W_ℤ and Proposition 23.

gaps.title: The bound O(X^{1/4}) for pairs of ternary quadratic forms with a fixed reducible cubic resolvent ([4, proof of Lemma 12])
gaps.detail: Needed in the proof of Bhargava-Shankar Lemma 2.4: if g is a reducible integral binary cubic form of height X, the number of GL_2(ℤ) × SL_3(ℤ)-orbits on W_ℤ whose cubic resolvent form 4 Det(Ax − By) is GL_2(ℤ)-equivalent to g is O(X^{1/4}). gaps.title: The uniformity for totally ramified primes rests on a class-field-theory argument that no source read proves
gaps.detail: BST Proposition 29 says N(Y_p; X) = O(X/p^2) 'follows easily from class field theory' and refers to Datskovsky-Wright, J. reine angew. Math. 386 (1988), p. 15, which is not public. The node reconstructs the standard argument for the maximal part (cubic fields totally ramified at p): the Galois closure of an S3-cubic field lies in a ring class field of its quadratic resolvent, Disc(K) = D_2 f^2 with f the conductor, p | f iff p is totally ramified, the 3-rank of Pic(O_f) is at most omega(f) + 2 more than that of Cl(K_2), and the sum of h_3 over quadratic fields is O(Y). The facts 'Disc(K) = D_2 f^2 with f the ring-class conductor' (Hasse) and the 3-rank bound for Pic(O_f) are not stated in any source read; they need their own nodes (or supplier contracts) consuming ClassFieldTheory Layer 13 and GlobalNumberFields Layer 11. The non-maximal part of Y_p, needed by BST Theorem 8 for acceptable specifications that allow non-maximal orders, is left to the uniform tail estimates of ArithmeticStatistics:ST.2 (for example Bhargava's geometric sieve applied to the codimension-2 locus of forms with a triple root).

gaps.title: The p-adic change-of-variables formula for polynomial maps has no owner in the atlas
gaps.detail: Needed statement: let U ⊆ Z_p^n be compact open and ψ: U → Q_p^n a map given by polynomials with coefficients in Q_p whose Jacobian determinant does not vanish on U. Then ψ is a local homeomorphism onto an open set, and for every nonnegative measurable φ on Q_p^n, ∫_{Q_p^n} φ(y)·#(ψ^{-1}(y) ∩ U) dy = ∫_U φ(ψ(x))·|det Dψ(x)|_p dx (Haar measure); together with the multivariable Hensel lemma (p-adic inverse function theorem) it rests on (Igusa, An introduction to the theory of local zeta functions, §7.4; Serre, Lie algebras and Lie groups, Part II). Mathlib has only the one-variable hensels_lemma over ℤ_[p] and no Haar-measure theory specific to Q_p^n (no MeasurableSpace instance on ℤ_[p] at the pin). Searched all atlas stages for 'change of variables', 'Igusa', 'p-adic integration', 'Jacobian', 'inverse function', 'Hensel': LogicAndDefinabilityInNumberTheory:LD.2 (definable integration, rationality of Igusa series) and TropicalAndBerkovichArithmetic:TB.7 mention p-adic integration but do not plan this formula. The source uses it implicitly in the proof of Proposition 3.12 (sourceIssue ArithmeticStatistics/E505). Recommendation: plan it once in a foundational p-adic analysis owner and import it here and in AnalyticNumberTheory:AN.8 (local zeta integrals).

gaps.title: The uniformity O(X/p²) for all integral binary cubic forms with p² | disc is only partly planned
gaps.detail: Proposition 3.16's per-prime bound needs Davenport–Heilbronn's Proposition 1 (the source's [19]): the GL_2(Z)-classes of integral binary cubic forms with |disc| < X and p² | disc number O(X/p²) uniformly in p. The forms with p² | disc are those nonmaximal at p (W_p) and the maximal ones totally ramified at p. ST.2 plans the W_p estimate (Bhargava–Shankar–Tsimerman Proposition 29) and ST.3 plans ArithmeticStatistics:ST.3/cubic-fields-totally-ramified-at-large-primes-are-sparse only for forms maximal at every prime. The union over all integral forms is stated by neither. It is not needed by Theorem 3.17 in this roadmap's route.

gaps.title: The Delone–Evertse uniform bound for cubic Thue equations has no owner
gaps.detail: Needed statement: an integral binary cubic form g with nonzero discriminant has at most 12 solutions (x, y) ∈ Z² of g(x, y) = 1 (Delone 1930 for negative discriminant, Evertse 1983 for positive discriminant; the source's [22], [25], not read). DiophantineApproximationAndTranscendence plans Thue's finiteness theorem (DT.1/thue-equation-finiteness) and effective bounds (DT.4), not a uniform count. The same input is used by ST.1's Proposition 2.16. It is not needed by Theorem 3.17 in this roadmap's route, which uses tail-estimate-for-square-divisors-of-the-discriminant instead of the per-prime bound.

gaps.title: Smith's 2^∞-Selmer distribution theorem (owned by ArithmeticStatisticsPartIISmithMethod)
gaps.detail: Stated input, not planned in ST.5: Smith I (JAMS 39 (2026)), Theorem 1.2: if A/ℚ satisfies Assumption 1.1 (ArithmeticStatistics:ST.5/smith-twist-family-hypothesis) then for r ≥ 0, lim_{H→∞} #{d ∈ ℤ \ {0} : |d| ≤ H, r_{2^∞}(A^d/ℚ) = r}/(2H) = 1/2, 1/2, 0 for r = 0, 1, ≥ 2 (with Remark 1.3's rate for r ≥ 2), proved through Smith II Theorem 2.14 and its §3 deduction. Per the confirmed finding RT-PAPER-BURUNGALE-TIAN-26/13 the proof (fixed-point Selmer groups, grids, bilinear equidistribution of symbols, regridding, Proposition 7.9's Hoeffding argument, governing expansions, Theorem 8.12 and the Markov-chain endgame) belongs to the accepted Part II ArithmeticStatisticsPartIISmithMethod, which imports ST.5. ST.5 therefore files no request (it would close a cycle): ArithmeticStatistics:ST.5/even-congruent-twists-have-corank-zero-given-smith-law takes Smith's conclusion as an explicit hypothesis, and the Part II discharges it to obtain Burungale–Tian Theorem 3.3 unconditionally. ST.5 supplies the Part II with the carrier (ArithmeticStatistics:ST.5/p-infinity-selmer-corank-distribution-in-twist-families), Assumption 1.1, the random alternating matrix laws P^Alt (ArithmeticStatistics:ST.5/alternating-matrix-kernel-law) and the conversion to Burungale–Tian's squarefree family.

gaps.title: Orbit parametrisations and counts for 3-, 4- and 5-Selmer elements
gaps.detail: The parametrisations of n-Selmer elements of E_{A,B}/ℚ by locally soluble orbits (n = 3: SL_3 on ternary cubic forms; n = 4: pairs of quaternary quadratic forms; n = 5: SL_5 × SL_5 on 5 ⊗ ∧²5), with integral representatives and stabilisers E[n], and the corresponding geometry-of-numbers counts and sieves, are in the scope of ArithmeticStatistics:ST.1 and ST.2 but are not among the source-scoped parametrisations those stages select (binary quartics for 2-Selmer). ST.5 states the theorems with their proof outlines; the decomposition of Bhargava–Shankar arXiv 1007.0052, 1312.7333 and 1312.7859 into ST.1/ST.2 nodes is missing.

gaps.title: Second-moment proof of Bhargava–Shankar–Swaminathan
gaps.detail: Theorem 1.2 of arXiv 2110.09063 (average 2-Selmer size ≤ 6 for Jacobians of locally soluble genus-one curves), the parametrisation of 2-Selmer groups of hyperelliptic Jacobians by pairs of n-ary quadratic forms, the counting of special SL_4- and PSO_A-orbits via equidistribution, and the assembly of §7 are not decomposed.

gaps.title: Kane's character-sum estimates and Swinnerton-Dyer's combinatorial theorem
gaps.detail: Swinnerton-Dyer's theorem (the proportion π_d(n) of local data with dim Sel_2 = d tends to α_d as the number of prime factors grows; Proc. Cambridge Philos. Soc. 145 (2008), not public) and Kane's analytic estimates (arXiv 1009.1365 §§3–7) are not decomposed. Heath-Brown's papers (Invent. Math. 111, 118) are not public.

gaps.title: BKLOS binary-cubic parametrisation and counting over number fields
gaps.detail: BKLOS §§3–8: the correspondence between φ-coverings and SL_2(F)-orbits of binary cubic forms (Theorems 4.2, 5.3), integral models (Theorem 6.2, Proposition 6.1, Corollary 7.1), and the count via Bhargava–Shankar–Wang, 'Geometry-of-numbers methods over global fields I' (BKLOS ref. [7], Theorem 13) with the uniformity estimate of ref. [8], Theorem 17. Not decomposed; the counting theorem over number fields has no accepted owner (the Bhargava–Shankar–Wang routes to ST.0–ST.3 were not accepted).

gaps.title: Cassels–Tate pairing and its isogeny adjointness
gaps.detail: Needed: for a p-isogeny φ : E → E' over a number field, Ш(E')[φ̂]/φ(Ш(E)[p]) carries a nondegenerate alternating pairing induced by the Cassels–Tate pairing (φ is adjoint for the pairing; BES ref. [14], Theorem 1.2), hence has even 𝔽_p-dimension. No atlas stage plans the Cassels–Tate pairing (EllipticCurves Layer 7 plans Ш but not the pairing; SelmerIwasawaCohomology L1–L2 plan duality of Selmer structures, not the pairing on Ш).

gaps.title: Local invariants of isogenous elliptic curves at 2 and 3
gaps.detail: Dokchitser–Dokchitser, 'Local invariants of isogenous elliptic curves', Trans. Amer. Math. Soc. 367 (2015), Lemmas 4.6–4.7 (norm-index expressions for c(E')/c(E) under a quadratic twist over 2-adic and 3-adic fields) and Table 1 (BKLOS Proposition 10.4). Not read; no atlas owner.

gaps.title: Rubin's CM lemmas
gaps.detail: Rubin, 'Elliptic curves with complex multiplication and the conjecture of Birch and Swinnerton-Dyer' (LNM 1716, 1999), 5.22, Proposition 3.14 and Proposition 5.3, are cited by BKLOS and imported through the ComplexMultiplicationAndExplicitReciprocity CM.1/CM.3 requests; the text is not public and was not read, so the exact statements are taken from BKLOS's citations.

gaps.title: Canonical measure on ℤ_p-points (Oesterlé–Serre) and the orthogonal Grassmannian
gaps.detail: BKLPR Proposition 2.1 (the measure on X(ℤ_p) for a finite-type ℤ_p-scheme as the limit of normalised counts modulo p^e, and the vanishing on lower-dimensional subschemes, after Oesterlé and Serre), Proposition 4.4 (OGr_n is smooth projective of relative dimension n(n−1)/2) and Propositions 4.5, 4.9 (components and Schubert loci). No atlas owner was found for the Oesterlé–Serre measure.

gaps.title: p-rank marginal of A_1
gaps.detail: The identity Σ_{G : dim G[p] = 2n} A_1(G) = Prob(X_{Ш[p],1} = 2n) (the p-rank marginal of BKLPR's A_1 is Delaunay's rank-one law) is used in the (r = 1)-part of the consequence (iii); BKLPR Theorem 1.6(c) (T_r equals Delaunay's distribution) implies it but its proof through [Del01] was not read. The r = 0 part is proved in ST.5 through the alternating kernel law.

gaps.title: Generic mod-p image of E_{A,B}
gaps.detail: For odd p, the curve y² = x³ + Ax + B over ℚ(A, B) has no rational point of order p (its mod-p Galois image is GL_2(𝔽_p), Igusa). No atlas stage was found that plans this generic-image statement.

gaps.title: de Jong's function-field 3-Selmer bound
gaps.detail: A. J. de Jong, 'Counting elliptic surfaces over finite fields', Moscow Math. J. 2 (2002), 281–311: available as DVI only; not read. The statement is taken from Poonen–Rains §1.2 and Bhargava–Shankar §1.

gaps.title: Wood's moment-determination theorem (proof not decomposed)
gaps.detail: ST.5/moments-determine-cohen-lenstra-limits-for-all-p-and-u cites Wood, Random integral matrices (Amer. J. Math. 2019) Theorem 3.1, whose proof is Theorem 8.3 of Wood, 'The distribution of sandpile groups of random graphs' (J. Amer. Math. Soc. 30 (2017), arXiv 1402.5149, §8). That proof (moments bounded by |∧²G| determine the limit, via an inclusion–exclusion over subgroups with explicit convergence) was not read or decomposed. It is needed for p = 2 and for u ≥ 1; for p odd and u = 0 the EVW route (ST.5/moment-convergence-implies-distribution-convergence) is complete. Owner: ST.5 (random-group distributions); decompose arXiv 1402.5149 §8.

gaps.title: MacWilliams recursion for symmetric matrices of given rank
gaps.detail: The product formula is taken from the public restatement (arXiv 2509.10332, citing MacWilliams 1969, Theorem 2) and checked by enumeration over F_2 for s ≤ 4; MacWilliams' proof (Amer. Math. Monthly 76 (1969), 152–164, not publicly available) was not read. The recursion step outlined in the node (extension of a symmetric s × s matrix by a row, column and corner, with the rank jump 0, 1 or 2) must be written out and solved, separately for odd q and for characteristic 2 (alternating versus non-alternating forms).

gaps.title: Certified D_4 comparison
gaps.detail: LOWW's table gives the proven D_4 averages of h_3(K) over ℚ only numerically (≈ 1.12, 1.34, 2.01, 1.41). Proving that each differs from the prediction (40/27, 16/9, 8/3, 8/3) needs an explicit error-bounded evaluation of Σ_F h_3(F)Res_{s=1}ζ_F/(ζ_F(2)Disc(F)²) over quadratic F with a proved tail bound; the node records the structural comparison (weighted versus uniform average of h_3(F)) and leaves the inequalities as this gap.

gaps.title: Existence of the enhanced Cohen–Lenstra limits (Lipnowski–Tsimerman Definition 5.16)
gaps.detail: Definition 5.16 writes CL_{n,ℓ} as a limit over g without proving that it exists or has total mass one (PAPER-LIPNOWSKI-TSIMERMAN-18/E16; ArithmeticStatistics/E622). The blueprint defines the finite-g laws, the existence proposition EnhancedCohenLenstraLimitExists and the limit, and makes the conjecture conditional on existence. A proof of existence (for example by a moment method for the joint cokernels of 1 − F^{n_j}, which are not coprime polynomials in F) is missing; Example 5.17 gives only a positive lim inf at odd ℓ.

gaps.title: Finite-field abelian-variety inputs owned by the proposed Part II AbelianSchemesAndArithmeticModuliPartIIFiniteFields
gaps.detail: The Part II (route 10 of PAPER-LIPNOWSKI-TSIMERMAN-18, accepted; no design and no stage ids yet) owns: (a) the corrected Lemma 5.11 (elliptic-power-source): for p split in one of the nine class-number-one imaginary quadratic fields there is E_0/𝔽_p with log n_{E_0^g} = (1/2)g² log g + O_p(g²); (b) the corrected Theorem 0.1 (main-unpolarized-source, Lee 2022): log B(p, g) = O_p(g²); (c) Frobenius polynomials of abelian varieties over 𝔽_p, their multiplicativity and isogeny invariance, and #A(𝔽_{p^r}) = P_A-values (weil-polynomial, isogeny-polynomial, point-count-isogeny); (d) the prime-field endomorphism algebras: End⁰ of a simple A/𝔽_p is a CM field of degree 2 dim A unless its Frobenius is ±√p, which is the isogeny class of B_0 (prime-field-end-algebra, Proposition 4.14); (e) the corrected Lemma 5.19 (elliptic-pgroups-large): for odd p, E(𝔽_p) and E(𝔽_{p²}) are not both p-groups. ST.5 imports these once the Part II is designed; the Part II imports ST.0's counting measures and must not import ST.5, so no cycle arises.

gaps.title: The GUE spacing law is not planned anywhere
gaps.detail: Lipnowski–Tsimerman compare μ_g with the GUE normalized spacing law μ_GUE (Gaudin–Mehta distribution, defined through the Fredholm determinant of the sine kernel). No roadmap plans it (AnalyticNumberTheory:AN.5 plans random-matrix predictions only as conjectural models). The node is stated for every probability measure ν with ν((−∞, 0]) = 0, which covers μ_GUE once it is defined and shown to be absolutely continuous on [0, ∞); naming μ_GUE itself needs that definition.

gaps.title: EVW homological stability and uniform Betti bound (stated input)
gaps.detail: Owner: the accepted Part II InverseGaloisPartIIHurwitzHomologicalStability (Inverse Galois theory and arithmetic fundamental groups, Part II: homological stability of Hurwitz spaces), which has no stage ids yet, so no request is filed. Statements used, exactly: EVW Theorem 6.1 — if (G, c) is nonsplitting and k is a field in which |G| is invertible, there are A, B with U : H_p(Hur^c_{G,n}, k) → H_p(Hur^c_{G,n+deg U}, k) an isomorphism for n > Ap + B, and likewise on CHur^c_{G,n}; Corollary 6.2 — the same for Hur^c_{G,n}/G and CHur^c_{G,n}/G when G is centre-free; Proposition 7.8 — for (G, c) nonsplitting, G centre-free, c a rational class generating G, there is C(G, c) with dim H^i_ét(Hn^c_{G,n} ⊗ F̄_q, Q_λ) ≤ C(G, c)^{i+1} for all i, n and λ > max(|G|, q, n). ST.5 consumes only Proposition 7.8 for (G_A, c_A). Once the Part II has stage ids, add a request to the stage exporting the uniform Betti estimate; that Part II does not import ArithmeticStatistics, so no cycle arises.

gaps.title: Reduced Schur multiplier inputs for Wood's component counts
gaps.detail: Wood Proposition 4.1 and Remark 4.2, in the refined forms PAPER-WOOD-19 /68–/70 and /301, /304 (for odd q coprime to |F|, the q^{−1}-fixed points of the universal marked central extension over (g, m) number |H₂(F, c)[q − 1]| or 0 according to a parity/2-adic criterion), and the surviving-parity rank data /337, /338, are owned by the accepted Part II InductionRestrictionPartIIReducedSchur, which has no stage ids yet. It is upstream of ArithmeticStatistics (its consumers import it), so a request is added once it is designed.

gaps.title: Full mod-ℓ monodromy of M_1 and M_2 (Achter–Pries base cases)
gaps.detail: Achter–Pries Theorem 3.4 starts from M_ℓ(M_g ⊗ k) ≅ Sp_{2g}(F_ℓ) for g = 1, 2 (Deligne–Mumford, Publ. IHÉS 36, 5.15–5.16) and from the absence of a common nontrivial quotient of Sym(2g + 2) and Sp_{2g}(F_ℓ) (simplicity of PSp_{2g}(F_ℓ), PSp_2(F_3) ≅ A_4). No atlas stage plans the monodromy of the moduli of curves of genus 1 and 2; the genus-1 case could be supplied by the connectedness of the modular curve X(ℓ) over Q(ζ_ℓ) (tauceti ModularCurves), the genus-2 case has no owner.

gaps.title: Moduli of labelled stable hyperelliptic curves and clutching
gaps.detail: Achter–Pries Lemmas 2.5 and 3.1 use the moduli stacks of labelled stable Z/2-curves with given class vector, their clutching maps into the boundary Δ_{1,1}, and the splitting of Pic⁰[ℓ] of a compact-type curve along a clutching. The tauceti StableReduction roadmap (Layer 3) plans stable pointed curves but not these moduli with clutching maps, and no atlas stage plans the hyperelliptic boundary degeneration; an owner (a moduli-of-curves roadmap) is needed.

gaps.title: Vasiu's surjectivity criterion for Sp_{2g}
gaps.detail: The proof of Vasiu's Main Theorem 1.3 in the case G = Sp_{2g} over Z_ℓ (ℓ odd, (g, ℓ) ≠ (1, 3)): irreducibility of the adjoint representation of Sp_{2g}(F_ℓ) on sp_{2g}(F_ℓ) (Vasiu 3.7.1), the congruence-kernel lifting (4.1.2), the non-splitting of Sp_{2g}(Z/ℓ²) → Sp_{2g}(F_ℓ) (4.5) and the assembly (4.7). Not in Mathlib and not planned by any atlas stage; the node records the statement, the (1, 3) counterexample and the outline.

gaps.title: Generation of Sp(V) by symplectic transvections
gaps.detail: For a nondegenerate symplectic space V over a field, Sp(V) is generated by the symplectic transvections x ↦ x + a⟨x, v⟩v (Artin, Geometric Algebra, Theorem 3.25). Mathlib has transvections only for GL and SL; no atlas stage plans the symplectic statement. It should be owned by a linear-algebra or classical-groups layer.

gaps.title: Schur–Zassenhaus conjugacy for nonabelian coprime H
gaps.detail: LWZB Lemma 9.3 and Theorem 1.4 need that all sections of H ⋊ Γ → Γ are H-conjugate for H of order prime to |Γ|; for nonabelian H this is the conjugacy half of Schur–Zassenhaus (needs Feit–Thompson or a solvability hypothesis). Its planned owner is the accepted Part II ArithmeticStatisticsPartIIRandomGammaGroups, which imports ST.5, so ST.5 cannot request it without a cycle. ST.5 states both results with the explicit hypothesis (SZ) and proves (SZ) for abelian H (ST.5/complements-of-a-coprime-abelian-normal-subgroup-are-conjugate). Maintainer: the finite coprime Schur–Zassenhaus conjugacy should move to a foundational group-theory supplier that both can import.

gaps.title: Second-order count of binary cubic forms (Bhargava-Shankar-Tsimerman Sections 6 and 9) is not an ST.2 node
gaps.detail: Missing from ST.2: BST Theorem 27, the count of GL2(Z)-classes of irreducible integral binary cubic forms in a translate v_0 + mU_Z with two main terms c_1 m^{-4} X + c_2(m) X^{5/6} and error O(X^{5/6-1/48+eps}) uniformly in m (Shintani's second term, obtained by slicing and smoothing in the cusp, BST Section 6), and the uniformity input of the refined sieve over large squarefree n (Belabas-Bhargava-Pomerance; BST Section 9). ST.2's coverage states these would be planned in ST.2 if ST.3 states Roberts' conjecture. The second-order p-adic densities and Lemma 37 (BST Section 7) are ST.3's own gap 'Second-order terms (BST Sections 6, 7 and 9) are not decomposed'.

gaps.title: Geometry of numbers for pairs of integral ternary quadratic forms (quartic rings) is not an ST.2 node
gaps.detail: Missing from ST.2: the asymptotic count of GL3(Z) x GL2(Z)-orbits of irreducible integral pairs (A, B) of ternary quadratic forms with 0 < +-Disc < X, by signature (Bhargava, Annals 162 (2005): averaging over a fundamental domain, cusp analysis), its version with finitely many congruence conditions, the uniformity estimate O(X/p^2) for quartic rings non-maximal at p needed for the sieve to maximal orders, and (for the 2-torsion mean) the count of those orbits whose cubic resolvent is a given maximal cubic ring. ST.2 counts only binary quartic and binary cubic forms; its existing gaps (Proposition 23 = BS Theorem 2.19, and the O(X^{1/4}) bound for a fixed reducible resolvent) concern the same representation.

gaps.title: Geometry of numbers for quadruples of quinary alternating forms (quintic rings) is not an ST.2 node
gaps.detail: Missing from ST.2: the asymptotic count of GL4(Z) x SL5(Z)-orbits of irreducible integral A in Z^4 (x) wedge^2 Z^5 with |Disc| < X by signature, its congruence version, and the uniformity estimate for quintic rings non-maximal at p (Bhargava, Annals 172 (2010)).

gaps.title: Orbit parametrisations of 3-, 4- and 5-Selmer elements are not ST.1 nodes
gaps.detail: Missing from ST.1: (3) the bijection between Sel_3(E_{A,B}) and SL3(Q)-classes of locally soluble ternary cubic forms whose invariants (c4, c6) match (A, B) up to fixed scalars, with integral representatives and stabiliser E[3] (ST.1 has only the forms and their invariants: ternary-cubic-forms-and-their-invariants, invariance-of-ternary-cubic-invariants); (4) the representation 2 (x) Sym^2(4) of G = {(g2, g4) : det g2 det g4 = 1}/{(lambda^{-2} I2, lambda I4)} (pairs of quaternary quadratic forms), its invariants and the parametrisation of 4-Selmer elements by locally soluble orbits; (5) SL5 x SL5 acting on quintuples of 5 x 5 alternating matrices and the parametrisation of 5-Selmer elements (ST.1's quadruples under GL4 x SL5 are the quintic-ring representation). Same content as ST.5's gap 'Orbit parametrisations of 3-, 4- and 5-Selmer elements'.

gaps.title: Orbit counts for the 3-, 4- and 5-Selmer representations are not ST.2 nodes
gaps.detail: Missing from ST.2: the counts of integral orbits of bounded height (averaging over a fundamental domain, cutting off the cusp, main term vol * X^{5/6}) and the tail estimates for infinitely many congruence conditions, for SL3(Z) on ternary cubic forms, for G(Z) on 2 (x) Sym^2(Z^4), and for SL5(Z) x SL5(Z) on quintuples of 5 x 5 alternating matrices. ST.2's tail estimate (uniformity-estimate-for-infinitely-many-congruence-conditions) and counts are for binary quartic forms only.

gaps.title: Parametrisation and counting for the second moment of Sel_2 (Bhargava-Shankar-Swaminathan) are not ST.1/ST.2 nodes
gaps.detail: Missing from ST.1: the parametrisation of 2-Selmer elements of Jacobians of genus-one curves z^2 = f(x, y) (and hyperelliptic Jacobians) by orbits on pairs of n-ary quadratic forms 2 (x) Sym^2(n) (BGW 2017, BSW 2022/2025 items, listed as not decomposed in ST.1's coverage). Missing from ST.2: the count of special integral orbits of SL4 and PSO_A on quadratic forms with equidistribution (BSS Sections 5-7). ST.1/binary-quartic-parametrization-of-two-selmer (attaching z^2 = f(x, y) to sigma) is cited by id. Matches ST.5's gap 'Second-moment proof of Bhargava-Shankar-Swaminathan'.

gaps.title: BKLOS parametrisation and counting over number fields are not ST.1/ST.2 nodes
gaps.detail: Missing from ST.1: the parametrisation of phi-coverings / phi-Selmer elements of E^s for a 3-isogeny phi by SL2(F)-orbits of binary cubic forms with discriminant in a fixed class, integral representatives over O_F, squarefreeness away from a finite set (BKLOS Theorems 4.2, 5.3, 6.2, Proposition 6.1, Corollary 7.1). Missing from ST.2: geometry of numbers over a number field for SL2(O_F) on binary cubic forms (Bhargava-Shankar-Wang, Theorem 13) and the uniformity estimate (Theorem 17). Matches ST.5's gap 'BKLOS binary-cubic parametrisation and counting over number fields'.

gaps.title: Lemke Oliver-Wang-Wood and Datskovsky-Wright results are not ST.3 nodes
gaps.detail: Missing from ST.3 (its coverage lists PAPER-LEMKEOLIVER-WANG-WOOD-25 route 1 as not decomposed): relative class groups Cl_{K/k} with their G-action and the families of G-extensions with fixed infinity data (LOWW Section 7, used by the Cohen-Martinet surjection-moment conjecture); LOWW Theorem 1.1 (average of h_3 over extensions with a transitive 2-group containing a transposition); LOWW Theorem 6.1 (the proven D4 averages C_{G,Sigma} = (1 + 3^{-u(K/F)}) A_w). Also missing: Datskovsky-Wright's 3-torsion averages over quadratic extensions of a number field k != Q (a proved case of Cohen-Lenstra-Martinet; ST.5/cohen-lenstra-heuristic-for-quadratic-fields mentions it only as a remark).

gaps.detail: Missing: the relation between rigid and unrigid averages, E^- = E~^-/|Aut_{G'}(G)| (PAPER-WOOD-19 /13, cited at ST.3), the real multiplicity A(G, G') (/16, cited at ST.0) and its good-case value |c| |Aut_{G'}(G)| (Wood Lemma 2.1, /17, cited at ST.3). ST.3's coverage lists PAPER-WOOD-19 route 2 and ST.0's lists PAPER-WOOD-19 items 2-12, 14-16 as not decomposed.

gaps.detail: Missing from ST.0 (PAPER-WOOD-19 items 2-12, 14-16, 28, 98, listed as not decomposed in ST.0's coverage): quadratic extensions K of F_q(t) with prescribed completion at infinity (imaginary type F_q((t^{-1}))(sqrt t); real type split at infinity), ordered by the norm of the discriminant, the slices IQ_{=q^{2n}} and RQ_{=q^{2n}}, the averages E^+-_{F_q(t), q^{2n}}(G, G') and their rigid versions E~^+-, and the types G' <= G wr S2 with outside involutions c. ST.0/arithmetic-family and ST.0/family-defined-by-local-conditions are the intended hosts.

gaps.title: Primitive residue vectors modulo Q are not an ST.0 node
gaps.detail: Missing from ST.0 (BLS 'primitive-residue', listed as not decomposed in ST.0's coverage): R_m(Q) = {b in (Z/QZ)^m : gcd(Q, b_1, ..., b_m) = 1}, its multiplicativity under the Chinese remainder theorem, and #R_m(p^r) = p^{rm}(1 - p^{-m}) (BLS (5.10)). ST.5's Lean stand-ins FormDensity.primitiveVectors and card_primitiveVectors_primePow are the intended statements.

gaps.detail: Missing from ST.0 (Lipnowski-Tsimerman items unpolarized-count, ppav-count, polarization-fiber, listed as not decomposed): the finite set of isomorphism classes of g-dimensional ppavs over F_p with the uniform measure, A(p, g) = #{ppav classes}, B(p, g) = #{abelian variety classes}, n_A = #(Aut(A)-orbits of principal polarizations on A) and A(p, g) = sum_A n_A. sourceIssues.correction: The 'that is' identifies Goldfeld's statement, which §1.0.2 formulates for fundamental discriminants (both signs, ordered by |d|), with a density-one statement for positive squarefree n ≡ 1, 2, 3 (mod 8) ordered by n. The implication needs a comparison of the two families and orderings: E^(d) ≅ E^(m) for m the positive squarefree part of |d| (twists depend on the squareclass and E^(−m) = E^(m)); |d| = m or 4m according to the sign and m mod 4; by ST.0/density-one-restricts-to-subfamilies-of-positive-lower-density and ST.0/piecewise-rescaling-of-a-height the classes 1, 2, 3 (mod 8) carry exactly half of the fundamental discriminants ordered by |d| and density one within them transfers; root number −1 elsewhere (footnote 2) gives odd analytic order. With this comparison the stated result is right.
sourceIssues.reason: Goldfeld's conjecture in §1.0.2 is stated for '50% of the fundamental discriminants n', a different family (both signs, n ≡ 1 mod 4 or n = 4m) with a different ordering; the paper does not give the comparison. The weights are not equal: for m ≡ 1, 2, 3 (mod 4) the two fundamental discriminants with squarefree part m have |d| ∈ {m, 4m}, {4m, 4m}, {4m, m}. Numerically, among fundamental discriminants with |d| ≤ 2·10⁶ the proportion with m ≡ 1, 2, 3 (mod 8) is 0.49999.

sourceIssues.locator: Theorem 3.1 and Theorem 3.19, pp. 22 and 33 (arXiv v3)
sourceIssues.excerpt: A family F of elliptic curves defined by congruence conditions is then said to be large if, for all but finitely many primes p, the set Invp(F) contains all pairs (I, J) ∈ Zp × Zp such that p² ∤ ∆(I, J).
sourceIssues.printed: Theorem 3.1: 'When all elliptic curves E in any large family are ordered by height, the average size of the 2-Selmer group S2(E) is 3.'
sourceIssues.correction: Add the hypothesis that Inv_p(F) has positive measure for every prime p (equivalently Π_p M_p(F) > 0, i.e. N(F; X) ≫ X^{5/6}); all families the source applies the theorem to satisfy it.
sourceIssues.reason: Largeness constrains only all but finitely many p, and a local set Σ_p may be closed with null boundary and still have measure zero. Example: Σ_5 = {(I, J) : −J/27 has 5-adic digits in {0, 1}} and Σ_p unrestricted (beyond minimality) for p ≠ 5. The integers with base-5 digits in {0, 1} meet every residue class modulo m for 5 ∤ m, so Inv_p(F) is everything at p ∤ 30 and F is large, but M_5(F) = 0 and N(F; X) ≍ X^{1/3 + (log 2)/(2 log 5)} = o(X^{5/6}). Then (72) and (73) are both o(X^{5/6}) and the proof of Theorem 3.19 gives no limit.

restructure.detail: The atlas and RS-07 list SieveMethodsAndPrimePatterns:SV.2 (large sieve, bilinear decompositions) as an input of ArithmeticStatistics:ST.2 ('retain the large-sieve input for uniform family counting').
